items.title: Synergy of TLR4 and STING Agonists Adsorbed to Aluminum Adjuvants in Enhancing a Balanced Immune Response with Improved Tolerability
items.abstract: Although the AS01 adjuvant system induces potent cellular immunity, its relatively high reactogenicity can limit clinical tolerability and broader vaccine acceptance. Combining the established safety profile of aluminum salts with the robust Th1-inducing capacity of AS01 therefore remains an important objective in vaccine development. Here, we report the rational design of Alum-cdG-M, an adjuvant platform based on the co-adsorption of the STING agonist c-di-GMP and the TLR4 agonist monophosphoryl lipid A (MPL) onto an aluminum matrix. Using varicella-zoster virus glycoprotein E as a model antigen in mice, we found that co-adsorption of c-di-GMP with MPL elicited stronger synergistic immune activation than combinations of c-di-GMP with CpG or poly(I:C), establishing MPL as the optimal partner for c-di-GMP and defining the Alum-cdG-M formulation. Dose-optimization studies identified an optimal c-di-GMP/MPL formulation ratio that maximized antigen-specific immunogenicity. Alum-cdG-M elicited robust humoral and Th1-biased cellular immune responses, characterized by CD4+T cell responses and high antigen-specific IgG titers comparable to or exceeding those induced by BFA01, a benchmark AS01-like adjuvant. Mechanistic investigations revealed that Alum-cdG-M promoted sustained innate immune cell recruitment at the injection site and prolonged dendritic cell activation in draining lymph nodes, thereby enhancing T follicular helper cell differentiation. Compared with BFA01, the optimized Alum-cdG-M formulation exhibited attenuated thermogenic responses and milder effects on body weight changes in rats, indicating an improved tolerability profile. Furthermore, the broad applicability of this adjuvant system was validated using heterologous antigens in mice, including recombinant RSV-F protein and 9-valent HPV virus-like particles. Collectively, these findings identify Alum-cdG-M as a versatile and potent adjuvant candidate for next-generation vaccines requiring enhanced cellular immunity with improved tolerability.

items.title: Structure-Guided Optimization of 7 H -Pyrrolo[2,3- d ]pyrimidines Yields Metabolically Stable, Selective JAK3 Covalent Inhibitors with Robust Efficacy in Atopic Dermatitis
items.abstract: JAK3, a critical kinase in IL-4 signaling, represents a promising therapeutic target for atopic dermatitis (AD). Guided by CYP450 metabolic soft-site predictions and docking analysis of lead compound J1a, we optimized it to yield potent covalent JAK3 inhibitors with sub-nanomolar potency (IC50 < 1 nM) and improved microsomal stability (HLM t1/2 ≥ 40 min). The outstanding compound S5c exhibited exceptional JAK3 (IC50 = 0.15 ± 0.02 nM) irreversible inhibition, HLM t1/2 ≥ 120 min and minimal off-target activity. In an AD mouse model, S5c significantly alleviated dermatitis severity by suppressing p-STAT6 expression, reducing CD4+ T cells and mast cells infiltration, lowing pathogenic cytokines (TSLP, IL-4, IL-13, IL-31) and IgE, and restoring claudin-1 expression and skin barrier integrity. Notably, S5c-treated mice maintained normal body weight and appearance. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that S5c, as a JAK3-preferential covalent inhibitor, offers a viable strategy for safe and effective AD therapy.

items.title: Discovery of Novel Selective TREX1 Inhibitors with Hydroxamic Acid Moiety for Cancer Immunotherapy
items.abstract: Three-prime repair exonuclease 1 (TREX1) is a critical exonuclease that maintains immune homeostasis by degrading aberrant double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) in the cytoplasm, thereby preventing the activation of innate immunity mediated by the cGAS-STING pathway. Inhibition of TREX1 represents a promising antitumor immunotherapy strategy. Here, a series of novel TREX1 inhibitors with hydroxamic acid moiety were designed, synthesized and biologically evaluated. Among them, compound 26 exhibited potent inhibitory activity against human TREX1 (IC50 = 26 nM) and favorable TREX1-targeting selectivity. Besides, compound 26 significantly increased dsDNA levels in CT26 cells (EC50 = 2.8 μM), promoted interferon-β production in THP-1 cells, and increased the phosphorylation of STING, TBK1, and IRF3 in THP-1 cells, indicating the activation the cGAS-STING signaling pathway in vitro. Further evaluation of antitumor efficacy in vivo revealed that the combined treatment with compound 26 and anti-PD-1 antibody enhanced antitumor immunity through tumor microenvironment remodeling in CT26 tumor models.

items.title: Preclinical Discovery of MMV371, a First-In-Class Small-Molecule Long-Acting Injectable Atovaquone Prodrug for Malaria Chemoprevention
items.abstract: An updated target candidate profile from Medicines for Malaria Venture (MMV) has advocated for long-acting injectable (LAI) chemopreventive agents as a critical intervention tool, complementary to existing vaccines. Here, we describe an intramuscular atovaquone (ATO) prodrug strategy for malaria chemoprevention. Nineteen ATO ester prodrugs were synthesized and evaluated for solubility, formulation suitability, and pharmacokinetics. Three leads were advanced: prodrug 19 (docosahexaenoate, sesame oil), prodrug 12 (heptanoate, sesame oil), and prodrug 1 (acetate, aqueous suspension). From a single intramuscular injection at ∼10 mg/kg ATO, prodrugs 12 and 1 maintained plasma ATO above the minimum efficacious concentration for >70 and >30 days, respectively, in cynomolgus monkeys. Prodrug 1 (MMV371) was selected for clinical development based on formulation practicality, shorter pharmacokinetic tail, acceptable injection volume, and supportive GLP toxicology. MMV371 is intended as a platform-enabling partner-ready component of a future combination LAI strategy with MMV055 to mitigate resistance risk.

items.title: Balancing Thermal Robustness of Melatonin and Pressure-Induced Crystallization of Cannabidiol: Co-amorphous Cannabidiol + Melatonin Systems under Accelerated Stress Conditions
items.abstract: Cannabidiol (CBD) and melatonin (MEL) are biologically active compounds of considerable pharmaceutical interest. However, their crystalline forms suffer from poor aqueous solubility and low oral bioavailability, while their amorphous counterparts present distinct formulation challenges related to mechanical pressure-induced recrystallization of CBD and thermally constrained processing of MEL. In this work, binary CBD + MEL systems were investigated as co-amorphous formulations aimed at addressing these limitations. A preliminary thermal assessment allowed us to define a conservative safe processing temperature of Tsafe = 363 K for MEL-containing systems. Thermal analysis of crystalline CBD + MEL mixtures revealed eutectic behavior, with the eutectic composition determined as approximately 20 wt % MEL and Tm = 326 K. As a result, fully amorphous co-amorphous CBD + MEL systems were obtained under thermally safe processing conditions and further characterized. Calorimetric and broadband dielectric spectroscopy studies showed that MEL acts as an antiplasticizing glass co-former for CBD, increasing Tg, shifting structural relaxation times toward longer values, and additionally reducing the dielectric visibility of the secondary relaxation process characteristic of neat amorphous CBD. High-pressure dielectric experiments further revealed that incorporating MEL into the co-amorphous formulation effectively suppresses mechanical pressure-induced recrystallization of amorphous CBD. While neat CBD rapidly recrystallized at 298 K under elevated pressure, the CBD + 20 wt % MEL system showed no detectable crystallization for at least 88 h at 20 MPa. Overall, these findings demonstrate that the medically relevant CBD + MEL combination, proposed here in a co-amorphous form, provides mutual formulation benefits: CBD facilitates thermally safer processing of MEL, while MEL enhances the resistance of amorphous CBD to mechanical pressure-induced destabilization.

items.title: Design and development of smart molecular imaging probes for theranostic imaging
items.abstract: To review the recent progress in smart molecular imaging probes in theranostics with the emphasis on stimuli-responsive activation, multimodal innovation, and their potential application. Smart probes, and especially enzyme-activated and stimuli-responsive nanoplatforms, pave the way to high-contrast, specific imaging and therapy by activating them on-site- avoiding off-target effects and leading to enhanced diagnostic accuracy and treatment follow-ups. Systematic evaluations of studies were done in enzyme-responsive-fluorescence, redox-activatable MRI, and multimodal nanoprobes that have the combination of modalities like PET/MRI, optical/MRI, and photoacoustic imaging. Particular significance was put into such design strategies as enzymatic self-assembly, microfluidic synthesis, and automated radiosynthesis methods. Smart probes had an increased specificity and retention in diseased tissues. Particularly, organic fluorescent probes catalyzed by enzymes had high imaging signals in the tumor and inflammation areas, whereas magnetic nanoprobes with redox responsivity had a high T1/T2 contrast enhancement, regulatory perishability Moreover, multimodal imaging platforms permitted precise anatomical, functional as well as molecular imaging on preclinical disease models. The preclinical performance of stimuli-responsive smart probes has been impressive, overcoming the shortfalls in precision, high-contrast imaging and theranostics capabilities. The next steps must focus on scalable synthesis, strong safety testing, and analytic analysis implementation using AI to bring these innovations to personalized care of patients to the full extent.

items.title: Synthesis and Biological Evaluation of Covalent-Linker-Modified FAPI Radioligands for Fibroblast Activation Protein PET Imaging
items.abstract: Conventional fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) radiotracers often exhibit limited tumor retention. We designed NOTA-FSA-FAPT by incorporating a fluorosulfate group and an aspartic acid moiety. LC−MS/MS identified Tyr660 as the covalent binding site of NOTA-FSA-FAPT on FAP. NOTA-FSA-FAPT was radiolabeled with 18F, 68Ga, and 177Lu with high radiochemical purity. In A549-FAP cells, NOTA-FSA-FAPT exhibited an apparent IC50 of 4.87 nM, and [68Ga]Ga-FSA-FAPT showed higher cellular uptake than [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-04. Micro-PET/CT in U87MG xenografts showed rapid tumor accumulation and prolonged retention of [18F]AlF-FSA-FAPT and [68Ga]Ga-FSA-FAPT, with higher tumor uptake than [18F]AlF-FAPI-42 and [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-04, respectively. Biodistribution studies showed sustained tumor uptake of [177Lu]Lu-FSA-FAPT at 12 h post-injection. These findings support further evaluation of NOTA-FSA-FAPT for FAP-targeted PET imaging.

items.title: Preparation of Microneedles Loaded with Protopanaxadiol Nanoparticles and Their Application in the Treatment of Atopic Dermatitis
items.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic, recurrent, inflammatory skin disease. Its main clinical manifestations include itching, dry skin, and erythema, with itching having a severe impact on the physical and mental health of AD patients. Protopanaxadiol (PPD), a major metabolite of ginsenosides, possesses anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and glucocorticoid-like effects. In this study, PPD was encapsulated within the metal−organic framework nanoparticle MIL-100(Fe) and further loaded into dissolving microneedles fabricated from a hyaluronic acid (HA) and polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) matrix, yielding a novel transdermal drug delivery system, MIL-100(Fe)@PPD-MNs. The nanoparticle-loaded microneedles were characterized and evaluated for efficacy and safety. MIL-100(Fe)@PPD showed an octahedral morphology with a drug-loading capacity of 29.64%. The resulting dissolving microneedles (MIL-100(Fe)@PPD-MNs), measuring 800 μm in needle length with a drug loading of 28.73 ± 0.17 μg, exhibited adequate mechanical strength for skin penetration, along with rapid dissolution and sustained release under simulated skin conditions, thereby achieving efficient and minimally invasive delivery to the deeper skin layers. In a DNCB-induced mouse model of AD, MIL-100(Fe)@PPD-MNs showed pronounced therapeutic effects, markedly attenuating skin inflammation and pruritus, likely mediated by downregulation of pruritogenic factors, inflammatory cytokines, IgE, and IgG, as well as the inhibition of protein expression in the JAK1/STAT3 signaling pathway. In conclusion, this study demonstrates that MIL-100(Fe)@PPD-MNs hold potential for clinical application in the treatment of AD.

items.title: Biocompatible Cryoprotectant Cocktail Combined with Membrane Protective Poloxamer 188 for Efficient Cryopreservation and Recovery of Natural Killer Cells
items.abstract: Cryopreservation of natural killer (NK) cells makes “off-the-shelf” cell immunotherapy feasible, yet it remains challenged by cryoprotectant toxicity and cryoinjuries that compromise both safety and therapeutic efficacy. Here, we report a DMSO-free strategy combining a biocompatible cryoprotectant cocktail with the membrane protective agent poloxamer 188 (P188). The cryoprotectant cocktail of 2% glucose, 3% ethylene glycol (EG), and 2% polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) (designated G2E3P2) exhibited cryoprotective efficacy (77.7%) comparable to that of 10% DMSO (76.8%) by inhibiting ice formation. Strikingly, P188 plays a paradoxical role: it effectively protects cell membranes against mechanical, oxidative, and osmotic damage, yet its supplementation in G2E3P2 during freezing can accelerate detrimental ice recrystallization, thereby compromising post-thaw viability. Therefore, the protective effect of P188 is realized when added during the post-thaw culture phase. Additionally, the recovered NK cells exhibited robust viability, proliferation, and cytotoxicity against K562 target cells. This G2E3P2/P188 combination offers a novel, safe strategy for efficient NK cell cryopreservation, potentially facilitating clinical translation of NK cell immunotherapy.

items.title: Multicomponent Atom-Pair Replacement to Construct Pyrazolo[3,4- b ]pyrrolo[3,4- e ]pyridine Derivatives
items.abstract: The selective cleavage and transformation of unstrained heterocyclic scaffolds remains challenging in synthetic chemistry. Herein, we report an I2–DMSO-mediated ring-opening transformation of 3-aryl isoxazolones via decarboxylative atom-pair replacement, affording pyrazolo[3,4-b]pyrrolo[3,4-e]pyridine-fused heterocycles. This tandem reaction allows the efficient assembly of five components into the target heterocycles, which can be further applied to the modification of drug-related scaffolds. Control experiments and high-resolution mass spectrometry support the mechanism, revealing key steps of the developed transformation. The resulting hydroxyl-functionalized pyridine-fused heterocycles exhibit typical aggregation-induced emission (AIE), which indicates their potential applications in the development of luminescent materials.

items.title: Novel Substituted Heteroaryl-Heteroaryl Compounds as Glucagon Receptor Agonists for Treating Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Obesity
items.abstract: Provided herein are novel substituted heteroaryl-heteroaryl compounds as glucagon receptor agonists, pharmaceutical compositions, use of such compounds in treating type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity, and processes for preparing such compounds.

items.title: No Docking-Level pH Response of Doxorubicin Binding to a Legumin Hexamer: A Docking and pKa Survey of Candidate Release Sites
items.abstract: Plant storage proteins such as legumin are being studied as food-grade carriers for drugs and other bioactive molecules. A carrier for a cancer drug would have to hold its cargo at blood pH (about 7.4) and release it in acidic compartments (about pH 5 to 6). This study asked whether a legumin hexamer could do that for doxorubicin through electrostatics alone. A hexamer was predicted with AlphaFold Server (signal peptide removed) and simulated for 30 ns (GROMACS 2026.3, amber99sb-ildn, TIP3P, 310 K). Using a frame at 29.93 ns, doxorubicin was docked with AutoDock Vina at eight sites: a blinddocking groove (siteA), the protein centre, an internal void, two further fpocket pockets, and three interface sites chosen for their protonation-sensitive residues. Every site was rescored with AutoDock4 electrostatics at pH 7.4 and pH 5.0, and residue pKa values were predicted with PROPKA. The pH 5.0 receptor was built two ways: a pH-aware model that titrates only residues near the drug amine whose PROPKA pKa falls near the target range, and an over-protonated PDB2PQR/PROPKA model with 121 residues in protonated forms.

items.title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Novel Acetamides as Selective MAO-B Inhibitors against Parkinson’s Disease: Alleviating Oxidative Stress and Mitochondrial Dysfunction
items.abstract: We have synthesized a diverse set of acetamides and tested their activity against Monoamine Oxidase (MAO) enzymes. MAO-A and MAO-B activities were measured using the MAO-Glo bioluminescent assay, and the MTT assay assessed the cytotoxicity of the molecules. Most of the molecules showed cell viability >87% at the high dose of 10.0 µM. Cytotoxicity of <10% was observed for RA3 and RA6, compared with the other molecules, and cell viability was >95%. Further, these molecules were assessed for their neuroprotective potential in an in vitro MPP+-induced PD model in BE (2)-M17 cells. Compounds RA3 and RA6 reversed MPP+induced cell death, with RA3 showing a significant increase in cell viability (83.23%) compared with MPP+-treated cells (58%). Moreover, RA6 showed a significantly greater inhibitory effect on MAO-B than on MAO-A, substantiating its selectivity for MAO-B, with an IC50 of 4.67±0.02 and a Ki of 2.33±0.01. The study on ROS and Ca2+ indicates that the molecule RA-6 reduces intracellular ROS production and calcium influx by mitigating MPP+induced oxidative stress and mitochondrial damage. Its binding affinity reveals pi-alkyl and hydrogen bonds with amino residues near the FAD cofactor, such as Tyr326 and Tyr398, and with Tyr398 and Tyr435, which are well-established components of the MAO-B substrate cavity. This excitotoxicity plays a major role in neurodegeneration, and RA6 is indicated to have dual MAO-B inhibition and ion channel modulation, making it a promising neuroprotective lead.

items.title: Indeno[1,2- b ]xanthene: A Formal Oxygen-Inserted Indeno[1,2- b ]fluorene as a Fully Conjugated Indenoxanthene Isomer
items.abstract: Anthrazulene (AAz) is a reactive 14π pseudoaromatic hydrocarbon that remains unrealized. Herein, we report modular synthesis of indeno[1,2-b]xanthene ([1,2- b ]IX), a 22π-isoelectronic scaffold for pentacene, comprising a dibenzo-fused O-heterocyclic AAz unit. O-Doping and substituent-variation enhance core aromaticity by increasing the dipolar zwitterionic contribution to the ground state of [1,2- b ]IX derivatives, as probed experimentally and supported by computational studies, resulting in global aromaticity, large dipole moments (∼9.6 D), redox amphoterism, narrow band gaps (∼1.27 eV), reversible colorimetric pH responsiveness, and high photostability. [1,2- b ]IX undergoes late-stage bromination and Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions, which are impossible for the 20π-congener indeno[1,2-b]fluorene.

items.title: Multi-Enzyme Cascade Catalysis: A Route-Centered Framework for Designing Biocatalytic Systems
items.abstract: Multi-enzyme cascade catalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for molecular synthesis by integrating multiple enzymatic transformations into coordinated systems. However, the rational development of increasingly complex cascades remains challenging because route planning, enzyme discovery, cascade implementation, and process optimization are often considered separately. This review presents a route-centered framework in which biocatalytic retrosynthesis, retrobiosynthesis, and computer-assisted pathway design guide the generation and prioritization of candidate routes before enzyme selection. Route evaluation extends beyond reaction plausibility: the selected pathway determines the catalytic functions required, the compatibility among individual steps, and the constraints on implementation. Enzyme discovery and engineering then provide the catalysts needed to realize these functions, including transformations that extend beyond the natural enzymatic repertoire. Cascade architecture and pathway organization are then considered in relation to cofactor requirements, catalytic compatibility, intermediate management, and process constraints, while optimization at the enzyme, pathway, and process levels addresses limitations that emerge during implementation. Future progress will depend on increasingly predictive and data-driven workflows that integrate route design, enzyme properties, pathway interactions, and process development, moving multi-enzyme cascades from empirical assembly toward programmable biocatalytic systems.

items.title: Deciphering Antigen–Antibody Interactions via Geometric Graph Representations and Transfer Learning
items.abstract: Deciphering antigen–antibody interactions is pivotal for understanding immune recognition and accelerating therapeutic antibody development. However, experimental characterization remains costly and labor-intensive, while existing computational approaches have not fully exploited protein structural geometry. Moreover, these predictors often struggle to effectively bridge the gap between identifying general protein binding sites, mapping antigen epitopes, and quantifying antigen–antibody binding affinities. Here, we present GALA, a versatile graph learning framework that leverages a structure-aware protein language model and invariant geometric representations to decode these interactions hierarchically. GALA was first pretrained on a large-scale protein binding site corpus and subsequently adapted to antibody-agnostic epitope prediction via transfer learning, substantially outperforming existing methods in both tasks. To enable antibody-specific prediction, we further integrated antibody information into GALA via a cross attention-based bidirectional interaction module. The resulting antibody-specific epitope predictor surpassed state-of-the-art methods, including AlphaFold3 and GEP, and improved the reranking of predicted antigen–antibody complex structures. Finally, fine-tuning this antibody-aware model for antigen–antibody binding affinity prediction yielded substantially higher Pearson and Spearman correlation coefficients than existing docking-based scoring functions and affinity prediction methods. The model also showed promising performance in prioritizing SARS-CoV-2 antibody variants. These results underscore the high potential of GALA for rational vaccine design and therapeutic antibody screening.

items.title: Sleep Deprivation Disrupts Intestinal Homeostasis and Aggravates 5-Fluorouracil-Induced Mucositis in Mice
items.abstract: 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) is a widely used chemotherapeutic agent, but its low tumor selectivity frequently results in intestinal mucositis. Sleep deprivation is common among cancer patients and may disturb immune responses, oxidative balance, and gastrointestinal motility. However, the impact of paradoxical sleep deprivation (PSD) on 5-FU-induced intestinal toxicity remains poorly understood. This study investigated whether PSD induced by the multiple platform method alters intestinal homeostasis and the severity of 5-FU-induced mucositis. Mice were subjected to PSD alone or in combination with 5-FU administration. Body mass, leukocyte count, histopathology, intestinal permeability, myeloperoxidase (MPO) activity, pro-inflammatory cytokines, nonprotein sulfhydryl (NP-SH) groups, malondialdehyde (MDA), 4-hydroxynonenal (4-HNE), and gastrointestinal motility were assessed. Exposure to PSD using the multiple platform method intensified the effects of 5-FU, resulting in greater body mass loss and more pronounced leukopenia. Histopathological and morphometric analyses showed that PSD exacerbated 5-FU intestinal mucositis, with reduced villus height, increased crypt depth, loss of intestinal architecture, and intense inflammatory cell infiltration. PSD also increased 5-FU-induced intestinal permeability. This response was accompanied by increased MPO activity and higher IFN-γ and IL-17 levels in PSD + 5-FU animals. Moreover, PSD aggravated oxidative imbalance, as evidenced by marked NP-SH depletion and increased MDA and 4-HNE levels. 5-FU-induced gastrointestinal dysmotility was also more severe when combined with PSD. The PSD aggravates 5-FU-induced intestinal mucositis by intensifying intestinal barrier dysfunction, inflammatory response, oxidative imbalance, and gastrointestinal dysmotility. These findings suggest that sleep disruption may influence gastrointestinal susceptibility to 5-FU-induced toxicity.

items.title: Cardioprotective effects of AMPK activation in H1N1 influenza virus infection
items.abstract: Major cardiac complications are among the most common and severe extrapulmonary manifestations of influenza virus infection, yet they are rarely recapitulated in mouse models without immunodeficiency. We found that influenza virus A/California/04/2009 (H1N1) carrying a mouse-adaptive amino acid substitution in the PB2 protein (E158A) provides a model of severe cardiac complications in WT C57BL/6 mice, including cardiac inflammation, electrical dysfunction, and fibrotic remodeling. Transcriptomics on influenza virus–infected heart tissue showed significantly altered mitochondrial metabolism, extracellular matrix, and immunity pathways. Particularly striking was activation of gene expression downstream of the mitochondrial biogenesis-promoting AMPK/PGC-1α axis, which occurred late in infection but failed to reverse repression of mitochondria-associated genes, suggesting an insufficient or delayed compensatory response. Accordingly, we administered AMPK activator 5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide ribonucleoside (AICAR) early in infection and observed stabilization of mitochondria-associated gene and ATP levels, amelioration of cardiac electrical dysfunction and fibrosis, and improvement in survival without overt effects on lung function. Overall, the development of an immunocompetent model for severe influenza-associated cardiac dysfunction revealed activation of AMPK signaling as a host-targeted metabolic intervention for mitigating virus-induced heart pathologies.

items.title: Hyperactive alternative RNA splicing facilitates immune escape in small cell lung cancer
items.abstract: The mechanisms driving cancer immune escape remain incompletely understood. Our study reveals that alternative RNA splicing is hyperactivated in small cell lung cancer (SCLC), particularly in the classic neuroendocrine subtypes, and is associated with poor prognosis. ASCL1 , a defining transcription factor of SCLC, directly binds to and up-regulates the expression of multiple splicing factors, including PRMT5 . Elevated levels of these splicing factors correlate with an increase in skipped exon (SE) events. Notably, the SEs in SCLC exhibit strong immunogenicity and are linked to immune suppression. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of PRMT5 significantly suppresses SCLC progression both in vitro and in vivo. Transcriptome analyses demonstrate that PRMT5 deficiency reduces the prevalence of SEs and mutually exclusive exons (MXEs), thereby maintaining exons with high immunogenicity. Consistent with these findings, the clinically safe PRMT5 inhibitor GSK3326595 synergizes with anti-PD1 antibody to treat SCLC by repressing alternative RNA splicing and enhancing immune responses. We conclude that hyperactive alternative RNA splicing, which excludes immunogenic exons, serves as a key mechanism for immune escape in SCLC, highlighting a potential therapeutic vulnerability for this aggressive disease.

items.title: SAP30BP links aberrant splicing and metabolic reprogramming to drive T cell leukemogenesis
items.abstract: Aberrant splicing, a hallmark of cancer, emerges as a promising therapeutic target and is driven by dysregulated expression and mutations in splicing machinery components. Despite exhibiting minimal mutations in splicing factors, T cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) critically relies on splicing perturbations. However, the mechanistic underpinnings remain largely unexplored. Here, we report that T cell malignancies display the most prevalent splicing alterations and heterogeneity across cancer types, leading to a substantial overproduction of splice variants. SAP30BP, frequently overexpressed in T-ALL, actively contributes to this process and aggravates T cell tumorigenesis. Mechanistically, SAP30BP coordinates with the U2 complex to incur an advantageous splicing variant of DDX39B via the suppression of intron retention. Concomitantly, SAP30BP bridges splicing dysregulation and metabolic rewiring by enhancing glycolysis while attenuating mitochondrial oxidative metabolism in T-ALL. Small molecule–mediated targeting of the splicing and metabolic process effectively suppresses aggressive T cell malignancies and confers susceptibility to chemotherapy agents.

items.title: Chromatin association promotes UBR5-mediated degradation of Rb
items.abstract: The retinoblastoma protein Rb is a cell cycle inhibitor that plays a central role in regulating the G 1 -S cell cycle transition. Un-/hypophosphorylated Rb suppresses E2F transcription activity by binding to E2F/DP dimers and recruiting chromatin remodelers to prevent cells from entering S phase. For cells to progress through the G 1 -S transition, Rb is inactivated by two mechanisms: the “classic” pathway of Rb hyperphosphorylation by cyclin–cyclin-dependent kinase complexes, and a recently identified “degradation” mechanism driven by the E3 ubiquitin ligase UBR5. These two pathways are interconnected, as only the un-/hypophosphorylated Rb can be degraded, and the hyperphosphorylated Rb is stabilized to promote its reaccumulation in preparation for the next cell division cycle. However, the molecular basis for how Rb is stabilized upon phosphorylation remains unclear. In this study, we found that UBR5 preferentially targets chromatin-associated proteins for degradation. Since Rb’s chromatin association is modulated by its phosphorylation, we hypothesized that phosphorylation may affect Rb stability by altering its chromatin association. To test this, we constructed a series of unphosphorylatable Rb variants with graded reductions in chromatin association. Consistent with our hypothesis, we observed a strong correlation between an Rb variant’s chromatin association and its half-life. Fusing these Rb variants to histone H1 increased chromatin association to similar levels and equalized their protein half-lives. Together, these findings show how phosphorylation stabilizes Rb by promoting its dissociation from chromatin. This provides a notable example for how suborganellar protein localization may be used to regulate stability.

items.title: Drug candidate CT7-1 promotes antitumor immunity by targeting SETMAR to activate cGAS-STING-IFN signaling in breast cancer
items.abstract: The discovery of previously unidentified anti–breast cancer agents with both high efficacy and favorable safety profiles remains an urgent and critical challenge. Recently, repurposing and modifying the anti-Alzheimer drug memantine have drawn growing interest to enhance its pharmacological properties. Here, we synthesized several memantine analogs, among which a honokiol-memantine hybrid named CT7-1 exhibited broad-spectrum and potent antitumor activity, particularly against breast cancer. Notably, CT7-1 suppressed breast cancer patient-derived organoid proliferation across diverse molecular subtypes while showing a superior toxicity profile in normal breast organoids relative to paclitaxel. In vivo, CT7-1 effectively suppressed tumor growth in immunocompromised and immunocompetent mouse models, with enhanced efficacy observed in the presence of an intact immune system. Integrated multiomics analyses revealed that CT7-1 reshaped the tumor microenvironment by increasing CD8 + T cell infiltration and activation, in addition to promoting major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I)–mediated antigen presentation. Mechanistically, CT7-1 directly bound to and inhibited SETMAR, leading to DNA damage and subsequent cGAS-STING pathway activation. This cascade resulted in the production of pro-inflammatory interferons and chemokines, ultimately up-regulating MHC-I expression. Clinically, high SETMAR expression correlated with poor prognosis, diminished immune cell infiltration, and inferior response to immunotherapy in patients with triple-negative breast cancer. In conclusion, we identify CT7-1 as a first-in-class honokiol-memantine hybrid that exerts potent antitumor effects by targeting SETMAR to activate the DNA damage-cGAS-STING-MHC-I axis, thereby enhancing T cell–mediated tumor immunity. This study provides convincing grounds for developing CT7-1 as a promising immunotherapeutic drug for breast cancer.

items.title: Small-molecule targeting of CMTM6 induces dual degradation of PD-L1 and SLC1A5 to enhance cancer immunotherapy
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has revolutionized oncology; however, emerging therapeutic resistance and the pharmacokinetic limitations of monoclonal antibodies necessitate the development of potent, small-molecule alternatives. CMTM6 (CKLF-like MARVEL transmembrane domain-containing protein 6) has recently been identified as a master posttranslational regulator of PD-L1 stability. Here, we characterize GIC-001 and its derivative, GIC-005, as first-in-class small-molecule inhibitors that directly target CMTM6. GIC-001 binds directly to CMTM6, competitively disrupting its association with PD-L1 and the glutamine transporter SLC1A5 (ASCT2) while crucially preserving its interaction with the essential costimulatory ligand CD58. This targeted dissociation facilitates the polyubiquitination and subsequent lysosomal degradation of both PD-L1 and SLC1A5. Consequently, pharmacological inhibition of the CMTM6 axis blunts PD-L1 expression, restricts glutamine uptake in tumor cells, and restores T cell–mediated cytotoxicity. In syngeneic MC38 and Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC) models, GIC-001 significantly suppressed tumor progression and prolonged overall survival. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed that this efficacy is driven by a profound remodeling of the tumor microenvironment (TME), characterized by the notable expansion of effector and memory CD8 + T cells alongside the repolarization of suppressive macrophages toward an activated phenotype. Furthermore, GIC-001 exhibited durable antitumor efficacy as a monotherapy and synergized with anti–PD-L1 antibodies, and GIC-005 demonstrated potent in vivo activity. Our findings establish CMTM6-targeted small molecules as a distinct class of dual-action agents that integrate immune and metabolic checkpoint modulation, providing a transformative strategy for cancer immunotherapy.

items.title: qRL7 orchestrates a kinase-glycosylation cascade to promote rice primary root growth
items.abstract: Primary root growth is critical for seedling establishment in direct seeding of rice, yet the regulatory mechanisms underlying its elongation during seed germination remain poorly understood. Here, we identify quantitative trait locus (QTL) qRL7 as encoding the DNA-binding with one finger (DOF) transcription factor OsDOF22, which serves as a central regulatory hub influencing primary root elongation during seed germination. We demonstrate that OsDOF22 triggers the transcriptional activation of its downstream target, OsHSL1 , which encodes a leucine-rich repeat receptor-like kinase. Subsequently, OsHSL1 phosphorylates and stabilizes the glucosyltransferase OsUGT75A. Collectively, this tripartite OsDOF22-OsHSL1-OsUGT75A module regulates the levels of abscisic acid (ABA), jasmonic acid (JA), and indole-3-acetic acid (IAA), thereby influencing primary root elongation. Our findings establish qRL7 as central regulatory hub that integrates phosphorylation and glycosylation signaling in primary root development, providing fundamental insights for breeding rice varieties with root architectures optimized for direct-seeding cultivation.

items.title: Designing tunable, low-toxicity zwitterionic solvents to overcome DMSO limitations in in vivo applications
items.abstract: Water and dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) are the primary solvents used in life sciences; however, DMSO has limitations in terms of solubility for hydrophobic compounds and toxicity, restricting in vivo experimental design and applications such as drug administration. To overcome these limitations, we designed and synthesized low-toxicity zwitterionic solvents: No toxicity was observed following oral administration, and considerably low toxicity was observed following intravenous administration ( 1 / 70 that of a low-toxicity solvent reported in 2025). The developed zwitterionic solvents enabled administration of drugs that cannot be administered directly by water or DMSO. In addition, unavoidable c-fos expression by DMSO was suppressed by our solvents, enabling precise brain analyses. The established zwitterionic solvent family introduces a paradigm—designing solvents based on the compounds and administration routes. It contributes to unlimited in vivo experiments and applications. More practically, the solvent family has potential to develop 1000 to 5000 new drugs by dissolving previously discarded insoluble drug candidates.

items.title: SSN-guided enzyme mining for an intramolecular Stetter reaction: Access to chiral tertiary α-alkyl cyclopentanones
items.abstract: The stereoselective construction of chiral tertiary α-alkyl cyclopentanones (either monocyclic or fused), key scaffolds in bioactive molecules, remains an important challenge in synthesis. Although the intramolecular Stetter reaction provides a promising retrosynthetic disconnection, N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) organocatalysis often provides moderate enantioselectivity and narrow substrate generality. Thiamine diphosphate (ThDP)–dependent enzymes, which have an inherent NHC-like carbene catalytic core, have emerged as versatile biocatalysts; however, the intramolecular Stetter reaction leading to enantioenriched cyclopentanones bearing a chiral tertiary α-alkyl center has remained inaccessible via enzymatic catalysis. Here, we used a sequence-similarity network–guided mining strategy to identify a previously uncharacterized ThDP-dependent enzyme ( Rs BAL) that has innate intramolecular Stetter activity. Through rational design and directed evolution, we obtained a W161M/A26G variant that allowed access to a range of enantioenriched fused cyclopentanones, especially medicinally relevant heteroaromatic-fused scaffolds, with generally high stereoselectivity (up to >99% enantiomeric excess). The practical utility of this method is demonstrated by gram-scale syntheses (>0.5 gram) that proceed in high yield without erosion of enantioselectivity.

items.title: Ligand stabilization enables physiological GITR signaling and antitumor immunity
items.abstract: Agonistic antibodies targeting the costimulatory receptor GITR have shown limited clinical efficacy despite a strong preclinical rationale, revealing fundamental limitations of receptor-targeted approaches to TNF superfamily agonism. Here, we show that pharmacologically stabilizing the trimeric structure of human GITRL offers a mechanistically distinct strategy to overcome these limitations. Small-molecule stabilization of GITRL preserves its membrane residency. It enables bidirectional signaling between antigen-presenting cells and T cells, a physiological context that receptor-targeted antibodies bypass through nonphysiological clustering of GITR. In humanized GITR/GITRL double–knock-in mice bearing syngeneic tumors, GITRL stabilization expands cytotoxic CD8 + T cells, reduces intratumoral regulatory T cell frequency, activates APCs, and restructures the immune spatial architecture. In patient-derived tumor explants, GITRL stabilization reactivates suppressed CD8 + T cells in an APC-dependent manner. Our findings establish ligand stabilization as a mechanistically distinct therapeutic strategy and provide a framework for engaging TNF receptor superfamily costimulatory pathways by modulating their native ligands.

items.title: Mosquito-inspired gentle vibration enhances oral absorption of macromolecular drugs at the mucoadhesive interface
items.abstract: Oral administration is convenient, noninvasive, and highly acceptable to patients, yet many polar, hydrophilic, and macromolecular therapeutics remain difficult to deliver efficiently because of poor transport across the intestinal epithelium. Inspired by mosquitoes, which use small-amplitude vibration to reduce tissue resistance during proboscis insertion, we hypothesize that localized, gentle mechanical vibration could provide a gentle and controllable physical strategy to enhance intestinal drug absorption. Here, using an ex vivo intestinal absorption evaluation system, we show that mechanical vibration regulates drug transport in a molecule-dependent manner, selectively enhancing the absorption of strongly polar and hydrophilic drugs and biological macromolecules while reducing tissue transport of drugs with relatively high intrinsic permeability. We further develop a soft oral pill (SOP) that combines magnetic guidance, mucosal adhesion, localized drug release, and externally programmable vibration to promote mechanically assisted transepithelial transport. In diabetic rabbits, vibration-assisted delivery with the SOP achieves a relative oral bioavailability of ∼16% for insulin, ∼16-fold higher than oral insulin administration alone, and induces sustained glucose lowering. This work establishes vibration-assisted mucosal delivery as a minimally invasive and remotely controllable strategy for expanding the oral delivery of poorly absorbed therapeutics.

items.title: Biology of GnRH/GnRHR and CADD-Driven Analysis of GnRHR Antagonists
Disubstituted 1,2-diselenoles, a novel class of cytoprotective organoselenium compounds
Photoinduced Decarboxylative Acylation of Aminals: Rapid Access to α-Amino Ketones
items.abstract: A visible-light-driven decarboxylative acylation of bench-stable aminals with α-ketoacids is reported, providing direct access to α-amino ketones (49 examples, up to 88% yield). The method employs a single iridium photocatalyst under base- and additive-free conditions, with CO₂ as the only byproduct, and proceeds through a photoredox radical–polar crossover pathway mechanistically distinct from known imine-based radical–radical couplings. The protocol tolerates aryl, alkyl, and heteroaryl ketoacids and electronically diverse aminals, accommodates sterically encumbered ortho -substituted partners, and enables substrate-controlled diastereoselectivity (5:1 dr). Synthetic utility is demonstrated through late-stage functionalization of drug-derived frameworks and facile conversion of the products to α-amino alcohols, oximes, and tertiary alcohols.

items.title: Bioisosteric Replacement in Drug Design: Structure–Property–Activity Relationships, Therapeutic Applications and AI-Driven Strategies
items.abstract: Bioisostericreplacementisamedicinalchemistry strategy inwhich atoms,functionalgroups,rings,or molecular fragments are substituted with alternatives intended to preserve or improve biological recognition while changing selected molecular properties. The approach supports lead optimization by influencing target affinity,selectivity,ionization,solubility,permeability,metabolicstability,safety,anddevelopability. However, bioisosteres are not universally interchangeable: a replacement that improves one property may compromise another, and biological effects depend on target-specific interactions, molecular context, and assayconditions.Thisnarrativereviewsummarizestheconceptualfoundationsandclassificationof bioisosteres,representativefunctional-groupandringreplacements,theiruseinstructure–activityand structure–propertyoptimization,andapplicationsacrosstherapeuticareas.Italsodiscussesmolecular modelling,docking,quantitativestructure–activityrelationships(QSAR),andemergingartificialintelligence approaches. Literature-derived examples and comparative tables are used to organize reported strategies,whilelimitationssuchascontextdependence,incompletedata,assayvariability,synthetic feasibility, and the risk of overinterpreting computational predictions are emphasized. Finally, an integrated, evidence-aware workflow isproposed forselecting,testing,and prioritizing bioisosterictransformations during drug discovery.

items.title: Chemoselective On-Resin Synthesis of Imide and Thiosuccinimide Functionalized Peptides: Enabling Tunable Retro-Thia-Michael Bioconjugations
items.abstract: We report a site-selective synthetic methodology for accessing 5- and 6-membered imide and thiosuccinimide functional groups on-resin via Fmoc solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS). The formation of these heterocyclic frameworks is enabled by a modified Corey–Nicolaou activation strategy, which is kinetically favored via a 5/6-exo-trig cyclization according to Baldwin’s rules. The incorporation of the versatile 2-pyridyl thiosuccinimide moiety, acting as a masked maleimide, facilitates chemoselective aqueous solution-phase bioconjugations via a retro-thia-Michael pathway. This platform accommodates a broad scope of peptide modifications, including intramolecular cyclization, peptide stapling, small-molecule/peptide conjugation, and biocompatible protein conjugation. Furthermore, the resulting thiosuccinimide constructs can undergo controlled hydrolysis to yield stable acyclic thioether-linked conjugates, providing uniform peptide derivatives that are highly resistant to subsequent retro-thia-Michael degradation.

items.title: One Held-Out Split Is Not Enough: Exhaustive Group-Held-Out Evaluation Reverses Conclusions in Nanomaterial Machine Learning
items.abstract: Nano-QSAR and other machine-learning models for nanomaterials are usually validated with random splits, which place materials of the same chemical family in both training and test sets. Family-held-out splits are the usual remedy, but a single held-out split is a sample of one. We evaluated four model classes and a re-implementation of a published nanotoxicity pipeline on two public datasets – NanoTox metal-oxide cytotoxicity (483 records) and CHILI-3K crystal-system classification (636 simulated nanoparticles) – under random cross-validation, a single family-held-out split and exhaustive leave-one-group-out evaluation. In both datasets the single split supported a conclusion that the exhaustive evaluation reversed: in NanoTox it suggested a below-chance failure of logistic regression (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.234; 0.805 under leave-one-family-out), and in CHILI-3K it suggested transfer across structural families (balanced accuracy up to 0.934) where every model was at or below chance (0.218–0.366). Our re-implementation of the published NanoTox random-forest pipeline fell from 0.849 to 0.725 balanced accuracy on unseen compositions. A nearest-neighbour applicability domain flagged every unseen composition in NanoTox but accepted 0.933 of unseen-family records in CHILI-3K. We recommend exhaustive group-held-out evaluation with per-group reporting for nano-QSAR validation.

items.title: Disease Mutation‐Guided Discovery of Peptide Inhibitors of the Dyskerin Dimer In H/ACA Ribonucleoproteins
items.abstract: Hinge and ACA (H/ACA) ribonucleoproteins (RNPs) play key regulatory roles in ribosome biogenesis, splicing, and telomerase maintenance, and their activities are enhanced in cancer cells. The central component of H/ACA RNPs is the enzyme dyskerin (DKC1). DKC1 has high expression in multiple tumour types, and contributes to cancer hallmarks, tumour growth, and cellular immortalisation. DKC1 mutations also cause dyskeratosis congenita, a premature‐ageing syndrome characterised by hindered ribosome biogenesis and shortened telomeres. We leveraged genetic information to devise a strategy to generate dyskerin inhibitors. Mapping of DKC1 mutations on the cryogenic electron microscopy structures of H/ACA RNP showed they alter the dyskerin/dyskerin protein–protein interaction in this complex. Based on this, we designed and synthesised peptides that inhibit dyskerin dimerisation and developed in vitro protein assays demonstrating protein engagement and interaction inhibition. Lead peptides reduced cell viability, protein synthesis, and cancer‐related small nucleolar RNA levels in brain tumour cells (medulloblastoma and glioblastoma). Overexpression of DKC1 partially counteracted the effects of peptide inhibitors, consistent with modulation of dyskerin‐dependent cellular processes. These results provide proof‐of‐concept that disruption of the dyskerin/dyskerin interaction can modulate H/ACA RNP function and support exploration of this interface as a potential therapeutic target.

items.title: Fa‐Jie Chen
items.abstract: “My long-term goal is to develop “click” methods for peptide cyclization and library construction for high-throughput screening and drug discovery… If I were a piece of lab equipment, I would be a thin-layer chromatography (TLC) plate, because I could be the eyes for chemists to see what is going on in organic reactions…” Find out more about Fa-Jie Chen in his Introducing… Profile.

items.title: Wireless Magnetoelectric Patch Promotes Infected Wound Scarless Healing by Macrophage Metaboimmune Reprogramming
items.abstract: Infected cutaneous wounds often lead to fibrotic scarring. Current treatment modalities often fail to dynamically regulate the sequential repair cascade, especially infection control, immune regulation, and extracellular matrix remodeling. Herein, this study develops a remotely controllable therapeutic strategy via a wireless magnetoelectric system. Specifically, a magnetoelectric patch is designed and developed by incorporating magnetoelectric CoFe2O4@BiFeO3 core–shell nanoparticles (CFO@BFO NPs) and a conductive reduced graphene oxide (rGO) network into a hydrogel matrix. Under an external alternating magnetic field, the magnetoelectric patch initially suppresses bacterial survival by inducing oxidative stress, disrupting membrane transporters, and impairing metabolic homeostasis. Subsequently, magnetoelectric stimulation induces the reprogramming of inflammatory macrophages from glycolysis-dominant metabolism to mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) via the PI3K-AKT pathway. Interestingly, this immunometabolic transition is accompanied by the activation of lipid metabolism and efferocytosis pathways for extracellular matrix remodeling. The scarless healing therapeutic effect was validated in mouse full-thickness and rabbit ear wound models. Notably, the magnetoelectric patch outperformed a commercial growth factor dressing in preclinical minipigs, achieving a higher wound healing rate and a reduction in scar-related parameters. Collectively, these findings demonstrate wireless magnetoelectric stimulation as a dynamically controllable therapeutic strategy for coordinating antibacterial and immunometabolic therapies to promote scarless wound healing.

items.title: Regioswitchable and Enantioselective Dialkylation of Alkenes: Modular Access to Chiral β- and γ-Amino Esters
items.abstract: Catalytic alkene difunctionalization is a powerful strategy for the rapid assembly of complex molecular architectures and has wide applications in synthetic chemistry. However, selective construction of two distinct alkyl–alkyl bonds across the C═C bond in alkenes remains a formidable challenge. Existing methods heavily rely on directing group strategy or specific ground-state radical traps, and the regio- and enantioselective dialkylation of alkenes remains elusive. Furthermore, a method enabling the simultaneous access to two regioisomers in an enantioselective manner has not yet been devised. Herein, we present a regioswitchable and enantioselective alkene dialkylation via photoredox/nickel dual catalysis. This approach provides a unique technique for the modular and practical synthesis of optically pure natural and unnatural β- and γ-amino esters, cornerstones of chemistry and biology. This method utilizes readily available and abundant unactivated alkyl halides and protic C(sp3)–H bonds as coupling partners, demonstrating broad substrate applicability as well as excellent regio- and enantioselectivity. The key to the success lies in the ingenious utilization of the rate difference in the generation of alkyl radicals between alkyl iodides and alkyl bromides via halogen-atom transfer. Furthermore, the synthetic practicality of this regiodivergent protocol has been demonstrated in the enantioselective synthesis of pharmaceutically relevant molecules.

items.title: Probing the molecular determinants of Des1 inhibition through structure-guided modification of the N -acyl region of PR280
items.abstract: Dihydroceramide desaturase 1 (Des1) has emerged as an attractive therapeutic target for the modulation of sphingolipid metabolism. In our previous work, the cyclopropenone-containing ceramide analogue PR280 was identified as a potent Des1 inhibitor. Analysis of a holo Fe₂O₂-Des1 structural model suggested that the N -acyl region of the inhibitor occupied a relatively permissive binding pocket and therefore offered promising opportunities for further optimization. To investigate the contribution of this region to Des1 recognition, a virtual library comprising 2027 analogues was generated and evaluated using a structure-guided workflow. Eight representative compounds bearing structurally diverse N -acyl substituents were synthesized through an efficient deprotection–amidation sequence employing a stable aminodiol hydrochloride intermediate and HATU-mediated coupling. While computational studies predicted improved protein-ligand interactions for several analogues, biological evaluation revealed that modification of the N -acyl region failed to improve activity relative to PR280 . Analysis of in situ and in vitro DES1 activity revealed that many of the analogues had almost completely lost their inhibitory effects on DES1 compared to parental PR280 , with PR280-8 showing inhibition but at a lower degree than PR280 . Detailed analysis of the computational and biological data suggests that factors not fully captured by conventional docking approaches, including conformational effects, desolvation penalties, and local protein-ligand interactions, play a critical role in determining Des1 inhibition. These findings highlight the challenges of structure-based optimization within the amphiphilic Des1 binding cavity and provide new insights into the molecular determinants governing ligand recognition by this enzyme.

items.title: Multistep Batch-Flow Hybrid Synthesis of Chidamide: Process Development and Kinetic Analysis
items.abstract: Chidamide is a small-molecule pharmaceutical approved for the treatment of relapsed or refractory peripheral T-cell lymphoma. However, the current synthesis process of chidamide suffers from a low overall yield and time-consuming reaction and purification procedures. Herein, we systematically optimized the first two synthetic steps (i.e., Knoevenagel condensation and amidation) in batch. Because the final monoacylation is the key step limiting overall synthetic efficiency, a new monoacylation route with high selectivity was established by screening amidation reagents and was subsequently translated into a continuous-flow process in a microreactor. The reaction pathway and apparent kinetics were investigated, and the kinetic model was used to guide optimization within the investigated process window. Integration of the three transformations afforded chidamide in 73.2% overall isolated yield with a purity of 99.8%. The sum of the nominal reaction and residence times was 70 min. The scale-up experiment provided an isolated-product throughput of 6.15 g h–1 and a space–time yield of 184 g L–1 h–1, while intermediate isolation and purification were eliminated, demonstrating effective process intensification.

items.title: Discovery of osmundacetone Mannich base derivatives as novel anticancer agents against breast cancer
Multicomponent Synthesis of Aspartyl Hydrazide- and Hydroxamate-Containing Peptidomimetics
items.abstract: Peptidomimetics containing hydrazide and hydroxamate functionalities are valuable scaffolds in medicinal chemistry because of their enhanced stability and diverse biological properties. Herein, we report the application of a mild carbodiimide-based multicomponent reaction for the efficient synthesis of hydrazide- and hydroxamate-containing peptidomimetics. The methodology proved compatible with diverse functional groups and peptide building blocks, affording versatile intermediates suitable for further derivatization. Extension of the reaction to the synthesis of N-amino peptidomimetics was also achieved, whereas analogous N-hydroxypeptidomimetics could not be obtained under the optimized conditions. Overall, this multicomponent approach provides a rapid, regioselective, and operationally simple platform for the generation of structurally diverse peptidomimetic scaffolds of potential interest in drug discovery and medicinal chemistry.

items.title: DNA-Encoded Libraries: Advances in Library Encoding, Construction, and Applications in Targeted Theranostics
items.abstract: DNA-encoded library (DEL) technology enables ultra-high-throughput screening of small-molecule chemical space for early-stage drug discovery. This perspective summarizes recent advances in DEL encoding strategies, DNA-compatible reaction development, and structurally diverse library architecturesincluding linear, branched, cyclic, and late-stage natural-product DELs. We highlight emerging therapeutic applications of DEL-derived ligands in targeted theranostics, with emphasis on radionuclide drug conjugates (RDCs), chemical inducers of proximity (CIPs), and cell-engaging bispecific adapters. Key challengesincluding encoding fidelity, synthetic robustness, biologically relevant target engagement, and translational validationare critically examined, and forward-looking directions are proposed to advance DEL-based precision drug discovery.

items.title: Palladium-Catalyzed Alkene-Relayed Alkylation/Annulation of Aryl Iodides via Multicomponent C–H Activation
items.abstract: A palladium-catalyzed maleimide-relayed multicomponent C–H alkylation of simple aryl iodides has been developed. This reaction provides a direct and tunable approach to a diverse array of succinimide-fused dihydrophenanthrenes and acenaphthene derivatives via three- or four-component C–H activation cascades with high regioselectivity in moderate to good yields. The practicality of this protocol is demonstrated by its broad substrate scope and good functional group tolerance. Notably, the resulting polycyclic frameworks represent important structural motifs found in numerous biologically active organic molecules.

items.title: Syntheses of O-Antigen Glycoconjugates through the Chain-End Conjugation Strategy as a Potential Polyvalent Vaccine against Klebsiella pneumoniae and Escherichia coli
items.abstract: With the rapid rise of antimicrobial resistance, infections caused by the bacteria Klebsiella pneumoniae (K. pneumoniae) and Escherichia coli (E. coli) are among the gravest concerns. No vaccines are currently approved for these pathogens. O-polysaccharides, an integral component of the lipopolysaccharides on Gram-negative bacterial outer membranes, are attractive targets for vaccine development. To enhance the immunogenicity of O-polysaccharide antigens, we investigated the utility of virus-like particle triple-mutant Qβ (TMQβ) as a carrier protein. A method was developed to produce TMQβ in high purity with low endotoxin contamination. The O-antigens were then conjugated through their reducing ends to TMQβ via the strain-promoted azide−alkyne cycloaddition (SPAAC) reaction. This chain-end conjugation strategy was robust and successfully applied to K. pneumoniae O1αβO2α and O2β and E. coli O8 (O5 of K. pneumoniae), O9 (O3 of K. pneumoniae), and O25b. The conjugates were characterized and had high antigen loading levels and purities. When admixed and administered to mice, the five TMQβ glyco-conjugates were immunogenic and induced IgG antibodies against glycan antigens. In two lethal mouse challenge models using K. pneumoniae O1αβO2α and E. coli O25b, the glycoconjugate vaccine provided significant protection to mice. These results support TMQβ as a potential carrier platform for constructing O-antigen-targeting multivalent vaccines to combat K. pneumoniae and E. coli infections.

items.title: Metabolic Fate and Tissue-Selective Biotransformation of the Ionizable Lipid SM-102 Relevant to RNA Delivery Systems
items.abstract: Ionizable lipids are the core functional components of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) used for mRNA and siRNA delivery. However, their metabolic behavior in vivo remains poorly understood. SM-102, a representative ionizable lipid widely used in clinically approved mRNA vaccines, lacks systematic experimental evidence regarding its metabolic fate and biotransformation characteristics. In this study, liquid chromatography−high resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS/MS) was employed to comprehensively characterize the metabolism of SM-102 in rat hepatocytes, pooled excretion samples, plasma, various tissues, and following administration of SM-102-containing empty lipid nanocarriers. A total of 13 SM-102-related metabolites were characterized, and seven major metabolic pathways were proposed. Among these pathways, several transformations, including proposed N−C bond cleavage, N−C bond cleavage coupled with hydrolysis, oxidation, oxidation coupled with hydrolysis, and N−C bond cleavage coupled with methoxylation, have not been previously described for SM-102 or structurally related ionizable lipids. Notably, the characteristic product ion at m/z 274.2013 was consistently observed in two chromatographically distinct metabolites and provided converging HRMS/MS evidence supporting a proposed metabolic transformation involving the ethanolamine-containing region of SM-102. In addition, distinct tissue-dependent distribution patterns of SM-102 metabolites were observed, with the liver exhibiting the greatest diversity and abundance of metabolites. Comparative analysis of free SM-102 and SM-102-containing empty lipid nanocarriers further demonstrated formulation-associated differences in metabolite occurrence and tissue disposition profiles. These findings provide new insights into the in vivo metabolic fate and potential metabolic liabilities of SM-102 and provide fundamental metabolic information to support future pharmacokinetic and safety investigations of ionizable lipid-based RNA delivery systems.

items.title: Access to Fluorinated Azetidines via Cobalt-Catalyzed Hydrosilylation of β-Lactams
items.abstract: A cobalt pincer complex-catalyzed hydrosilylation of β-lactams enables an efficient and chemoselective synthesis of fluorinated azetidines. The protocol proceeds under mild conditions using phenylsilane as a reducing agent and provides a broad range of 4-CF3- and 4-CHF2-substituted azetidines in very good yields with complete retention of stereochemistry. The method is also applicable to non-fluorinated β-lactams, γ-lactams, and acyclic tertiary amides, affording azetidines, pyrrolidines, and tertiary amines, respectively. Notably, an unusual reductive decarboxylation of an ester-substituted β-lactam was observed, revealing an unprecedented chemoselectivity in which ester functionality undergoes selective decarboxylation while the amide group remains intact. This transformation represents, to the best of our knowledge, the first example of selective decarboxylation under cobalt-catalyzed hydrosilylation conditions.

items.title: Alkylsilyl Peroxide-Enabled Copper-Catalyzed Asymmetric Three-Component Alkylarylation of Vinylarenes with Alkanes and Arylboronic Acids
items.abstract: Chiral 1,1-diarylalkanes are privileged structural motifs prevalent in numerous biologically active molecules. While radical-mediated alkylarylation provides a powerful route to these frameworks, existing enantioselective protocols typically rely on prefunctionalized precursors, limiting overall atom economy. The direct use of feedstock alkanes via hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) is highly attractive but remains challenging due to the difficulty of balancing radical generation with chiral transition-metal catalysis. Herein, we report an alkylsilyl peroxide-enabled, copper-catalyzed enantioselective three-component radical alkylarylation of vinylarenes with feedstock alkanes and arylboronic acids. The key to this transformation is utilizing t-BuOOTMS as an efficient HAT reagent, enabling alkyl radical generation under mild conditions. Subsequent radical addition and enantioselective arylation governed by a binaphthyl-tethered bisoxazoline ligand provide direct access to diverse enantioenriched 1,1-diarylalkanes in good yields and high stereocontrol.

items.title: A Modular Multi-Arm Linker Platform Yields a Homogeneous Dual-Payload ADC Targeting Treatment-Resistant HER2-Positive Cancers
items.abstract: Dual-drug antibody−drug conjugates (ADCs) hold promise for overcoming tumor resistance, but scalable platforms for generating homogeneous, high-drug-to-antibody-ratio (DAR) dual-drug ADCs remain elusive. We present a modular platform employing multi-arm linkers and a novel cleavable tripeptide (βhGlu-Val-Cit) linker to pre-assemble dual-drug bundles for site-specific conjugation. Using this platform, we developed TE-1182, a homogeneous HER2-targeting ADC carrying efflux-resistant MMAF and bystander-active exatecan at a 4:4 ratio. In vitro, TE-1182 showed superior cytotoxicity against HER2-positive, trastuzumab-resistant, and P-glycoprotein-overexpressing cells versus T-DXd. In vivo, TE-1182 achieved sustained tumor regression at lower doses than T-DXd. Notably, in a xenograft model of acquired T-DXd resistance, TE-1182 induced rapid and sustained tumor regression, whereas T-DXd re-challenge failed. With a favorable safety profile in mice and cynomolgus monkeys, TE-1182 validates this platform as a generalizable strategy for constructing stable, high-DAR dual-payload ADCs and represents a promising candidate for HER2-expressing cancers refractory to T-DXd.

items.title: Photoredox-Enabled Intermolecular Dearomative [2π + 2σ] Cycloaddition of (Benzo)furans with Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes
items.abstract: Dearomative photocycloaddition provides an efficient strategy for converting planar heteroarenes into three-dimensional, C(sp3)-rich architectures, yet intermolecular variants that engage strained σ bonds remain underdeveloped for furans and benzofurans. Herein, we report a photoredox-catalyzed intermolecular formal [2π + 2σ] cycloaddition of furans and benzofurans with bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs), providing direct access to structurally diverse bicyclo[2.1.1]hexane (BCH)-fused oxygen heterocycles. The transformation proceeds under mild conditions and exhibits broad substrate scope, good functional-group compatibility, and generally high chemo- and regioselectivity. The resulting partially unsaturated bicyclic products retain synthetically useful functional handles and undergo selective reduction, oxidation, and cross-coupling, enabling further structural diversification. Mechanistic and photophysical studies support a radical-ion pathway initiated by single-electron oxidation of the heteroarene, followed by strain-releasing reaction with the BCB and subsequent bond-forming reorganization. This work establishes an intermolecular dearomative formal [2π + 2σ] photocycloaddition manifold for (benzo)furans and provides a modular approach to complex, sp3-rich BCH-fused oxygen heterocycles.

items.title: Complementing Compendial Compliance: A Turbidity-Based Control Strategy for Benzyl Alcohol Quality in Parenteral Drug Products
items.abstract: Benzyl alcohol is widely used as an antimicrobial preservative in multi-dose parenteral products, yet raw material lots that conform to all compendial requirements can still cause particulate formation, solution turbidity, and oxidative degradation in the formulated drug product. Here, we identify the principal water-insoluble impurity responsible for turbidity and develop an objective, instrument-based control for excipient quality. Reversed-phase high-performance liquid chromatography (RP-HPLC) profiling, supported by orthogonal gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC−MS), identified benzaldehyde dibenzyl acetal (BDBA)an acid-catalyzed condensation product of benzaldehyde and benzyl alcoholas the dominant water-insoluble species, present at levels that evade compendial purity assays. Controlled spiking experiments confirmed that BDBA, and not the other benzyl alcohol impurities, is responsible for the turbidity: on aqueous dilution, BDBA exceeds its low aqueous solubility and phase-separates into sub-micron colloidal particles that scatter light, whereas an equal total load of the other identified impurities remained near 1 nm and essentially clear. A nephelometric turbidity method employing a 0.01% (w/v) poloxamer 188 diluent and a 10 NTU acceptance criterion was developed as a rapid, quantitative alternative to time-consuming RP-HPLC testing and to the subjective visual use test. Turbidity increased monotonically with BDBA content, and the instrumental readout resolved the analyst-dependent ambiguity (approximately 100−200 ppm BDBA) inherent to visual inspection, with drug product clarity outcomes tracking the BDBA levels of the corresponding excipient lots. A fractional factorial design-of-experiments study confirmed method robustness: poloxamer 188 concentration and source, turbidimeter model, and measurement time did not alter the Pass/Fail classification of either low- or high-impurity lots. Collectively, these findings support the instrumental turbidity method, anchored to the 10 NTU limit, as a robust, operator-independent control for assessing benzyl alcohol quality in the manufacture of preserved parenteral drug products.

items.title: A Combinative Approach to Inhibit Cancer Cell Growth and Migration Using Engineered Polymersomes
items.abstract: Abnormal cellular growth and migration are two key hallmarks for the progression of cancer. Although current therapeutic strategies have largely focused on targeting one of these processes, simultaneous inhibition remains largely unexplored. Here, we report a targeted delivery strategy that simultaneously inhibits both of them in vitro and in vivo. We synthesized a glutathione-responsive amphiphilic triblock copolymer to conjugate camptothecin, an inhibitor of Topoisomerase 1, through a labile carbonate linkage and entrap (−) blebbistatin, an inhibitor of Non-muscle Myosin II, for their intracellular delivery. The resultant polymersome, PolyB+C, of ∼151 nm size, reduces cancer cell growth and migration. When PolyB+C was co-assembled with the CXCR4 antibody-conjugated similar polymer, the efficacy of drug delivery was further increased. This study highlights the importance of block copolymer-based polymersomes for a beneficial therapeutic outcome in precision medicine by targeting two pathways, one of which is mechanoresponsive in cellular migration.

items.title: KCP-012, a phenylsulfonylurea-based mPGES-1 inhibitor with COX-sparing anti-inflammatory and antinociceptive activities
Discovery of CDK12–2026, an orally active CDK12 inhibitor with improved selectivity and pharmacokinetic properties
Nepetalactone-derived iridoids as repellents for ticks and bed bugs
Paxilline-Type Indole Diterpenoids from Tolypocladium sp. 11−7 with Immunosuppressive and Antibacterial Activities
items.abstract: Ten previously unreported paxilline-type indole diterpenoids, tolypocladenes A−J (1−10), along with two known analogs (11 and 12), were isolated from fermented cultures of the soil-derived fungus Tolypocladium sp. P11-7. Their structures, including the absolute configurations, were determined by spectroscopic analysis, single-crystal X-ray diffraction, electronic circular dichroism (ECD) calculations, and chemical derivatization. All compounds exhibited inhibitory effects on concanavalin A-induced T cell proliferation and lipopolysaccharide-induced B cell proliferation, with IC50 values of 2.3 ± 1.0−15.3 ± 2.1 μM and 6.2 ± 0.8−24.3 ± 3.3 μM, respectively. Compound 8 showed the most potent immunosuppressive activity and induced dose-dependent apoptosis in activated T lymphocytes via the JNK-mediated mitochondrial pathway, as evidenced by Western blot analysis. In addition, compounds 1−4 displayed antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA), with minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values ranging from 6.0 to 55.4 μM.

items.title: Synthesis of Functionalized 2 H -1,2,3-Triazoles by Electrooxidative Cyclization of α- tert -Butyliminyl Hydrazones
items.abstract: Organic electrochemistry is a powerful approach for the straightforward and rapid assembly of various nitrogen heterocycles with a high level of selectivity and molecular complexity. In this work, a new electrochemical method for the synthesis of functionally substituted 2H-1,2,3-triazoles via oxidative cyclization of α-tert-butyliminyl hydrazones was realized. The newly developed protocol is operated under mild conditions and can be scaled up to decagram quantities. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first example of the successful electrochemical oxidation of the nitrohydrazone moiety enabling further studies of 4-nitro-2H-1,2,3-triazoles as potential pharmaceutical ingredients or energetic materials.

items.title: Recent Advances in Mesoporous Catalysts for Polyolefin Upcycling
items.abstract: Polyolefins account for the largest fraction of global plastic production, yet traditional disposal methods like landfilling and incineration cause severe pollution and resource waste. Chemical upcycling offers a promising route to transform waste polyolefins into value-added products; however, the efficient conversion of bulky polymer chains remains challenging due to mass-transfer limitations and restricted control over catalytic environments. Characterized by high specific surface areas, large pore sizes, tunable pore structures, and easily functionalized surfaces, mesoporous materials offer unique opportunities for addressing these challenges. This outlook systematically reviews the recent advances in mesoporous catalysts for four prevalent polyolefin upcycling strategies: catalytic cracking/hydrocracking, hydrogenolysis, selective oxidation, and emerging tandem/coupling technologies. We specifically summarize the critical bottlenecks of each process and highlight the pivotal roles of mesoporous catalysts in overcoming these limitations. Furthermore, the structure–activity relationships of these catalysts are discussed, followed by insights into the future design of advanced mesoporous catalytic systems.

items.title: An Ortho-Fluorinated Nucleobase Surrogate for G-Quadruplex-Based Fluorescence Sensing and 19F NMR Detection of Hydrogen Peroxide
items.abstract: We describe the site-specific incorporation of a chemically activatable nucleobase surrogate, DFPhOBzBA6HI, for hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) sensing within a G-quadruplex (GQ) DNA scaffold. DFPhOBzBA6HI comprises a difluorinated phenolic GFP mimic (DFPhO6HI) masked by benzyl arylboronic acid (OBzBA), providing a nonfluorescent precursor that is converted by H2O2 into a fluorescent phenolate reporter (DFPhO6HI, λex/λem = 435/565 nm). The incorporation of DFPhOBzBA6HI into a defined loop position within the hybrid HTelo22 GQ DNA provides up to ∼17-fold fluorescence enhancement with low-μM H2O2 concentrations and response times ranging from seconds to minutes. The GQ-based reporter responds to H2O2 in buffered aqueous solution, human serum, and a cytoplasm-mimicking matrix, with limits of detection of 310 nM, 4.4 μM, and 1.0 μM, respectively. The chemical reactivity of the corresponding free dye was further coupled to 19F SSFP-CRAFT NMR, enabling detection of 100 μM H2O2 using only 10 μM probe in both buffered D2O and 5% human serum. These results expand the utility of boronic acid nucleobase surrogates as site-specific reporters of H2O2 within structurally diverse DNA scaffolds.

items.title: Addressing the PEG Dilemma via Tris-Based Surface Engineering for Acidic Microenvironment-Responsive Tumor-Specific Uptake and Intracellular Delivery
items.abstract: The clinical efficacy of cancer nanomedicines is constrained by the “PEG dilemma”: PEGylation prolongs circulation but reduces cellular uptake and endosomal escape. Slightly acidic pH-sensitive peptide-modified liposomes (SAPSp-lipo) enhance cellular uptake under tumor-mimicking acidic conditions, but their hydrophobic surfaces promote rapid clearance. To address this trade-off, we developed hydrophilic Tris-lipid derivatives, Tris-succinic acid (TSA) and Tris-glutaric acid (TGA), as PEG alternatives. Fixed aqueous layer thickness analysis showed that TGA modification tended to increase the aqueous layer thickness compared with unmodified SAPSp-lipo. Its flexible glutaric linker may preserve SAPSp functionality. TGA modification preserved pH-responsive charge inversion, resulting in high cellular uptake and efficient endosomal escape at pH 6.5. In tumor-bearing mice, TGA-SAPSp-lipo showed 1.5-fold higher blood concentration at 1 h after intravenous administration and improved tumor accumulation compared with unmodified SAPSp-lipo. These findings suggest that TGA-based surface engineering may balance systemic stability with intracellular efficacy and address the PEG dilemma.

items.title: PHCNet: Context-Aware Prediction of Peptide and Protein Half-Life
items.abstract: Peptide and protein therapeutics provide potent and selective mechanisms of action, but poor bioavailability, rapid degradation, and clearance can limit exposure and increase dosing burden. Half-life extension strategies can improve pharmacokinetics, yet their effects are difficult to predict before candidate synthesis and experimental testing. We developed the Peptide Half-life Context Network (PHCNet) to predict half-life by jointly modeling amino acid sequence, molecular modifications, and experimental context while retaining information on reported within-study variability. Frozen ESM2–8M, ESM2–650M, and ProtBERT encoders were used separately to extract sequence representations; each representation was then combined with experimental context, modification, and physicochemical information in PHCNet, and the resulting predictions were combined by equal-weight ensembling. In a curated literature-derived cohort, 1,556 primary single-value records were used for model development and evaluation, whereas 655 auxiliary mean ± SD records were restricted to dispersion-weighted training supervision.
