In an exploratory measurement-level 10-fold internal evaluation on the cohort previously used in model development, pooled outer-test predictions from the equal-weight ensemble yielded an RMSE of 0.5324, an R2 of 0.7186, and a Pearson correlation of 0.8478, compared with an RMSE of 0.5708 for the Extra Trees baseline. Lower performance under sequence- and source-grouped evaluation indicates that the primary estimate reflects interpolation within the available literature data. PHCNet provides a context- and reliability-aware framework for learning from heterogeneous half-life measurements; its potential use in candidate prioritization requires validation in independent retrospective cohorts and prospective experimental studies.

items.title: Mitochondrial G-Quadruplex-Binding Ruthenium(II) Complexes Remodel Cancer Cell Respiration and mtDNA-Encoded Gene Expression
items.abstract: Mitochondrial DNA G-quadruplexes (G4s) represent emerging yet largely unexplored targets for anticancer therapy. Herein, we report two triphenylphosphonium (TPP)-functionalized Ru(II) polypyridyl complexes ( 1 and 2 ) designed to combine mitochondrial targeting with G4 recognition. Spectroscopic investigations revealed strong interactions with mitochondrial G4s, although these were partially attenuated by competing duplex DNA. Both complexes exhibited cytostatic activity against HCT116 colorectal cancer cells in 2D and 3D models, accompanied by concentration- and time-dependent cellular accumulation. Notably, their activity was synergistically enforced by combination with metformin or the glucose transporter inhibitor BAY-876. Seahorse metabolic profiling revealed substantial perturbations of cellular bioenergetics, affecting mitochondrial respiration, extracellular acidification, and ATP production. Most strikingly, quantitative real-time PCR revealed a marked and selective downregulation of mitochondrially encoded genes, while nuclear gene expression remained widely unaffected. Together, these findings identify mitochondria-targeted Ru(II) complexes 1 and 2 as promising modulators of mitochondrial gene expression and energy metabolism, highlighting a potential strategy for anticancer intervention.

items.title: Enhancing Pharmaceutical Production with Scaled-Up Laser-Driven Annular Photoreactors
items.abstract: We report the design, fabrication, and performance of a kilogram-scale, laser-driven annular photoreactor for preparative photochemistry. Building on a previously reported 0.5 W light-diffusing-fiber (LDF) prototype, we increased reactor volume ∼8× and scaled delivered optical power by ∼1600× by employing a different LDF and an 800 W diode laser. Externalizing photon generation keeps electrical and heat-generating components remote from hazardous chemical environments, facilitating the use in ATEX-rated facilities, and enables full enclosure of the emitted light for improved operational safety. The prototype was evaluated on a nickel-catalyzed C–N cross-coupling, delivering high, reproducible conversions across a range of flow rates, optical powers, and photocatalyst concentrations. Compared with a benchmark LED-driven tubular photoreactor, the present design increased the efficiency of delivered photon utilization within the reactor volume by ∼3×. A mechanistic PDE model was applied to accurately predict conversion across the ∼1600× scale-up in laser power (parity R2 = 0.981). These results indicate that laser-driven annular photoreactors offer a safe, controllable, and scalable platform capable of a model-projected multikilogram-per-day photochemical production suitable for small-molecule pharmaceutical manufacturing.

items.title: Issue Publication Information
Issue Editorial Masthead
Structure-Based Design of Fungal Chitin Synthase Inhibitors: Targeting Catalytic Pockets and Translocation Channels
items.abstract: The limited treatment options for invasive fungal infections, together with the rise of antifungal resistance, have intensified the search for new drug targets. Chitin synthase (CHS) is an attractive antifungal target because it catalyzes the formation of chitin, a structural component of the fungal cell wall, and has no mammalian counterpart. The recent determination of high-resolution cryo-electron microscopy structures of fungal and oomycete CHSs has provided a structural basis for structure-guided drug design. Drawing on the binding modes and structure–activity relationships of known inhibitors, this review examines strategies for designing new compounds that target either the cytosolic catalytic pocket or the transmembrane translocation channel of CHS. It further considers how computational biology and artificial intelligence could expand these approaches.

items.title: Deterministic Sub-100 µs Bare-Metal FPGA Spatial Voxel Screening and Dual-Target Structural Discovery of Allosteric TYK2 JH2 Inhibitors Selective Over JAK2
items.abstract: Selective allosteric inhibition of the tyrosine kinase 2 pseudokinase domain (TYK2 JH2) over the catalytic Janus kinase 2 domain (JAK2 JH1) avoids dose-limiting hematologic toxicities while treating autoimmune pathology. Here, we report a dual-target virtual screening and multi-seed consensus docking investigation comparing human TYK2 JH2 (PDB: 6NZP, 2.35 Å) against off-target catalytic JAK2 JH1 (PDB: 4IVA, 1.50 Å; 1.887 Å conserved binding-site Cα RMSD). From 2,500 unique chemical structures curated across ChEMBL 34, known JH2 controls, and structure-guided oral-window analogs, medicinal chemistry alert triage (PAINS, Brenk, NIH), physicochemical filtering (280 ≤ MW ≤ 490 Da), and hinge-binding pharmacophore matching retained 385 qualified 3D conformers. De novo SMILES redocking of clinical allosteric inhibitor deucravacitinib (BMS-986165) into 6NZP achieved ΔG = −8.733 kcal/mol (4.412 Å element-aware heavy-atom RMSD), while active-versus-decoy classification across known JH2 binders and clinical drug decoys achieved ROC-AUC = 0.867. Multi-seed AutoDock Vina consensus docking (seeds 42, 137, 2026) identified scaffold-hopped ChEMBL 34 leads including CHEMBL6914 (ΔGTYK2 = −10.72 ± 0.04 kcal/mol, ΔΔGTYK2-JAK2 = −1.11 kcal/mol, LLE = 3.05, Val690 = 3.34 Å, Lys642 = 2.86 Å) and CHEMBL266324 (ΔGTYK2 = −10.11 ± 0.12 kcal/mol, ΔΔG = −1.79 kcal/mol, QED = 0.654), alongside oral-window analog OIK-TYK2-003 (MW = 421.46 Da, LLE = 4.14, ΔGTYK2 = −8.84 ± 0.02 kcal/mol). Streaming 4,096-byte (16 × 16 × 16) pharmacophore grids via direct userspace PCIe Gen3 x16 BAR0 MMIO to a Xilinx UltraScale+ FPGA (agfi-0b55f06c15a385187 on AWS EC2 f2.6xlarge) achieved 87.03 µs P50 (102.998 µs P99) latency, 0.25 KB constant O(1) on-chip state, and 100% bit-exact determinism at 9 W average (10 W max) VCCINT core power.

items.title: Multitask Neural Networks for Multi-Solvent Solubility Prediction: Joint Learning with Lipophilicity, Melting Point, and Hydration Free Energy
items.abstract: The accurate prediction of solute solubility (LogS) and related properties such as partition coefficient (LogP), melting point (MP), and hydration free energy (∆Ghyd) plays a vital role in molecular design and specifically drug discovery. Data-driven machine learning approaches have received considerable attention due to their ability to provide fast and accurate predictions. However, the scarcity of high-quality datasets poses a significant obstacle to their wide applications. One strategy to circumvent this challenge is to employ multitask (MT) models which allow sharing of information and exploitation of correlations across various tasks, thereby addressing the limitations in data for specific tasks. In this work, two MT algorithms based on neural networks and the multi-explanation graph attention network (MEGAN) were developed and used for the simultaneous prediction of 19 tasks comprising 16 datasets of LogS together with one dataset of each of LogP, MP, and ∆Ghyd as helping tasks. In addition, single-task (ST) versions of the aforementioned models together with four more models, namely graph attention networks, random forest regression, Gaussian process regression, and support vector regression were analyzed for comparative purposes. It was found that both MT-DNN and MT-MEGAN models trained on all 19 tasks on average outperform all the other models when comparing the mean R2 values, with MT-DNN additionally achieving the lowest weighted RMSE and enabling predictive performance even for datasets with fewer than 50 data points. However, for the individual tasks there was no consistent improvement of the MT models.

items.title: MDwizard: GUI software for interactive binding site analysis, MD simulation and physics-based residue mapping.
items.abstract: Post-docking analysis, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation and pharmacophore classification are commonly used methods in computational hit discovery. Although several open-source and commercial tools exist for each process, there is no single graphical user interface (GUI) which helps researchers navigate from post-docking analysis to classification of residues with MD. Moreover, MD simulation in Windows is usually implemented through docker which is impractical for novice users. To address this issue, we present MDwizard, a GUI with easy one-click installation for Windows and Linux. MDwizard includes interactive 3D and 2D protein-ligand (PL) interaction maps, surface/van der Waals visualisation along with sketching and docking. MD simulation setup is interactive, while trajectory/analysis plots are automated. Furthermore, MDwizard assists in classifying residues with dynamic interaction occupancy and per residue SMINA AD4 score contribution. Four case studies (EGFR, MAO-B, ABL1 and ERα) showcase the effectiveness of the platform. MDwizard can be downloaded from https://sourceforge.net/projects/mdwizard/ .

items.title: Expanding the Toolbox for β-Fluoroamine Synthesis: Mechanistic and Stereochemical Insights into I(III)-Mediated Aminofluorination of Cinamyl Carbamates.
items.abstract: The aminofluorination of allyl carbamates represents a valuable strategy for the synthesis of β-fluoroamine scaffolds, which are of high interest in medicinal chemistry. In this study, we explore three complementary methodologies for this transformation: (i) direct aminofluorination using TolIF 2 , (ii) in situ generation of PhIF 2 from PhIO and Base·HF complexes, and (iii) a sequential process involving aziridination followed by fluorine-induced ring-opening. Mechanistic insights were gained through experimental data, Hammett analysis, and DFT calculations. The direct TolIF 2 -mediated approach efficiently afforded fluoro-oxazolidinones with high syn selectivity, particularly for electron-poor substrates, while the in situ PhIF 2 method proved less effective due to competing side reactions. The sequential strategy allowed for controlled access to either syn - or anti -diastereomers, depending on the fluorinating agent used, with DMPU·HF favoring anti -products and Et 3 N·HF leading to varying selectivity depending on substrate electronics. Mechanistic studies revealed the key role of HF clusters and hydrogen bonding in dictating stereoselectivity, with aziridine protonation serving as a crucial determinant of the reaction outcome. These findings provide a deeper understanding of aminofluorination strategies, enabling improved stereocontrol and expanding the synthetic potential of β-fluoroamine derivatives.

items.title: Photoswitchable azobenzene-1,3-oxathiolan-5-one hybrids as potent and reversible tyrosinase inhibitors: design, synthesis, and photopharmacological evaluation
Development and Evaluation of Neurotensin Receptor 1-Targeted Cyclic Peptide PET Probes for Tumor Imaging
The Limits of Library Scaling in Virtual Screening
items.abstract: Virtual screening libraries have expanded dramatically in recent years. Previous work has argued that screening larger libraries produces better experimental outcomes. This claim relies on two links: that larger libraries produce better scores, and that better scores produce better outcomes. In this study, we tested both. The first link shows rapidly diminishing returns: across six target-scoring function combinations, the score gains decreased as libraries grew even in log scale. The relationship was better described by a saturating power law than by the log-linear model previously reported. The second link is unreliable: a single chemical feature can markedly change the hit rate when the docking scores are similar. These findings suggest that increasing library size is not a reliable route to better experimental outcomes.

items.title: Molecular dynamics and docking study of an illustrative VHH-like model at MICA α3 and small-molecule ENPP1 and EZH2 ligands
items.abstract: Some tumours evade natural killer (NK) cells by proteolytically cleaving the stress ligands MICA and MICB near the cell membrane within their α3 domains. Here I evaluated an illustrative, computationally constructed VHH-like model, VHH1, in complex with the isolated human MICA α3 domain (UniProt residues 182 to 274) using structure prediction, explicit-solvent molecular dynamics (MD), and implicit-solvent rescoring, alongside small-molecule docking against two additional tumour immune-evasion targets, ENPP1 and EZH2. Across The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) cohorts in UALCAN (8,609 primary tumours and 738 unpaired normal tissue samples across 24 cohorts), median MICA transcript levels in tumours exceeded normal tissue medians in 13 of 24 cohorts overall, and in 9 of the 17 cohorts with more than five normal samples, while normal tissues also carried substantial baseline MICA RNA (medians 2.40 to 5.07 log2[TPM + 1]), indicating that bulk transcript levels alone do not establish tumour specificity. Sequence alignment confirmed that the human MICA and MICB α3 domains share 87 of 93 residues (93.5% identity), but MICB binding was not tested by docking or MD. AlphaFold 3 folded the individual VHH1 and MICA α3 domains with high confidence (chain pTM 0.87 and 0.85 to 0.86; n = 5 samples from seed 250104442), but the predicted complex had moderate global confidence (pTM 0.57 to 0.60) and low interface confidence (ipTM 0.13 to 0.22). Across three independent 100 ns MD simulations (2,001 frames per replicate), VHH1 remained internally folded (whole-run internal Cα RMSD 1.11 to 1.55 Å; domain-fitted Cα RMSF 0.67 to 0.72 Å) and retained contacts with the isolated MICA α3 domain in three distinct binding orientations. Replicates 1 and 3 maintained contact with four MICA α3 anchor residues (Ser193, Thr198, Gln228, and Arg247), whereas Replicate 2 shifted onto a lateral stalk surface involving framework region 3 residues; persistence in a pre-assembled complex does not prove binding affinity or shedding inhibition. Comparative single-trajectory OpenMM MM/GBSA estimates across 33 time-correlated frames per replicate (20 to 100 ns) were −49.1 ± 14.0, −20.2 ± 10.9, and −30.6 ± 5.0 kcal/mol for Replicates 1, 2, and 3, respectively. In AutoDock Vina 1.2.7 (n = 3 seeds per ligand), redocking the co-crystallised ligand TZV into human ENPP1 (PDB 6WEW) passed validation (top-pose RMSD 0.67 to 0.91 Å; best score −9.95 kcal/mol), although neither TZV nor the proposed model compounds Compound 1 (−9.10 kcal/mol) and Compound 2 (−10.32 kcal/mol) achieved inner-sphere Zn2+ coordination. Redocking S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (SAH) into human EZH2 (PDB 5HYN, chains A and D) failed validation (top-pose RMSD 7.78 to 7.86 Å) because Vina scored the crystal pose (−5.57 kcal/mol as-is; −7.05 kcal/mol after local minimisation) worse than alternative poses (−8.24 kcal/mol), rendering the tazemetostat docking result (−8.94 kcal/mol) strictly exploratory. All findings are unvalidated computational predictions that require experimental testing.

items.title: Neuropeptide Signaling in Cancer Progression and Targeted Interventions
items.abstract: As pivotal signaling mediators linking the nervous, immune, and neoplastic systems, neuropeptides orchestrate cross-system communication, tumor microenvironment remodeling, and immune modulation. Solid tumors hijack neurotrophic pathways to recruit nerve fibers, thereby establishing intratumoral neuropeptide-driven regulatory axes. Overexpressed neuropeptide receptors also provide targets for imaging and therapy. This review centers on the neuropeptide–receptor axis to elucidate the mechanisms driving tumor progression, invasion, neuroremodeling, and immune suppression. We critically analyze how receptor topology, ligand specificity, and signaling dynamics dictate design strategies for molecular imaging and therapeutic agents. Integrating emerging advances in probe engineering, peptide–drug conjugates, and receptor-antagonist-mediated immune modulation, we underscore the translational potential of these systems in theranostic applications. Finally, we assess the clinical feasibility of neuropeptide targets, offering a systematic framework for the advancement of neuropeptide-based precision oncology.

items.title: Priming of AGO2 by type I interferons balances inflammation and antiviral immunity
items.abstract: Argonaute-2 (AGO2)–mediated RNA silencing contributes to antiviral defenses in plants and insects and may contribute to mammalian immunity, too. However, it is unknown whether AGO2 is modified upon infection or inflammation in mammals. We identified that the ubiquitin ligase RING-finger protein 126 (RNF126) interacts with and ubiquitinates AGO2 to enhance its small interfering RNA or microRNA loading. Using data from cells in vitro and mouse tissues, we propose that RNF126 is induced by type I interferon (IFN-I) signaling and promotes the ability of AGO2 to silence proinflammatory genes and inhibit viral replication. Lipid nanoparticle delivery of RNF126 mRNA to mice inhibited inflammation and viral replication. These findings identify cross-talk of IFN-based immune signaling and AGO2-mediated RNA silencing and suggest that the RNF126-AGO2 axis helps to balance inflammatory and antiviral immune protection.

items.title: Revisiting the Biosynthetic Cyclization of Indole Sesquiterpene Alkaloids: Proposal of a Spiro -Indolenine Pathway and Synthesis of Prelecanindole
items.abstract: Indole sesquiterpene and indole diterpene alkaloids constitute a distinctive class of natural products characterized by complex polycyclic ring architectures and diverse potent biological activities. In indole sesquiterpenes, the characteristic indole-containing pentacyclic skeleton is biosynthesized from 3-farnesylindole through epoxidation followed by a sequential cationic cyclization. Although the cyclization enzyme has been identified, the details of its cyclization mechanism remain unclear. Here, we propose a new biosynthetic mechanism involving a spiro-indoleninium intermediate, which contrasts with the long-standing mechanism proposed in the 1970s that proceeds via a tertiary-to-secondary carbocation rearrangement. We demonstrated the feasibility of this new mechanism by means of density functional theory (DFT) calculations, which do not support the conventional mechanism and also by chemical emulation: the putative spiro-indolenine intermediate was synthesized from two fragments through stereoselective cyclopropanation as a key reaction and subsequently converted to prelecanindole, a common biosynthetic intermediate of indole sesquiterpene alkaloids, under mild acidic conditions.

items.title: Binding kinetics enable tumor-selective MAPK and growth suppression by a Type 1 RAF inhibitor
items.abstract: Targeting the RAS/MAPK pathway has long been constrained by dose-limiting toxicity in normal tissues at doses required for durable tumor control. Although Type 1.5 RAF inhibitors improved selectivity in BRAF(V600X)-monomer tumors, a comparable strategy for RAF dimer-driven cancers, including those with RAS mutations, has been lacking. We describe ELV-3111, a potent Type 1 RAF inhibitor that inhibits RAF dimers and exploits binding kinetics for tumor selectivity. ELV-3111 primes RAF in normal tissues, and its rapid dissociation during drug clearance generates drug-free RAF dimers that paradoxically activate MAPK signaling. RAS-mutant tumors are spared, where RAF is already primed. Combined with a MEK inhibitor, ELV-3111 restored normal tissue signaling while deepening tumor pathway inhibition, producing regressions across RAS- and BRAF-mutant experimental models. Thus, inhibitor dissociation kinetics provide a generalizable source of therapeutic index.

items.title: Mechanisms of nucleosome disruption shape epigenetic inheritance pathway choice
items.abstract: Maintaining cell identity requires duplicating the genome and epigenome during S phase. As DNA is copied, histones extracted from parental nucleosomes are transferred to nascent strands, which preserves the position of epigenetic marks. How the replisome coordinates these processes is unclear. Using reconstitution with purified yeast proteins, kinetic measurements, structural biology, mass spectrometry and genomics, we examined nucleosome-replisome encounter and histone transfer. Parental nucleosomes can be unwrapped ahead of the fork by the MCM helicase, aided by FACT and Ctf4, or by Tof1. Nucleosomal DNA unwrapping by MCM creates a FACT binding site, helping strip histones off DNA. Ctf4 enhances FACT-stimulated histone extraction, retains parental histones and hands them to Tof1, en route to lagging-strand redeposition. Thus, extraction via Ctf4 commits histones to lagging-strand transfer.

items.title: Solid-Phase Synthesis of Membrane-Permeable Nucleoside Di- and Triphosphates as Bioorthogonal Chemical Probes
items.abstract: Nucleoside mono-, di- and triphosphate analogues can function as bioorthogonal chemical probes for incorporation into cellular DNA during DNA synthesis yet require a biolabile 5′-phosphate protecting group to facilitate their cellular uptake. Solution-phase synthesis of these pronucleotides is often limited by difficult purification of intermediates and final products. Solid-phase synthesis could overcome these difficulties yet has not been reported for pronucleotides. Here, we describe development of a modular solid-phase synthesis of mono-, di- and triphosphate pronucleotides. The method combines a nucleoside immobilised on polystyrene resin via a disiloxyl linker with iterative phosphoramidite chemistry using two symmetric phosphoramidites to incorporate the 5′-phosphates. The phosphoramidite to introduce the terminal phosphate comprises biolabile protecting groups that are retained during cleavage of the target pronucleotide from the solid support. Application of this strategy provided a panel of 16 thymidine and 5-vinyl-2′-deoxyuridine (VdU) pronucleotides in ≥95% purity and yields of 72–90%. Inverse electron-demand Diels-Alder (IEDDA) click-chemistry with a fluorescent tetrazine confirmed efficient DNA labelling with VdU pronucleotides in Plasmodium falciparum, a model organism without a thymidine kinase and with a requirement for pronucleotide chemical probes. This solid-phase approach facilitates access to membrane-permeable mono-, di- and triphosphate analogues, expanding the pronucleotide toolbox.

items.title: SynADC: An AI4Science Agent for Bi-Conjugate Antibody-Drug Conjugate Design
items.abstract: Background. A bi-conjugate antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) carries two distinct linker-payload modules on one antibody. Interpreting a design requires researchers to connect antibody identity, attachment sites, payload occupancy, and evidence generated for different molecular species. Objective. We developed SynADC as an agentic research workflow that connects artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) outputs with a defined bi-conjugate candidate, quality checks, and a documented decision for the next design. Methods. We examined software verification records and an archived HER2 case comprising an engineered trastuzumab S378C construct with two maytansinoid and two auristatin modules (nominal drug-to-antibody ratio [DAR] 4). We evaluated the links among the construct record, payload property predictions, receptor-specific docking, covalent geometry, exploratory molecular dynamics, literature, patent retrieval, and final report. Results. The software verification record reported 28 passing checks for approval, arm-specific structural analysis, artifact integrity, and resume behavior. The saved HER2 case connected four intended conjugations, 102 annotated payloads, 170 receptor-level docking records from 115 identifiers, and a 1.0-ns Fc trajectory with 100 frames generated within the SynADC workflow using OpenMM with ff14SB and GAFF2 family parameters. Seven literature and seven patent investigations fed a completed post-MD evidence report. The construct had no validated whole-ADC rank or experimental efficacy result. Conclusions. SynADC demonstrates integration of AI/ML, structural, and research outputs around a traceable bi-conjugate design. A prospective comparison is needed to determine whether this workflow reduces decision time and experimental cost or improves the yield of qualified candidates.

items.title: Photothermal Catalysis for the Cross-Ketonization of Carboxylic Acids
items.abstract: Ketones are a valuable class of compounds due to their utility in the synthesis of natural products and drug molecules. Although carboxylic acids are attractive ketone precursors, direct methods for converting carboxylic acids to ketones without stoichiometric activating reagents or harsh organometallic nucleophiles remain limited. In this work, we developed a platform for the photothermal cross-ketonization of unactivated aryl and aliphatic carboxylic acids using a photothermally active metal oxide catalyst. Under traditional thermal conditions, this process typically requires bulk temperatures > 300 °C, promoting side reactions and limiting functional group tolerance. Acting as a dual ketonization catalyst and a photothermal agent, this catalyst enables challenging reactivity in just 90 minutes of red-light irradiation. The photothermal method accommodates structurally diverse carboxylic acids, including drug-like molecules, and aryl esters, enabling challenging cases where the corresponding free acids undergo competing decarboxylation. Catalyst characterization indicates that photothermal pre-activation drives carbonization and reduction of MnO2, resulting in an improved photothermal catalyst. Mechanistic studies support a Claisen-condensation type mechanism followed by decarboxylation of a β-ketoacid intermediate. More broadly, this work demonstrates the power of integrating catalytic activity with photothermal conversion within a single material, enabling challenging bimolecular reactivity under mild red-light irradiation.

items.title: The Design, Synthesis, and Evaluation of Novel Positive Allosteric Modulators Targeting the Mu‐Opioid Receptor
items.abstract: Positive allosteric modulators (PAMs) of opioid receptors represent a promising approach for the development of new analgesics. Through specific binding to allosteric sites of the opioid receptors, allosteric ligands can tune the efficacies of the naturally occurring opioid ligands in the body, thereby eliciting fewer side effects than orthosteric opioid agonist drugs. A potent lead μ‐opioid receptor (MOR) PAM, BMS‐986122, was previously identified by the Bristol–Myers–Squibb company via a high‐throughput screen using β ‐arrestin recruitment assays. BMS‐986122 was able to enhance the potency of the agonist endomorphin‐I by 7‐fold with a binding affinity for the allosteric site close to 5 μM. Herein we report the syntheses of over 40 analogs, for which PAM activity was evaluated via Nb33 and β ‐arrestin 2 recruitment assays. Notably, using a panel of four distinct functional assays downstream of MOR activation, we have identified novel PAMs ( R )‐ 4g , 9b , 9h , 9m, and 9s, which displayed robust cooperativity (log αβ ), including three PAMs that displayed biased modulatory profiles, preferentially favoring the potentiation of DADLE‐mediated signaling in certain pathways over others.

items.title: Visualization of Cetuximab‐EGFR Interactions on Live‐Cell Surface Using an Environment‐Sensitive Fluorescent Probe
items.abstract: Cetuximab (Cet), a monoclonal antibody (mAb) targeting epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), plays a critical role in the treatment of colorectal cancer and head–neck cancer. However, a subset of patients experiences nonresponsiveness or develops resistance after cetuximab treatment. In order to explore antigen‐antibody interactions potentially related to therapeutic efficacy, we developed a novel environment‐sensitive activatable fluorescent probe ( 2PCA‐SBD‐Cet ) for the visualization of the dynamic interaction between cetuximab and EGFR on live cell surfaces, enabling wash‐free imaging. This probe exhibits a large Stokes shift (116 nm), an appropriate labeling ratio (dye/protein = 2.0), and excellent environmental sensitivity. Upon specific binding to EGFR, the cetuximab‐EGFR interface may create a relatively hydrophobic microenvironment that contributes to fluorescence activation. The fluorescence intensity was positively correlated with EGFR expression levels. Overall, this probe provides a useful approach for visualizing cetuximab‐EGFR interactions on live cells and for investigating factors that may influence antibody binding and therapeutic efficacy, thereby offering a preliminary basis for exploring its potential application in pharmacodynamic evaluation.

items.title: Ligand-Controlled Chemodivergent β-Methylene C(sp3)–H Heteroarylation of Aliphatic Acids
items.abstract: Achieving ligand-controlled chemodivergence in C–H activation is still difficult because several competing reaction pathways are available when multiple C–H bonds are present. We describe a Pd(II)-catalyzed, chemodivergent β-methylene C(sp3)–H heteroarylation of free aliphatic acids in which two distinct classes of bidentate pyridone ligands each deliver a different product. These two ligands also overcome a long-standing inhibitory effect of heteroaryl iodides, demonstrating the potential of this protocol to serve as a general C(sp3)–C(sp2) coupling method using readily available aliphatic acids as the alkylating partner. Mechanistic experiments and DFT analyses reveal that π–π stacking between the quinoline motif and the heteroaryl ring lowers the barrier for rotation of the carbon–palladium bond, favoring protodepalladation to the reductive Heck product, whereas the oxime ether ligand lacks this interaction and steers the key intermediate toward β-H elimination to give the oxidative Heck product.

items.title: Supramolecular Iron(II)‐Anchored Porphyrin Glycoassemblies Enable Galectin‐Targeted Photodynamic Therapy
items.abstract: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) relies on photosensitizers that generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) upon light irradiation to trigger cytotoxic effects in target tissues. Porphyrins are among the most widely used PDT photosensitizers due to their strong visible‐light absorption and efficient ROS generation, although their broad application is limited by poor aqueous solubility, aggregation, and limited selectivity. Here, Fe(II)‐anchored porphyrin nanocages displaying peripheral lactose residues were prepared by coordination‐driven subcomponent self‐assembly to combine photodynamic activity with multivalent glycan presentation. The resulting cubic Fe 8 L 6 architectures were characterized by NMR spectroscopy, UV–vis spectroscopy, dynamic light scattering, and transmission electron microscopy. The zinc‐metalated porphyrin nanoassembly, [ 1‐Zn ][BF 4 ] 16 , generated both singlet oxygen and superoxide upon red‐light irradiation, providing access to multiple ROS pathways. Isothermal titration calorimetry revealed high‐affinity binding to galectin‐3 ( K d = 2.65 ± 0.26 µM), a lectin commonly upregulated in epithelial cancers. A549 cells treated with [ 1‐Zn ][BF 4 ] 16 exhibited potent light‐induced cytotoxicity with negligible dark toxicity, with a phototoxicity index (PI) of 55, while pre‐treatment with lactose or thiodigalactose was protective against [ 1‐Zn ][BF 4 ] 16 toxicity. These results demonstrate that coordination‐driven self‐assembly provides an effective strategy for integrating multivalent lectin recognition and photodynamic activity within a single nanoscale architecture.

items.title: Access to the F-Ring Core of Viridicatumtoxin A via Decarboxylative Alkylation of Methylenetetracyclines at the C6 Position
items.abstract: A visible-light-mediated decarboxylation alkylation method is reported, which can introduce different alkyl groups at the C6 position of methylenetetracycline in one step while simultaneously aromatizing the C-ring of tetracycline. This method is readily applicable to various alkyl radical precursors derived from primary, secondary, and tertiary carboxylic acids, as well as methylenetetracycline substrates containing amides and free alcohols. The F-ring core of the natural product Viridicatumtoxin A, the isopentenyl fragment of Hypomycetin, and a novel, unexpected oxa-7-membered ring tetracycline analogue were also successfully synthesized using this method. Furthermore, the synthesized tetracycline analogues exhibited excellent antibacterial activity against Gram-positive Staphylococcus aureus.

items.title: New quinoline–pyridine hybrids targeting Pim-1 kinase: design, synthesis, docking studies, radiolabeling, and antitumor evaluation
items.abstract: Quinoline–pyridine hybrids 4a–h were designed as Pim-1 kinase inhibitors; 4c (IC50 = 0.46 μM) was twice as potent as VRV, and 131 I-4b showed selective tumor uptake in Ehrlich tumor-bearing mice (tumor-to-muscle ratio up to 5.0).

items.title: Allosteric Remodeling of Conformational Dynamics Enables Engineering of Dual-Mode LanPM1 Proteases
items.abstract: LanPM1 zinc metallopeptidases are important RiPP maturation proteases that remove leader peptides through sequential endoproteolytic cleavage and aminopeptidase trimming. Inefficient leader-peptide removal can limit the maturation and engineering of RiPP natural products, yet rational strategies for improving both processing modes remain poorly developed. Here, we identify a conserved loop_II/IV-domain IV interaction network that distinguishes LanPM1 proteases from representative canonical M1 aminopeptidases. Using EryP, a model LanPM1 protease from erythreapeptin biosynthesis, we show that broad disruption of this interface compromises catalysis, whereas selective perturbation of specific interface contacts suppresses aminopeptidase activity while accelerating endoproteolytic processing and altering cleavage-site preference. Structural and molecular dynamics analyses further reveal that these mutations remodel the conformational ensemble of EryP toward open-like states that expose an extended peptide-accommodation groove while preserving local amino-terminal peptide recognition at the catalytic center. Guided by this model, we combined mutations from two interdomain regulatory regions to generate EryP variants with enhanced dual-mode processing and improved tolerance toward motif-disrupted and non-cognate leader substrates. These findings establish a strategy for engineering dual-mode LanPM1 proteases through tunable interdomain dynamics.

items.title: “Fluorine Effect”-Promoted Cu-Catalyzed Asymmetric Radical Cyanofluoroalkylation of Fluoroalkenes to Access Chiral Quaternary α-Fluorinated Nitriles
items.abstract: Chiral quaternary α-fluorinated nitriles were efficiently synthesized via asymmetric radical cyanofluoroalkylation of fluoroalkenes, exhibiting outstanding reactivity and enantioselectivity. The fluorine incorporation enhances the metabolic stability of this series of chiral nitriles and their derivatives by suppressing their potential racemization. This strategy holds substantial significance for the late-stage modification and functionalization of bioactive and pharmaceutical molecules. In this strategy, enantioselective radical cyanation could occur at a dialkyl-substituted tertiary carbon center, which has been a great challenge in previous work. On the other hand, this method indirectly constructs a quaternary fluorinated stereocenter, offering a new approach to the synthesis of chiral fluorinated compounds. Mechanistic studies indicate that the presence of the fluorine atom plays a crucial role in enhancing both reactivity and enantioselectivity.

items.title: Tetrahydro-Dewar Pyridines: Rigidified Piperidines for Drug Discovery

Corrigendum to “The Pt(IV) complexes of norcantharidin axial-modulated by carboxylic acid ligand: Synthesis, characterization, in vitro/in vivo anticancer efficacy and hypoxic activity” [Eur. J. Med. Chem., 320 (2026) 1–17/119365]
Photosensitized Intermolecular Transposed TTEnT-Single-Electron Transfer Paternò-Büchi Reaction between Densely Substituted Styrenes and Aryl Aldehydes
items.abstract: Over the past decade, significant advances have been made in the photochemistry of triplet styrenes. Radical addition of these reactive intermediates to various acceptors, triggering photocyclization reactions, has attracted considerable attention. Herein, we report a visible-light-induced photocatalytic system that enables the intermolecular transposed triplet–triplet-energy-transfer (TTEnt) with single-electron transfer (SET) Paternò-Büchi (PB) cycloaddition of per-substituted styrenes for the first time. This strategy fully takes advantage of inherently strong reducing properties of the triplet-state per-substituted styrene intermediate, conferred by the planar geometry. Subsequent SET between the highly reducing intermediate and aromatic aldehydes enables the facile construction of highly substituted oxetanes with excellent chemoselectivity. Complementing the established PB-type cycloaddition, this study not only opens new avenues for the photochemical utilization of sterically hindered alkenes but also enriches the reaction mode and versatility of photochemical activation in constructing complex heterocycles.

items.title: Novel Pyrazole-Fused Compounds as VRK1 Inhibitors for Treating Glioblastoma or Neuroblastoma
items.abstract: Provided herein are novel pyrazole-fused compounds as VRK1 inhibitors, pharmaceutical compositions, use of such compounds in treating glioblastoma or neuroblastoma, and processes for preparing such compounds.

items.title: Advances in Synthetic Methodologies for Isotopic Labeling of Organic Molecules
items.abstract: Radioactive and stable isotopes are essential tools in the discovery and development of new agrochemical and pharmaceutical molecules. Consequently, the body of research focused on developing novel synthetic methodologies for isotope incorporation into bioactive molecules continues to grow. Progress in this field has largely been driven by innovative catalytic methods, including late-stage functionalization (LSF) methods like hydrogen isotope exchange (HIE), carbon isotope exchange (CIE), molecular skeletal editing, biocatalysis, and other labeling approaches. These methods enable efficient and sustainable site-specific introduction of isotopes into bioactive molecules at late stages of synthesis. Given the broad applications across various scientific fields, this comprehensive, critical, and accessible review summarizing diverse isotope labeling methodologies will be of great benefit to researchers in academia as well as professionals in the pharmaceutical and agrochemical industries. This review focuses primarily on recent developments in catalytic methodologies for incorporating 2H, 3H, 11C, 13C, 14C, 15N, 18O, 18F, and 34S isotopes into organic molecules, along with a brief overview of well-established methods reported in this field.

items.title: Dual-Acting Ligands as Histamine H3 Receptor Ligands and L-Type Ca2+ Channel Inhibitors
items.abstract: The challenging development of drugs for neurological diseases caused by multifactorial characteristics and imbalances of several neurotransmitters and ions in the CNS demonstrates the importance of new therapeutic options. Synergistic or additional effects of multitarget-directed ligands are beneficial for these indications since they act simultaneously on multiple involved targets. Herein, we report the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of dual-target-directed modulators by combining a histamine H3 receptor (H3R) antagonist structural motif with various pharmacophores for Ca2+ channel inhibition, including dihydropyridines and dihydropyrimidines. Besides the high H3R affinities, we were particularly interested in the activity at two specific L-type Ca2+ channels (Cav1.2 and Cav1.3) due to their potential pathophysiological role in numerous neurological disorders, including Parkinson’s disease and autism spectrum disorders. Compounds 3f (1-(2,6-dimethyl-4-phenyl-5-(4-(3-(piperidin-1-yl)propoxy)benzoyl)-1,4-dihydropyridin-3-yl)ethan-1-one) and 5b (1-cyclohexyl-3-(3-(4-(3-(piperidin-1-yl)propoxy)phenyl)propyl)urea) were identified as lead compounds with nanomolar affinities for the H3R (Ki values of 1.56 nM and 8.41 nM, respectively) and micromolar Ca2+ channel inhibition (Cav1.2 IC50 = 25.5 and 103.9 μM, Cav1.3 IC50 = 40.9 and 43.5 μM, respectively) and were further evaluated for their use-dependency. Interestingly, the keto-substituted dihydropyridine 3f with H3R pharmacophore linked directly to the dihydropyridine showed the lowest H3R Ki values. The urea derivatives with a cyclohexyl side chain (5a, 5b, and 5e) showed a preference for Cav1.3. The results of this study provide new insights into the structure–activity relationship of these dual-acting ligands and are essential for lead structure optimization to accomplish dual inhibitory effects.

items.title: Asymmetric Partial Hydrogenation of Quinazolines: Overcoming Catalyst Poisoning by a Robust yet Active Solo-Coordination-Vacant Ir(III) Pincer Catalyst
items.abstract: Catalytic asymmetric partial hydrogenation of quinazolines to afford enantioenriched 3,4-dihydroquinazolines, a privileged scaffold in medicinal chemistry, is a long-standing challenge likely due to product-induced catalyst deactivation. Here, we report a robust yet highly reactive solo-coordination-vacant Ir(III) pincer catalyst being capable of overcoming this poisoning challenge. This catalyst enables the asymmetric partial hydrogenation of a broad range of quinazolines, affording 3,4-dihydroquinazolines in high yields (up to 98%) and excellent enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee). In a dedicated catalyst-loading study, the loading could be reduced to 0.001 mol % (10 ppm, TON = 38,000). Mechanistic investigations, including NMR spectroscopic detection of a key Ir–H intermediate and base-dependence studies, support a catalytic cycle proceeding through a well-defined Ir(III)-hydride species and suggest that an alkali-metal-assisted pathway is unlikely to be dominant.

items.title: Histidine Buffer Protects Human Insulin against AAPH-Induced Oxidation but Exacerbates t -BHP-mediated Degradation
items.abstract: Recombinant therapeutic proteins and peptides are highly susceptible to physicochemical instability during manufacturing and long-term storage, with oxidative stress presenting a major challenge. Histidine (His) is widely used as a buffer in biopharmaceutical formulations and may provide antioxidant protection; however, its effect on product stability can depend on the specific nature of the oxidative stress. In this study, human insulin formulations containing 20 mM His or phosphate buffer (pH 7.0) were exposed to oxidative stress induced by 2,2′-azobis(2-amidinopropane) dihydrochloride (AAPH) or tert-butyl hydroperoxide (t-BHP). Physical instability was evaluated using micro-flow imaging and size-exclusion chromatography, while chemical degradation was characterized by reversed-phase high-performance liquid chromatography (RP-HPLC), liquid chromatography−mass spectrometry peptide mapping, and electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy. The results showed that under AAPH stress, His markedly reduced particle and soluble aggregate formation and preserved insulin main-peak purity. After 2 weeks at 40 °C, RP-HPLC purity was 91.28% in His formulations compared with 78.85% in phosphate formulations, and an oxidation-associated impurity localized to the B1−B13 region was detected only in the phosphate formulation. Furthermore, an AAPH-associated 5,5-dimethyl-1-pyrroline N-oxide (DMPO) radical-adduct signal was detected in phosphate formulations but not in His formulations. In contrast, under t-BHP stress, His exacerbated both aggregation and chemical degradation, with main-peak purity decreasing to 89.45% compared with 92.16% in phosphate, and no comparable DMPO-detectable signal was observed under t-BHP conditions. These findings demonstrate that the effect of His on insulin stability is oxidant-dependent and highlight the importance of matching excipient selection to the relevant oxidative stress pathway rather than assuming universal antioxidant protection.

items.title: Discovery of ASTX295, a Potent, Next-Generation Small Molecule Antagonist of MDM2 with a Differentiated Pharmacokinetic Profile
items.abstract: Inhibition of murine double minute 2 (MDM2)-p53 protein−protein interaction with small molecules has been shown to reactivate p53 and inhibit tumor growth. However, the use of MDM2 antagonists in the clinic has been associated with target-related hematological toxicities. Here, we describe the identification of a novel isoindolinone MDM2 antagonist with a targeted human pharmacokinetic profile (plasma half-life of 4−8 h) as a strategy to overcome the on-target bone-marrow toxicity associated with earlier MDM2 antagonists. A combination of structure-aided design and optimization of physicochemical properties led to the identification of 15 (ASTX295), which has been tested in a clinical trial in advanced solid tumors with wild-type TP53 (NCT03975387).

items.title: Extracellular Vesicle Bioinformatics in Heart Failure Pharmacology and Translational Biomarker Development
items.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is clinically heterogeneous, and established biomarkers incompletely capture inflammation, remodeling, metabolic dysfunction, and variability in the treatment response. This critical review examines extracellular vesicle (EV) bioinformatics as a complementary approach to mechanism-informed HF research. EV cargo can enrich selected molecular signals, but circulating populations have mixed cellular origins and overlap with non-EV plasma compartments. We assess analytical platforms, preanalytical confounding, computational reproducibility, and the evidence for linking EV modules to clinical phenotypes and therapeutic mechanisms. Selected clinical trial records provide contexts for hypothesis generation rather than evidence of validated EV endotypes. We outline requirements for leakage-resistant modeling, external validation, comparison with matched samples and established biomarkers, and fit-for-purpose biomarker development. Prospective studies must establish incremental value and operational feasibility before EV signatures can inform treatment selection or adaptive trial decisions.

items.title: Discovery of an Orally Bioavailable 2-Pyridyl Amide Lead with Intracellular Potency and In Vivo Efficacy against Mycobacterium tuberculosis with Favorable Safety
items.abstract: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) poses significant challenges to effective treatment and the discovery of novel anti-tuberculosis agents. Herein, we report a systematic modification of the GSK hit, GSK1750922A, to generate a lead effective against MDR-TB. The detailed SAR study identified 29l as a potent and selective inhibitor of Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv with an MIC of 0.39 μg/mL. This compound retained excellent activity across a panel of MDR-TB clinical isolates with MICs as low as 0.0695−0.55 μg/mL. Compound 29l exhibited potent intracellular efficacy against M. tuberculosis-infected macrophages, and oral administration of 29l reduced the pulmonary and splenic bacterial burden by ∼2-fold to 3-fold in a murine tuberculosis infection model. In a repeated-dose toxicity study, 29l showed no mortality at the tested dosage of 125 mg/kg and 250 mg/kg. Collectively, the potent antimycobacterial activity, favorable preclinical developability, in vivo efficacy, and safety profile identify 29l as a promising lead for further development of therapeutics against MDR-TB.

items.title: Engineering Mechanically Tunable Polymer Scaffolds for Osteoblast-Osteoclast Co-Culture
items.abstract: The study reports two biomimetic scaffolds with distinct mechanical properties, mucin-polyethylene glycol (mucin−PEG) and poly(2-(dimethylamino)ethyl methacrylate-co-hydroxyethyl methacrylate) (PD-HEMA), as platforms to support the co-culture of osteoblasts and osteoclasts for bone remodeling. MC3T3-E1 pre-osteoblasts and RANKL-induced RAW 264.7 osteoclasts were co-cultured on the scaffolds, and cellular responses were evaluated by immunofluorescence, qRT-PCR, alizarin red staining, flow cytometry, and western blotting. Both types of scaffolds exhibit interconnected porous architectures with swelling characteristics. PD-HEMA demonstrated a higher storage modulus and structural stability, whereas mucin−PEG provided a biologically favorable microenvironment that promoted osteoblast−osteoclast interactions. Mucin−PEG scaffolds exhibited enhanced expression of osteogenic and bone remodeling markers, including osteocalcin (OCN), osteoadherin, and Cathepsin K, while PD-HEMA scaffolds promoted greater extracellular matrix mineralization, evidenced by increased alkaline phosphatase (ALP) expression and alizarin red staining. The scaffolds can serve as potential in vitro models to investigate bone remodeling, osteoporosis pathophysiology, and the preclinical evaluation of bone regenerative therapies.

items.title: Thermodynamic Dissection Cooperativity into PPI and Ligand Entropic Contributions in PROTAC and Molecular Glues
items.abstract: Douglass’ cooperativity α and Ciulli’s cooperativity α’ represent the same physical parameter in three-body induced-proximity systems, yet they remain unexplainable for paradoxes such as thermodynamic steric-driven negative cooperativity with favorable contact of a ternary complex evidenced by a cryo-EM structure. We noticed that in the “partial-embedded” model, a substantial portion of giant ligand remains exposed outside and does not engage with the host protein’s force field. This exposed ligand part incurs an entropic cost due to the restriction of translational/orientational degrees of freedom without thermodynamic compensation. This large, mass-dependent unfavorable ligand entropy penalty normally shifts binding affinity to 104∼108-fold. ITC thermodynamic cycle analysis confirmed the dramatic entropy loss among the reaction pair. Subtracting the ligand entropy, the real cooperativity was composed of two parts: one was conformation energy loss/gain of PROTAC, and another was energy contribution in PPI, which was proportional to the buried PPI area, driven by dispersed water, and the positive cooperativity was often in the range 0∼−4 kcal/mol.

items.title: nido -Carborane-Conjugated Modification Enhances Antimicrobial Peptide Performance: Antimicrobial and Antibiofilm Effects, Stability, and Synergy with Polymyxin B against Acinetobacter baumannii
items.abstract: Carboranes are hydrophobic groups with a rigid cage-like hybrid skeleton, exhibiting three-dimensional aromaticity and enzymatic resistance. These unique properties hold promise for enhancing the druggability of antimicrobial peptides. Herein, we report a nido-carborane conjugation strategy that successfully generated a lead peptide, CB19-B, through three rounds of optimization involving conjugation site screening, amino acid substitution, and linker replacement. CB19-B exhibited significantly enhanced antimicrobial potency, improved stability, and low hemolysis, along with excellent anti-drug-resistant and antibiofilm abilities. Furthermore, it was effective in bacterial peritonitis, catheter-associated biofilm infection, and skin wound infection caused by Acinetobacter baumannii. Notably, CB19-B exhibited synergistic antimicrobial effects with polymyxin B both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistic studies revealed that CB19-B delivers antimicrobial effects through membrane disruption and oxidative damage induced by reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation. Collectively, CB19-B, obtained via the nido-carborane conjugation strategy, possesses the dual potential as a candidate against A. baumanniiinfection and as a polymyxin B adjuvant.

items.title: Development of Dual Functional Molecules Targeting Histone Deacetylases and Human Caseinolytic Protease P
items.abstract: Based on compound 1, a potent activator of human caseinolytic protease P (hClpP), we designed and synthesized a class of dual functional molecules capable of simultaneously activating hClpP and inhibiting histone deacetylases (HDACs). Structural optimization of the linker region led to the identification of compound 13, which activated hClpP more potently than 1 (EC50 = 0.27 μM vs 0.35 μM) and exhibited strong pan-HDAC inhibition (IC50 = 0.29 μM). Biochemical and cellular studies demonstrated that 13 effectively inhibited HDACs in Molm13 cells with high selectivity for HDAC6, while simultaneously activating cellular hClpP, promoting degradation of hClpP substrates, and inducing pronounced mitochondrial dysfunction. Functionally, 13 potently inhibited cell proliferation and robustly induced apoptosis in Molm13 cells. Compound 13 showed good pharmacokinetic profile and displayed significantly stronger antitumor activity in a Molm13 xenograft mouse model compared to a potent hClpP activator ONC212, highlighting its therapeutic potential for the treatment of acute myelogenous leukemia (AML).

items.title: Alzheimer Protease Target Redux
items.abstract: The membrane-embedded protease γ-secretase produces the amyloid β-peptide that notoriously deposits in the brain in Alzheimer’s disease. Inhibitors of this enzyme are toxic, but modulators are promising. A medicinal chemistry campaign described in this issue solved the difficult problem of balancing potency, selectivity, and solubility to discover the advanced clinical candidate nivegacetor.

items.title: Assembly of Trifluoromethyl-Substituted Dihydrobenzoimidazo[2,1- b ]thiazoles via Cascade Annulation of 2-Mercaptobenzimidazoles with CF3-Imidoyl Sulfoxonium Ylides
items.abstract: An efficient and practical approach to the synthesis of trifluoromethyl-substituted dihydrobenzoimidazo[2,1-b]thiazoles has been developed via a [3 + 2] annulation of 2-mercaptobenzimidazoles with CF3-imidoyl sulfoxonium ylides (TFISYs) under metal-free conditions. The reaction features simple operation, environmentally benign and mild conditions, readily available reactants, broad substrate scope, high efficiency and scalability, providing a facile and straightforward entry to biologically valuable N,S-containing fused tricyclic heterocyclic derivatives.

items.title: Photocontraction of Thietane Dioxides: A Modular Route to Functionalized Cyclopropanes
items.abstract: Cyclopropanes are important structural motifs in medicinal chemistry, and considerable efforts have been devoted to developing synthetic methods that accommodate diverse substitution patterns and functional-group profiles. Within the synthetic toolbox, ring-contraction strategies remain relatively underexplored, despite their potential to enable late-stage ring construction, provide access to challenging substitution patterns, and reduce reliance on protecting-group manipulations. In this context, we developed a modular approach to access functionalized 2-arylcyclopropanes based on the photochemical SO 2 extrusion from thietane dioxides. The method offers synthetic flexibility through complementary and straightforward precursor syntheses involving sulfene-alkene [2+2] cycloaddition or nucleophilic addition to thiete dioxides. The contraction process is catalyst-free, requires neither highly reactive reagents nor stoichiometric metal reagents and accommodates a broad range of N-, O-, P-, and C-based substituents. Its synthetic utility is demonstrated through the development of one-pot nucleophilic addition-photocontraction sequences, integration with skeletal editing to convert oxetanes into cyclopropanes, and implementation in continuous flow using UV LEDs irradiation. Experimental and computational investigations support a mechanism initiated by triplet-state fragmentation, followed by stereospecific cyclization of a singlet diradicaloid with concomitant SO 2 extrusion. This work establishes photochemical SO 2 extrusion as a versatile ring-contraction strategy complementary to established approaches to functionalized cyclopropanes.

items.title: Utilization of an Activity-Based Probe to Explore Interactomes of DXP Synthase
items.abstract: During infection, bacteria rapidly adapt to evade the host immune response, enduring nutrient limitation and other harsh conditions. To aid adaptation, bacteria have evolved multifunctional proteins capable of sensing environmental changes and modulating signaling and enzyme activity in response to host-derived stresses. We hypothesize that the bacterial central metabolic enzyme 1-deoxy-d-xylulose 5-phosphate synthase (DXPS) is multifunctional: in its canonical role, DXPS catalyzes the synthesis of DXP via a ThDP-dependent ligand-gated mechanism using pyruvate and d-glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate (d-GAP); additionally, it exhibits species-specific alternative activities and structural/mechanistic features, suggesting bacteria exploit DXPS in distinct ways to survive in different infection contexts. Here, we demonstrate ABP 1, an acetyl phosphonate activity-based probe, as a tool to interrogate species-specific DXPS inhibition and function. We found that DXPS homologs with low sequence similarity are comparably inhibited/labeled by ABP 1, and competitive activity-based protein profiling using ABP 1 allows detection of species-specific inhibitor potencies. Crosslinking of ABP 1 to DXPS maintains the enzyme as the dimer in a closed conformation. Intriguingly, pulldown experiments using immobilized E. coli or P. aeruginosa PAO1 DXPS-ABP 1 adducts with matching lysates (E. coli MG1655 or PAO1) suggest a broader role for DXPS in metabolism/cellular regulation in bacteria and the potential for pathogen-specific DXPS functions. These findings establish ABP 1-enabled pulldowns as a platform to explore DXPS multifunctionality and identify pathogen-specific DXPS-protein complexes, opening avenues to explore DXPS biology and for the development of antibacterial strategies targeting pathogen-specific DXPS functions.

items.title: Synthesis of Apo-Carotenal- and Retinal-Derived Esters and Amides for Probing Lecithin:Retinol Acyltransferase
items.abstract: Lecithin:retinol acyltransferase (LRAT) esterifies all-trans-retinol to support opsin-chromophore regeneration and vitamin A storage, yet chemical tools for investigating this enzyme remain limited. We synthesized matched retinoid- and apo-carotenal-derived haloacetates and haloacetamides to define how electrophile reactivity, polyene length, and linkage identity govern LRAT inhibition. Extended conjugation necessitated low-temperature coupling and chromatography-free purification of unstable bromoacetates. Inhibition was quantified by measuring retinyl ester formation in bovine retinal pigment epithelium microsomes and with purified recombinant truncated LRAT. In microsomes, retinyl haloacetate potency increased more than 4000-fold from fluoroacetate to iodoacetate (apparent IC50 values of 110 and 0.026 μM, respectively), while bromo- and iodoacetamides also exhibited low-nanomolar apparent potency. The recombinant assay preserved the leaving-group dependence but compressed the potency range. Tandem mass spectrometry confirmed covalent modification of the active-site cysteine, Cys161, following retinyl bromoacetate treatment, identified by a carboxymethyl adduct. LRAT tolerated substantial polyene truncation, although full-length retinoid scaffolds were most potent. Amide-linked analogues retained more consistent activity across assay formats, highlighting the influence of linkage identity and assay environment. Together, these findings define chemical determinants of LRAT inhibition and establish a modular platform for developing probes targeting its catalytic cysteine.

items.title: Directing-Group-Driven Intramolecular [2+2] Photocycloaddition Catalyzed by Chiral-at-Metal Rh(III): Divergent Assembly of Oxa-, Thia-, Aza-, and All-Carbon Tricyclic Cyclobutane Scaffolds
items.abstract: Chiral polycyclic cyclobutane‑embedded architectures are privileged motifs in bioactive natural products and pharmaceutical candidates, yet general catalytic platforms to assemble heteroatom‑diversified tricyclic cyclobutane frameworks remain rare. Herein, we disclose an intramolecular enantioselective [2+2] photocycloaddition catalyzed by a chiral‑at‑metal Rh(III) complex via bidentate‑directing‑group‑assisted N,O‑chelation. Unlike conventional photocycloaddition manifolds relying on triplet‑energy transfer or charge‑transfer activation, stereochemistry‑defining N,O‑chelation preorganizes substrate geometry around the chiral metal center in the ground state before photoexcitation. Photoexcitation takes place on the intact catalyst‑substrate chelate complex rather than free substrate; no intermolecular energy transfer or charge‑separation processes operate, and intersystem crossing proceeds within the chelate to confine triplet‑state reactivity inside the chiral coordination sphere. This renders high‑fidelity stereochemical induction independent of the substrate’s intrinsic chromophore properties. Under blue‑light irradiation, the reaction furnishes chiral tricyclic cyclobutanes with up to three stereocenters (including one quaternary stereocenter), affording excellent diastereoselectivity (>20:1 dr) and enantioselectivity (up to >99 % ee). This unified catalytic platform enables divergent synthesis of four tricyclic classes: oxa‑, thia‑, aza‑, and all‑carbon cyclobutane skeletons, a capability unattainable with prior organocatalytic or Lewis‑acid‑based photocycloaddition protocols. The method tolerates electronically diverse aryl rings, various heteroaryl directing groups and other functional substituents. Importantly, gram‑scale synthesis is achievable at unchanged catalyst loading with full retention of yield and stereopurity, highlighting its practical utility for building large chiral polycyclic compound libraries for biomedical screening.

items.title: Evaluating cofolding methods for protein–macrocycle structure prediction
items.abstract: The accuracy of general-purpose cofolding models in predicting binding poses for novel protein–macrocycle complexes with little experimental structural precedent remains poorly characterized. We developed MacroCycle-Benchmark, which links chemically verified ligand structures to their experimental binding poses and protein environments across 1,861 cases. We evaluated six general-purpose cofolding models on a common set of 1,772 cases. With ligand SMILES as input, 22.7–30.8% of top-ranked predictions had a ligand heavy-atom root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) <2 Å after binding-site superposition and a local distance difference test score for protein–ligand interactions (LDDT-PLI) >0.8. Success rates were 10.7–16.5 percentage points lower for complexes released after each model’s training cutoff than for those released earlier. Among post-cutoff cases with evaluable similarity to pre-cutoff benchmark structures, all six models had success rates below 8% in the lowest-similarity group. In paired comparisons of cyclic peptides that could be represented by residue sequences and covalent linkages, Boltz-2 and RoseTTAFold 3 each recovered more experimental binding poses with sequence input than with SMILES. For macrocycles with 30–40 ring atoms, 97.5–100% of each model’s failed top-ranked SMILES predictions had a ligand heavy-atom RMSD of at least 2 Å even after ligand-only superposition. In these cases, the models failed to recover the bound conformation of the ligand itself, limiting their ability to reproduce the experimental binding mode. These findings indicate that current cofolding models have limited ability to generalize to macrocycle binding modes with little structural precedent in the benchmark. Predicted poses for such complexes should be used cautiously in structure-guided macrocycle design.

items.title: Homoleptic ruthenium(II)-N-heterocyclic carbene complexes with metal-to-ligand charge transfer phosphorescence lifetimes up to 11 μs
items.abstract: [Ru(tpy)2]2+ (tpy = 2,2’:6’,2’’-terpyridine) and its derivatives are weakly emissive or non-emissive with extremely short metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) lifetimes. [Ru(tpy)2]2+ possesses a 3MLCT lifetime of about 0.25 ns. Herein we report a series of homoleptic Ru(II)-N-heterocyclic carbene (Ru(II)-NHC) complexes ([Ru(LH)2](PF6)2, [Ru(LPhMe2)2](PF6)2, [Ru(LPhOMe)2](PF6)2, and [Ru(LNaph)2](PF6)2) which are structurally analogous to [Ru(tpy)2]2+, however, display phosphorescence in deaerated acetonitrile solution at room temperature with record 3MLCT lifetimes up to 11.2 μs which is longest among any homoleptic Ru(II) complexes reported to date. Transient absorption spectroscopy and time-dependent density functional theory calculations have unambiguously supported these results. The homoleptic Ru(II)-NHC complexes possess higher 3MLCT state energies (2.35-2.58 eV) compared to both benchmark [Ru(bpy)3]2+ (bpy = 2,2’-bipyridine, 2.13 eV) and [Ru(tpy)2]2+ (2.07 eV) complexes, and their polypyridyl derivatives. They have been used as photosensitizers in challenging visible light induced [2+2] cycloaddition reactions, and dearomative cascade catalysis via energy transfer processes. Such photoreactions have not been accessible previously by using benchmark [Ru(bpy)3]2+ photosensitizer or its derivatives.

items.title: Synthesis of Chiral Tertiary Propargylic Alcohols by Using Dual Catalytic Activity of Halohydrin Dehalogenases
items.abstract: Chiral tertiary propargylic alcohols offer considerable synthetic versatility, as their hydroxyl and alkyne groups allow further functionalization and provide access to structurally diverse compounds, including pharmaceuticals and natural products.Therefore, the development of efficient strategies for their asymmetric synthesis continues to be an important objective in organic chemistry.Herein, a biocatalytic approach to enantiopure propargylic building blocks via halohydrin dehalogenase (HHDH)-catalyzed cascade reactions is reported.Starting from racemic propargylic 1,2-chloroalcohols, the enzyme catalyzes intramolecular dehalogenation to form an epoxide intermediate, which subsequently undergoes regioselective azidolysis in the presence of sodium azide.This cascade consists of two consecutive kinetic resolutions, affording chiral tertiary propargylic 1,2-azido alcohols and 1,2-chloroalcohols with enantiomeric excesses of up to >99.9% and isolated yields of up to 49%.The reactions were scaled up to gram-scale synthesis and performed at substrate concentrations of 200 mM.Subsequent synthetic transformations demonstrated the versatility of the obtained building blocks for the preparation of chiral propargylic amino alcohols, α-methylene cyclic carbonates, isocoumarins, phosphoramidates, or more complicated synthetic motives such as cyclic compounds obtained through ring-closing metathesis.

items.title: Skeletal muscle proteomics reveals metabolic phenotype–specific adaptations to exercise training in health, obesity, and type 2 diabetes
items.abstract: Exercise training improves metabolic health, including whole-body insulin sensitivity, yet the molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. We applied proteomics and phosphoproteomics to skeletal muscle biopsies from lean men, and men with obesity or type 2 diabetes (T2D), obtained before and after 8 weeks of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) under basal and insulin-stimulated conditions. Before HIIT, protein expression showed a stepwise progression from lean to obesity to T2D. HIIT induced more pronounced proteomic remodeling in obesity and T2D compared with lean men, characterized by increased mitochondrial and decreased proteasomal contents. Phosphoproteomic responses were diagnosis dependent, revealing distinct insulin signaling adaptations. Mechanistically, AMP-activated protein kinase γ2 (AMPKγ2) emerged as a prominent HIIT-regulated protein, exhibiting increased incorporation into AMPKα2β2 complexes across all phenotypes, and AMPKγ2 overexpression in human myotubes increased basal glucose oxidation. These findings elucidate molecular pathways underlying exercise-induced insulin sensitization and suggest AMPKγ2 as a candidate regulator for exercise-induced metabolic adaptation.

items.title: Bioinspired mucolytic microrods for active mucus penetration and enhanced antibiotic delivery against H. pylori
items.abstract: Helicobacter pylori infects half of the global population and is a major driver of gastric cancer. Clinical eradication remains challenging because antibiotics must survive the acidic gastric lumen, penetrate the viscoelastic mucus barrier, and reach bacteria residing near the gastric epithelium. Here, we report a biomimetic oral delivery system that integrates rod-shaped morphology, acid protection, active mucolysis, and localized antibiotic delivery. The platform consists of clarithromycin-loaded Santa Barbara Amorphous-15 silica microrods coated with a pH-responsive alginate-pronase conjugate. The coating protects clarithromycin and pronase under acidic gastric conditions, while the less acidic inner mucus microenvironment promotes coating detachment and pronase-mediated mucolysis, enabling active mucus penetration. In vitro and in vivo studies show that these bacteria-mimicking microrods significantly enhance mucus penetration and increase gastric residence time twofold. In a murine infection model, the platform achieved 100% eradication at 15 milligrams per kilogram and maintained 90% clearance at 7.5 milligrams per kilogram, producing a ∼2000-fold bacterial burden reduction compared to free clarithromycin. This bioinspired, shape-guided strategy offers a promising paradigm for localized gastrointestinal therapy.

items.title: From genetic risk factor to therapeutic target: The CREB3L4-GDF15 axis drives prostate cancer immune evasion
items.abstract: Advanced prostate cancer (PCa) is characterized by rapid progression and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, contributing to poor clinical outcomes and limited therapeutic responses. Mendelian randomization (MR) uses genetic variants as instrumental variables to assess causal associations while minimizing confounding and reverse causation. Through integrative proteogenomic analysis, including MR and colocalization across 438,178 males, we identified CREB3L4 as associated with PCa risk. CREB3L4 overexpression promoted tumor growth in mice, accompanied by activation of cholesterol metabolism, androgen receptor (AR) signaling, and immunosuppression. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed CREB3L4 enrichment in human PCa cells. Interaction analysis identified enhanced growth and differentiation factor (GDF) signaling in CREB3L4 + tumor cells, with CD8 + T cells as the primary receivers. Ligand–receptor analysis and coculture experiments identified GDF15 as the key mediator, through which tumor cells suppressed CD8 + T cell proliferation and activation via TGFBR2 signaling. In vivo, GDF15 neutralization attenuated CREB3L4-driven tumor growth and CD8 + T cell dysfunction, whereas prostate-specific CREB3L4 knockout or adeno-associated virus-mediated knockdown suppressed tumor growth and restored CD8 + T cell function. Clinical analyses confirmed elevated CREB3L4 and GDF15 expression in PCa, inversely associated with CD8 + T cell infiltration and immunotherapy response. Collectively, these findings reveal that CREB3L4 promotes AR signaling-mediated GDF15 expression, driving CD8 + T cell dysfunction and identifying the CREB3L4–GDF15 axis as a potential therapeutic target in PCa.

items.title: Ubiquitination of USP5 by a bacterial effector inhibits NLRP3 inflammasome activation
items.abstract: The intracellular pathogen Legionella pneumophila employs a repertoire of effector proteins to manipulate the host ubiquitin signaling and subvert host immune responses. In this study, we reported that the L. pneumophila effector GobX (Lpg2455) functions as a ubiquitin ligase to target the host deubiquitinase USP5. Ubiquitination of USP5 by GobX inhibits its deubiquitination activity. Furthermore, this ubiquitination enhances the interaction between USP5 and the host E3 ligase MARCHF7, thereby facilitating MARCHF7-dependent ubiquitination of NLRP3. This modification targets NLRP3 for autophagic degradation, ultimately suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation in macrophages. Our findings uncover a sophisticated strategy in which a bacterial effector hijacks the host ubiquitination machinery to dampen inflammasome signaling.

items.title: A programmable cell-free biosensor device for on-demand detection of pathogens and antibiotics
items.abstract: Cell-free systems provide a versatile platform for engineering customizable, gene circuit-based biosensors for decentralized, low-cost molecular diagnostics. Nevertheless, their performance in complex samples is often compromised by matrix interference, necessitating laborious preprocessing that restricts field deployment. Here, we developed a programmable, on-demand, cell-free kit (POCKit) that integrates sample pretreatment with point-of-care detection. The POCKit device comprises a negative pressure storage chamber and a sampling-sensing chamber, which can be connected to a microneedle array or pipette module for sample collection, filtration and target detection via a freeze-dried cell-free molecular reaction network. The POCKit enables detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection in wound exudates, interstitial fluids and artificial sputum within one hour. It also detects tetracycline in food and environmental water, distinguishing tetracycline-spiked samples from negative controls without specialized equipment or tedious preparation. A portable fluorescence imaging box and smartphone application further support real-time signal acquisition and analysis, offering a ready-to-use platform for on-site diagnostics across biomedicine, food safety, and environmental monitoring.

items.title: Aclarubicin disrupts RNA polymerase II progression at replication-coupled histone genes
items.abstract: Anthracyclines are effective chemotherapeutic agents that cause DNA and chromatin damage. One member of the anthracyclines, aclarubicin, has gained therapeutic interest due to its ability to kill cancer cells through chromatin-based mechanisms, thus avoiding the off-target effects associated with DNA damage. However, the molecular mechanism of action leading to aclarubicin-induced chromatin damage remains elusive. Here we performed Cleavage Under Targets and Tagmentation (CUT&Tag) of RNA polymerase II (Pol II) and other transcriptional regulators in human cells following aclarubicin treatment. We found that aclarubicin strongly disrupts the replication-coupled histone genes, resulting in a nonproductive accumulation of Pol II transcription machinery at levels exceeding those at other genes. We attribute this sensitivity to the dense Pol II loading and rapid transcription of the histone genes, which intensify the chromatin-disrupting effects of aclarubicin. Together, our findings shed light on the mechanism of aclarubicin as an anticancer drug and point to the replication-coupled histone genes as a target for therapeutic intervention.

items.title: The circSRSF5-FUS-EIF4A3 regulatory circuitry protects Ewing sarcoma cells from EWS::FLI1 small-molecule inhibition
items.abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have become a key focus in cancer research due to their high stability, diversity, and ability to regulate various biological processes. This study explores the impact of small-molecule inhibition of EWS::FLI1 oncogene by YK-4-279 in Ewing sarcoma (ES). ES is a rare and highly aggressive childhood cancer driven by fusion proteins that disrupt normal gene regulation and promote tumor growth. Current treatments rely on intensive chemotherapy with serious long-term side effects, emphasizing the need for targeted therapies. A promising new approach targets the interaction between EWS::FLI1 and the RNA helicase DHX9 through the small molecule YK-4-279, which displays strong antitumor effects and has advanced to clinical trials. Transcriptome profiling revealed widespread changes in circRNA expression after YK-4-279 treatment, with a notable up-regulation of circSRSF5 . Functional and mechanistic evidence identifies a key role for circSRSF5 in tumor cell survival by stabilizing the anti-apoptotic protein eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4A3 (EIF4A3) and contributing to therapy resistance. These findings uncover a previously unidentified role for circRNAs, particularly circSRSF5 , in ES pathogenesis and treatment response.

items.title: Cryo-EM reveals a transmembrane allosteric site and activation mechanism for the SERCA calcium pump
items.abstract: Impaired sarco-endoplasmic reticulum Ca 2+ -ATPase (SERCA) activity contributes to defective calcium handling and cellular dysfunction in cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, yet the structural basis of small-molecule SERCA activation has remained unknown. SERCA is a ubiquitous P-type ATPase that restores cytosolic Ca 2+ to the sarco-endoplasmic reticulum and is essential for cardiac Ca 2+ cycling and cellular energy homeostasis. Here, we used cryogenic electron microscopy to define how two chemically distinct activators, CDN1163 and UM-52, enhance SERCA function. Structures at 2.6 Å and 3.1 Å resolution show that both compounds bind the same previously unrecognized activation hotspot in the transmembrane domain, a shallow groove formed by helices M3 and M4 and capped by M1. Despite limited chemical similarity, both activators share conserved interactions with Ser265 and Trp272 and stimulate Ca 2+ -dependent ATPase activity. Activator binding promotes a catalytically competent, calcium-bound E1-like conformation of SERCA that may involve altered protein-lipid interactions. These findings establish a structural framework for rational design of potent next-generation SERCA activators.

items.title: Large 77Se NMR Signal Enhancements in Solutions by Overhauser Dynamic Nuclear Polarization at 9.4 T for Real-Time Reaction Monitoring
items.abstract: 77Se nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) is a key method to probe selenium functional centers in biology and materials science, yet its practical application is severely hindered by its intrinsically low sensitivity due to the low gyromagnetic ratio (19% of 1H) and natural abundance (7.6%). Overhauser effect dynamic nuclear polarization (OE-DNP) has recently emerged as a promising method for generating steady-state signal enhancement in high-field liquid NMR at room temperature. However, its application to 77Se has remained unexplored to date. Here, we present liquid-state OE-DNP as a route for 77Se NMR.
