At 9.4 T, we report 102 to 103 fold signal enhancements for organoselenium compounds, including the drug candidate ebselen, with polarization buildup within seconds. The large enhancements are the result of efficient electron-to-nuclear polarization transfer with OE-DNP coupling factors of ≳|0.4|, the highest reported so far at high magnetic fields (≥3 T) for NMR-active nuclei. The replenishable signal enhancements allow reaction monitoring by NMR on timescales longer than nuclear T1. As a proof of concept, we monitor a diselenide metathesis reaction over 48 h, capturing species evolution for kinetic studies. This effect can be further expanded to the heavier chalcogen, tellurium, as demonstrated by 123Te OE-DNP with similar efficiency.

items.title: Hybrids of 4-cyano-2-aryl-1,3-oxazole-5-sulfonamides with a 3-phenyl-1,2,4-oxadiazole motif: rational design, synthesis, in silico profiling, and antiproliferative activity against HepG2, A549, T98G, and HeLa human cancer cell lines
items.abstract: Multi-target anticancer agents attract growing interest for overcoming resistance and improving selectivity. Hybrids combining 1,2,4-oxadiazole and 1,3-oxazole scaffolds may target multiple oncogenic pathways simultaneously, yet the structural determinants of their activity remain poorly defined. Fourteen 1,3-oxazole/1,2,4-oxadiazole hybrids were designed, synthesized, and tested against HeLa, A549, HepG2, and T98G cancer lines, with non-cancerous NCTC clone 929 for selectivity. Two series were prepared: acyclic-linked hybrids (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12; –(CH2)n–, n = 2-7) and piperidine-linked analogs (13, 14). Activity depended steeply on linker length, peaking in compound 12 (n = 7), the most potent derivative (HeLa CC50 = 14.73 ± 2.02 µM; A549 CC50 = 43.92 ± 3.71 µM; HepG2 CC50 = 394.95 ± 24.01 µM; SI = 8 toward HeLa). Compounds 13 and 14 were inactive. Analysis of molecular geometry and electronic structure across the –(CH2)n–, series suggests compounds 2, 4, and 6 cannot engage productively with protein active sites: their tweezer-like geometry directs electron density into intramolecular contacts rather than outward-facing interactions. Lengthening the linker in 8, 10, and 12 shifts the geometry toward a more linear arrangement. Docking predicts interaction with the E6AP-binding pocket of HPV18 E6, with compound 12 occupying it at ΔG = –9.0 kcal/mol, consistent with the pronounced sensitivity of HPV18-positive HeLa cells. Virtual profiling implicated stress-response signaling (ARE, MMP, ATAD5) and aromatase. Compound 12 showed very low similarity to ChEMBL bioactives (p ≤ 0.3) and low predicted target-interaction probability, suggesting a potentially unrecognized mechanism. Linker length thus emerges as the principal determinant of antiproliferative activity in this hybrid class, defining compound 12 as a lead for HPV-associated cancers, with activity hypothesized to disrupt the oncogenic E6-E6AP interaction.

items.title: Discovery and Structure–Activity Relationship Optimization of a Novel Rv1625c Agonist Chemotype with Antitubercular Activity
items.abstract: Rv1625c/Cya has emerged as a promising target for the development of treatment-shortening therapies for tuberculosis. Screening of an Enamine compound library identified sBVQ004 as an initial hit, and rapid hit optimization led to compound 1, which was subsequently confirmed as an Rv1625c/Cya agonist. Structure–activity relationship studies identified lead compound 25 with potent activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv under cholesterol-dependent growth conditions (MIC = 0.27 μM) and strong intramacrophage activity (EC50 = 0.079 μM). Compounds 1 and 25 showed oral bioavailabilities of 84.5% and 51.9% in mice, respectively. Repeat twice daily (BID) oral dosing of compound 1 resulted in a dose- and time-dependent decrease in systemic exposure. Despite this pharmacokinetic limitation, the potency and overall profile of this chemotype encouraged continued optimization.

items.title: Development of Catalytically Inactive APOBEC3A Variants with Enhanced Thermal Stability and Expression Yield
items.abstract: APOBEC3A (A3A) is a single-stranded (ss) DNA cytidine deaminase implicated in cancer mutagenesis and therapy resistance, making it a compelling cancer target. However, wildtype A3A is toxic to bacteria complicating recombinant protein production. To enable structural and deamination-independent analyses, catalytically inactive variants are often used, most commonly A3A-E72A and A3A-E72Q. We previously showed that the E72Q substitution destabilizes the enzyme, reducing thermal stability and ssDNA binding compared to an alanine substitution. Here, we applied nonequilibrium alchemical free energy calculations to identify stabilizing substitutions at the catalytic residue, which predicted hydrophobic substitutions such as E72V. Based on this analysis, E72V, E72G, and E72M were selected for experimental validation and evaluated for thermal stability, ssDNA binding affinity, secondary structure percentage, and propensity to unfold and aggregate. Consistent with alchemical predictions, E72V maintained thermal stability, ssDNA binding, and folding properties comparable to E72A. Notably, E72V also provided an approximately 2-fold increase in bacterial expression yield while avoiding the substantial batch-to-batch yield variability observed with E72A. The equivalent E255V substitution in the closely related APOBEC3B catalytic domain (A3Bctd) yielded higher thermal stability, comparable ssDNA binding, and an approximately 3-fold improvement in expression yield relative to its alanine counterpart. These results identify A3A-E72V and A3Bctd-E255V as improved catalytically inactive scaffolds and establish a foundation for APOBEC3 protein engineering for crystallographic studies and structure-guided drug development.

items.title: Long‐Lived Fluorinated Foldamer Channels Conduct Protons Through a Plausible Confined Carbonyl–Water Relay
items.abstract: Artificial proton channels that combine high conductivity with strict exclusion of water and competing ions remain challenging. Herein, we report a series of fluorinated aromatic amide foldamers ( 1 ‐ 6 ) that intramolecularly fold into transmembrane channels with angstrom‐scale pores. The lead compound, channel 1 , features an intrinsic pore diameter of approximately 2.0 Å and mediates rapid H + transport across lipid bilayers, with an EC 50 value of 40 nM (∼6.0 x 10 −7 mol% relative to lipid), a single‐channel conductance of 196.2 pS, and long‐lived open states lasting up to 170 s. Notably, 1 displays high H + selectivity over Cl − , Na +, and K + (selectivity ratios of 192.0, 132.6, and 41.3, respectively) with no measurable enhancement of water permeability. Combined molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, DFT calculations, and hydrogen‐deuterium exchange experiments indicate a predominantly dehydrated pore and support a novel confined hybrid proton‐relay mechanism, in which pyridone carbonyl O‐atoms cooperate with one or a few (protonated) water species, distinct from conventional water‐wire conduction. Beyond its transport function, 1 induces apoptosis and exhibits potent anticancer activity, with IC 50 values of 2.7–5.4 µM against four cancer cell lines.

items.title: Identification of Potent Target VDAC1 for Hepatocellular Carcinoma Therapy with the Natural Chloroxanthone–Xanthone Heterodimer Molecule Inducing Ferroptosis
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major cause of cancer‐related mortality, underscoring the need for actionable targets and effective small‐molecule therapeutics. Voltage‐dependent anion channel 1 (VDAC1), a key regulator of mitochondrial homeostasis, remains incompletely explored as a therapeutic target in HCC. From the endophytic fungus Penicillium sp. RM, we isolated two pairs of enantiomeric heterodimers ( 1 and 2 ) and their monomers ( 3 and 4 ). Penirmxanthone A ( 1 ) is the first reported chloroxanthone‐xanthone heterodimer, whereas penirmxanthone B ( 2 ) features a previously undescribed chloroxanthone‐gentisin scaffold. In vitro, (+)‐ 1 suppressed aggressive phenotypes of HCC cells and induced ferroptosis. Chemical proteomic, biophysical, and genetic analyses identified VDAC1 as a direct and functionally required target of (+)‐ 1 . Mechanistically, (+)‐ 1 engages VDAC1 through K239 and N241, destabilizes the V‐Set and Transmembrane Domain Containing 2 Like (VSTM2L)‐VDAC1‐Hexokinase 2 (HK2) complex, promotes VDAC1 oligomerization, and impairs mitochondrial membrane potential and energy metabolism, culminating in ferroptosis. VDAC1 knockout attenuated these effects, whereas VDAC1 re‐expression restored them. In vivo, VBIT‐4 diminished (+)‐ 1 ‐induced antitumor and ferroptosis‐related effects. Collectively, these findings identify (+)‐ 1 , to our knowledge, as the first natural product that directly targets VDAC1 to promote its oligomerization and induce ferroptosis, highlighting VDAC1 oligomerization as a potential therapeutic target in HCC.

items.title: Enantioselective C(sp3)–C(sp3) Radical Coupling Through Photoinduced Electron Donor–Acceptor Activation
items.abstract: The enantioselective construction of C(sp 3 )–C(sp 3 ) bonds via radical pathways remains a formidable challenge, particularly when two transient alkyl radicals must be selectively coupled within a chiral catalytic environment. Here we report a photoinduced enantioselective C(sp 3 )–C(sp 3 ) radical coupling for the synthesis of α‐fluoroalkylated secondary alcohols, enabled by dual electron donor–acceptor (EDA) activation and chiral nickel catalysis. Central to this approach are two EDA activation events: one directly generates a primary alkyl radical from a carboxylic acid‐derived redox ester, whereas the other generates an alkoxy radical that undergoes intramolecular 1,2‐hydrogen atom transfer to form a secondary α‐oxy alkyl radical. Stereocontrolled interception of these radicals by a chiral nickel complex enables enantioselective C(sp 3 )–C(sp 3 ) bond formation. The reaction exhibits broad substrate scope and functional‐group tolerance, including the late‐stage functionalization of complex bioactive molecules. Mechanistic studies further support the proposed asymmetric radical coupling pathway.

items.title: Beyond a Single Best Representation: Target‐Specific Benchmarking of Frozen Molecular Embeddings and Fingerprints for Bioactivity Prediction
items.abstract: Transformer‐based embedding models have emerged as powerful tools for learning continuous molecular representations from large chemical corpora and are routinely deployed frozen, as general‐purpose feature extractors, whenever a single representation must serve many targets at once. However, their ability to capture structure‐bioactivity relationships remains highly dependent on the target system and the evaluation framework employed. Here, we present a large‐scale benchmark comparing molecular embeddings with classical fingerprints for bioactivity prediction across 126 diverse protein targets, using a rigorously curated dataset derived from ChEMBL. Several transformer‐based models, including ChemBERTa, MoLFormer XL, MegaMolBART, SMI‐TED289M, and MolEncoder, were evaluated in a frozen state alongside traditional fingerprints such as ECFP4, MACCS, Topological Torsion, and Atom Pair. Overall, fingerprints marginally outperform embeddings on average (mean F1 under the uncertainty‐rejection regime: 0.891 vs. 0.879), although top‐performing embeddings, particularly MegaMolBART and SMI‐TED289M, achieve competitive results on multiple targets. Critically, we introduce an uncertainty‐aware classification framework that incorporates adaptive rejection thresholds, substantially reducing the performance gap between the two representation families. The results demonstrate that target‐specific difficulty, rather than the choice of molecular representation, is the primary driver of predictive variability, a finding with direct practical implications for virtual screening and lead optimization workflows.

items.title: Design, synthesis and biological evaluation of novel indole-benzamide/sulfonamide hybrids as dual-acting agents for epilepsy-depression comorbidity
Scaffold Rigidification on Fentanyl Skeleton via an SP3-Rich Azaspiro[3.5]nonane Core: Targeting Opioid Induced-Respiratory Depression
Design, synthesis and biological evaluation of novel fusidic acid derivatives with tumor resistance reversal activity
Lithium coordination compound reduces nephrotoxicity and enhances therapeutic effects in Alzheimer’s disease female mice
An Allosteric CLR N-Terminal Swing-Out Mechanism for RAMP-Mediated Adrenomedullin Receptor Selectivity
items.abstract: Three receptor activity-modifying proteins (RAMP1–3) form heterodimers with the calcitonin (CTR) and calcitonin-like (CLR) G protein-coupled receptors and determine their selectivity for six CGRP family peptide agonists. These ligand–receptor systems are drug targets for migraine headache, diabetes and obesity, and circulatory system disorders. Here, we used molecular dynamics simulations and pharmacological assays of receptor chimeras and point mutants to identify a crucial allosteric component of the mechanism by which RAMP2 and RAMP3 modulate CLR to confer selectivity for two adrenomedullin (AM) peptides. We found that the extracellular domain (ECD) of RAMP2 and RAMP3, but not RAMP1, stabilized a partially unwound “swing-out” conformation of the CLR ECD N-terminal α-helix to accommodate the unique binding mode of the midregion of the AM peptides. The inability of the CTR N-terminus to adopt the swing-out conformation contributed to the distinct peptide selectivity profile of the three CTR-RAMP amylin receptors. By exploiting the CLR swing-out conformation, we engineered AM antagonist peptide variants with enhanced affinity and selectivity for CLR-RAMP2 and -RAMP3. Our results reveal the long-sought mechanism of RAMP-altered CLR ligand selectivity and have significant implications for drug development targeting the CLR- and CTR-RAMP complexes.

items.title: Suppressing Post-Surgical Recurrence in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer via Trop2-Targeted 64Cu-PET/NIR Dual-Modal Imaging-Guided Surgery
items.abstract: The modular integration of near-infrared (NIR) fluorescence and positron emission tomography (PET) on a single tumor-targeted nanobody offers a promising approach for precision tumor imaging and image-guided surgery. Here, we report a compact water-soluble trifunctional building block, IR-DOTA-NCS, which pre-integrates an NIR fluorophore, a DOTA chelator for 64Cu, and an isothiocyanate handle in a fixed 1:1:1 stoichiometry, enabling conjugation of a Trop2-targeting nanobody with a fixed 1:1 fluorophore/chelator ratio in a single step. The resulting probe, Trop2-IR-DOTA, enabled high-contrast dual-modal PET/NIR imaging of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) with receptor-mediated tumor uptake confirmed by blocking studies and exhibited favorable biosafety. In a fluorescence-guided resection model, a quantitative fluorescence threshold accurately identified tumor-negative margins, and guided surgery significantly reduced postoperative recurrence and lung metastasis while prolonging survival. This work provides a chemically rationalized platform for constructing dual-modal nanobody probes for precision image-guided cancer surgery.

items.title: Dual-Site Affinity-Directed Conjugation Enables Site-Specific DAR4 Antibody−Drug Conjugates from Native IgG
items.abstract: Antibody−drug conjugates (ADCs) with a drug-to-antibody ratio (DAR) of 4 can be produced using branched payload linkers, engineered attachment sites, or interchain-disulfide-based conjugation. Here, we developed an affinity-directed chemical strategy for placing one payload at each of four native Fc residues without antibody engineering or branched payload linkers. Using native trastuzumab, sequential application of Lys248- and Lys288-directed AJICAP reactions first demonstrated the modification of both lysine pairs. We then installed two thioester-based acyl-transfer arms on a single cyclic peptide that binds the fragment crystallizable (Fc) region, enabling dual-site modification in one affinity-directed step. After hydroxylamine-mediated scaffold removal, peptide mapping and changes in proteolytic cleavage supported Lys248 and Lys288 as the predominant modification sites. Conjugation with a maleimide-containing exatecan linker-payload produced a DAR4-enriched ADC with an average DAR of approximately 3.8. Intact mass spectrometry and hydrophobic interaction chromatography supported DAR4 as the principal species, and size-exclusion chromatography showed approximately 97% monomer. The ADC was evaluated by plasma profiling over 21 days in rats and produced sustained tumor-growth inhibition at 5.0 mg/kg in the human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive NCI-N87 xenograft model. Trastuzumab deruxtecan at 2.5 mg/kg served as a pharmacological reference. These results establish dual-site AJICAP conjugation as a strategy for constructing a four-site DAR4 ADC architecture on native IgG.

items.title: Enantioconvergent N -Alkylation of Indoles with Alcohols Promoted by an Axially Chiral Iridacycle
items.abstract: Achieving chemo- and enantioselective N-substitution of indoles presents significant challenges for catalytic method development. Herein, we report an enantioconvergent N-substitution of indoles with racemic secondary alcohols enabled by a newly developed axially chiral biaryl-supported iridacycle and chiral phosphoric acid. This borrowing-hydrogen process proceeds through an intriguing sequence involving transfer hydrogenation of indole, enantioselective reductive amination of an indoline intermediate, and subsequent rearomatization. Controlled reaction temperatures also enable selective access to the N-substituted indolines prior to rearomatization. The catalytic process accommodates diverse indoles and unactivated secondary alcohols without additional stoichiometric reagents, providing a direct and atom-economical approach to enantioenriched N-substituted indoles, including analogs of established drug candidates.

items.title: Molecularly Woven Quasi-3D Covalent Organic Frameworks Enable Piezocatalytic PANoptosis for Potent Cancer Immunotherapy
items.abstract: Metastatic breast cancer remains refractory to current immunotherapies due to insufficient immunogenic cell death and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments. Here, we engineer a piezocatalytic quasi-3D covalent organic framework (COF) nanoplatform (PPyrr-COF NPs) through a molecular weaving strategy, in which aligned polypyrrole (PPyrr) chains are covalently integrated into the COF scaffold, enabling efficient piezocatalysis-driven immunotherapy. Theoretical and experimental analyses demonstrate that the covalent linkage between the PPyrr chains and the COF skeleton creates z-axis-oriented electron-transport pathways, increases charge density, and narrows the bandgap, thereby substantially augmenting piezocatalytic oxidation activity. Under ultrasound irradiation, PPyrr-COF NPs generate abundant reactive oxygen species, which trigger a distinct PANoptotic cell death pathway and robust immunogenic cell death, characterized by the release of damage-associated molecular patterns. In murine 4T1 breast cancer models, PPyrr-COF NPs combined with ultrasound irradiation not only suppress primary tumor growth but also inhibit distant tumors and prevent lung metastasis. These effects are mediated by systemic antitumor immunity, including dendritic cell maturation and cytotoxic T lymphocyte infiltration, supported by transcriptomic analysis revealing regulation of PANoptosis and immune-related pathways. This work establishes a strategy for designing high-performance organic piezocatalysts and presents a noninvasive synergistic approach for cancer immunotherapy.

items.title: Photocatalytic Radical Relay Cyclization of N -Allyl Hydrazones with Diazo Compounds: Access to Ester-Containing and Fluorinated Dihydropyrazoles
items.abstract: A photocatalytic radical relay cyclization of N-allyl hydrazones with diazo compounds was developed for the efficient synthesis of structurally diverse dihydropyrazoles. Under mild photocatalytic conditions in environmentally benign solvents, diazo-derived carbon radicals generated via PCET (proton-coupled electron transfer) - like activation undergo regioselective addition to the C=C bond of N-allyl hydrazones, followed by intramolecular cyclization to furnish dihydropyrazoles. The method features broad substrate scope, low diazo loading, and good tolerance of several halogenated and electron-rich aryl substituents, accommodating diverse diazo compounds, including fluorinated variants, and enabling the rapid incorporation of ester and fluorinated motifs into dihydropyrazole scaffolds. The synthetic utility of this strategy is further demonstrated by late-stage functionalization of bioactive molecules and the concise synthesis of a fluorinated pesticide with an unreported synthetic route.

items.title: A TME-Selective PEGylated Anti-Mesothelin Nanobody Unmasked by Single-Cell Antigen-Specificity Profiling in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
items.abstract: Mesothelin (MSLN) is an attractive antibody target in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), yet its therapeutic utility is constrained by expression on normal ductal epithelium. Using single-cell RNA sequencing across three independent, treatment-naive PDAC cohorts, we demonstrate that MSLN is confined to the ductal lineage and is expressed by both malignant and adjacent normal ductal cells at comparable per-cell frequencies (tumour ductal 46−68%; normal ductal 29−58%). Apparent tumour enrichment in bulk data reflects ductal-compartment expansion rather than cell-intrinsic tumour specificity, defining an inherent on-target/off-tumour liability for conventional anti-MSLN antibodies. To decouple tumour engagement from normal-tissue binding, we engineered a conditionally activatable, polyethylene glycol (PEG)-masked anti-MSLN single-domain antibody (VHH) via structure-guided, site-specific conjugation of a 30 kDa maleimide-PEG to a paratope-proximal cysteine. Surface plasmon resonance confirmed that masking attenuates target binding ∼9-fold (KD 5.12 nM vs 0.568 nM for the de-masked VHH), predominantly through a reduced association rate. The masked conjugate exhibits attenuated binding in plasma-mimicking conditions and is preferentially de-masked by the glutathione-rich tumour interstitial fluid (TIF; 340.0 ± 65.0 μM versus plasma 3.58 ± 2.95 μM). After systemic administration to tumour-bearing mice, Ni-NTA-enriched antibody recovered from tumour displayed a de-masked fraction of 64.1 ± 13.2% versus 12.1 ± 5.9% in matched plasma. These findings provide proof of concept for a single-cell-informed, microenvironment-activated design paradigm for lineage-restricted tumour antigens.

items.title: Phenol-Induced Micelle Formation of Poloxamer 188 in Pharmaceutical Formulations Affected by Benzyl Alcohol, Solvent Deuteration, and Temperature
items.abstract: Biopharmaceutical formulations require multiple excipients to ensure stability and sterility over the lifetime of the drug. Nonionic surfactants are commonly used to prevent protein aggregation while small molecule preservatives are used to prevent microbial contamination. However, the combination of surfactants such as poloxamer 188 (P188) with preservatives such as phenol and benzyl alcohol in aqueous solution can lead to turbidity and large-scale phase separation despite each individual component being well within respective solubility limits. Small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) has recently shown that turbidity in P188/phenol solutions is preceded by a micelle regime driven primarily by phenol concentration. To understand and control the morphology and formation of micelles in P188/preservative mixtures, here we use SAXS to characterize solution structure and phase boundaries as a function of a variety of parameters. Results indicate that the phenol-induced unimer-to-micelle transition is linearly dependent on the concentration of a second preservative, benzyl alcohol, in quaternary mixtures with P188. A new phase, the pre-micelle phase, is observed when benzyl alcohol is added for some compositions of samples; its phase diagram is also determined. The effects of temperature and the use of D2O compared to H2O on the phase behavior are also investigated. Collectively this study will help the pharmaceutical industry better understand formulations containing P188 and preservatives with controlled and predictable solution structure.

items.title: The Role of Mannitol, Inulin, and Leucine on the Aerosolization and Stability of Inhalable Cannabidiol Powders Produced by Spray-Freeze-Drying
items.abstract: Cannabidiol (CBD) has shown therapeutic potential for inflammatory lung diseases; however, the development of inhalable dry powder formulations remains challenging because of its thermolabile nature, lipophilicity, and tendency to agglomerate. This study investigated spray-freeze-drying (SFD) as an alternative particle engineering technique to prepare inhalable CBD dry powder formulations using mannitol, inulin, and l-leucine as excipients. CBD formulations containing different combinations of these excipients were prepared and evaluated for yield, drug content, residual solvent content, morphology, crystallinity, aerosolization performance, stability, cytotoxicity, and anti-inflammatory activity. The prepared formulations showed yields ranging from 16% to 33%, with drug content above 95%. Scanning electron microscopy revealed that excipient-containing formulations produced round and porous particles, whereas CBD alone formed flaky and sticky particles. All formulations remained crystalline after SFD. Aerosolization studies demonstrated that formulations containing leucine exhibited superior performance, with fine particle fractions of 67.5% and 62.5%. Stability studies showed that although some morphological changes occurred under different humidity conditions, aerosolization performance remained largely unchanged. In vitro studies on A549 cells demonstrated that excipient-containing formulations reduced CBD cytotoxicity while maintaining comparable anti-inflammatory activity. Overall, this study demonstrates that SFD is a promising approach for producing inhalable CBD powders and that excipient selection, particularly the addition of leucine, plays an important role in improving aerosolization.

items.title: Second-Generation Route Development and Scale-Up for the Synthesis of (1 R ,3 R )-3-(3,5-Bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl)-2,2-dichlorocyclopropane Carboxylic Acid
items.abstract: A second-generation multikilogram synthesis of (1R,3R)-3-(3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl)-2,2-dichlorocyclopropane-1-carboxylic acid (1) is described, delivering improvements in efficiency, robustness, and scalability over the first-generation route. Key limitations, including high reagent costs, low-yielding single diastereomer purification, and multiple isolations, were addressed through substrate modification, reaction optimization, and strategic step sequence changes. Central to this process, reoptimization of the bis-arylative Heck coupling was achieved by replacing the acetate protecting group with a tert-butyldimethylsilyl group on the bis-allylic alcohol coupling partner, enabling an efficient transformation without a costly silver base and aryl iodide. Upstream improvements demonstrate an effective d-mannitol per-acylation reaction catalyzed by methanesulfonic acid and Zn-mediated elimination without using solvent quantities of AcOH. Finally, the two telescoped sequences minimized the number of unit operations and cycle time over the first-generation route. The nine-step process delivered 66 kg of 1 in 14% overall yield with >99% purity and up to 99.7% chiral purity.

items.title: Process Development for the Drug-Linker of Sacituzumab Tirumotecan
items.abstract: Herein are described the route scouting efforts and process development work for the drug-linker of the antibody–drug conjugate sacituzumab tirumotecan. The development of a scalable and robust process for this molecule necessitated the development of new workup and isolation techniques given the complex physical properties of the polyethylene glycol (PEG)-containing compounds and the inherent reactivity of these conjugatable molecules. Starting from the initial reported synthesis, the work described here resulted in a streamlined process that significantly reduced the number of potent compound handling steps, hazardous solvent usage, and, most notably, greatly improved overall throughput to ensure supply.

items.title: Nanofibrous Catalysts for Local Prodrug Activation through Bioorthogonal Uncaging Reactions
items.abstract: Bioorthogonal chemistry through implant-based catalysis provides powerful strategies for site-specific drug activation, enabling therapeutic control beyond what conventional systemic dosing or local delivery depots can achieve. In oncology, this approach is particularly compelling because dose-limiting systemic toxicity often prevents therapeutic drug exposure at the tumor, limiting treatment efficacy. Despite its promise, in vivo implementation remains limited by challenges such as catalyst instability, insufficient spatial confinement, and uncontrolled diffusion of activated drugs. This Perspective focuses on recent efforts to localize and sustain bioorthogonal uncaging reactions within living systems, with a particular emphasis on heterogeneous catalytic approaches. Building on advances that employ metallic nanoparticles as bioorthogonal catalysts, we highlight both their successes and the outstanding barriers associated with biofouling, catalyst leaching, and mass-transport constraints. Here we propose nanofibrous catalytic implants as an emerging platform for localized bioorthogonal chemistry. By integrating metallic nanocatalysts within nanofibrous implants, these systems can combine high surface area, efficient reactant transport, mechanical adaptability, and prolonged catalyst retention. We discuss fabrication strategies, key biological considerations, and future design principles that may guide the development of safer and more precise implant-based drug activation technologies.

items.title: ModBinddG as a Physics-Based Oracle: Training Drug Discovery AI Models with Little or No Experimental Data
items.abstract: AI models of drug–target binding affinity are limited by the scarcity of experimental data, particularly for novel or understudied targets. Here, we show that ModBinddG, a rapid molecular-simulation-based method for predicting absolute binding free energies, can serve as a physics-based oracle that generates synthetic affinity data accurate enough to train predictive AI models with little or no experimental data. First, we demonstrate across 16 diverse chemical series and 16 X-ray structures, with diverse protein conformations and binding modes, that ModBinddG predicts absolute binding free energies with a mean unsigned error of approximately 1 kcal/mol without per-series calibration. We then show that a target-specific AI model trained solely on ModBinddG predictions, using no experimental labels, accurately ranks the held-out experimental affinities. Extending this idea to general drug–target interaction (DTI) models, we introduce ModBindAL, an active-learning framework that uses ModBinddG as the oracle to iteratively augment a general DTI model (DeepConvDTI). Across three additional kinase targets, synthetic data augmentation improved test-set Pearson correlation for all three targets tested. Because two distinct AI architectures both benefit from the ModBinddG oracle, the accuracy of the synthetic data rather than any specific model appears to drive the improvement. In the course of this work, we identified and corrected substantial train/test contamination and a missing-negative-example issue in the CARA benchmark, establishing a fairer baseline for evaluation. Together, these results indicate that high-quality synthetic absolute binding affinity data from a physics-based oracle can build and improve AI models of drug–target affinity with minimal experimental data, with direct implications for all stages of early drug discovery.

items.title: Ancestors of Arylmalonate Decarboxylase Show Increased Activity, Stability, and Stereoselectivity
items.abstract: Bacterial arylmalonate decarboxylase (AMDase) generates a wide spectrum of α-chiral carboxylic acids in high optical purity, including several non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and chiral building blocks. However, extant AMDase from Bordetella bronchiseptica (BbAMDase) and related enzymes of the same family have three main limitations: (i) low operational and thermal stability, (ii) limited substrate spectrum regarding the size of the smaller substituent on the α-C-atom, and (iii) low stereoselectivity towards α-alkenyl-α-alkyl malonic acids. To address these limitations, we expanded the structural diversity of the AMDase family by ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR). The phylogenetic analysis of the decarboxylase revealed conserved structural in the hydrophobic active-site cavity, a catalytic motif crucial for activity and selectivity. AMDase ancestors showed higher stability, activity, and, in one case, also stereoselectivity than BbAMDase. While variation of amino acids of the hydrophobic pockets had increased activity and expanded substrate scope in previous work, this structural motif was found to be remarkably conserved throughout the reconstructed ancestors. The substrate scope of the ancestors towards a set of arylmalonic and alkenylmalonic acids was very similar to that of BbAMDase. Inversion of the stereoselectivity by switching the catalytic cysteine residues (G74C/C188G, numbering according to BbAMDase) was successful for ancestor N5, but reduced the activity of evolutionary more distant N131. This shows that a direct transfer of mutations between related enzymes might not be possible even if the active site cavities are conserved. Ancestor N131 exhibited a 294-fold improvement in half-life time and a 1.8-fold increased specific activity (25.1 U mg–1) toward 2-methyl-2-phenyl malonate in a preparative scale application. Computational analysis provided a potential explanation for improved stability by an increase in surface Glu side chains, which form a protective hydration shell that enhances solubility and mitigates aggregation. Ancestor N31 formed 2-methyl-but-3-enoic acid from its corresponding malonic acid in high optical purity (99.7% eeR).

items.title: Bio-based ionic liquids and deep eutectic solvents: emerging antimicrobials
items.abstract: The search for new antimicrobial agents has never been more urgent amid rising resistance to conventional treatments. Ionic liquids (ILs) and deep eutectic solvents (DESs) are highly tunable chemical systems with notable antimicrobial properties. Recent research indicates that bio-based variants of ILs/DESs, incorporating components derived from biological sources, exhibit selective antimicrobial activity. This review highlights recent advances in antimicrobial research on bio-based ILs/DESs, emphasizing structure–activity relationships and efficacy trends across Gram-positive, Gram-negative, and fungal pathogens. We provide comprehensive criteria for assessing the biocompatibility of ILs/DESs, including cytotoxicity and biodegradability. These developments underscore the potential of bio-based ILs/DESs as versatile antimicrobials and highlight the need for standardized toxicity screening, mechanistic assays, and data-driven design approaches to accelerate discovery.

items.title: Effective kinase-catalyzed biotinylation with ATP-biotin to monitor protein phosphorylation
Inhibitory molecules reveal functional regions beyond the active site in staphylococcal and mammaliicoccal exfoliative toxins
authors: Luís Eduardo de Almeida Passos Cerbino
items.abstract: Exfoliative toxins (ETs), produced by species of the genera Staphylococcus and Mammaliicoccus , are glutamyl endopeptidases (GEPs) with high specificity for desmoglein-1 (Dsg1), unlike the V8 protease from Staphylococcus aureus , which exhibits broad substrate specificity. Despite the clinical and veterinary relevance of ETs, the structural basis of this substrate specificity remains unclear, and no selective inhibitors are currently available; conventional active-site serine protease inhibitors, in particular, are ineffective against these toxins. Here, we show that secondary structural regions distinct from the catalytic site of ETs constitute potential targets for inhibition of their esterolytic activity. Suramin and heparin inhibited ETs, but not the V8 protease, and displayed biphasic dose–response profiles indicative of multiple ligand-binding events. Mutations in the necrosis-linked region of exfoliative toxin C (ExhC) from Mammaliicoccus sciuri and deletion of the L1 loop in exfoliative toxin E (ETE) from Staphylococcus aureus markedly reduced the inhibitory effects of both compounds. Molecular docking revealed preferential binding of both ligands to electropositive surfaces formed by these secondary structural regions. In contrast, the equivalent region in the V8 protease exhibited a predominantly negative electrostatic potential. Together, these findings identify non-catalytic structural regions as promising inhibitory hotspots for future inhibitor development and provide new insights into the structural basis of ET inhibition.

items.title: Discovery of ( R )- F22a : A Potent and Orally Bioavailable Benzofuran-Based Monoamine Reuptake Inhibitor Derived from Venlafaxine for Attentsion-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)
items.abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) remains a substantial clinical challenge, motivating the discovery of monoamine reuptake inhibitors with differentiated pharmacological properties. Herein, we describe the discovery and characterization of (R)-F22a, an orally bioavailable and brain-penetrant monoamine reuptake inhibitor optimized from the venlafaxine scaffold. (R)-F22a exhibited comparable inhibitory potency at the human norepinephrine transporter (hNET; IC50 = 113 nM) and the human serotonin transporter (hSERT; IC50 = 162 nM), with weaker activity at the human dopamine transporter (hDAT; IC50 = 1401 nM). In spontaneously hypertensive rats, (R)-F22a attenuated locomotor hyperactivity following both acute and repeated administration, whereas no significant change in spontaneous locomotor activity was detected in normotensive Wistar rats under the conditions tested. Repeated oral dosing of (R)-F22a for 14 days was generally tolerated, with no treatment-related mortality. Collectively, these findings support further preclinical evaluation of (R)-F22a.

items.title: Cascade-Responsive Supramolecular Porphyrin Nanoprodrugs for Mitochondrion-Targeted Photodynamic Chemotherapy
items.abstract: A cascade-responsive supramolecular porphyrin nanoprodrug (FP-SPN) was developed to combine mitochondrial photodynamic therapy (PDT) with reactive oxygen species (ROS)-activated chemotherapy (CT). FP-SPN was constructed through multivalent host−guest recognition between a tetra-azobenzene-functionalized porphyrin (TPP-Azo4) and cyclodextrin derivatives carrying folate (FA), triphenylphosphonium (PPh3), or thioketal-linked doxorubicin (DOX). The assembled nanoprodrug remained stable under physiological conditions, while the acid-sensitive linkage allowed PEG shedding in acidic environments, exposing the mitochondrial targeting group PPh3 and further facilitating mitochondrial localization. Upon 660 nm irradiation, the photosensitizer porphyrin generated ROS, which directly caused mitochondrial damage and cleaved the thioketal linker to release activated DOX. This supramolecular porphyrin nanoprodrug offers a practical approach to integrating multilevel cascade targeting, light-triggered drug release, and combined photodynamic chemotherapy.

items.title: Resolving Chlorine Sites in Pharmaceuticals by Integrated Site-Resolved Zeeman-Perturbed NQR, Solid-State NMR, and Electron Diffraction Crystallography
items.abstract: Many active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and high-value chemicals feature covalently bonded chlorine functionalities that influence molecular packing, stability, and bioavailability. However, site-resolved structural characterization of chlorine sites in powders remains challenging, especially in systems with multiple chemically or crystallographically nonequivalent sites, disorder, or hydration sensitivity. We report here a novel combined 35Cl nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR), 35Cl Zeeman-perturbed NQR (Zp-NQR), 35Cl solid-state NMR, and three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED/microcrystal electron diffraction) approach to characterizing powdered chlorine-bearing chemicals. Case studies of ketoconazole and chloramine-T demonstrate the utility of the approach in characterizing local structural heterogeneity and the hydration state. The role of crystal packing and noncovalent interactions on the spectroscopic observables is provided through an analysis of chlorzoxazone and five of its cocrystals, of which three are novel. Compared to ultrahigh-field NMR spectra alone, NQR and Zp-NQR spectra provide improved sensitivity to small changes in the electric field gradient and in the degree of disorder around chlorine. Experimental NQR/Zp-NQR data combined with gauge-including projector augmented-wave density functional theory (GIPAW-DFT) provide local structural constraints for a partially dehydrated chloramine-T phase. The refinement protocol does not require single crystals, and in the case of NQR experiments, intact tablets containing APIs are analyzed directly without further treatment or grinding. As a proof of principle, commercial tablets are shown to contain ketoconazole in the same crystalline form as that seen for the pure API. The general approach could be extended to other complex solids incorporating quadrupolar nuclei and is not limited to solid-form screening, polymorph identification, and differentiation of salts and cocrystals.

items.title: Discovery of PW82 as a Potent and Selective GSPT1 Molecular Glue Degrader for Acute Myeloid Leukemia
items.abstract: Targeted protein degradation is a promising therapeutic approach for acute myeloid leukemia (AML), but few GSPT1-targeting molecular glue degraders have advanced to clinical trials. CC-885 and its derivative CC-90009 demonstrate clinical potential, though CC-90009 suffered from poor oral exposure. MRT-2359, with improved bioavailability, is in trials for solid tumors. We report the structure-based optimization of CC-885, leading to PW82, a novel CRBN-recruiting GSPT1 degrader. PW82 induces potent and selective GSPT1 degradation without affecting canonical CRBN neosubstrates and displays superior antiproliferative activity across AML cell lines. It exhibits favorable oral exposure and, to our knowledge, is among the most potent and competitive GSPT1 degraders, with a balanced profile of potency, selectivity, and pharmacokinetics, including acceptable microsomal stability and plasma protein binding. PW82 overcomes venetoclax resistance and synergizes with azacitidine in vivo. Collectively, these findings highlight PW82 as a promising lead for AML therapy and support its continued preclinical development.

items.title: Endometrial Micro- and Nanoplastics Exposure and Recurrent Spontaneous Abortion: Evidence from a Human Study and Computational Toxicology
items.abstract: Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) are increasingly recognized as human environmental contaminants, but their polymer-specific relevance to uterine reproductive health remains unclear. We analyzed endometrial tissues from 82 reproductive-age women, including 43 with recurrent spontaneous abortion (RSA) and 39 controls, using laser direct infrared imaging, scanning electron microscopy, and pyrolysis-GC/MS. Endometrial MNPs were detected in nearly all samples, indicating widespread internal exposure at a clinically relevant reproductive site. Across Bayesian kernel machine regression, weighted quantile sum regression, and quantile g-computation, polypropylene (PP) and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) showed the most consistent positive associations with RSA status, with single-polymer odds ratios of 11.48 (95% CI, 2.02–66.38) and 5.04 (95% CI, 1.08–23.19), respectively. Multiaxis integration linked these polymer-specific signals to a 210-gene program enriched in an SPP1 + macrophage-decidual stromal niche. NEAT1, PPARG, S100A8, and GSDMD were retained as mechanistic candidates supported by distinct genetic, expression, or pathway evidence. Network perturbation prioritized GSDMD-PPARG interplay, and drug-repurposing analyses nominated metformin for preclinical evaluation. These observational and computational findings suggest that PP- and PVC-associated endometrial MNP burdens may mark RSA risk through inflammatory maternal–fetal-interface programs, warranting prospective, multicenter, and additive-resolved validation. These findings prioritize polymer-specific mechanisms at the maternal–fetal interface for testing in future reproductive health research.

items.title: Transition-Metal-Free Amination of Aryl Halides via Facile Aryne Generation
items.abstract: Despite continued advances in transition-metal-catalyzed amination of aryl halides, persistent challenges, including costly scale-up, sensitivity to steric hindrance, and catalyst poisoning by heteroaromatic rings, necessitate the development of metal-free alternatives. Aryne intermediates are an attractive option due to their high reactivity, yet facile aryne generation from aryl halides remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we disclose a transition-metal-free amination strategy for aryl halides that uses KHMDS with an 18-crown-6 additive, proceeding via aryne intermediates. The reactions use exclusively commercial reagents, proceed at room temperature, and achieve near “dump-and-stir” simplicity for reaction setup. The methodology is applicable to a wide range of aryl and heteroaryl halides with excellent chemoselectivity, including (S)-3,3′-dibromo-2,2′dimethoxy-BINOL and strongly Lewis basic substrates such as quinoline and pyrimidine that typically impede Pd-catalyzed aminations. Both primary and secondary amines participate, including sterically hindered 1-adamantylamine and diisopropylamine, providing a basis for preparative scale synthesis and evaluation of medicinally relevant aryl halides and amines.

items.title: Photoredox Decarboxylative Halogen Atom Transfer Strategy for C(sp2)–O/N Bond Construction
items.abstract: Indole-3-carboxylates and indole-3-amides are privileged scaffolds in drug discovery, yet their conventional synthesis often requires stoichiometric activating agents or metal catalysis. Herein, we report a metal-free, visible-light-driven photocatalytic decarboxylative acylation using 3-indolyl-α-keto acids as key intermediates. Under mild conditions, the reaction with alcohols or amines affords a diverse array of indole-3-carboxylates and amides in high efficiency and selectivity. The process proceeds via a decarboxylation/halogen-atom transfer/nucleophilic substitution cascade, employing alkyl halides as acyl cation surrogates without the need for hypervalent iodine reagents. Control experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the reaction is initiated by reductive quenching of the excited-state photocatalyst by the substrate and that halogen-atom transfer between the acyl radical and the alkyl halide is the preferred pathway to the key acyl bromide intermediate. This mild and operationally simple protocol offers a practical new approach for the late-stage introduction of indole-3-acyl units.

items.title: Stoichiometry-Informed Optimization of a Natural Product des -Formylflustrabromine (dFBr): Discovery of a Potent and Efficacious Positive Allosteric Modulator of α4β2 Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptor as a Preclinical Lead for Nicotine-Use-Disorder Pharmacotherapy
items.abstract: The α4β2 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (nAChR) is a key mediator of nicotine reinforcement and represents an important target for smoking-cessation therapeutics. Positive allosteric modulators (PAMs) enhance endogenous cholinergic signaling without directly activating the receptor and may offer advantages over orthosteric agonists. des-Formylflustrabromine (dFBr, 6a), the first reported selective α4β2 PAM, has been widely studied; however, the structural determinants governing activity, particularly across the two α4β2 receptor stoichiometrieshigh-sensitivity (HS; (α4)2(β2)3) and low-sensitivity (LS; (α4)3(β2)2)remain poorly understood. Here we report a stoichiometry-informed medicinal chemistry campaign exploring structure−activity relationships of the dFBr scaffold. Systematic modifications of the indole core and side-chain regions identified several derivatives with enhanced potentiation relative to dFBr (6a), including GAT1712, GAT1728, and GAT1739. Notably, GAT1728 showed excellent potentiation at HS (EC50 = 0.94 ± 0.17 μM) and LS receptors (EC50 = 0.25 ± 0.11 μM) and significantly reduced nicotine self-administration in mice without affecting noncontingent behavior.

items.title: End-to-End Continuous Flow Synthesis of a Bench-Stable Sulfamoylating Reagent: Application to the Preparation of a Key Edoxaban Intermediate
items.abstract: The N-Boc analogue of the Burgess reagent transfers a sulfamoyl group to amines and alcohols under mild conditions, and its use to install sulfamate and sulfamide motifs is well precedented on laboratory scale. Although these motifs occur in many active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), industrial use of the reagent is limited for two reasons: it is not amenable to storage, and its precursor, N-Boc-sulfamoyl chloride, is itself labile and forms in a strongly exothermic reaction. Herein, we report an efficient end-to-end continuous flow synthesis of the crystalline, bench-stable analogue N-(tert-butoxycarbonyl)-N-[4-(dimethylazaniumylidene)-1,4dihydropyridin-1-ylsulfonyl]azanide. In a two-stage tubular reactor system, the sulfamoyl chloride is generated at 0–5 °C and trapped in-line with DMAP within a total residence time of about 5 min, giving the product in 71% yield and 99.6% HPLC purity. The utility of the reagent in API synthesis was demonstrated in the batch preparation of an Edoxaban precursor, which in turn enabled a shorter route that uses the flow-generated sulfamoyl chloride directly.

items.title: Proton Relays Versus Direct Transfer in Polyketide Cyclisations: Solution Rejection, Bioinspired Complexes, and Enzyme-Pocket Rescue
items.abstract: Nature builds the polycyclic cores of tetracycline and aromatic polyketide antibiotics by folding linear polyketide chains through regioselective aldol and Claisen cyclisation cascades.Whether the proton transfers driving these cascades proceed by direct collision with a base or by hopping along hydrogen-bonded solvent wires (a Grotthuss proton relay) remains unresolved.Here we test when proton relays fail and when they prevail in a three-seed pilot diagnostic evaluation across 1,142 reaction paths spanning solution models, bioinspired complexes, and an enzyme active site.In unconstrained solution, a free base approaches the carbon acid to direct contact, making direct proton transfer outcompete multi-water wires whose assembly and charge separation impose an energetic cost.This outcome reverses once direct contact is blocked or the proton wire is preorganised.Screening three bioinspired levers shows that Grotthuss relays dominate when the base is held at least 5 Å from the carbon acid, when a bifunctional shuttle bridges donor and carbonyl oxygen simultaneously, or when the wire is preorganised on a rigid triol ring.Translating these rules into unconstrained, non-peptide catalysts reveals that chelating a diketone to MgCl 2 or ZnCl2 with a bulky pyridine base (2,6-di-tert-butyl-4-methylpyridine) keeps the base off the carbon acid, allowing a single bridging water to lower the median barrier (suggestive at three seeds).Finally, a 241-atom cluster of TcmN (PDB 3TVQ) confirms that the enzyme pocket blocks direct carbon-acid transfer to Asp57 unless bridged by a cavity water, while a two-water wire shuttles protons to His128.

items.title: Photothermal Nucleophilic Aromatic Substitution via a Traceless Carboxylate Directing Group
items.abstract: Intermolecular nucleophilic aromatic substitution remains challenging for arenes lacking strong electron-withdrawing groups. Here, we report a photothermal amination–decarboxylation strategy that uses an ortho-carboxylate as a traceless activating group. Under red-light irradiation, inexpensive carbon black enables amination of 2-bromobenzoic acids followed by decarboxylation, providing formal amination products of electronically neutral and electron-rich aryl bromides without transition-metal catalysis. The method accommodates primary aliphatic amines, anilines, and cyclic secondary amines, and its synthetic utility is demonstrated through preparative-scale synthesis and access to pharmaceutically relevant compounds. Competition experiments, substituent correlations, and density functional theory calculations support hydrogen-bond-assisted substitution and implicate steric constraints in the unusual preference for primary over secondary amines. Changing the leaving group from bromide to fluoride reverses this selectivity. Time-course measurements and reactions of a preformed intermediate support sequential substitution and decarboxylation. These findings establish a removable carboxylate activation strategy for extending intermolecular photothermal C–N bond formation beyond strongly activated electrophiles.

items.title: ADMET-Engine v2.0: Scaffold-Validated Multi-Modal Graph and QSAR Ensembling with Calibrated Epistemic Uncertainty, Applicability Domain Quantification, and Analytical Pharmacokinetics
items.abstract: Late-stage attrition in small-molecule drug discovery remains disproportionately driven by off-target cardiotoxicity—chiefly human ether-à-go-go-related gene (HERG/Kv11.1) potassium channel blockade—and hepatic cytochrome P450 3A4 (CYP3A4) drug–drug interactions. Although deep graph neural networks have proliferated in computational toxicology, deployed academic pipelines routinely suffer from four methodological failure modes: (i) random train/test partitioning that leaks congeneric chemical series across splits and inflates apparent ROC-AUC; (ii) uncalibrated raw neural logits misinterpreted as decision probabilities; (iii) absence of explicit applicability domain (AD) verification to warn medicinal chemists against out-of-distribution extrapolation; and (iv) disconnection from deterministic medicinal chemistry rules and structural alert filters. We present ADMET-Engine v2.0, an open-source computational medicinal chemistry framework trained on 16,270 unique standardized CHEMBL v37 compounds under a strict Bemis–Murcko scaffold split (8,252 unique core frameworks; zero core overlap across train, calibration-validation, and held-out test partitions). ADMET-Engine integrates four structurally heterogeneous model families—a Chemprop-grade 45-dimensional one-hot Directed Message-Passing Neural Network (DMPNN) with an O(E) reverse-edge indexing algorithm eliminat-ing O(N2) batch memory blowup, a residual ECFP4+physicochemical deep neural network, an ExtraTrees non-linear QSAR ensemble, and an L2-regularized logistic QSAR classifier—calibrated via validation-set temperature scaling and combined through convex negative log-likelihood optimization. On completely unseen core scaffolds (n = 1,627), the calibrated consensus ensemble achieves ROC-AUC = 0.7836 (PR-AUC = 0.8955, Brier = 0.1656, ECE = 0.0328) on HERG (n = 1,177) and ROC-AUC = 0.7664 (PR-AUC = 0.8506, Brier = 0.1875, ECE = 0.0541) on CYP3A4 (n = 516), improving by +0.216 ROC-AUC over the prior unscaled scalar-feature baseline. Every inference further computes sub-millisecond bit-packed ECFP4 Tanimoto applicability domain diagnostics, weighted epistemic uncertainty (σepi), exact analytical BOILED-EGG gastrointestinal and blood–brain barrier permeation, QED, Fsp3, Pfizer 3/75 promiscuity, and PAINS/BRENK toxicophore atom highlighting on 2D structures.

items.title: Solid-Phase Total Synthesis of Wewakazole B
items.abstract: Wewakazole B is a cytotoxic cyclododecapeptide isolated from the marine cyanobacterium Moorea producens, containing three embedded oxazole heterocycles derived from serine and threonine residues. Reported total syntheses of Wewakazole B rely exclusively on solution-phase strategies, which are stepintensive and poorly suited to modular analogue generation. Here we report a solid-phase peptide synthesis route to Wewakazole B enabled by custom Fmoc-protected oxazole and methyloxazole amino acid building blocks. These heterocyclic residues were prepared through a modular dipeptide-based route employing DAST-mediated cyclodehydration followed by oxidative aromatization. The building blocks were incorporated directly into Fmoc-SPPS using a combination of automated and manual coupling, avoiding late-stage heterocycle installation. Macrocyclization of the resulting linear precursor, followed by purification via normal-phase chromatography afforded Wewakazole B in 20% overall yield. To our knowledge, this represents the first solid-phase total synthesis of Wewakazole B and establishes a generalizable, building-block-based platform for the synthesis of oxazole-rich cyclic peptides and their structurally defined analogues.

items.title: Why Applicability Domains Pass Conventional Validation: Close-Neighbour Provenance
items.abstract: Chemists judge a QSAR prediction by asking whether the molecule resembles the training data. This check is the applicability domain (AD), usually the similarity to the nearest training molecule, and the OECD lists it as a validation principle. We asked whether it still flags bad predictions when the test molecules come from papers the model has never seen. We used 39 ChEMBL targets and three model families. The AUC for flagging errors above one log unit falls from 0.664 with scaffold-disjoint splits to 0.568 when publications are withheld. It falls to 0.494 on future publications. The main cause is where close neighbours come from. In the standard test 55% of molecules have a close training neighbour from their own paper and only 9% have one from another paper. A Butina-0.4 cluster holdout leaves those neighbours in place and the AD does not change. Removing the neighbours, or removing the papers, makes it collapse. The failure is sharper for the pass/fail gate practitioners actually deploy. A permissive 0.35 cutoff separates errors in the standard test (0.144 inside against 0.408 outside) and not on withheld papers (0.372 against 0.362). We also calibrated a cutoff honestly, on a publication-disjoint split. A cutoff promising 15% error cannot be found at all in 7 to 13 of 20 splits. Where it exists it admits 2.3% or fewer of the molecules at about 2 times the promised error. Six similarity metrics and three model-based uncertainty scores all degrade in the same direction. We give a cutoff sweep and a one-number diagnostic. The diagnostic is the share of validation molecules with a close neighbour from a different paper, which is 9% here. It flags validation sets that cannot test reliability on new publications.

items.title: Automated Radiosynthesis, Preclinical Validation, and First-in-Human PET Evaluation of the SSTR2 Antagonist [18F]AlF-NOTA-Asp2-PEG2-JR11
items.abstract: Somatostatin receptor subtype 2 (SSTR2) antagonists are promising for tumor PET/CT, but reducing liver and kidney uptake without compromising tumor targeting and enabling scalable fluorine-18 radiotracer production remain important goals. We developed [18F]AlF-NOTA-Asp2-PEG2-JR11 and evaluated its preclinical properties and first-in-human PET/CT performance. Automated radiosynthesis required approximately 40 min and achieved >98% radiochemical purity. Compared with [18F]AlF-NOTA-JR11, the modified tracer showed higher AR42J cellular uptake and greater xenograft tumor uptake through 120 min. Competitive blocking reduced xenograft uptake by >90%, supporting SSTR2-specific targeting. In 10 participants, no adverse events were observed; imaging showed predominantly renal clearance and an effective dose of 0.0137 ± 0.0017 mSv/MBq. Uptake in 29 lesions from six participants was sustained between 60 and 120 min. Paired [18F]FDG imaging revealed heterogeneous uptake patterns, whereas available biopsies suggested qualitative PET-SSTR2 concordance. These findings support further clinical evaluation of this SSTR2-targeted tracer.

items.title: Inflammation-Programmed Tumor Endothelium Enables Active Nanoparticle Transport for Enhanced Cancer Therapy
items.abstract: Efficient delivery of nanotherapeutics to solid tumors remains limited by the tumor endothelial barrier, but it is unknown how tumor vasculature regulates the transport of nanotherapeutics compared to healthy vasculature. Here, we identify an inflammation-associated tumor vascular phenotype that enables nanoparticle transport across endothelium. Using intravital microscopy, we showed that inflammatory tumor microenvironments reduced the glycocalyx coverage on endothelial vasculature and exposed intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1), thereby promoting active nanoparticle–endothelium interactions and transendothelial transport. Low-dose X-ray radiation to tumors at 6 Gy further amplified this vascular phenotype. Guided by these insights, we engineered high-drug-content paclitaxel nanocrystals functionalized with anti-ICAM-1 antibodies and demonstrated that combining endothelial-targeted paclitaxel nanocrystals with low-dose radiation significantly enhanced tumoral drug delivery and antitumor efficacy. This work reveals tumor endothelium as a programmable biological interface for nanotherapeutic transport and establishes vascular targeting as a strategy to overcome drug delivery barriers for cancer therapies.

items.title: Programmable Deaminative Functionalization enabled by Nitrate Anion
items.abstract: Aliphatic amines constitute a vast reservoir of molecular diversity, yet their potential for deaminative functionalization remains largely untapped. Harnessing this resource requires cleaving stable C–N bonds without sacrificing molecular architecture or sensitive functionalities. Here, nitrate-enabled deamination unlocks the direct conversion of complex amines into chlorides for divergent functionalization, extending the synthetic reach beyond the constraints of conventional diazonium chemistry. Our platform transforms valuable bioactive amines into electrophilic linchpins for carbon–heteroatom and carbon–carbon bond formation, with nucleophilic substitutions proceeding without intermediate isolation. The mild conditions preserve acid-sensitive functionalities, including acetals and Boc-protected amines, and accommodate complex molecules and FDA-approved drugs. Gram-scale synthesis and parallel diversification establish the preparative utility and downstream versatility of the platform both in academic and industrial settings.

items.title: DESIGN AND SYNTHESIS OF PYRROLO[2,3-D]PYRIMIDINES AND THIENO[2,3-D]PYRIMIDINES BEARING A 5-(PIPERAZIN-1-YLSULFONYL)-1,3-OXAZOLE-4-CARBONITRILE MOIETY
items.abstract: The structural modification of biologically relevant heterocyclic scaffolds through the incorporation of sulfonamide-containing fragments represents a promising strategy for the development of novel drug-like compounds.Fused pyrimidine systems, particularly pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidines and thieno[2,3-d]pyrimidines, are of considerable interest due to the broad spectrum of biological activities exhibited by their derivatives and their potential as promising molecular scaffolds for the development of novel therapeutic agents.In this study, synthetic approaches to nine novel heterocyclic compounds combining pyrrolopyrimidine or thienopyrimidine scaffolds with a 1,3-oxazole-4-carbonitrile moiety via a sulfonylpiperazine linker were investigated.In silico ADMET predictions were performed for all compounds, and their drug-likeness properties were evaluated.The five thienopyrimidines 3a-3e were isolated in 82-92% yield and the four pyrrolopyrimidines 5a-5d in 76-86% yield.The latter series had higher predicted lipophilicity and lower predicted aqueous solubility.All nine compounds were predicted to be CYP3A4 substrates and CYP2C9 inhibitors.Compounds 5c and 5d lacked a hepatotoxicity alert but retained a predicted hERG II liability.These findings identify solubility and safety endpoints for experimental follow-up.

items.title: A pre-registered protocol for interpreting docking scores in generative molecular design
items.abstract: Generative molecular design has defaulted to docking score as a proxy for binding quality, however the capacity of the harness used to separate binders from non-binders on a specific target of interest is rarely verified. A survey of 32 papers between 2023 and 2026 found that such upfront validation is the exception rather than the standard. In this paper, we set out a protocol to validate the harness using a cohort of measured actives and property matched but topologically dissimilar decoys, through the identical configuration later applied to the generative models and a baseline, with pass and fail criteria registered publicly before that run. This procedure was performed on DYRK1A, using 1,219 actives, 60,950 property-matched decoys and 382 compounds of measured weak or inactive potency. The harness cleared its pre-registered ROC AUC floor (0.658 vs. 0.650) but enrichment at 1% came in at 3.12, missing its target of 5.00, and scores tracked closely with heavy atom count (ρ = −0.729). After the validation, an equal-budget comparison was run across four arms: a property-matched baseline, a target-agnostic SMILES-LSTM, a sequence-conditioned model, and a pocket-conditioned model. The pocket-conditioned model had the best raw median score (−10.39 vs. −9.07 for the baseline) but yielded the worst ligand efficiency of every arm, alongside the worst drug-likeness, the highest compute cost, and the molecules least similar to the active cohort in their chemical properties. Normalising for size, no model was able to outperform a random baseline draw. A docking score presented without proper harness validation cannot be interpreted, and ligand efficiency deserves a place beside every raw score.

items.title: Zirconium-Enabled Chain-Walking SH2: Quaternary Carbons from Olefins and Carboxylic Acids
items.abstract: Hindered quaternary centers are ubiquitous in natural products and impart favorable properties to potential drug candidates. Installation of these motifs is often challenging, although recent advances in bimolecular SH2 cross-coupling have streamlined their synthesis. The use of feedstock terminal and internal olefins as 1º radical precursors for SH2 cross-coupling would greatly increase the accessible three-dimensional chemical space, but this strategy has remained underexplored. Here, we report the selective coupling of 1º radicals, generated with Schwartz’s reagent from internal and terminal olefins, with 2º and 3º radicals derived from N-hydroxyphthalimide (NHPI) esters. The reaction exhibits broad substrate scope, notably tolerating oxidatively labile functional groups that are traditionally problematic in photoredox catalysis. We further demonstrate synthetic utility in the late-stage functionalization of bioactive molecules. Finally, we highlight two potential applications for linker-length screening in the context of PROTAC drug candidates.

items.title: Direct-to-Biology Bifunctional Screening Reveals Noncanonical Mechanisms of Targeted Protein Degradation
items.abstract: Targeted protein degradation (TPD) has emerged as a powerful strategy for modulating protein function through small-molecule-induced proximity between a protein of interest (POI) and typically an E3 ubiquitin ligase to promote its proteasomal degradation. Despite significant progress, most degraders co-opt a narrow set of E3 ubiquitin ligases, motivating mechanistically agnostic strategies for discovering new routes to degradation. Here, we pursued a “degrader-first” approach using direct-to-biology (D2B) synthesis to construct and screen a 114-member library of BRD4-targeting bifunctional molecules to identify chemically tractable ligases that support TPD. Multiple compounds were found to induce Cullin-RING ligase (CRL)-dependent degradation, and two top hits were selected for mechanistic characterization. Unexpectedly, neither operates through canonical heterobifunctional E3 recruitment. Instead, one undergoes oxidative activation to generate a reactive electrophile that promotes degradation through DCAF11- or DCAF16-containing CRL4 complexes in a cell-context-dependent manner. The second acts through a bivalent bromodomain-binding mechanism that likely induces target conformational contraction and potentiates endogenous CRL3–SPOP-mediated ubiquitination. These findings highlight the capacity of D2B discovery approaches to expose noncanonical modalities of TPD while underscoring the importance of rigorous mechanistic deconvolution in interpreting screening-derived degraders.

items.title: Novel Phytochemical Conjugate Disrupts Tubulin Dynamics and Induces Mitochondrial Apoptosis To Suppress Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
items.abstract: Microtubule-targeting agents remain the most effective chemotherapeutics for triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). However, their clinical utility is frequently limited because of the emergence of systemic toxicity and drug resistance. To address these challenges, a novel series of 1,2,3-triazole-linked chalcone-phytophenolic acid hybrids (7a–o) has been designed and synthesized by integrating three pharmacologically active scaffolds into a single molecular framework. Among 15 synthesized analogues, compound 7i emerged as the lead candidate, exhibiting selective low-micromolar cytotoxicity against TNBC cells while demonstrating substantially lower toxicity toward normal cells. Mechanistic studies revealed that compound 7i targeted tubulin by binding to the colchicine-binding pocket, thereby disrupting microtubule dynamics, promoting abnormal tubulin aggregation, and leading to G2/M cell cycle arrest. This disruption initiated a cascade of intracellular events characterized by excessive intracellular and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species generation, mitochondrial membrane depolarization, activation of the Bax/Bcl-2/caspase-3 apoptotic pathway, PARP cleavage, and DNA fragmentation, ultimately leading to mitochondrion-mediated apoptosis. Consistent with these mechanistic findings, compound 7i significantly suppressed tumor growth in an orthotopic 4T1 mouse model while exhibiting a minimal systemic toxicity. Altogether, these findings identify the novel compound 7i as a promising tubulin-targeting triazole-chalcone-phytophenolic acid hybrid with potent and selective anticancer activity.

items.title: Defining a Surface ζ-Potential Window for Optimal Lymphatic Trafficking and Immunization of Liposomal Vaccines
items.abstract: How surface ζ-potential governs nanocarrier trafficking from the skin to draining lymph nodes (LNs) remains unresolved in vaccine delivery. Herein, we have constructed a library of 31 liposomal formulations spanning approximately +41 mV to −60 mV and screened the lymphatic drainage efficiency in vivo. The screen revealed a nonmonotonic relationship: LN accumulation was not monotonically linked to ζ-potential but concentrated within an optimal fitted window of −2.73 mV to −25.43 mV. Guided by this window, we designed four anionic lipids and formulated liposomes within the high-efficiency range. These formulations independently reproduced the predicted drainage window. Mechanistically, strongly negatively charged liposomes (<−30 mV) were physically trapped by the subcutaneous collagen fibers network, whereas weakly negative liposomes exploited transcellular transport mediated by lymphatic endothelial cells. Using the optimal ζ-potential, we coloaded the Axl receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor R428 with tumor antigens to develop a cancer vaccine that dramatically enhanced antigen delivery, elicited potent CD8+ T cell responses, and significantly suppressed prostate tumor growth. These findings establish surface ζ-potential as a fundamental design parameter for LN-targeted liposomal vaccines.

items.title: NMR Reveals Coupled Ligand and Protein Conformational Equilibria That Modulate the Affinity of MDM2-Inhibitory Peptoids
items.abstract: Peptoids, atypical peptides with N-substitutions, are a promising drug modality for targeting protein–protein interactions. The binding affinity of an MDM2-inhibitory peptoid decreases by more than 100-fold upon removal of the backbone-restricting methyl groups attached to the α-carbons, although this modification alters the population of the all-trans amide-bond isomer by only 1.6-fold. This discrepancy raises the possibility that backbone flexibility affects not only ligand preorganization but also the conformational ensemble of the target protein. Here, we used NMR to examine the binding mode of the MDM2-peptoid complexes. ZZ-exchange experiments demonstrated that peptoid isomers containing cis amide bonds bind less favorably to MDM2 than the all-trans amide bond isomer. In addition, observation of the I19 δ1-methyl resonance of MDM2 in complex with the peptoids revealed that MDM2 exists in equilibrium between an open state, corresponding to the crystal structure of the MDM2-peptoid complex, and a semiclosed state, which retains partial interactions between the N-terminal region of MDM2 and the ligand-binding cleft. Increased population of the semiclosed state correlated with reduced binding affinities of the peptoids. We propose that cis-trans isomerization of the peptoid amide bonds and the conformational equilibrium of MDM2 within the peptoid complex synergistically contribute to the more than 100-fold decrease in binding affinity. These results identify coupled ligand and protein conformational equilibria as determinants of binding affinity and suggest conformational-plasticity control as a potential design principle for oligomeric ligands targeting protein–protein interactions.

items.title: Nitrate, not virus: reinterpreting salivary Raman signatures of COVID-19 and neurodegeneration
items.abstract: Raman spectroscopy of dried saliva has been proposed as a rapid test for COVID-19, Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease, with classifiers reaching areas under the curve (AUC) near 0.9 or higher. We reanalysed the public spectra behind these reports: 70 participants with Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease or no neurological disease, and 101 participants with active, past or no SARS-CoV-2 infection. Two features of the data shape every comparison. The two cohorts share 33 control participants, and diagnosis is nearly aliased with acquisition session: Parkinson's patients and controls never appear in the same session. The band at 1048 cm-1, previously assigned to protein and to tryptophan-rich viral regions, behaves as an isolated spectral component consistent with the symmetric stretch of nitrate. In a mixed model with session as a random effect, the nitrate-to-protein ratio was about four-fold higher in active COVID-19, in patients who had recovered and tested negative twice, and in Alzheimer's disease. Within the one session shared by patients and controls, raw nitrate intensity was 2.6-fold higher in patients (AUC 0.81, 95% CI 0.62–0.95) while protein bands did not fall. Nitrate did not separate active from past infection (AUC 0.50) or Alzheimer's disease from COVID-19, and the effect held across integration windows, baseline orders and normalisations. Spike-in simulations in real control spectra reproduced the observed nitrate discrimination but accounted for only part of the full-spectrum performance, and calibration offsets of the observed size were undetectable. The Parkinson's classifier had no chemical counterpart. In these cohorts, salivary Raman signatures report a shared, non-specific rise in salivary nitrate, plausibly linked to hospital care, rather than a diseasespecific fingerprint.

items.title: Anticancer Activity of New K858 Δ2‐1,3,4‐Thiadiazoline Analogs on Breast Cancer
items.abstract: Here we describe the synthesis and anticancer activity of chloro‐, dichloro‐, and nitro‐substituted racemic Δ 2 ‐1,3,4‐thiadiazoline derivatives (TDZ1–4) related to K858, a known inhibitor of the mitotic kinesin Eg5 (also called kinesin spindle protein, KSP, or KIF11). The compounds were evaluated against two hormone‐dependent breast cancer cell lines, human MCF‐7 and mouse LM05‐Mix, using K858 as the reference compound. All compounds were active, and the dichloro derivatives TDZ1 and TDZ3 showed comparable or improved potency relative to K858, with low toxicity toward nontumorigenic MCF‐10A cells. TDZ1 and TDZ3 induced apoptosis, G2/M cell cycle arrest and monopolar spindle formation, a phenotype compatible with Eg5 inhibition. Complexes between each compound and Eg5 (bound to Mg 2+ and adenosine diphosphate, ADP) were modeled by molecular docking and molecular dynamics, considering both enantiomers. These studies do not support a single enantiomer as the sole contributor to binding, suggesting that both enantiomers may contribute to the anticancer activity.

items.title: Regioselective C‐4 Benzylation of 5‐Aminopyrazoles With p‐Quinone Methides for Preparing Unsymmetrical Triarylmethanes and Their Evaluation as Antiplasmodial Agents
items.abstract: A Sc(OTf) 3 ‐mediated, regioselective C‐4 benzylation of 5‐aminopyrazoles with para ‐quinone methides is reported as an efficient strategy for the synthesis of unsymmetrical triarylmethanes. Most of the synthesized compounds were evaluated for their antiplasmodial activity. Two of the compounds 3ab and 3ai exhibited promising, concentration‐dependent antiplasmodial activity, while in vivo evaluation of 3ai significantly prolonged the mean survival time of infected animals.

items.title: Graded, not all-or-none: single-cell Raman reveals antifungal suppression in Candida
items.abstract: Heavy-water (D2O) labelling with single-cell Raman spectroscopy is becoming a basis for rapid antifungal susceptibility testing, but its read-outs are usually population means or the share of cells above a cut-off. Neither can tell whether a drug slows every cell (graded suppression) or stops some cells while others continue (all-or-none suppression). We reanalysed 10,348 public single-cell spectra from eight Candida strains exposed to amphotericin B (AmB), flucytosine (5-FC), micafungin (MCF) and voriconazole (VOR). Two-state mixtures anchored to unlabelled cells were fitted to the C–D label distributions, and graded, switch, free and null dose-series models were compared by BIC. The graded model was preferred for 15 of 27 series, including 5-FC in all five tested strains; across five robustness variants only one graded series moved clearly to a model with off cells. Coexisting off and labelled cells at one dose were robust only for AmB in C. glabrata 368 and MCF in C. krusei.
