In simulations built from the observed cells, a cut-off classifier reported a uniformly dimmed population at 20 % of control as 20 % “active” cells, whereas the mixture recovered the fully labelled population; a fully active minority of 5 % was detected in 88–98 % of simulated datasets. Label build-up saturated within the assay window (k = 0.37–0.58 h 1), so end-point labels understate rate - suppression. Distribution-level analysis, rather than cut-offs, is needed before Raman read-outs are interpreted as numbers of active or tolerant cells.

items.title: Diversified Synthesis of Nonclassical C‐Glycosides Through Cooperative N‑Heterocyclic Carbene and Photoredox Catalytic Acylation
items.abstract: C ‐Glycosides have attracted sustained interest because of their exceptional metabolic stability and diverse biological activities; nevertheless, they remain far less explored than their O ‐ and N ‐glycoside counterparts. In particular, the diversified synthesis of nonclassical C ‐glycosides constitutes an even more formidable challenge in synthetic chemistry. Herein, we report an N ‐heterocyclic carbene (NHC)/photoredox dual‐catalytic strategy that installs proximal and remote acyl groups at non‐anomeric positions of saccharides, delivering structurally unique nonclassical C ‐glycosides. The installed acyl groups function as versatile synthetic linchpins that can be readily converted into various aglycone functionalities, including alkenyl, hydroxyalkyl, and allyl groups. This protocol facilitates the diversity‐oriented synthesis of several medicinally interesting C ‐glycosides, including indole‐ and quinoline‐containing C ‐glycosides, as well as ribosyl Z‐/E‐ tamoxifen analogues. Preliminary mechanistic studies, including control experiments and photochemical investigations, support a radical catalytic manifold. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further rationalize the high stereoselectivity observed in the glycosylation steps of the two‐component and three‐component reactions, respectively.

items.title: Hypoxia-Driven, Self-Accelerating Immolative Photosensitizer Enabling Effective and Safe Photodynamic Therapy
items.abstract: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is an emerging cancer treatment modality, but its clinical translation is hindered by the persistent post-PDT phototoxicity of existing photosensitizers. To address this challenge, we herein report a hypoxia-driven, self-accelerating immolative photosensitizer in which PDT itself drives posttherapy detoxification. This is demonstrated with AIE photosensitizers with an N-oxidation-mediated photoinduced electron transfer (PET) feature, which creates a charge-separation state with pronounced electron–nuclear hyperfine coupling feature, enabling efficient intersystem crossing. This N-oxidation thus converts the highly emissive fluorophore TBP into the robust type I photosensitizer TBPO. Critically, the N-O bond could be selectively cleaved by cytochrome P450 reductases under hypoxia, immolating TBPO back to TBP. Unlike previously reported ROS-driven immolative photosensitizers, this hypoxia-mediated immolation does not consume therapeutic ROS and is accelerated by PDT-aggravated hypoxia. Consequently, TBPO exhibits a self-propelled detoxification mechanism, ensuring an initial high PDT efficacy while minimizing residual phototoxicity after therapy. Moreover, this transition process is self-reported by the fluorescence light-up. This molecular design achieves both potent hypoxia-resistant PDT and fail-safe posttreatment safety, addressing two long-standing barriers to clinical PDT. This paradigm shift offers a general design principle for therapy-fueled self-detoxifying photosensitizers toward outpatient PDT without lifestyle restrictions.

items.title: Legumain identified as a direct binding protein of Rhein through PROTAC-integrated chemical proteomics
Design and synthesis of neamine–linezolid and neamine–ciprofloxacin conjugates intended as amphiphilic hybrid antibiotics: unexpected loss of activity and structure–activity insights
Substrate Promiscuity of an Acetyltransferase Drives Euphorbia Diterpenoid Diversity in Petty Spurge
items.abstract: Acylated diterpenoids from Euphorbia species are bioactive natural products with multidrug resistance reversal and anticancer effects. Their biological profiles are strongly shaped by regioselective acylation, yet the enzymatic logic that installs multiple acetyl groups on structurally divergent diterpenoid scaffolds has remained poorly understood. Here, by integrating tissue-specific transcriptomics, phylogenetic analysis, and functional screening, we identify Ep17169 from Euphorbia peplus as a clade 3 BAHD acetyltransferase that accepts both macrocyclic jatrophane and polycyclic ingenane scaffolds as substrates. Biochemical and computational analyses reveal that Ep17169 displays scaffold-dependent regiodivergent acetylation, favoring C7-OH acetylation on a jatrophane substrate while preferentially acetylating the C20-OH of ingenol. Time-course experiments reveal sequential acetylation with position-dependent rates and are consistent with a spontaneous C3-to-C5 acetyl migration within the ingenane framework. Cavity engineering using ingenol (4) as the substrate yields C20-selective monoacetyltransferase variants (N388F and G390F) with WT-comparable activity (31–35% conversion). Its multifaceted activity—dual-scaffold recognition, regiodivergent acetylation, sequential catalysis, and the demonstrated engineerability of its ingenane-binding pocket—makes Ep17169 a promising starting point for the biocatalytic diversification of pharmacologically relevant diterpenoids. Collectively, our findings reveal how distal cavity residues control substrate reorientation to govern the trade-off between catalytic promiscuity and strict regioselectivity, providing a structural design logic that can potentially be explored beyond the Euphorbia system.

items.title: Quinazolinone ring-opening enables development of aminobenzamide HDAC6 inhibitors with reduced HDAC8 affinity
items.abstract: Quinazolinone ring opening yielded aminobenzamide derivatives with potent and selective HDAC6 inhibition (relative to HDAC8), demonstrating antiproliferative activity against breast cancer cells and enhanced efficacy in combination with bortezomib.

items.title: Nanotechnology Meets Brain Diseases: Emerging Therapeutic Strategies for Drug Delivery
items.abstract: Brain diseases, encompassing neurodegenerative disorders, cerebrovascular diseases, and brain tumors, impose a profound global health burden. Conventional therapeutic strategies often fail due to the formidable blood–brain barrier (BBB) and complex pathological microenvironment of the central nervous system (CNS). The rapid evolution of nanotechnology offers unprecedented opportunities to overcome these delivery hurdles. This review comprehensively summarizes recent developments in engineered nanoplatforms for the diagnosis and targeted therapy of brain diseases. It first outlines the pathological characteristics and nanoprobe-enhanced diagnostic methods for various brain disorders, followed by a critical evaluation of five major classes of nanocarriers for CNS drug delivery: lipid-based, polymeric, inorganic, bio-derived, and hybrid nanocarriers. This evaluation highlights their structural attributes and delivery efficiencies. The discussion then examines advanced strategies to improve delivery precision, including multilevel targeting (e.g., BBB penetration and specific cell targeting), stimuli-responsive theranostics, and functional surface modifications. Linking these nanotechnological innovations to specific neurological diseases highlights their clinical potential. Finally, the review addresses current translational challenges, including biosafety, scalable manufacturing, and interindividual variability, and offers a forward-looking perspective on the rational design of next-generation precision neuro-nanomedicines.

items.title: pH-Triggered Contractile Dendritic-Cell-Decorated DNA Hydrogel for Efficient In Situ Tumor Cell Restriction and Immune Activation
items.abstract: The extracellular matrix (ECM) and immune system serve as critical barriers against tumor metastasis. However, in the complex tumor microenvironment (TME), the ECM exerts an immunosuppressive effect and its degradation synergistically facilitates tumor metastasis. Simultaneously regulating the ECM structure and eliciting a robust immune response remains a major challenge. Herein, we develop an intelligent DNA hydrogel (CDDTG) embedded with “C”-motif sequences that undergoes acid-triggered contraction via formation of i-motif structures. Upon peritumoral injection, the contracted CDDTG hydrogel can form a dense physical barrier that tightly wraps around tumor spheroids, enabling in situ tumor cell trapping and restriction. Concurrently, the hydrogel releases endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-targeting tetrahedral DNA (FAL-Td@GOx) loaded with glucose oxidase (GOx). GOx catalyzes glucose oxidation to gluconic acid, further acidifying the TME and reinforcing hydrogel contraction while generating hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) within the ER. This ER-targeted ROS production depletes intracellular glucose, triggers ER stress, and induces immunogenic cell death (ICD) in tumor cells. The resulting ICD promotes exogenous dendritic-cell (DC) activation and amplifies antitumor T-cell responses, thereby reversing immunosuppression. By synergistically combining a mechanically retractable physical barrier with ER stress-driven immunotherapy, CDDTG hydrogel effectively suppresses tumor cell migration and invasion in vitro and potently inhibits lung and bone metastasis in vivo. This work establishes a smart artificial ECM platform that integrates physical cell restriction with immune activation, thereby offering a promising strategy for antimetastatic therapy.

items.title: Hepatocyte-Selective Targeted Degradation of Proteins Across Compartments
items.abstract: Targeted protein degradation represents an emerging therapeutic strategy for a wide range of diseases. However, current approaches often face limitations in terms of internalization efficiency, cell-type selectivity, and generality. To date, a universal platform for efficient degradation of diverse targets spanning the intracellular, membrane-associated, and extracellular spaces remains yet established. Here, we develop disulfide-induced selective chimeras (DISCs)─a versatile class of degraders composed of nanobodies conjugated to N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc)-functionalized polydisulfides (PDS). DISCs combine hepatocyte-specific targeting, dual internalization routes, and broad substrate versatility across protein localizations. Their mechanism of action leverages the synergistic effects of GalNAc-mediated asialoglycoprotein receptor (ASGPR) targeting and endocytosis, thiol–disulfide exchange-driven cellular uptake facilitated by PDS, and NPGY peptide-mediated lysosomal sorting. DISCs effectively degrade membrane proteins, including human epidermal growth factor receptor-2 (HER2) and protein tyrosine kinase 7 (PTK7), in hepatocytes, resulting in potent inhibition of cancer cell proliferation. Furthermore, we extend the application of DISCs to extracellular proteins by demonstrating efficient degradation of proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9), which leads to upregulated hepatic low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR) expression with enhanced low-density lipoprotein-cholesterol (LDL-C) clearance in vitro and in an exogenous acute hyperlipidemia mouse model (C57BL/6J). Additionally, the DISC platform is readily adaptable to intracellular targets, such as kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene homologue (KRAS). DISCs represent a versatile and modular platform for targeted degradation of proteins with diverse locations─whether membrane-bound, extracellular, or intracellular─with precise hepatocyte specificity, highlighting substantial therapeutic potential.

items.title: LICA: A Multiview Relation-Aware Equivariant Graph Neural Network with Interfacial Atomic-Pair Attention for Protein–Ligand Binding Affinity Prediction
items.abstract: Accurate prediction of protein–ligand binding affinity is foundational in structure-based drug design, yet existing 3D graph models often mix heterogeneous chemical relations and dilute sparse interfacial signals through global pooling. We present LICA, a relation-aware equivariant graph neural network that explicitly distinguishes covalent, spatial, and interfacial contacts on a unified 3D graph. A multiview readout extracts complementary information from the ligand, the pocket, and explicit interfacial atom pairs. Trained under a leakage-controlled Tanimoto split and tested independently on CASF-2016, LICA shows that prediction errors concentrate in sparsely sampled extreme-affinity regions, exhibiting a regression-to-the-mean extrapolation bottleneck. Ablation studies demonstrate that the explicit interfacial atom-pair attention provides a meaningful geometric inductive bias rather than merely adding parameters. This bias is particularly effective for spatially directional interactions, such as cation−π contacts. Using structural annotations as a reference, we further show that the learned interface attention highly overlaps with true short-range contacts. However, case studies reveal that these attention weights serve as a qualitative map of physical interactions and should not be interpreted as a quantitative decomposition of binding free energy. Overall, explicit interface pairing improves affinity regression while yielding a chemically verifiable representation of protein–ligand interactions.

items.title: Identification of Active Small Molecules Targeting the Endopeptidase RipA from Mycobacterium tuberculosis
authors: Nathalya Cristina de Moraes Roso Mesquita
items.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis relies on tightly regulated peptidoglycan remodelling to maintain cell wall integrity during growth, division, and infection. The endopeptidase RipA is essential for daughter cell separation and has been implicated in pathogenicity and reactivation from dormancy, emerging as a promising tuberculosis drug target. Using a fragment-based drug discovery approach, we identified novel RipA-binding molecules as starting points for drug design. Orthogonal biophysical methods confirmed the interaction of nine fragments with RipA. Structural clustering revealed two main chemotypes: tetrahydropyran rings and flat rings or heterocycles. Functional assays showed that some fragments inhibited RipA enzymatic activity, while others enhanced it, perhaps by mimicking the RipA/RpfB synergistic complex. Two molecules also displayed inhibitory activity against reference strains of the M. tuberculosis complex. Flow cytometry and TEM analyses indicated that morphological alterations may be associated with RipA disruption. Collectively, our findings provide insights into RipA-ligand interactions and identify promising scaffolds for developing new anti-tuberculosis agents.

items.title: Mechanistic Insights into Ni(I)–Isocyanide Catalyzed Cross-Coupling Reactions: A Density Functional Theory Study of Reactivity and Selectivity
items.abstract: Cross-coupling reactions are of fundamental importance in organic and medicinal chemistry due to their ability to construct structurally complex molecules efficiently. Among transition-metal catalysts, nickel, particularly Ni(I) species, has attracted increasing attention because of its low cost, earth abundance, and electronic flexibility. In this study, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were employed to comprehensively investigate the reaction mechanism of Ni(I)-isocyanide catalyzed cross-coupling and to uncover the factors governing the preference for Kumada cross-coupling over undesired homocoupling pathways. Our results reveal the critical role of molecular rotations, a factor that is often overlooked in computational mechanistic studies. We demonstrate that subtle rotational dynamics can significantly influence reaction selectivity by modulating the accessibility and energetics of competing pathways, with a selectivity-determining barrier of 9.0 kcal/mol. In addition, a systematic analysis of steric and electronic descriptors of the key Ni(III) intermediate shows that combining the percent buried volume (%Vbur) and the topological fuzzy Voronoi cells (TFVC) charge on nickel (q(Ni)) in a two-descriptor multilinear regression reproduces the experimental isolated yields of 13 substrates (R2 = 0.853, Q2(LOO) = 0.724), revealing the decisive role of the organic group transferred from the Grignard reagent. Overall, this work establishes molecular rotational effects as an important mechanistic determinant and offers valuable design principles for the development of more efficient and selective nickel-catalyzed cross-coupling processes.

items.title: Sialic Acid-Functionalized CuS for Efficient Prevention and Treatment of H3N2 Viral Infections
items.abstract: Influenza is an acute respiratory infectious disease that seriously endangers human health. Metal nanoparticles exhibit antiviral properties; however, they suffer from limited potency. The metal nanoparticles with enzymatic activity selected and modified with ligands are expected to enhance their antiviral activity. In this study, copper sulfide (CuS) nanoparticles were synthesized, lactose acid was linked to CuS by SH-PEG-NH2, and sialic acid was conjugated to galactose through an enzymatic method to prepare sialic acid-functionalized CuS (CuS-Sa). CuS-Sa effectively prevents the immune escape caused by mutations in the influenza virus RNA through a dual mechanism: The peroxidase-like activity of CuS is utilized to destroy the viral envelope, while sialic acid (which can block the interaction between the virus and the receptor) inhibits the membrane fusion mediated by the hemagglutinin HA protein. The results showed that the inhibitory effect of CuS-Sa nanoparticles on influenza virus was superior to that of CuS and CuS-Gla nanoparticles, mainly acting at the virucidal stage and during cell internalization of the virus. In a mouse model of H3N2 virus infection, CuS-Sa can scavenge excess reactive oxygen species and inhibit inflammatory storm, while improving pulmonary edema and protecting lung injury. Therefore, CuS-Sa exerts excellent prevention and therapeutic effects. CuS-Sa has great potential for application as a virus adsorbent and disinfectant and can be applied in the prevention and treatment of viral infections.

items.title: Design and synthesis of novel pyridine-typed phenylahistin derivatives based on co-crystal structures for anticancer through inhibition of microtubules and caspase-mediated apoptosis
Hydrogen Sulfide-Mediated Metabolic Reprogramming for Enhanced Tumor Photodynamic Therapy
items.abstract: Metabolic plasticity allows tumor cells to dynamically adapt to harsh microenvironments, conferring elevated oxidative stress tolerance and enhanced cellular reductive capacity, which often compromises the therapeutic efficacy of ROS-based therapies. To address this challenge, we developed a peptide-conjugated tumor-targeting platform (PC-TPEPy-S) that integrates hydrogen sulfide (H2S)-mediated metabolic modulation with photodynamic therapy (PDT) to enhance ROS-induced tumor ablation. Guided by αvβ3 integrin-targeting peptides, PC-TPEPy-S is specifically internalized into tumor cells. Upon GSH-triggered activation, the released H2S dysregulates mitochondrial function and suppresses oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), thereby redirecting glucose metabolism toward glycolysis while limiting substrate availability for the pentose phosphate pathway. This metabolic perturbation renders cancer cells more vulnerable to oxidative stress. The combination with ROS-based therapy triggers a reinforcing cycle between metabolic and redox pathways, greatly enhancing the potency of photodynamic therapy. Both in vitro and in vivo studies demonstrate that PC-TPEPy-S effectively suppresses tumor growth with minimal systemic toxicity. This work provides a promising strategy for integrating gas-mediated metabolic reprogramming with ROS-based therapy to improve the outcomes of cancer treatment.

items.title: Structural Insights into Erm-Mediated rRNA Methylation Underlying Antibiotic Resistance
items.abstract: SAM-dependent Erm enzymes confer resistance to clinically important MLSB antibiotics (macrolides–lincosamides–streptogramin B) by methylation of the rRNA (rRNA) target. However, the molecular basis of the Erm–rRNA interaction remains poorly understood, hindering the development of effective Erm inhibitors to preserve antibiotic efficacy. Here, we integrate NMR and computational data to investigate the interaction between ErmB, prevalent in pathogenic Gram-positive bacteria, and a minimal RNA substrate mimicking the rRNA target. We demonstrate that Erm–RNA complex formation is critically dependent on the SAM cofactor, which shapes the conformational space of the entire catalytic domain, priming ErmB for specific recognition of its RNA substrate. Using NMR-guided docking, we derive experimentally validated structural models of the ErmB–RNA complex that reveal a vast and dynamic binding interface comprising ErmB’s N- and C-terminal domains, as well as the cationic interdomain cleft. These insights into the Erm enzyme function provide a foundation for the rational design of potent and selective drugs to combat pathogenic bacteria.

items.title: Enantioselective Radical Difunctionalization of Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes via Carbonyl Catalysis: Access to Multisubstituted Cyclobutanes
items.abstract: Multisubstituted cyclobutanes represent privileged structural scaffolds widely found in natural products and pharmaceutical molecules. Their rigid three-dimensional geometry makes cyclobutanes excellent bioisosteres to replace planar aromatic rings. Radical addition to bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) has emerged as a powerful strategy for the construction of diverse multisubstituted cyclobutane derivatives. Nevertheless, asymmetric radical addition reactions of BCBs remain severely underdeveloped and pose a formidable challenge in organic synthesis. This limitation primarily arises from the severe steric hindrance and the inherent difficulty in achieving precise stereocontrol during radical transformations. Herein, with a chiral pyridoxal as the catalyst, we successfully achieve an asymmetric radical addition of BCBs with α-amino acid esters and Togni II reagents. The reaction proceeds via a radical carbonyl catalysis pathway. The imine formed between pyridoxal and an α-amino acid ester undergoes single-electron transfer (SET) with a Togni II reagent, delivering a pyridoxal-stabilized α-amino radical and a fluoroalkyl radical. Stereoselective addition of the radicals to BCBs affords chiral α-amino acid esters bearing multisubstituted cyclobutanes in high yields, with moderate to excellent diastereo- and enantioselectivities. This transformation represents a new addition reaction of BCBs with excellent stereocontrol, which provides a highly efficient strategy for the synthesis of pharmaceutically valuable polysubstituted cyclobutanes.

items.title: Skeletal Editing of Pyrimidines to Access 3-(Alkylthio)pyridines
items.abstract: A skeletal editing strategy converts pyrimidines into 3-(alkylthio)pyridines using sulfonium salts as multifunctional synthons. The method enables pyrimidine-to-pyridine scaffold hopping, C3 thioether incorporation, and installation of independently variable C2 and C6 substituents. Mechanistically, the reaction involves pyrimidine activation and ring opening to the aza-streptocyanine intermediate, followed by addition of an in situ generated sulfur ylide and subsequent ring closing.

items.title: Heteroatom‐Modulated Aggregation of Diketopyrrolopyrrole Derivatives by Single‐Atom Substitution to Construct NIR‐II‐Absorbing Photothermal Agents With Over 90% Efficiency
items.abstract: Organic small‐molecule photothermal materials with second near‐infrared (NIR‐II) absorption have attracted enormous interest for biomedical applications, yet simultaneously achieving strong NIR‐II absorption and high photothermal conversion efficiency remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report to conduct the heteroatom‐modulated aggregation of diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP) derivatives (named as DAQ‐T and DAQ‐Fu) by single‐atom substitution to construct high‐performance NIR‐II‐absorbing photothermal agents. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction and density functional theory calculations reveal that oxygen‐for‐sulfur substitution precisely modulates electrostatic potential distributions and tailors intermolecular π–π interactions by leveraging the distinct electronegativities of chalcogens, driving a transformation from H ‐aggregation in DAQ‐T to J ‐aggregation in DAQ‐Fu. The resulting J ‐aggregated DAQ‐Fu nanoparticles feature a distinct absorption band at 1064 nm with a molar extinction coefficient of 3.26 × 10 4 L mol −1 cm −1 , and exhibit an outstanding photothermal conversion efficiency of 92.4%. This photothermal effect exerts potent antitumor efficacy by regulating apoptosis and immune‐related signaling pathways, enabling the synergy of photothermal therapy and as‐induced immunogenic cell death to suppress both primary and distant tumors growth with about 90% and 63% inhibition rates, respectively, under biocompatible irradiation. This work demonstrates atom‐precise aggregation modulation, offering a promising pathway to engineer NIR‐II‐absorbing organic small‐molecule photothermal agents for synergistic photothermal cancer immunotherapy.

items.title: miRNA–mRNA Binding Prediction Model Using Unknown and Experimentally Nondetected Interaction Data
items.abstract: MicroRNA (miRNA)– messenger RNA (mRNA) interactions inhibit gene expression, including the expression of disease-associated genes, and therefore have broad applications in drug discovery and therapeutics; however, experimental identification is challenging owing to the vast number of possible combinations and the high cost of experimentation. In this study, we developed a method for predicting miRNA–mRNA interactions using pseudonegative sampling and ensemble learning. Unlabeled miRNA–mRNA pairs were randomly sampled as pseudonegative training data, and 100 LightGBM classifiers were constructed to reduce dependence on particular training data selections. Using 248 experimentally nondetected interaction pairs collected through a literature review, we evaluated the ensemble binding scores and explored the usefulness of different sequence-derived explanatory variables. The combination of screening, k-mer first–last distance, and CKSNAP showed better discrimination between experimentally confirmed binding pairs and nonbinding pairs than the other feature combinations examined in this exploratory analysis. These findings suggest that pseudonegative sampling-based ensemble learning provides a useful framework for investigating miRNA–mRNA interactions.

items.title: Synthesis and Preclinical Evaluation of [18F]AlF-FAPI-JR11: A Novel Heterodimeric PET Tracer Targeting Fibroblast Activation Protein and Somatostatin Receptor 2
items.abstract: Neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) exhibit profound intratumoral and spatiotemporal heterogeneity that limits single-target imaging. We developed [18F]AlF-FAPI-JR11, a bispecific PET tracer linking the SSTR2 antagonist JR11 with a fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-targeting quinoline derivative via a hydrophilic NOTA-based linker to cover both tumor cells and stromal compartments. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations supported the feasibility of dual binding to FAP and SSTR2. The tracer was prepared by one-step [18F]AlF chelation, achieving high radiochemical purity (>95%), robust in vitro and in vivo stability, and favorable hydrophilicity (log D absolute value = 1.91). [18F]AlF-FAPI-JR11 exhibited higher cellular uptake than monomeric tracers in A549-FAP and AR42J cells. In micro-PET/CT imaging, it showed enhanced tumor uptake and retention with reduced renal, cholecystic, and intestinal background, yielding improved tumor-to-kidney ratios versus [18F]AlF-JR11 and tumor-to-cholecyst and tumor-to-intestine ratios versus [18F]AlF-FAPI-42. This dual FAP/SSTR2-targeting strategy provides a scaffold for mitigating tumor heterogeneity and supporting future theranostic exploration.

items.title: Discovery of SARS-CoV-2 Nsp14 Methyltransferase Inhibitors with Potent Antiviral Activity
items.abstract: To pursue SARS-CoV-2 nsp14 methyltransferase (MTase) inhibitors as COVID-19 therapeutics, we have performed structure–activity relationship studies on prototypic bisubstrate inhibitor 5, exploring the sulfonamide linker, nucleobase and ribose ring. Our work has led to multiple potent inhibitors including 28, which has an antiviral EC50 value of 90 nM (in A549 ACE2/TMPRSS2 cells) and a high selectivity index (CC50/EC50). Furthermore, we have established that selected compounds are highly selective over human RNA MTase hRNMT. Also importantly, we have shown that compound 28 inhibits nsp14 MTases from MERS-CoV and bat SARS-like coronavirus SHC014-CoV. However, we have also witnessed the complexity of simultaneous optimization of antiviral potency and drug-like properties. Overall, our work strongly supports nsp14 MTase inhibitor discovery as a promising strategy to combat SARS-CoV-2 and other coronaviruses of pandemic potential.

items.title: Compliance-Conditioned Molecular Generation Across Optical, Polymer, and Central Nervous System Targets with Graph Neural Network Ensembles
items.abstract: Generative molecular design usually optimises a single physical or biological target while treating regulatory bans and safety risks as an afterthought. At the same time, reinforcement learning against a single surrogate readily exploits out-of-distribution features or collapses onto narrow scaffolds. We evaluate a unified compliance-conditioned generation framework that embeds explicit regulatory and safety gates directly into REINVENT policy-gradient fine-tuning, guided by four-architecture 2D graph neural network ensembles (GINE, GATv2, MPNN, and CARATE) and audited by an independent ExtraTrees holdout excluded from training rewards. Across three distinct chemical domains on a single RTX 3060 GPU, the framework resolves domain-specific failure modes. For UV-Vis chromophores (400–450 nm), graph-ensemble rewards align training and holdout gains above 70% in-band yield across 3 seeds while cutting cross-seed variance nearly fourfold. For engineering polymers (Tg 450–550 K), where 15.07% of the curated corpus fails REACH or bisphenol-A rules, compliance-gated generation reaches 99.97% compliance with a fourfold increase in target-band yield. For non-hallucinogenic central nervous system ligands (5-HT1A versus cardiac 5-HT2B and hERG anti-targets), supervised warm-starting overcomes reward sparsity but triggers a selectivity trap that degrades cardiac safety. Smooth multiobjective safety fine-tuning paired with Bemis–Murcko scaffold memory resolves both cardiac safety and mode collapse, restoring uniqueness to 0.994. Finally, retrosynthetic audits confirm strong synthetic accessibility across all domains, and ab-initio TD-DFT screening on 50 UV-Vis candidates confirms visible absorption in 65.2% of converged structures while quantifying the residual surrogate-to-quantum gap.1

items.title: Proteomics Identification of Matrix Metalloproteinases in Mice, Dogs, and Humans after Spinal Cord Injury
items.abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is a devastating condition that results in paralysis and other complications, such as diminished life expectancy. After SCI, the primary mechanical injury sets in motion secondary pathogenesis. There are no FDA-approved drugs for the treatment of SCI. While rodent SCI models are widely used, drugs that have shown efficacy in these models of SCI have failed in clinical translation. Naturally occurring SCI in pet dogs provides a more heterogeneous population for assessment of the potential for clinical translation. Matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) and related ADAMs (adisintegrin and metalloproteases) play a role in the pathology and homeostasis/repair of the central nervous system (CNS). Two challenges exist in addressing the involvement of these enzymes in SCI. First, there exist several dozen MMPs and ADAMs in vertebrates. This complication is compounded by the fact that these enzymes exist in three forms, of which only the active form is catalytically competent. Currently available methods for the identification of the various forms in the disease often do not discriminate among them. We used an affinity resin of our design, coupled with mass spectrometry, to identify and quantify active MMPs/ADAMs in human cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) after SCI, in dog CSF after a naturally occurring SCI, and in spinal cord tissue in a mouse model of SCI. We found elevated levels of active MMP-14 in humans and mice, and active MMP-9 in dogs. The selective inhibitor that targets MMP-9 and MMP-14, (R)-ND-336, decreased oxidative stress and inflammation markers in lipopolysaccharide-treated SH-SY5Y cells and holds the promise of a potential treatment for SCI.

items.title: Photocatalytic Cross-Coupling of Sulfoxonium Ylides with Silyl Enol Ethers for the Synthesis of 1,4-Diketones
items.abstract: 1,4-Diketones are pivotal intermediates in organic optoelectronics, where stringent metal-impurity constraints challenge conventional synthesis. Herein, we report a metal-free visible-light photocatalytic cross-coupling of silyl enol ethers with sulfoxonium ylides using 4CzIPN, affording 1,4-diketones under mild conditions without metal catalysts, bases, or additives. The use of bench-stable sulfoxonium ylides as α-carbonyl radical precursors enables an operationally simple protocol with broad substrate scope encompassing aryl, heteroaryl, and aliphatic coupling partners, as well as late-stage functionalization of drug and natural product derivatives. The metal-free nature of both the key C–C bond-forming step and the subsequent heterocycle-forming transformations minimizes metal introduction at the critical synthetic stages, providing a practical platform for ultralow-metal-residue synthesis.

items.title: Merging substrate permissive biocatalysis with chemical derivatization to build post-translationally modified lipidated peptides
items.abstract: Lipidation enhances the pharmacologically desirable properties of peptides and proteins. However, biocatalytic lipidation is often constrained by the enzymatic selectivity for the peptide and the lipid substrates. Here, we combine substrate-permissive biocatalysis with chemical derivatization to generate structurally diverse lipidated peptides. We demonstrate the use of promiscuous enzymes to install lanthionine crosslinks and azole heterocycles in peptide substrates, which subsequently undergo sequential diazotransfer and copper-mediated azide–alkyne cycloaddition to append lipid moieties. This workflow accommodates saturated, aromatic, heterocyclic, and fluorinated lipids and extends to chemically synthesized peptides, including head-to-tail macrocyclic peptides containing non-proteinogenic amino acids. Site specificity for chemical lipidation is controlled by the incorporation of lysine residues at any desired location, as well as enzymatic conversion of N-terminal glutamine to pyroglutamate. Efficient modification across lanthipeptides, linear azol(in)e-containing peptides, and head-to-tail macrocycles demonstrates compatibility with distinct peptide architectures. By decoupling peptide maturation from lipid installation, this modular chemoenzymatic strategy expands access to site-selectively lipidated, post-translationally modified peptides and provides a foundation for exploring how lipid identity influences peptide function.

items.title: Indanonalkene Photoluminescent Platform: From Reaction-Encoded Fluorescence to Adaptive Soft Materials and Chemical Biology
items.abstract: Dynamic covalent chemistry provides a powerful framework for constructing adaptive molecular and materials systems, while fluorescence offers a sensitive and noninvasive means to visualize chemical processes in real time. In most reported systems, however, these two components are combined only modularly: fluorophores are appended as passive reporters, and the resulting optical signals are only indirectly related to the underlying bond-forming or bond-breaking events. This separation limits the ability of fluorescence to faithfully encode chemical state, transformation pathway, and reaction history. In this Account, we describe a unified platform based on indanonalkene-derived conjugate acceptors in which chemical reactivity and fluorescence are intrinsically coupled within the same molecular scaffold. These acceptors undergo nucleophilic addition, conjugate substitution, intramolecular cyclization, and elimination reactions that directly reorganize the π-conjugation pathway and alter excited-state decay. Consequently, otherwise weakly emissive or nonemissive intermediates are converted into fluorescent products, allowing covalent transformations to be reported stoichiometrically and in real time. Three complementary photophysical modes underpin this platform. Cyclization-regulated fluorescence emission (CRFE) arises when reaction-induced ring formation rigidifies the scaffold and suppresses nonradiative relaxation. Displacement-induced fluorescence emission (DIFE) results from substitution of sulfur-based leaving groups by amine-containing nucleophiles, which reconfigures the electronic structure and restores emission. In addition, donor-excited photoinduced electron transfer (d-PeT) enables conjugate acceptors to function as reaction-cleavable fluorescence quenchers for activity-based sensing. Together, these mechanisms establish a modular strategy for translating local chemical reactivity into optical outputs that report not only the presence of a stimulus but also the structural state and pathway of molecular transformation. We trace the evolution of this platform from its initial use in real-time visualization of soft-material synthesis, remodeling, and degradation to thiol-triggered self-propagating cascades, programmable multistate fluorescent switches, and fluorogenic dynamic covalent polymers and vitrimer-like networks. We then discuss its expansion into chemical biology, including position-selective cysteine modification, reversible peptide macrocyclization, cysteine-guided protein-backbone editing, vicinal dithiol labeling, albumin-targeted fluorogenic prodrugs, covalent membrane anchoring for imaging protein aggregation, and global intracellular thiol-redox sensing. These applications demonstrate how related reaction pathways can be adapted across molecular, macromolecular, and cellular length scales while retaining an intrinsically encoded optical response. Across these studies, the central design principle remains constant: fluorescence is not an appended label but a direct consequence of chemical transformation. By integrating reaction, reporting, and function within one scaffold, the indanonalkene platform provides a reaction-encoded optical language connecting small-molecule sensing, adaptive soft materials, protein engineering, and live-cell imaging. This framework offers broader opportunities for designing programmable fluorogenic systems capable of sensing, processing, and responding to chemical information in complex environments.

items.title: Photoinduced Selective Oxidative γ-Hydroxylation of Pyrrolidone
items.abstract: The direct and selective C–H functionalization of pyrrolidones continues to represent a significant challenge in synthetic chemistry because of their intrinsic chemical inertness. Herein, a new visible-light-driven strategy is described for the direct and selective γ-C–H hydroxylation of pyrrolidones under mild and metal-free conditions. This approach utilizes a photoexcited dicarbonyl compound to produce a triplet biradical species, which promotes hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) from the γ position of pyrrolidone. The generated iminium intermediate is then captured by water, which functions as the oxygen source, as clearly verified by 18O-labeling experiments. The transformation displays a wide substrate scope along with good tolerance toward various functional groups. The synthetic applicability is further validated through gram-scale synthesis and the flexible derivatization of γ-hydroxy products into a range of C–C and C–X bond formations, including asymmetric processes and late-stage functionalization of bioactive compounds. This work overcomes persistent limitations of traditional oxidation chemistry, offering a green, efficient, and diversity-oriented pathway to valuable hydroxylated pyrrolidone frameworks for use in medicinal chemistry and drug discovery.

items.title: Programmed Metal-Ion Reconstruction of Small-Molecule Nanoassemblies for Thermoresponsive Hydrogel-Mediated Photothermal Antibacterial and Immunoregulatory Wound Repair
items.abstract: MRSA-infected wound repair remains challenging because persistent bacterial colonization, oxidative stress, and dysregulated inflammation mutually reinforce each other within the wound microenvironment. Although multifunctional hydrogels have been widely explored for infected wound management, many systems still rely on the physical combination of independently functioning components, limiting structural integration, and functional coupling. Here, we report a programmed metal-ion reconstruction strategy in which chlorogenic acid (CGA) and glycyrrhizic acid (GA) were first assembled under Ag+ mediation to form Ag-containing nanoassemblies (AGC), followed by stepwise Fe3+ coordination to generate reconstructed Ag/Fe-integrated nanoassemblies (AGCF). This reconstruction altered the local coordination environment and enhanced near-infrared responsiveness and photothermal conversion while retaining the ROS-regulating activity. Incorporation of AGCF into a PNIPAM/PVA network yielded a preformed thermoresponsive hydrogel dressing, P/P@AGCF, exhibiting temperature- and microenvironment-dependent Ag/Fe release. Under 808 nm irradiation, P/P@AGCF markedly enhanced MRSA killing and biofilm disruption while reducing the intracellular ROS accumulation and promoting fibroblast migration. In the MRSA-infected full-thickness wound model, P/P@AGCF reduced bacterial burden, accelerated wound closure, enhanced blood perfusion and angiogenesis, and improved inflammatory resolution, collagen deposition, and tissue remodeling. Proteomic analysis, Western blotting, Nrf2 nuclear translocation analysis, in vivo Nrf2 immunofluorescence, and ML385 inhibition collectively supported an important role of Nrf2/Keap1/HO-1 signaling in the oxidative-stress regulation and immunoregulatory effects of P/P@AGCF, accompanied by attenuation of JAK2/STAT3 inflammatory signaling and macrophage transition toward a reparative phenotype. This work establishes a programmed metal-ion reconstruction strategy for converting natural small-molecule nanoassemblies into structurally integrated hydrogel therapeutics that couple photothermal antibacterial activity with ROS regulation and immunomodulation for MRSA-infected wound healing.

items.title: Exploring Sesquiterpene Lactone Scaffolds From Ambrosia tenuifolia: Structural Diversification and Antiparasitic Profiling Against Trypanosoma cruzi
items.abstract: Chagas disease, caused by the protozoan parasite Trypanosoma cruzi , remains a major public health concern in endemic regions. Natural products represent an important source of structurally diverse molecules with potential antiparasitic activity. In this study, sesquiterpene lactones isolated from Ambrosia tenuifolia were explored as bioactive scaffolds and chemically diversified through semisynthetic modification to investigate how oxidation patterns, conjugation, and hybridization influence antiparasitic activity across parasite stages through a comparative phenotypic screening strategy. A small library of natural compounds and derivatives was evaluated against different developmental stages of T. cruzi , including epimastigotes, trypomastigotes, and intracellular amastigotes. Several derivatives displayed measurable trypanocidal activity in the micromolar range, both oxidized analogs and the conjugated molecular hybrid showing pronounced trypanocidal effects, with the latter displaying the most promising activity across the different parasite stages evaluated. These findings highlight the influence of oxidation patterns and hybrid architecture on the antiparasitic profile of sesquiterpene lactones and provide insights into structure–activity relationships within this class of natural products. Overall, this study expands the chemical space of sesquiterpene lactones and identifies a conjugated hybrid as a promising candidate for further investigation based on its multistage activity against T. cruzi .

items.title: Atroposelective synthesis of biaryls with artificial SNAr enzymes
items.abstract: Artificial enzymes have been widely employed for the construction of molecules featuring point chirality. However, application of these biocatalysts for the assembly of less common stereogenic elements such as chiral axes, which are a key feature of numerous bioactive compounds and chiral catalysts, is far less explored. Here, we show that S N Arases previously developed to set point chirality can also be used to construct axially chiral biaryl motifs. We identifed a pair of miniature enantiocomplementary NTF2-like enzymes (S N Ar ax1 and S N Ar ax2 ) that differ by only four mutations and allow enantiodivergent synthesis of biaryls through desymmetrizing S N Ar processes. These enzymes can process a broad range of dichloropyrimidine electrophiles and (thio)phenol nucleophiles to construct a diverse array of pyrimidine-containing biaryls with excellent yields (up to 99% yield) and enantioselectivities (up to >99% e.e. ). The products generated feature a halide substituent that serves as a functional handle for further synthetic manipulations that proceed with retention of stereochemical information. Computational modelling of S N Ar ax1 and S N Ar ax2 shows that their opposing selectivity profiles can be traced to an altered backbone conformation in the C -terminal region that subtly reshapes the electrophile binding pocket. This study expands the synthetic capabilities of artificial S N Ar biocatalysts and shows how these systems can be adapted to accurately control chiral axes within complex three-dimensional structures.

items.title: A Small Molecule Mimic of α-ketoglutarate Dependent JmjC Domain Containing Lysine Demethylase Enzyme
items.abstract: Regulation of epigenetic modifications is a natural process important in the mammalian development as well defense system. Their dysregulation leads to autoimmune disease conditions and cancers. Understanding the cause of their aberrant occurrences can lead to better therapies. The Lysine methylation being a key epigenetic modification, is dynamically and tightly regulated by Lysine methyltransferases and Lysine demethylases. Its demethylation mechanism, however, needs more thorough understanding. Here, we report a small molecule chemical model of the JmjC domain containing Lysine demethylases that mimics the removal of methyl group from methylated Lysine analogues. Our studies agree with the proposed mechanism of demethylation catalysed by the non-heme Fe(II) containing based dioxygenases whereby we have detected the formation of an intermediate ‘Hydroxy-DMA’ as well as formaldehyde as a byproduct of demethylation. We also confirmed the same mechanism of demethylation on the actual substrate, N,N-dimethyl-L-Lysine, via LCMS. This chemical model provides a mechanistic insight into Lysine demethylation and highlights the potential of chemical models in understanding the fundamental chemistry of epigenetic regulation via Lysine demethylation.

items.title: Discovery of a Linked Fragment That Creates a Potent Half-Site Binder and Functional Antagonist of a Riboswitch RNA
items.abstract: Fragment-based ligand discovery has identified RNA-targeted hits, but progressing these hits into potent, biology-altering leads has remained unrealized. During transcription, the bacterial thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP) riboswitch samples a complex structure, stabilized by TPP, that sequesters the start codon region to create a translation-inhibiting OFF state. SHAPE-informed fragment screening previously identified a quinoxaline ligand (Kd = 25 μM) that, when linked to a cobinding piperazine fragment, yielded Z1 (Kd = 0.2–0.6 μM). We used structure–activity relationships to create Z2 with ∼50 nM affinity and ligand efficiency exceeding the native ligand. Structure determination by cryo-EM reveals that every heteroatom in Z2 (n = 6) forms direct hydrogen bonds with the RNA. Z2 engages exclusively at a mini-3-helix junction to stabilize a half-open riboswitch conformation distinct from both ligand-free and TPP-bound states. Cotranscriptional folding and cell-based experiments show that Z2 competes with TPP for binding but does not stabilize the native regulatory OFF state. Z2 thus functions as an RNA-targeted antagonist, displacing the native ligand and disrupting the regulatory logic of the riboswitch. These results establish a pathway for creating high-efficiency RNA–ligand interactions and identify half-site occupancy as a mechanism for antagonizing RNA function.

items.title: Chemotype-Symmetric Junction-Tree VAE for SARS-CoV-2 Mpro Inhibitor Design
items.abstract: The main protease (Mpro) of SARS-CoV-2 is inhibited by covalent drugs such as nirmatrelvir, whose activity comes from a reactive warhead that bonds to the enzyme. Designing safer analogs of these inhibitors is hard because standard drug-likeness objectives optimise away the very warhead that makes them work, and because the fused-aromatic scaffolds they are built on are where generative models most often produce invalid structures. This work presents a generative framework that improves predicted safety while preserving both the warhead and target affinity. Built on a junction-tree variational autoencoder, it represents each molecule as a tree of chemical fragments, encodes it into a continuous latent space, and generates analogs by decoding new points near a known inhibitor’s latent code. A chemotype-symmetric fragment vocabulary gives uniform coverage across the diverse Mpro inhibitor chemotype classes, and a graph-attention attachment scorer conditioned on the latent code reassembles their edgefused ring chemistry at decoding time, reconstructing 19 of 20 top-active targets faithfully. Over this latent space the framework runs a constrained six-objective search that trades off drug-likeness, synthetic accessibility, warhead retention, predicted potency, lipophilicity, and warhead reversibility. Predicted potency comes from a deep-ensemble bioactivity surrogate, whose disagreement across the ensemble also sets an anchor-relative uncertainty cap that gates the search away from chemistry it has not seen. The optimiser is NSGA-III, selected after benchmarking a catalogue of multi-objective methods on this pipeline. From all twenty anchors, spanning five Mpro inhibitor chemotype classes, the framework produces a de-duplicated library of 1,013 analogs and retains the source warhead in 85% of the parents that carry one. A perwarhead analysis shows predicted mutagenicity is governed by the warhead class rather than by covalency, the reversible nitrile of the marketed inhibitors being as clean as non-covalent chemistry while the irreversible chloroacetamide and Michael warheads carry the liability. The final Pareto front of 138 analogs is predicted as safe as or safer than each analog’s own source inhibitor on four of eight ADMET endpoints and at parity on mutagenicity, with the warhead retained in 94% of the front and docked binding within AutoDock Vina’s scoring error of the parents, at a modest predicted-potency cost. The strongest single candidate is a dual-warhead analog of nirmatrelvir, predicted safer than the drug on seven of eight endpoints. This safety advantage over the source inhibitors, obtained without erasing the warhead, is the central result, and one that objectives penalising the covalent warhead cannot reach without discarding the mechanism.

items.title: Proximity-Induced Targeted Degradation of Microtubule-Associated Protein Tau Pre-mRNA Using Small Bifunctional Molecules
items.abstract: Dysregulation of RNA processing caused by single-nucleotide mutations can profoundly alter cellular homeostasis and drive disease. A prominent example is the aberrant alternative splicing of the microtubule-associated protein tau (MAPT) gene, which leads to imbalances in 3R and 4R tau isoforms and is associated with multiple tauopathies. In particular, mutations such as the disinhibition–dementia–parkinsonism–amyotrophy complex (DDPAC) variant promote exon 10 inclusion, increasing the 4R/3R ratio and contributing to tau aggregation and neurodegeneration. Antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) can reduce MAPT mRNA levels, while small molecules have been developed to modulate MAPT pre-mRNA splicing by targeting regulatory RNA structures. Here, we investigated an alternative approach based on Proximity-Induced Nucleic Acid Degradation (PINAD), in which an RNA-binding ligand is conjugated to an RNA-cleaving warhead. We designed and synthesized a library of 24 bifunctional small molecules derived from a previously reported MAPT pre-mRNA SRE-binding ligand. Screening in SH-SY5Y cells identified PINAD-23, which reduced MAPT mRNA levels in a dose-dependent manner and decreased the expression of both 3R and 4R tau isoforms. Biochemical studies using a model MAPT RNA showed that PINAD-23 binds the target RNA and promotes RNA cleavage. Defined cleavage products detected under metal-free conditions supported a contribution from a base-mediated pathway, while Cu(II) binding by the diimidazole warhead and Cu(II)-dependent RNA cleavage supported the involvement of a copper-dependent pathway. These findings provide a proof of concept for converting a previously characterized MAPT RNA-binding ligand into a bifunctional small molecule capable of inducing target RNA cleavage and reducing downstream tau expression.

items.title: Synthesis of Diversifiable Bicyclic Isoxazole Cores for Applications in Medicinal Chemistry and Drug Discovery
items.abstract: Partially saturated bicyclic scaffolds are valuable structural motifs in medicinal chemistry, combining C(sp3)-rich, three-dimensional structural features with spatially and electronically distinct (hetero)aromatic systems. Herein, we report an efficient synthetic approach to functionalized dihydroisoxazolopyridinones, providing access to an underexplored class of isoxazole-containing fused bicyclic scaffolds bearing synthetically versatile amine and ketone functionalities. The synthetic utility of these scaffolds was further demonstrated through complementary derivatization strategies, providing access to a structurally diverse range of derivatives and enabling systematic exploration of this chemical space.

items.title: Dual-Target Structural Discovery of Orally Bioavailable Selective KRAS G12D Inhibitors Accelerated by Deterministic Sub-100 μs Userspace PCIe BAR0 MMIO Spatial Voxel Screening
items.abstract: Noncovalent inhibition of oncogenic KRAS G12D requires high-affinity recognition of the mutant Asp12 carboxylate and inducible Switch-II pocket while maintaining oral drug-like physicochemical properties (MW ≤ 500 Da) and selectivity over wild-type (WT) KRAS.Here, we report a dual-target, structure-based virtual screening and consensus docking investigation comparing GDP-bound KRAS G12D (PDB: 7RPZ ) against GDPbound WT KRAS (PDB: 4OBE ).From 2,500 unique chemical structures curated from ChEMBL 34, literature Switch-II controls, and structure-guided oral-window scaffolds, medicinal chemistry alert triage (PAINS, Brenk, NIH) and Lipinski basic-amine filtering retained 536 qualified three-dimensional (3D) conformers.Redocking of crystallographic MRTX1133 (PDB ligand 6IC ) into 7RPZ reproduced the experimental X-ray geometry to 0.418 Å heavy-atom RMSD (-14.68 kcal/mol) under bound ring-pucker preservation, recovered the canonical 2.74 Å Asp12 ionic salt bridge from unbiased de novo SMILES conformers, and achieved 1.000 ROC-AUC separating known Switch-II binders from negative controls.Multi-seed AutoDock Vina consensus docking (seeds 42, 137, 2026) identified two selective lead series: an oral-window Switch-II analog, OIK-G12D-009 (MW = 476.60Da, ΔG G12D = -11.26± 0.03 kcal/mol, ΔΔG G12D-WT = -4.32kcal/mol, LLE = 4.91, Asp12 = 3.43 Å), and a structurally distinct scaffold-hopped ChEMBL 34 chemotype, CHEMBL51 (Morgan Tanimoto = 0.083 to MRTX1133, MW = 395.43Da, ΔG G12D = -10.50± 0.01 kcal/mol, ΔΔG G12D-WT = -3.86kcal/mol, LLE = 5.28, SA = 2.14, Asp12 = 3.07 Å).To enforce cycle-accurate spatial tensor verification with minimal host DRAM overhead, 4,096-byte (16 × 16 × 16) molecular pharmacophore grids were streamed via direct userspace PCIe Gen3 x16 BAR0 memory-mapped I/O (MMIO) to a Xilinx UltraScale+ FPGA ( agfi-0b55f06c15a385187 on AWS EC2 f2.6xlarge ), achieving 84.51 ns posted write latency, 87.02 μs P50 C BAR0 tensor streaming, 0.25 KB constant O(1) on-chip state, and 100% bit-exact determinism at 6 W V CCINT steady-state power.Together, these findings establish an audithardened computational framework for identifying orally bioavailable, mutant-selective KRAS G12D lead candidates.

items.title: Protactinium, Neptunium, and Plutonium Solubilization and Extraction Mediated by Polyoxometalates
items.abstract: Understanding how chelators impact solubility, complexation, and partitioning of early actinides is essential for nuclear applications. Herein, we investigate how the aqueous speciation of protactinium, neptunium, and plutonium is impacted by three main polyoxometalates (POMs) topologies as inorganic chelators: the Wells-Dawson α 2 -P 2 W 17 O 61 10- (P 2 W 17 ), the Keggin-type POMs PW 11 O 39 7- (PW11), SiW 11 O 39 8- (SiW 11 ), GeW 11 O 39 8- (GeW 11 ), and BW 11 O 39 9- (BW 11 ), and a Lindqvist-type POM W 5 O 18 6- (W 5 ). These six POMs stabilize Pu(IV) in water, exemplified by crystallization of a new Pu-POM compound, Cs 12 Pu IV (SiW 11 O 39 ) 2 ·H 2 O. Additionally, P 2 W 17 , PW 11 , SiW 11 and GeW 11 trigger reduction of the usually stable neptunyl(V) ion, [NpO 2 ] + , and form [Np IV (POM) 2 ] n- complexes, which is effective at both millimolar and tracer-level concentrations. In contrast, W 5 and BW 11 do not promote [NpO 2 ] + reduction under the tested conditions. Negatively-charged POM complexes render Np(IV) and Pu(IV) extractible via liquid-liquid extraction with quaternary ammonium Aliquat® 336 in kerosene. While protactinium typically requires highly corrosive fluoride solutions to solubilize, the POMs complex and solubilize it under mild conditions (pH ~5 and without fluoride), unlocking Pa extraction with quaternary ammonium. Quantitative separation of 233 Pa/ 237 Np is achieved with the combination of POMs plus Aliquat® 336, yielding >99% radiopurity 233 Pa and 237 Np in a single step (separation factor Pa/Np > 1300). Experiments with the long-lived 231 Pa also revealed that POMs increase the solubility of Pa 2 O 5 ·nH 2 O (s) , overcoming both Pa(V) hydrolysis and competitive complexation with fluoride. This study unravels a general strategy for POM-mediated reduction of neptunyl(V) to Np(IV) in water and separation of Pa, Np, and Pu. This is the first reported complexation of protactinium with POMs, expanding the chemical toolkit to study this elusive element.

items.title: Targeting the Intrinsically Disordered N‐Terminal Domain of the Prion Protein: A New Frontier for Antiprion Therapeutics
items.abstract: Intrinsically disordered proteins and regions have long been considered challenging pharmacological targets because they lack stable 3D structures and well‐defined binding pockets. Nevertheless, advances in structural biology, biophysics, and computational drug discovery have demonstrated that their dynamic conformational ensembles can be selectively targeted. The cellular prion protein (PrP C ) exemplifies this emerging paradigm. Although antiprion strategies have traditionally focused on its structured C‐terminal domain, the intrinsically disordered N‐terminal region plays essential roles in metal ions homeostasis, neuroprotective signaling, membrane interactions, and prion propagation. In this review, we summarize and examine the physiological and synthetic ligands that bind to the PrP C N‐terminal domain or fragments thereof whose interactions have been characterized at the molecular level using biochemical and biophysical approaches. We discuss the molecular determinants of ligand recognition, the structural and functional consequences of binding, and their therapeutic implications. By integrating current structural, biophysical, and pharmacological evidence, this review aims to define the structural principles governing the selective targeting of the intrinsically disordered N‐terminal region of PrP C , and to provide a framework for the rational development of novel antiprion therapeutics.

items.title: Cross-Dehydrogenative Coupling of Indoles with Fluorinated Primary Alcohols through Cocatalysis of DMAP and Na2CO3
items.abstract: An efficient and facile method for the synthesis of 3-hydroxyfluoroalkylated indoles is described in this paper. The site-specific dehydrogenative hydroxyfluoroalkylation reaction of various indoles with fluorinated primary alcohols, such as 2,2,2-trifluoroethanol, 2,2-difluoroethanol, 2,2,3,3,3-pentafluoropropanol, and 2,2,3,3,4,4,4-heptafluorobutanol, proceeded smoothly under DMAP/Na2CO3 cocatalysis to provide 3-hydroxyfluoroalkylated indoles in moderate to excellent yields (up to >99% yield). Various groups, including the synthetically useful functional groups Cl, Br, CO2Me, and Ac, remained intact during the reaction. It provided a practical strategy for installation of useful, fluorinated units into N-heterocycles by using readily available fluorinated alcohols. The mechanism study revealed the formation of fluorine-containing aldehyde intermediates.

items.title: Regioselective esterification of ginsenoside Rg1 yields anti-DENV derivatives with reduced viral NS3 expression
Discovery of novel DNA-PK/tubulin dual-targeting inhibitors as potential anticancer agents and chemosensitizers
High Affinity Bivalent Ligands Targeting the Dopamine D1-Histamine H3 Receptor Heteromer Reduce Amyloid-Beta-Induced Neuronal Cell Death
items.abstract: The dopamine D1 receptor (D1R) and histamine H3 receptor (H3R) were reported to form heteromers in vitro and in vivo. Moreover, the D1R−H3R heteromer forms a macromolecular complex with NMDA-receptor subunits, which presented neuroprotective effects upon antagonization. We herein report the synthesis of 14 novel bivalent ligands designed to target this heteromer, incorporating distinct pharmacophores linked by spacers of varying composition and length. Comprehensive pharmacological profiling identified promising compounds displaying low-nanomolar affinity at D1R and subnanomolar affinity at H3R. Antagonistic ligands showed high selectivity across the dopamine and histamine receptor families and provided evidence of a bivalent binding mode in cells co-expressing D1R and H3R. Compound 45 (UR-NR330) was selected for evaluation in vitro using primary mouse embryonic cortical cells. Remarkably, this bivalent ligand significantly reduced amyloid-beta (Aβ)-induced neuronal cell death. These compounds provide powerful chemical tools to further investigate the biology and pharmacology of the D1R−H3R heteromer.

items.title: Guide DNAs Program Enzyme for Detection of Circulating Tumor DNA Without Target Denaturation and Amplification
items.abstract: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is fragmented, tumor‐derived cell‐free double‐stranded DNA (dsDNA) whose low abundance and limited sequence accessibility complicate detection under mild conditions. Here we show that guide DNAs (gDNAs) can program an exonuclease to interrogate native dsDNA under mild conditions and convert this access into a single‐molecule fluorescence readout. We found that gDNA 5′‐terminal chemistry regulates λ exonuclease (λExo) recruitment. Among those termini, anionic 5′‐phosphate and 5′‐carboxyl‐C10 phosphate enabled the strongest target‐dependent processing. Molecular simulations suggested a possible structural basis for these activity differences based on terminal positioning within the catalytic pocket. Coupling the optimized 5′‐carboxyl‐C10 phosphate gDNA with 10–23 DNAzyme turnover generated a single‐molecule fluorescence readout without target nucleic‐acid amplification. The assay detected dsDNA down to 10 fM across 10–1000 fM, showed a statistically significant response at an epidermal growth factor receptor ( EGFR ) L858R mutant fraction of 0.05% under the tested conditions, and was applied to 24 plasma samples (12 from patients with non‐small‐cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and 12 from healthy donors), achieving 91.7% sensitivity, 100% specificity, 95.8% accuracy, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC) of 0.97. This work establishes gDNA‐programmed enzyme access as a route for detecting low‐abundance duplex tumor DNA.

items.title: FcRn Silencing Accelerates Clearance of an LRRC15-Targeted [177Lu]Lu-Radioimmunoconjugate, Reducing Therapeutic Efficacy without Alleviating Hematologic Toxicity in Mice
items.abstract: The neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) is a key determinant of IgG half-life and systemic exposure of antibody-based therapeutics. While prolonged circulation enhances target engagement, it may also increase off-target toxicity for antibody conjugates delivering cytotoxic payloads, including radioimmunoconjugates. Here, we investigated whether disruption of FcRn-mediated recycling can modulate pharmacokinetics, tissue distribution, toxicity, and therapeutic efficacy of an LRRC15-targeted radioimmunotherapy (RIT). Murine IgG2a antibodies with identical LRRC15-binding specificity (mDUNP19) were compared: a wild-type version (mDUNP19WT) with retained FcRn binding and a mutant version (mDUNP19DM) containing I253A/H435A mutations that ablate FcRn binding. Both variants were conjugated with CHX-A″-DTPA and radiolabeled with 177Lu. Biodistribution, retention times for human dosimetry estimates, hematological toxicity, and antitumor efficacy were evaluated in LRRC15-expressing HuO9 subcutaneous osteosarcoma xenografts. Disruption of FcRn binding significantly accelerated systemic clearance of mDUNP19DM, resulting in an approximately four-fold reduction in blood circulation time and a shortened terminal half-life (16 h vs. 44 h) compared with the FcRn-binding mDUNP19WT177Lu-radioconjugate. Despite substantially lower late-phase blood radioactivity, both mDUNP19WT and mDUNP19DM177Lu-RIT induced comparable transient hematological toxicity, with nadirs at 2 weeks post-injection and recovery by 4 weeks. These findings indicate that marrow toxicity is dominated by early post-administration of 177Lu-radiation exposure. Further, depletion of FcRn binding resulted in a three-fold reduction in cumulative tumor uptake, which significantly reduced LRRC15-RIT efficacy. Relative to untreated controls, the median times to progression were 11.5 days compared to 73 days when treating with mDUNP19DM and mDUNP19WT177Lu-RIT, respectively. Overall, the data indicates that FcRn-mediated recycling is essential for targeted deposition of radionuclides and therapeutic efficacy of RIT. Further, reducing blood retention time by ablating FcRn−IgG interaction provides minimal protection against acute hematological toxicity. These observations demonstrate that modulating FcRn alone is insufficient to meaningfully reduce hematological toxicity, underscoring the need for alternative strategies to optimize efficacy and toxicity of IgG-based RIT.

items.title: Standardization Transformation of Softwood Protolignin to Benzoxazole Molecule With Tumor‐Selective Cytotoxicity
items.abstract: The protolignin standardization transformation into high‐value‐added pharmaceutical chemicals requires elaborate strategy design and catalytic system construction. Herein, a novel lignin valorization pattern to produce G‐lignin‐derived benzoxazoles from softwood is achieved, which involves the tandem CRF transformation of lignocellulose to C3‐alkyl guaiacol (C3‐G), stoichiometric diazotization‐reductive ammonification of C3‐G to aminophenol C3‐GAP, and photocatalytic cyclization of C3‐GAP to the benzoxazole C3‐GLB‐pCBA. The whole process can yield 6.2 wt% benzoxazole C3‐GLB‐pCBA from the aromatic guaiacyl rings of the original softwood lignin. Furthermore, the in vitro cytotoxicity assays with human osteosarcoma (HOS) cells, normal human osteoblast cells (hFOB1.19), and mouse 3T3 fibroblasts confirm the potential tumor‐selective cytotoxicity of the as‐synthesized G‐lignin‐derived benzoxazole C3‐GLB‐pCBA. Further TEA and LCA indicate the sustainability of the synthesis process of C3‐GLB‐pCBA from softwood. The success of the tandem pattern may inspire further studies on the high‐value utilization of lignin to produce pharmaceutical molecules.

items.title: Dual‐Force Strategy for Universal Clusteroluminescence in Non‐Conjugated Small Molecules
items.abstract: Non‐traditional luminophores (NTLs) without extended π‐conjugation are attractive for bio‐applications, yet an effective strategy to impart bright emission to non‐luminescent small molecules remains challenging. In this work, we report a modular strategy based on the diethylenetriamine (DETA)‐induced universal luminescence (DIUL) effect, which converts simple non‐conjugated precursors into highly emissive cluster‐based small molecules via synergistic dual‐force: ionic (─BF 4 − /─NH 2 + ) and hydrogen‐bonding (─NH─/─NH 2 ) interactions. The resulting seven derivatives exhibit >70% photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) in water, with emission independent of ring/chain structure, demonstrating a robust dual‐force mechanism that advances beyond hydrogen‐bond‐dominated aggregation‐induced emission (AIE) models. These probes show excellent water solubility, low cytotoxicity, and efficient cellular uptake, enabling high‐contrast dual‐color cellular and deep 3D tumor spheroid imaging, along with long‐term biocompatible zebrafish imaging. This work establishes a versatile modular functionalization platform for bright NTLs, offering fundamental insights into cooperative non‐covalent interactions and opening new avenues for designing multifunctional optical materials in bioimaging, sensing, and encryption.

items.title: Dual‐DUBTACs Enable Targeted Protein Stabilization via Multi‐DUB Engagement
items.abstract: Targeted protein stabilization has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy for restoring the abundance and function of disease‐relevant proteins. Deubiquitinase‐targeting chimeras (DUBTACs) offer a chemical approach to protein stabilization by recruiting deubiquitinases (DUBs) to promote target deubiquitination. However, current DUBTAC strategies generally rely on the recruitment of a single DUB, leaving the potential of engaging multiple DUBs through a common recruiter largely unexplored. Here, we report a dual‐DUBTAC strategy that enables targeted protein stabilization through the recruitment of two distinct DUBs. Using Degrasyn, a small‐molecule reversible covalent inhibitor of multiple DUBs, as a privileged scaffold, we engineered small molecules that selectively stabilize CFTR and cGAS and demonstrate that these compounds enhance target protein homeostasis through USP9X‐ and USP5‐mediated deubiquitination in cells. By decoupling substrate stabilization from reliance on a single DUB, the Dual‐DUB platform confers adaptability across diverse ubiquitin chain architectures and rewired proteostasis networks characteristic of heterogeneous tumors and could overcome potential drug resistance in future clinical applications. This strategy expands the chemical space for restoring protective proteins and establishes a general framework for functional reactivation of destabilized tumor‐suppressive pathways.

items.title: Biomimetic N‐Terminal Homologation of Amino Acids
items.abstract: Homologation is a key tactic used in the lead optimization of small‐molecule pharmaceuticals due to the potent impact such modifications can have on target affinity and physicochemical properties. However, while many elegant homologation strategies have been developed for the synthesis of β 3 ‐amino acids via decarboxylation, preparation of the β 2 ‐amino acid homologues remains underexplored. We report a general biomimetic strategy for the N ‐terminal homologation of amino acids using photoredox catalysis. Key to the success of this approach is a radical translocation cascade driven by single‐electron transfer. This methodology provides streamlined access to a range of cyclic and acyclic β 2 ‐amino acids and phosphonates, providing new synthetic opportunities within drug discovery programs.

items.title: Chemical Diversity, Genomic Basis, and Biological Activities of Secondary Metabolites Produced by Scedosporium Species
items.abstract: Scedosporium species are environmental filamentous fungi that cause respiratory infections in susceptible hosts, especially patients with cystic fibrosis (CF), as well as disseminated infections in the case of immunodeficiency. These fungi are life-threatening pathogens due to their limited susceptibility to the current antifungal drugs. Nevertheless, little is known about their pathogenic mechanisms. Fungal respiratory pathogens produce a wide range of secondary metabolites (SMs) that play an important role in the pathogenesis of infections by enabling the fungus to evade the host immune response, interact with other components of the lung microbiome, or acquire iron. According to their biosynthetic pathways, SMs belong to different chemical classes. This review summarizes the available data on SMs produced by Scedosporium species, including their potential biological activities and biosynthetic metabolic pathways, with a focus on the major chemical classes: (i) nonribosomal peptides; (ii) polyketides; (iii) terpenoids and meroterpenoids; and (iv) hybrid compounds produced by polyketide synthase−nonribosomal peptide synthases (PKS-NRPSs). The recent availability of genome sequences from different Scedosporium species has paved the way for deciphering the biosynthesis pathways of their SMs. This should also facilitate faster progress in unveiling the vast diversity of Scedosporium SMs, as demonstrated by the analysis of Scedosporium biosynthetic gene clusters comprising PKS-NRPS-encoding genes.

items.title: Discovery and Clinical Development of Ceperognastat, a Low-Dose, CNS-Penetrant O -Linked N -Acetylglucosaminidase Inhibitor
items.abstract: Postmortem brain examinations in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) reveal β-amyloid plaques, neurofibrillary tangles resulting from tau protein aggregation, and neuronal and synaptic loss, which collectively impair brain function. O-linked N-acetylglucosami-nidase (OGA) is an enzyme that removes O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc) from proteins including tau. In animal tauopathy models, OGA inhibition was shown to increase O-GlcNAc−tau levels, leading to reduced tau hyperphosphorylation and aggregation. These results inspired efforts to develop OGA inhibitors for the treatment of AD and tauopathies. Here we report the discovery and clinical development of ceperognastat (LY3372689), a low-dose, CNS-penetrant OGA inhibitor that has been evaluated in a completed phase II study in patients with early symptomatic AD.

items.title: Ferrous Ion-Activatable Thiol-Selective Covalent-Reversible Electrophiles to Enhance Erastin-Induced Ferroptosis
items.abstract: Ferroptosis is a unique form of cell death and characterized by the ferrous ion-based Fenton reaction to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) of lipid. However, ferroptosis could be inhibited by biothiols (i.e., GSH) because of their antioxidant function. Herein, we report a ferrous ion-activatable thiol-selective covalent electrophile to enhance Erastin-induced ferroptosis. This activatable electrophile containing a key pharmacophore of the endoperoxide bond remained caged and did not react with biothiols until it was activated by a ferrous ion to generate a highly reactive Michael acceptor, 1, 2-diacetylethylene. Notably, the activated thiol-selective electrophile reacted with thiols in a reversible covalent manner. Finally, a compound library of activatable electrophiles was constructed, generating a lead compound (17h) that did not inhibit cell growth but enhanced the Erastin-induced ferroptosis. Together, this study provides not only a novel mechanism to design activatable covalent electrophiles but also a unique covalent reversible ligand showing high reactivity and specificity toward biothiols.

items.title: Discovery of Pan-KRAS Inhibitor GNE-6226: Harnessing an Aminopyridine Pharmacophore to Broadly Target KRAS Mutants
items.abstract: RAS is the most frequently mutated oncogene in human cancer, yet limited treatments are available for patients with mutations beyond KRAS G12C. While pan-RAS inhibitors have entered the clinic to benefit a broader population of patients harboring RAS mutations, we sought to develop pan-KRAS inhibitors (selective for KRAS over HRAS and NRAS) that may offer an improved therapeutic index. Herein, we describe the discovery of GNE-6226, a pan-KRAS inhibitor exhibiting exquisite potency across a range of KRAS mutants. Using a structure-based design, we transitioned from mutant-selective inhibitors to a pan-KRAS inhibition profile, identifying the aminopyridine headgroup as a crucial motif. This headgroup establishes key ligand−protein interactions with conserved residues within the switch-II pocket while avoiding steric clashes with KRAS mutants. We present extensive cellular and in vivo profiling of GNE-6226, highlighting its robust MAPK pathway modulation and tumor growth inhibition in vivo across G12V- and G12D-mutant xenograft mouse models.

items.title: Dual Inhibitors of Brain Carbonic Anhydrases and Cholinesterases Protect against Amyloid-β-Induced Neurotoxicity and Improve Cognitive Function in Mice
items.abstract: This work introduces tacrine-based multitarget ligands inhibiting brain carbonic anhydrases (CAs) and cholinesterases (ChEs) for targeting distinct yet interrelated pathological aspects of Alzheimer’s disease (AD): cholinergic dysfunction and amyloid-β-induced neurovascular, oxidative, and inflammatory stress. Modular optimization identified a subset of compounds inhibiting target CAs with KI values of 1.6−89.6 nM and cholinesterases with IC50 values of 0.53−113 nM. In silico simulations confirmed dual-target binding with retention of canonical interactions and formation of complementary stabilizing contacts. In RA−SH−SY5Y cells exposed to oligomeric amyloid-β, selected compounds effectively reduced cytotoxicity and reactive oxygen species production while preserving mitochondrial integrity. In a mouse social recognition memory model, dual inhibitors enhanced memory retention up to 48 h, outperforming the single-target approach.
