Here, we present TH-CADD, a high-performance computer-aided drug discovery platform built on the New Generation Tianhe supercomputer. TH-CADD integrates target preparation and analysis, ligand preparation, similarity search, molecular docking, postdocking analysis, and molecular dynamics simulation into a unified computational framework. A Django-Vue architecture deployed on Tianhe Cloud provides web-based access to high-performance computing (HPC) resources through scheduler-controlled execution. By organizing established CADD tools into a coherent workflow, TH-CADD supports accessible, traceable, and scalable computational drug discovery. The platform supports multiple molecular input formats, automated preprocessing, large-scale screening, and molecular dynamics evaluation of selected protein–ligand complexes. TH-CADD’s contribution lies in the system-level integration, automated job management, and scalable execution of established computational methods on the New Generation Tianhe supercomputer, together with a unified workflow view that supports direct cross-module reuse of compatible task outputs.

items.title: TRIM28-mediated SUMOylation of ERG at K389 conveys PARP inhibitor resistance by inhibiting 53BP1 expression in CRPC
items.abstract: Both intrinsic and acquired resistance to poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPis) have emerged as a formidable challenge in clinical practice. Here, we report that the transcription factor E-twenty-six (Ets)-related gene ( ERG ) was highly expressed in PARPi-resistant prostate cancer and was correlated with PARPi resistance in castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) cells. ERG was posttranslationally modified by tripartite motif-containing 28 (TRIM28) as SUMOylation at lysine 389 (K389), which promotes DNA homologous recombination repair (HRR), thereby weakening the efficacy of PARPis. Mechanistically, the SUMOylation of ERG (K389) inhibited protein degradation mediated by the SPOP-mediated ubiquitin-proteasome pathway, thereby stabilizing the protein. Concurrently, this posttranslational modification increased HRR capacity by inhibiting 53BP1 expression, which in turn reduced PARPi sensitivity. Blockade of ERG K389 SUMOylation can effectively impair DNA repair efficacy and overcome PARPi resistance. These findings suggest that TRIM28-mediated ERG SUMOylation conveys resistance to PARPis by inhibiting 53BP1 expression; combined TRIM28/ERG targeting and PARPi therapy may improve outcomes for ERG-positive CRPC patients.

items.title: TLR5 drives metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis through lipid- and flagellin-induced hepatocyte injury signaling
items.abstract: Liver fibrosis is a strong predictor of clinical outcomes in metabolic dysfunction–associated steatohepatitis (MASH). Fibrosis is a consequence of persistent liver cell injury and inflammation in which Toll-like receptors (TLRs) play a key initiating role. Here, we test the hypothesis that TLR5 is involved in the development of MASH and fibrosis using a combination of clinical data from multiple independent patient cohorts, single-cell liver transcriptomics, and human in vitro and ex vivo models. Hepatic TLR5 expression, but not TLR2 or TLR4, is associated with liver fibrosis and mortality. Plasma levels of TLR5’s cognate ligand flagellin are increased in MASH with advanced fibrosis and fall with liver disease improvement. Mechanistically, we identify two parallel TLR5-mediated routes to hepatocyte injury: one elicited by flagellin and the other indirectly by lipid injury. Furthermore, hepatocyte TLR5 inhibition abrogates paracrine activation of hepatic stellate cells to suppress collagen production. This is also seen ex vivo in patient-derived precision-cut liver slices where TLR5 inhibition significantly reduces lipid-induced collagen deposition. These findings reveal a new role for TLR5 signaling, specifically in the development of advanced MASH fibrosis and may offer a novel disease-specific therapeutic approach.

items.title: Membrane-confined self-assembly enables localized bioorthogonal prodrug activation and selective cancer therapy
items.abstract: Bioorthogonal prodrug activation offers a promising approach for site-specific drug release, significantly reducing the systemic toxicity associated with conventional chemotherapy. However, challenges remain in precisely controlling prodrug activation at the target site while maintaining optimal selectivity, reactivity, and potency. Here, we report a dual-targeting peptide, TzFFY p HH, that integrates on-membrane enzyme-instructed self-assembly (EISA) with bioorthogonal chemistry to enable selective chemotherapy. Exploiting the overexpression of alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) on cancer cells, TzFFY p HH selectively anchors and self-assembles on the cancer cell membrane, enriching tetrazine (Tz) handles that act as bioorthogonal reactors to activate a trans -cyclooctene (TCO)-caged prodrug (TCO-Dox) for precise drug release. Upon topical administration, TzFFY p HH forms a hydrogel at subcutaneous tumor sites, enabling in situ prodrug activation for effective tumor inhibition. Notably, this localized chemotherapy elicits a potent antitumor immune response, which, when combined with anti-programmed death-1 antibody (αPD-1), synergistically potentiates therapeutic outcomes. By coupling supramolecular self-assembly with bioorthogonal reactivity on the cell membrane, this work establishes a chemically programmable platform for spatiotemporally controlled prodrug activation and provides a general strategy for integrating localized chemotherapy with immunotherapy.

items.title: USP8 inhibition suppresses prostate tumorigenesis via promoting RICTOR degradation to inhibit mTORC2 signaling
items.abstract: RICTOR plays an essential role in regulating mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2) kinase activity, but it remains largely elusive how RICTOR is aberrantly activated in human prostate cancer (PrCa). Here, we identify RICTOR as a substrate of Cullin 3–based ubiquitin ligase adaptor SPOP, an important tumor suppressor in PrCa. SPOP deficiency or cancer-derived SPOP mutations disrupt SPOP-mediated degradation of RICTOR, thereby promoting PrCa progression. Furthermore, we identify USP8 as its upstream deubiquitinase, and inhibition of USP8 specifically suppresses RICTOR/mTORC2 activity without affecting mTORC1. As such, the USP8 inhibitor induces RICTOR degradation concomitant with marked tumor suppression in vivo. Hence, these findings reveal an SPOP-USP8-RICTOR regulatory circuit that underlies PrCa tumorigenesis and provides a rationale for targeting RICTOR via USP8 inhibition as a therapeutic strategy for patients with PrCa.

items.title: In vivo screening reveals new regulators of natural killer cell development and functional response to acute cytomegalovirus infection
items.abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells are critical innate immune effectors in antiviral and antitumor responses. However, the factors governing NK cell development and function remain incompletely understood. To address this, we adopted an in vivo screening approach, generating a panel of mice deficient in genes differentially expressed across NK cell maturation stages or following viral infection. We performed a combinational screen comprising baseline immunophenotyping and mouse cytomegalovirus (MCMV) challenge. We identified regulators of NK cell development, including transcriptional regulators and proteins with putative trafficking functions. MCMV challenge studies additionally identified proteins that affected antiviral immunity independently of NK cell phenotypes, including a previously undescribed regulator of NK cell degranulation, synaptotagmin-like protein 3. Identified genes exhibited a trend toward reduced tolerance to loss of function in large-scale human sequencing studies and evidence for reduced NK cell numbers in a cohort of patients with immunodeficiency. Together, these findings provide a resource of NK-expressed genes important for NK cell maturation and function, with relevance to human health.

items.title: Hydrogen radical-participating spatiotemporal sequential therapy via hypoxia aggravation for hypoxia-amplified immunotherapy
items.abstract: The hypoxic characteristics of the tumor microenvironment and endogenous antioxidant defenses compromise the efficacy of oxygen-consuming oxidative therapy, positioning oxygen-free reductive stress as a new paradigm in tumor treatment. Nevertheless, the immunosuppressive characteristics of hypoxia and reductive stress pose significant challenges for advancing reductive stress-induced immunotherapy. Here, we constructed a hydrogen radical (H•) generator synergistically activated by near-infrared light and thiols, and first elucidated that photocatalytic H•-mediated reductive stress can elicit a robust antitumor immune response via the H•-featured mechanism. Nanoplatform HA@UFTL was engineered using lactate oxidase as an ideal H• partner, with the synergistic contribution enabling cross-amplified antitumor immunotherapy. The H•-participating spatiotemporal sequential strategy highlights a triple spatiotemporal sequential cascade, including dual sequential hypoxia exacerbation, sequential oxidative-reductive stress, and sequential organelle damage. By aggravating rather than alleviating hypoxia, HA@UFTL overcomes immunosuppression induced by hypoxia and reductive stress with H• as a universal building block, providing new insights for hypoxia-based immunotherapy.

items.title: Nanoparticle-enabled gene delivery for pediatric brain tumors
items.abstract: Pediatric brain tumors are the leading cause of disease-related death in children, yet effective treatment remains a major clinical challenge. These aggressive tumors have limited therapeutic options capable of crossing the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and frequently recur due to genetic or epigenetic alterations and treatment resistance. Gene therapy offers a promising strategy to address these limitations by modifying gene expression, correcting mutations, or introducing functional genes. Nanoparticle (NP) delivery systems facilitate this approach by protecting genetic cargo and enabling BBB penetration and tumor-specific uptake. This review summarizes current genetic engineering strategies and NP-based delivery systems for pediatric brain tumors, including their design principles and delivery mechanisms, highlights key therapeutic approaches under preclinical and clinical investigations, and discusses the major challenges and future directions in NP-mediated gene therapy for pediatric neuro-oncology. By critically evaluating these developments, we aim to underscore the transformative potential of NP-mediated gene therapies in reshaping treatment paradigms and improving outcomes and quality of life for children.

items.title: CHELATE: High-precision structure prediction for metalloproteins
items.abstract: Accurate prediction of ligand binding modes in non-heme metalloproteins remains challenging because conventional docking methods often fail to correctly identify poses with accurate metal-coordination geometries. Here, we introduce CHELATE, a machine learning-based post-docking filter that predicts the root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) of ligand metal-binding groups (MBGs) to filter out inaccurate poses and prioritise those with native-like metal coordination. We curated a dataset of over 50,000 metalloprotein–ligand systems spanning more than 20 metal ions, split based on protein-ligand similarity to enable evaluation on structurally distinct systems. Cross-docking benchmarks showed that, although existing docking methods often sample poses with accurate metal-binding group placement, they fail to rank them correctly. We quantify this using the MBG success rate, defined as the fraction of top-ranked poses with an MBG RMSD ≤ 1 Å relative to the crystal structure. Applying CHELATE as a post-docking filter improved MBG success rates from a baseline of 18% across all systems to 32%, 34%, and 40% for AutoDock Vina, smina, and GNINA, respectively, for systems for which at least one docking pose passed the filter. Feature importance analysis indicates that CHELATE predictions are informed by chemically meaningful features associated with metal coordination. Representative case studies illustrate the scope and limitations of CHELATE. Its low computational cost and compatibility with existing docking workflows make it a promising filtering strategy for a broad range of structure prediction methods, including protein–ligand co-folding models.

items.title: Protein chemical shift prediction in web browsers: seven major programs ported, benchmarked, and studied for what they help to reveal about NMR structures, AlphaFold models and molecular simulations
items.abstract: Motivation. Predicting NMR chemical shifts from protein structures is routine in structure validation, resonance assignment and the analysis of molecular dynamics simulations, but the available programs come as platform-specific executables, aging software stacks or upload-based servers, and some are no longer distributed. Results. Assisted by Claude Code, I ported seven chemical shift predictors to run entirely in the web browser with no installation and no data leaving the user's computer: UCBShift-X, SHIFTX2, SPARTA+, PPM_One (with its MD-ensemble variant PPM), CamShift, LEGOLAS and the random-coil predictor POTENCI. The web apps share similar interfaces that work for single structures or ensembles (from NMR, MD simulations and emulations, docking poses, etc.), and each reproduces its original implementation to printed precision. On 153 proteins with BMRB assignments, UCBShift-X is the most accurate structure-based predictor (best for 71 % of proteins), followed by SHIFTX2, SPARTA+ and PPM_One, and then by LEGOLAS and CamShift. However, I found that the input structure matters more than the predictor: For every program, AlphaFold models and crystal structures give about 15 % lower errors than the deposited NMR structures! Averaging over MD trajectories also improves most programs, especially CamShift, LEGOLAS and PPM. The ranking holds on three recently determined NMR structures not yet released at the PDB/BMRB, and comparing predictions on the NMR and AlphaFold 3 models shows which parts of each structure the shifts support and which parts they flag as potential outliers or assignment errors. Finally, I ported SLAE-CS, a very recent neural network that predicts only backbone 15N shifts: on the deposited NMR structures it is about as accurate as UCBShift-X, but on AlphaFold models and crystal structures its 15N errors are 17–28 % lower. Availability. Static web applications at https://pdbms.altervista.org/web-csp/ within the PDB Manipulation Suite platform (https://pdbms.altervista.org). For a full report with all methods, tables and data, see the semi-automated, extended version of this preprint at https://pdbms.altervista.org/web-csp/predictions_report/.

items.title: 1,2,4,5-Tetraoxane Conjugates as a Novel Ferrous Iron-Activatable Platform for Targeted Tumor Drug Delivery
items.abstract: Elevated intracellular labile ferrous iron is a hallmark of many cancers and can activate endoperoxide-containing molecules through Fenton chemistry. We developed a ferrous iron-activatable drug conjugate (FeADC) platform based on a 1,2,4,5-tetraoxane scaffold for tumor-selective drug delivery. Doxorubicin-loaded tetraoxane conjugates release their payload in the presence of Fe(II) via tandem endoperoxide reduction and retro-Michael elimination. These FeADCs exhibited potent antiproliferative activity across cancer cell lines with dysregulated iron metabolism while displaying markedly improved selectivity over doxorubicin in nontumorigenic cells. Fluorescence microscopy confirmed the efficient intracellular release of doxorubicin in HCT116 colorectal cancer cells. Moreover, in a colorectal cancer xenograft model, the tetraoxane conjugate achieved tumor growth inhibition comparable to that of doxorubicin administered at an equivalent dose. Collectively, these findings establish the 1,2,4,5-tetraoxane scaffold as a promising ferrous iron-responsive platform for tumor-activated prodrugs, enabling targeted drug release and potentially improving the therapeutic index of anticancer agents.

items.title: Collective Stereodivergent Synthesis of the [13]Graphanyl Isomers: Applications as Drug Analogues
items.abstract: Conformationally locked polycycles represent an attractive class of compounds in drug discovery campaigns for medicinal chemists. The three-dimensionality of these scaffolds can result in unique topologies and well-defined exit vectors, enhancing pharmacokinetic profiles and protein interactions that lead to the development of clinically approved therapeutics. One such scaffold that has remained largely underexplored is [13]Graphane, as the synthesis of its four stereoisomers is nontrivial. Herein, we describe a collective stereodivergent synthesis of all the stereoisomers of the [13]Graphane, their central derivatization with diverse functional groups for downstream functionalization. From a common epoxide precursor, we exploit dienyne ring closing cascade metathesis and stereospecific hydrogenation to build each isomer. By performing a decarboxylative radical coupling study on all the [13]G–COOH stereoisomers, we report ring inversions of the ccc- and ctt-[13]G radicals and study these by density functional theory calculations. Finally, we leveraged the different centrally functionalized [13]Graphanes to synthesize Adamantane-based drug analogues as examples of applications in drug design.

items.title: Synthesis, Structure, and In Vivo Evaluation of Analgesic Activity of N‐propargyl‐2‐methyl‐trans‐decahydroquinolin‐4‐one Oximes
items.abstract: Two new N‐propargyl derivatives of trans ‐2‐methyl‐decahydroquinolin‐4‐one and their corresponding oximes were synthesized from individual trans ‐epimers via N‐alkylation with propargyl bromide followed by oximation. A solvent‐minimized mechanochemical protocol enabled rapid conversion of the ketones into the target oximes within 3–5 min and provided isolated yields of about 96%, while a solution‐phase control using the same base required 5 h. Single‐crystal X‐ray diffraction confirmed the structures and stereochemistry of all four compounds and showed that oximation proceeds stereoselectively to give exclusively E ‐configured products while preserving the trans ‐fused bicyclic framework. Biological evaluation included an egg albumin denaturation assay, the hot plate test in mice, and acute oral toxicity studies. Both ketones and oximes showed marked protein‐stabilizing activity, with no consistent effect of oximation or C2 methyl‐group orientation in this assay. All four compounds showed increases in mean nociceptive‐response latency at selected time points, while the oximes, particularly those containing an axial methyl group, showed higher mean responses than the corresponding ketones at several early and intermediate time points. Acute oral toxicity studies classified all four compounds as toxicity class IV, with LD 50 values of approximately 1048–1295 mg/kg. Thus, oximation retained the low acute‐toxicity profile of the N‐propargylated ketones while preserving biological activity.

items.title: A Tailor-Made Guanidine Ionizable Lipid as a Bifunctional mRNA Carrier and Nitric Oxide Production Inhibitor
items.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are the leading clinical platform for mRNA delivery, yet their capacity to trigger macrophage-driven inflammatory responses remains a fundamental barrier to therapeutic safety and efficacy. Here, we introduce a design principle in which a tailor-made nitric oxide (NO) inhibitory motif is embedded directly into the ionizable lipid, creating a single molecular scaffold that simultaneously delivers mRNA and suppresses macrophage inflammation. Screening of a focused acyl-guanidine library in LPS-induced peritoneal macrophages identified G9 as a potent NO inhibitor and reprogrammed macrophage polarization from the pro-inflammatory M1 to the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. Conjugation of the G9 headgroup to a lipid tail yielded G9-1, an NO-inhibitory ionizable lipid that retains anti-inflammatory activity and preferentially delivers mRNA to pulmonary vascular endothelial cells and alveolar macrophages in vivo. In a murine model of acute lung injury (ALI), G9-1 LNPs loaded with IL-10 mRNA reduce pulmonary immune cell infiltration, suppress inflammatory cytokine production, and attenuate systemic inflammation. These results establish NO inhibition as an actionable molecular design principle for intrinsically anti-inflammatory LNPs and position G9-1 as a dual-function ionizable lipid for safer and more effective mRNA therapeutics.

items.title: MS Binding Assays for the Orthosteric Binding Site of Tetronarce Californica Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptor (nAChR) With (−)‐Epibatidine as Reporter Ligand
items.abstract: MS Binding Assays for the orthosteric binding site of Tetronarce californica nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (nAChR) as an alternative to radioligand binding assays are presented. As a reporter ligand, at first, rac ‐epibatidine was employed, as in radioligand binding assays often using rac ‐[ 3 H]epibatidine. For the quantification of rac ‐epibatidine in the binding samples, a fast and highly sensitive LC‐ESI‐MS/MS method has been developed. This method was finally used in saturation experiments with rac ‐epibatidine but also with its (+)‐ and (−)‐enantiomers as MS markers. Based on (−)‐epibatidine as the most affine ligand of these three compounds, also competitive MS Binding Assays have been established and used for the characterization of the binding affinity of a set of reference compounds. The affinities obtained with these new MS Binding Assays are in good accordance with those reported from radioligand binding experiments. This demonstrates that the new MS Binding Assays, in particular with (−)‐epibatidineas MS marker, represent a valuable and powerful alternative to radioligand binding assays frequently used so far for this purpose. Furthermore, the feasibility of simultaneous MS Binding Assays, in which (−)‐epibatidine and BTCP address the orthosteric and the ion channel binding site of the nAChR, respectively, in the same saturation experiment, has been demonstrated.

items.title: Deoxofluorination of Formyl-Substituted Boronates: A Practical Entry to Difluoromethyl-Containing Organoboron Building Blocks
items.abstract: A synthetic approach to CHF 2 -substituted aromatic, heteroaromatic, alkenyl, and cyclopropyl boronates was described, based on deoxofluorination of the corresponding aldehydes with the boron atom temporarily masked as a trifluoroborate. In a telescoped sequence, formylsubstituted pinacol boronates were converted into triethylammonium trifluoroborates with Et 3 N·3HF, deoxofluorinated with Deoxo-Fluor and Et 3 N·3HF in CH 2 Cl 2 or CH 2 Cl 2 – THF, and re-esterified with pinacol in the presence of TMSCl; isolated potassium trifluoroborates could be used as well. Two complementary sets of conditions, selected according to the electronic nature of the substrate, provided 36 target difluoromethyl-substituted boronates in 26–82% yield on up to 5 g scale. Pyridine, quinoline, thiophene, benzothiophene, thiazole, and pyrazole derivatives were obtained, including a boron analog of the 3-(difluoromethyl)-1-methylpyrazole core of succinate dehydrogenase inhibitor (SDHI) fungicides. The products underwent oxidation, Suzuki – Miyaura coupling, and metal-free amination to give difluoromethyl-substituted phenols, biaryls, and (hetero)aromatic amines; in this way, biaryls bearing ketone and aliphatic hydroxy groups, which are not compatible with deoxofluorination, were obtained.

items.title: Pharmaceutical wastewater remediation: occurrence, risk assessment, biological and advanced treatment technologies, and regulatory drivers
items.abstract: Pharmaceutically active compounds (PhACs) reach surface waters through municipal sewage, hospital effluent, and discharges from drug manufacturing, and conventional treatment removes many of them only partially. In this review, we bring together measured occurrence, risk, and performance data to compare conventional, biological, bioremediation, and advanced physicochemical options. A global survey of 1,052 river sites in 104 countries found at least one active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) above a level considered safe at 25.7% of sites, and treated effluent from a plant serving about 90 bulk-drug manufacturers contained up to 31,000 µg/L ciprofloxacin. Across 87 reported full-scale observations, conventional activated sludge removed a median of 92% of ibuprofen, 62% of sulfamethoxazole and only 11% of carbamazepine, with large seasonal and plant-to-plant variation. For high-strength industrial effluent, anaerobic and aerobic biological trains removed 71–97% of chemical oxygen demand (COD) at pilot and full scale, whereas ozonation alone removed only 10–56% and works better as a pre-treatment. Fungal reactors, high-rate algal ponds, and novel constructed wetlands have removed 40–98% of target PhACs in real wastewater but remain at pilot scale. For trace APIs, ozonation followed by biological post-treatment, and powdered or granular activated carbon both meet the 80% removal benchmark at full scale for about 0.07–0.27 CHF/m3; Fenton, solar, electrochemical, and sonochemical processes are better suited to concentrated, low-volume streams such as manufacturing effluent, hospital effluent, and membrane concentrates. Switzerland has required this “quaternary” treatment at selected plants since 2016; Directive (EU) 2024/3019 extends it to large EU plants by 2045, with pharmaceutical and cosmetics producers paying at least 80% of the cost, and Directive (EU) 2026/805 adds eight pharmaceuticals to the EU priority substances list. No single process removes every API. The most promising routes are hybrid trains that combine biological pre-treatment with oxidation or adsorption, together with treatment of hospital and manufacturing streams at source. Transformation products, polar persistent APIs, mixture toxicity, and selection for antimicrobial resistance remain major knowledge gaps.

items.title: Development of Covalent Cyclic Peptide Ligands for the NUP98::KDM5A Oncofusion through Sulfur(VI) Fluoride Reactivity Tuning
items.abstract: Covalent labeling of nucleophilic amino acids is a useful strategy for liganding ‘difficult-to-drug’ protein targets. Targeting cysteine has been highly successful because of its high nucleophilicity. Covalent ligands that modify lysine residues can provide broader proteome coverage for covalent inhibition. Sulfur(VI) fluorides are lysine-reactive electrophiles with highly tunable intrinsic reactivities, making them well-suited as covalent reactivity handles. Association of the NUP98::KDM5A fusion oncoprotein with chromatin via the PHD3 domain of KDM5A is a key driver of acute myeloid leukemia. Despite its therapeutic relevance, there are currently no high-quality chemical probes for this domain, owing to the solvent-exposed and extended H3K4me3-binding region. Here, we report the development of lysine-reactive cyclic peptides targeting KDM5A PHD3 via a sulfur(VI) fluoride reactivity-tuning approach. Through sulfur(VI) fluoride electrophile SAR, we identified a p-substituted aryl fluorosulfate that balanced PHD3 labeling, hydrolytic stability, and covalent adduct persistence. Using the optimized aryl fluorosulfate electrophile, we report covalent ligands designed to target KDM5A PHD3 and demonstrate their engagement with the NUP98::KDM5A fusion oncoprotein in cell lysate. Proteomic analysis also identified the H3K4me3 reader domain PHF23 as a target of the covalent cyclic peptides, indicating that these compounds may provide a starting point for developing ligands for the PHF23 PHD domain. This study highlights sulfur(VI) fluoride reactivity tuning as an effective approach for engaging ‘difficult-to-drug’ proteins.

items.title: Organocatalytic Asymmetric Multicomponent Dearomatizing Povarov Reactions
items.abstract: Herein, we disclose an organocatalytic asymmetric three-component dearomatizing Povarov reaction for the efficient and atom-economical construction of polycyclic chiral N-heterocycles containing a quaternary carbon stereocenter in generally good to excellent efficiency (up to 99% yield), diastereoselectivity (up to >50:1 dr), and enantioselectivity (up to 98% ee). Moreover, this catalytic asymmetric dearomatization in a multicomponent operation features the highly efficient construction of five continuous stereocenters and four new chiral rings in one step, proven biological activity of the products, and theoretical calculations of the reaction mechanism.

items.title: Inhalable Redispersible Gallium-Phenolic Complex Reprograms Lung Microbiota and ROS-NETs Crosstalk to Prevent Radiation-Induced Lung Injury
items.abstract: RILI remains a major complication of thoracic radiotherapy, in which reactive oxygen species (ROS) and altered pulmonary microbial signatures may contribute to neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) formation and tissue injury. Current preventive and therapeutic strategies fail to adequately address these interconnected pathways. Here, we report an inhalable, redispersible gallium-luteolin-PVP complex (PLGa) designed to prevent RILI by targeting ROS and lung microbiota-associated inflammatory signaling linked to NET formation. The PVP-stabilized metal-phenolic network confers exceptional colloidal stability, enabling PLGa to efficiently penetrate airway mucus, reach distal lung regions, including alveolar spaces, and achieve prolonged retention after inhalation. Gallium within PLGa restores pulmonary microbial homeostasis by suppressing pathogenic bacteria while promoting short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production derived from potential probiotics, thereby inhibiting LPS-TLR4-NF-κB-NETs-associated inflammatory signaling. Concurrently, luteolin effectively scavenges ROS and directly suppresses NETosis. These synergistic actions protect mitochondrial homeostasis and modulate radiation-induced damage. In a murine RILI model, inhaled PLGa, administered prophylactically, significantly mitigated acute inflammation, reduced NET formation, and attenuated the progression of chronic pulmonary fibrosis, as validated by multiomics analyses (transcriptomics, metabolomics, and 16S rRNA sequencing). Importantly, PLGa demonstrated excellent biocompatibility and minimal systemic toxicity. Collectively, this study identifies PLGa as a locally deliverable dual-pathway preventive platform that modulates the ROS-lung microbiota-NETs crosstalk. This work provides mechanistic insights and a promising translational strategy for the prevention of radiation-induced lung injury.

items.title: HiFiPL-Bench: A Fidelity-First and Bias-Aware Benchmark for Diagnosing Protein–Ligand Scoring Functions
items.abstract: Accurate prediction of protein–ligand binding affinities is fundamental to structure-based drug design, yet existing benchmarks are often limited by outdated structural coverage, uncertain local structural fidelity, and physicochemical or protocol-dependent bias. Here, we present HiFiPL-Bench, a fidelity-first and bias-aware benchmark curated from RCSB PDB and BindingDB through hierarchical filtering, manual electron-density validation, affinity verification, and property-matched decoy generation. Across nine representative scoring functions, HiFiPL-Bench revealed reduced performance in scoring, ranking, and most docking evaluations relative to CASF-2016, whereas a controlled screening-like task using computationally generated property-matched decoys produced model-specific gains and losses that altered relative rankings rather than uniformly lowering performance. Model-specific overlap and deoverlap analyses further showed that documented development-data exposure differed substantially among methods and that deoverlapped sensitivity analyses affected models and evaluation tasks nonuniformly. Together, these findings indicate that performance estimates remain sensitive to starting-structure curation, task-specific preparation, data set composition, decoy design, benchmark protocol, and recoverable development-data exposure. HiFiPL-Bench therefore provides a reusable diagnostic framework for evaluating scoring-function performance in a structurally curated and bias-aware benchmark setting.

items.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence Prescreening with Molecular Dynamics for the Design of Peptide-Based WWP1 Inhibitors as Promising Therapeutic Agents Against Breast Cancer, Including the Triple-Negative Subtype
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Breast cancer (BC) is the second most common noncutaneous cancer and the second leading cause of cancer-related death in women. BC is classified into three primary subtypes, with triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) having the poorest prognosis because it lacks specific targetable markers. Preclinical studies on TNBC indicated a common occurrence of diminished tumor-suppressor activity of PTEN, activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. Notably, published studies reveal that the WWP1 enzyme plays a pivotal role in driving PTEN degradation via ubiquitination, unveiling a promising therapeutic target for treating TNBC. In the search of new WWP1 inhibitors, we used artificial intelligence (AI)-driven computational strategies for de novo design of peptide-based WWP1 inhibitors and identified a hexapeptide, termed WI23-B , which demonstrated high nanomolar binding affinity to WWP1. In TR-FRET enzymatic assays, WI23-B inhibited WWP1 activity with an IC₅₀ of approximately 11 µM. In MCF7 and MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cell lines, WI23-B showed promising cytotoxic efficacy, particularly in combination with the PI3K inhibitor BYL719, also when it was loaded into nanocapsules. Collectively, these findings highlight WI23-B as a promising lead peptide with potent WWP1 inhibitory activity and synergistic antiproliferative effects when combined with PI3K inhibitors. While further structural optimization is required to enhance its potency and pharmacological properties, our results provide a strong foundation for the development of next-generation WWP1 inhibitors. Such agents have the potential to reshape therapeutic strategies for BC and TNBC by enabling more effective and less toxic treatment regimens, ultimately reducing the reliance on high-dose chemotherapy and minimizing adverse effects.

items.title: Photoinduced Decavanadate-Catalyzed Radical Polar Crossover Enables Selective C(sp3)–H Amination
items.abstract: Herein, we report the integration of decavanadate-mediated hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) photocatalysis with a radical-polar crossover (RPC) manifold to achieve efficient C(sp3)–N cross-coupling. This uniquely dual-functional photocatalytic system addresses the long-standing chemoselectivity limitation of conventional radical-based C–H amination, enabling the direct coupling of C(sp3)–H substrates with readily oxidizable primary heteroaryl amines that are generally incompatible with established RPC protocols. Xanthene, thioxanthene, and 9,10-dihydroacridine derivatives serve as reliable C(sp3)–H precursors in this transformation, affording diverse N-alkylated heteroarylamine products with broad substrate generality and excellent functional group tolerance. The synthetic practicality of this decavanadate photocatalytic strategy is further validated by its robust reactivity under natural sunlight irradiation, scalable gram-scale synthetic capability, and catalyst reusability. Systematic mechanistic investigations corroborate a cascade reaction pathway involving initial decavanadate-triggered HAT activation and subsequent radical-to-carbocation polarity inversion via RPC. Notably, this protocol is also readily applicable to secondary arylamines. Furthermore, the facile late-stage functionalization of structurally complex natural products and pharmaceutical molecules demonstrates the excellent synthetic utility and prospective application value of this method in drug modification.

items.title: Inhibitors of Gut Bacterial l -Dopa Decarboxylation with Reduced Susceptibility to Host Metabolism
items.abstract: Microorganisms in the human gut influence the efficacy and metabolism of host-targeted small molecule therapeutics, including the frontline Parkinson’s disease drug levodopa (l-dopa). Previous work has identified a mechanism-based inhibitor of gut bacterial decarboxylases that degrade l-dopa, α-fluoromethyltyrosine (AFMT). However, early experiments with AFMT in rodent models suggested undesirable in vivo metabolism by host tyrosine hydroxylase, producing α-fluoromethyldopa, a metabolite likely to worsen Parkinson’s phenotypes and prevent application as an l-dopa cotreatment. Here, we demonstrate oxidation of AFMT to α-fluoromethyldopa in vitro by recombinant human tyrosine hydroxylase. We then develop AFMT analogues that retain activity against bacterial decarboxylases but have reduced susceptibility to host hydroxylation. Suitable arenes for inhibitor design were identified using assays with commercially available noncanonical amino acids, which revealed aryl difluorination as a promising modification. Difluoroaryl AFMT derivatives are less prone to degradation by tyrosine hydroxylase in vitro yet still inhibit l-dopa metabolism by bacterial decarboxylases. This work exemplifies how substrate reactivity can streamline design of mechanism-based enzyme inhibitors, as well as how constraints posed by the host can be incorporated during development of microbiome-targeted therapeutics. The compounds reported here are promising starting points for future studies in animal models and further exploration of gut bacterial effects on l-dopa treatment efficacy.

items.title: An ingestible, bio-inspired self-powered electrocapsule for in situ ethanol clearance mitigates systemic and neurobehavioral toxicity
Quantum-accurate vibrational and conformational dynamics from small molecules to proteins with machine-learned force fields
Evolution-Guided Engineering of a Process-Compatible Thymidine Phosphorylase for the Scalable Cascade Biosynthesis of 2′/3′-Functionalized Purine Nucleoside Analogs
items.abstract: 2′/3′-Functionalized nucleoside analogs are valuable therapeutic agents and essential building blocks for nucleic acid-based medicines; however, their scalable biocatalytic synthesis remains challenging due to insufficient enzyme robustness under process-relevant conditions. Here, we developed an ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR)-guided engineering strategy integrated with kcat/Km-based virtual screening to generate a process-compatible thymidine phosphorylase (TP) variant for scalable nucleoside biosynthesis. Among the reconstructed candidates, ASR114 exhibited an optimal balance between soluble expression, catalytic efficiency, and thermostability, displaying an apparent half-life of > 386 h at 50 °C compared with 7.7 h for wild-type EcTP. Biochemical characterization demonstrated that ASR114 enhanced catalytic efficiency toward multiple 2′/3′-functionalized pyrimidine nucleoside donors, with up to a 5.4-fold improvement in kcat/Km values. Molecular dynamics simulations suggested that the enhanced catalytic performance of ASR114 was associated with reduced structural flexibility, optimized substrate interactions, and alleviated conformational strain during substrate recognition. By integrating ASR114, EcPNP, and EcADA into a multienzyme cascade system, we established a crude enzyme-based platform for the synthesis of diverse 2′/3′-functionalized purine nucleoside analogs. The optimized process was successfully scaled to 120 L, enabling kilogram-scale synthesis of eight nucleoside analogs with isolated yields of up to 80.3%. This study establishes an evolution-guided framework for engineering process-compatible biocatalysts by integrating ancestral enzyme engineering, computational prioritization, and process-oriented biocatalysis for the scalable synthesis of complex nucleoside analogs.

items.title: Characterizing Biopharmaceutical Materials with Neutron Scattering
items.abstract: Neutron scattering is a critical tool for studying the structure and dynamics of soft matter and biological materials. It is sensitive to light elements and isotope replacement and has high penetration power for insitu experiments. Applications of neutron scattering to investigate pharmaceutical materials have increased steadily in the past two decades. Here, we review research efforts across several important areas relevant to the pharmaceutical industry. These research areas include the structure determination of proteins and excipient molecules in solution, measuring protein−protein interactions, the interfacial behavior of biological materials at air−liquid and solid−liquid interfaces, protein clustering and its impact on the viscosity of concentrated protein solutions, the structures of nanocarriers including lipid nanoparticles, and more. We also introduce the neutron scattering techniques most commonly used for pharmaceutical researchnamely, small-angle neutron scattering, neutron reflectometry, neutron backscattering, and neutron spin echoand comment on common practices for using these techniques to study different materials. Overall, we showcase the various capabilities of neutron scattering to uncover fundamental structure and dynamic information for pharmaceutical materials.

items.title: Novel C–N bond-bridged heterobivalent β-carboline derivatives as lysosome-targeted antitumor agents targeting PPT1: design, synthesis, biological evaluation, and mechanism of action
Structural diversity of carbohydrate-based detergents for membrane protein studies
ATTEC-Based Autophagic Elimination of HBV Core Protein Achieves Potent Viral Suppression
items.abstract: HBV core protein (HBc) plays key roles in the viral lifecycle and hepatocarcinogenesis. While core protein allosteric modulators (CpAMs) have emerged as promising therapeutic agents, they are confronted with the issue of emerging drug resistance and lack the ability to degrade HBc. To surmount these challenges, by leveraging the class II CpAM NVR3-778 and an LC3 ligand ispinesib, we identified TK-96, a first-in-class autophagy-tethering compound (ATTEC) degrader, which induces the degradation of wild-type and drug-resistant HBc via the autophagic-lysosomal pathway. Remarkably, TK-96 exhibited subnanomolar antiviral potency in HepAD38 and HBV-infected HLCZ01 cells, indicating a more than 150-fold improvement in potency compared to NVR3-778. Furthermore, oral administration of TK-96 significantly inhibited viral replication and decreased hepatic HBc, as well as serum HBeAg and HBsAg levels, in an HBV carrier mouse model. Collectively, this study identifies a highly potent HBc degrader and underscores ATTEC-mediated degradation as a novel strategy for anti-HBV therapeutics.

items.title: Selective XPO1/CRM1 Inhibitor Verdinexor (KPT-335): The First and Only Oral Treatment Fully Approved by the U.S. FDA for Canine Lymphoma
Nonclinical Validation of the NexPTM Half-Life Extension Platform Using Human Growth Hormone as a Model Therapeutic Protein
items.abstract: NexP™ is a proprietary carrier platform engineered from human alpha-1 antitrypsin (A1AT) to extend the systemic exposure of therapeutic proteins while retaining biological activity. The NexP™ scaffold incorporates an additional N-linked glycosylation site and a mutation in the reactive center loop designed to reduce its intrinsic protease inhibitory activity. Human growth hormone (hGH) was selected as a model therapeutic protein to evaluate the pharmacological performance, safety profile, and developability of the NexP™ platform. ALT-P1, a long-acting hGH candidate, containing NexP™ at its C-terminus of hGH, was produced in mammalian cells and purified by a series of column chromatography steps. The purified protein was characterized Human growth hormone (hGH) was selected as a model therapeutic protein to evaluate the pharmacological properties, nonclinical safety, and developability of this platform. ALT-P1, an hGH fusion protein containing NexP™ at its C-terminus, was produced in mammalian cells and purified using chromatographic methods. ALT-P1 was characterized by physicochemical analyses, including SDS-PAGE, isoelectric focusing, size-exclusion chromatography, N-linked glycan profiling, and circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy. Binding affinity for the human growth hormone receptor and in vitro activity were further assessed by receptor-binding, MTS-based cell proliferation and luciferase reporter assays. Pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and toxicological profiles were evaluated in Sprague-Dawley rats and cynomolgus monkeys. Systemic exposure to ALT-P1 increased with increasing subcutaneous doses in rats, and pharmacokinetic studies demonstrated sustained systemic exposure in both species. ALT-P1 increased serum insulin-like growth factor I (IGF-1) levels in cynomolgus monkeys and promoted body weight gain and tibial growth in hypophysectomized rats. In a 26 week repeated-dose toxicity study in cynomolgus monkeys, ALT-P1 was generally well tolerated, with a no-observed-adverse-effect level (NOAEL) of 20 mg/kg, the highest dose tested. A GMP-manufactured clinical batch maintained its quality attributes and biological potency during long-term storage. Collectively, these findings support the further development of ALT-P1 as a long-acting hGH candidate and suggest the potential applicability of NexP™ as a half-life-extension platform for other biologic therapeutics.

items.title: Novel Spiroisatin Derivatives Potentially Useful for Preventing Myocardial Reperfusion Injury
items.abstract: Ischemia−reperfusion injury remains a major clinical challenge due to mitochondrial dysfunction and cell death. Here we report a novel series of spiroisatin derivatives as modulators of the mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP) targeted at the c-ring of F1/FO-ATP synthase. Structure−activity relationship analysis identified compound 15j with nanomolar in vitro potency in inhibiting mPTP opening while preserving ATP production. Molecular modeling supported distinct binding interactions within the c subunit of F1/FO-ATP synthase, rationalizing observed pharmacodynamics. Beyond mPTP inhibition, 15j positively modulates mitochondrial quality control pathways, including mitophagy and biogenesis, contributing to sustained mitochondrial homeostasis after reperfusion. These findings establish spiroisatin derivatives as a promising class of cardioprotective agents acting through convergent mechanisms on mitochondrial integrity and quality control.

items.title: Synthesis and Reactivity of Spirocyclopropyl Amines: A New Class of Conformationally Constrained Building Blocks for Drug Discovery
items.abstract: Spirocyclopropyl amines combine the conformational constraint of a spiro center with the electronic character of the cyclopropane ring, yet saturated azaspirocycles bearing two such rings remain scarce. Herein, we report the synthesis of mono- and dispiro-cyclopropyl saturated N-heterocycles from readily available lactams and cyclic imides via the Kulinkovich-de Meijere reaction and its Bertus-Szymoniak modification. The approach covers pyrrolidine, piperidine, piperazine, morpholine, thiomorpholine, thiomorpholine 1,1-dioxide, azepane, and 1,4-diazepane cores, and provides the first examples of dispiro-cyclopropyl piperidines, piperazines, morpholines, and thiomorpholines. Key intermediates were obtained in up to 95 g per run. Reductive Ndebenzylation with H2 over Pd/C in the presence of HCl is complete in 2 h and gives the parent amines in over 85% yield. Each spirocyclopropane lowers the pKa of the ring nitrogen by 0.7-1.5 units and raises logD by 0.4-0.5 units, which is 0.1-0.3 units less than the corresponding gem-dimethyl group. In human liver microsomes, tetramethyl substitution accelerates clearance up to 30-fold, whereas the dispiro benzamides are more stable than both their monospiro and their α-unsubstituted analogues.

items.title: A Dynamic W-VO2/Nb2C Heterostructure-Integrated Scaffold for Photothermally Amplified Sonodynamic Osteosarcoma Therapy and Bone Regeneration
items.abstract: The comprehensive clinical management of osteosarcoma requires an integrated approach to eradicate malignancies and subsequently reconstruct critical-sized bone defects. Herein, a spatiotemporally responsive therapeutic scaffold (WVM@GM) is engineered by embedding a tungsten-doped vanadium dioxide (W-VO2)/niobium carbide (Nb2C) Schottky heterojunction within a porous gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA). Upon near-infrared II (NIR-II) irradiation, the localized temperature rise triggers the metal–insulator phase transition (MIT) in W-VO2, narrowing the bandgap and strengthening the built-in electric field of the heterostructure. This dynamic electronic modulation effectively elevates the density of carriers under ultrasound (US) irradiation, thereby amplifying reactive oxygen species (ROS) production to achieve a highly efficient sonodynamic therapy (SDT). Following neoplastic clearance, modulating the external physical stimuli shifts the scaffold into a proregenerative mode. Specifically, the engineered biophysical microenvironment synergizes with the mechanical stimulation of low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) to drive bone tissue regeneration. Transcriptomic profiling reveals the activation of focal adhesion, Wnt, and PI3K-Akt signaling pathways, actively regulating the coupling of angiogenesis and osteogenic differentiation. In vivo evaluations validate that this platform effectively ablates tumors and successively rebuilds bone defects. Overall, this photothermally modulated heterojunction strategy establishes a rational and sequential paradigm for osteosarcoma therapy and bone tissue regeneration.

items.title: Deuteration as a General Strategy to Enhance Small Molecule-Based Photodynamic Therapy
items.abstract: Utilizing isotope effects has a long history in organic chemistry, and has recently been shown to improve fluorophore photophysics and azobenzene-based photoswitch kinetics. Herein, we report the deuteration of methylene blue (MB) and sulfonated tetraphenyl porphyrin (TPPS), both far-red singlet oxygen sensitizers (SOSs), which boosts the efficiency of reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation by >55%. We applied this knowledge to photodynamic therapeutic (PDT) settings by derivatizing deuterated methylene blue as 1) a ligand for the HaloTag protein (HTP) that leads to faster activation kinetics of the ROS-sensitive TRAAK channel, 2) as a fusion to a peptidic agonist of the glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor (GLP1R) to optically induce ablation of GLP1R-expressing cells, and 3) as a lysosome targeting sensitizer to induce spatiotemporally controlled lysosomal damage through lipid oxidation. Taken together, our strategy provides a simple way to improve well-studied singlet oxygen sensitizers through deuteration and leverages the best performing sensitizer across a set of different biological methodologies to study ion channel gating, as well as organelle and cell ablation.

items.title: Functionalized 2-Substituted Oxetanes through Epoxide Ring Expansion
items.abstract: The value of an oxetane building block depends on access to both its substitution pattern and a functional group that can be modified without consuming the ring. We examined the Corey-Chaykovsky ring expansion of alcohol-derived epoxides as an entry to functionalized 2-substituted oxetanes. Benzyl-protected allylic alcohols provided precursors for varying side-chain branching and substitution at the future C2 center. Productive expansion favored terminal epoxides, whereas substitution at both epoxide carbons strongly restricted oxetane formation and could lead to products consistent with epoxide-to-allylic-alcohol isomerization. Commercial enantiopure epoxides gave both enantiomeric oxetanylmethanol series while preserving the enantiomeric excess. The resulting alcohols were converted into primary and secondary amines, halides, ketones, and a carboxylic acid on multigram scales. The model alcohol was isolated in a single 403 g batch. Extension to homoallylic alcohols gave access to a complementary two-carbon side-chain series, including aminoethyl and iodoethyl derivatives and lithium 2-(oxetan-2-yl)acetate. These results connect precursor topology, stereochemical transfer, and downstream functionalization in a preparative approach to related oxetane building blocks.

items.title: Radical Sorting Enables Semiconductor-Driven Redox-Neutral C(sp 3 )–C(sp 3 ) Cross-Coupling
items.abstract: Selective formation of C(sp3)–C(sp3) bonds from carbon-centered radicals is inherently challenging, because competing radical homocoupling can compromise product selectivity. Here, we combine heterogeneous semiconductor photocatalysis with nickel-mediated radical sorting to achieve redox-neutral C(sp3)–C(sp3) bond formation. Under irradiation, graphitic carbon nitride (gCN) generates alkyl radicals from carboxylic acids and redox-active esters (RAEs) through complementary oxidative and reductive single-electron transfer, respectively, without the need for stoichiometric oxidants or reductants. A nickel catalyst channels these intermediates towards cross-coupling, providing access to a range of products bearing primary and secondary alkyl fragments, including saturated heterocycles, unnatural amino acids, and late-stage functionalization products. Kinetic modelling, radical-clock experiments, electrochemical measurements, and DFT calculations provide insight into the origin of radical sorting. The results are consistent with sequential radical capture at nickel and identify the suppression of homocoupling between RAE-derived radicals as a key kinetic feature.

items.title: PanJAK: predicting selectivity across the JAK family with deep learning
items.abstract: Predicting selectivity between closely related protein targets remains a major challenge in drug discovery. While drug-target affinity (DTA) models typically focus on predicting activity against individual targets, selectivity depends on resolving differences in activity between them. Here, we introduce panJAK, a DTA framework to predict selectivity across the four Janus kinase (JAK) paralogs. The model combines molecular representations with a ligand-conditioned encoding of structurally aligned binding pockets and predicts cross-paralog selectivity from differences in potency without requiring a selectivity-specific training objective. Using a curated dataset of approximately 10,000 compounds, we demonstrate that panJAK improves the quantitative prediction of selectivitywindows compared to established baseline models under scaffold-disjoint evaluation. Errors in individual potency predictions were positively correlated across paralogs and partly cancelled upon subtraction, resulting in more accurate selectivity estimates than expected under independent errors. Although prediction errors increased with chemical novelty, calibrated prediction intervals allowed for the identification of a subset of comparisons with high retrospective directional accuracy. These findings highlight the potential of adapting affinity-prediction models to address quantitative selectivity across homologous targets, supporting compound prioritization based on predicted selectivity profiles and associated reliability of those predictions.

items.title: Hijacking Prenyltransferases and Terpene Synthases for the Enzymatic Synthesis of Non‐natural C19, C24, and C29 Terpenoids
items.abstract: The terpenoid substrate analog 14‐ nor ‐farnesyl pyrophosphate (14‐ nor ‐FPP), lacking the methyl group Me14, was synthesized and enzymatically elongated to 18‐ nor ‐geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (18‐ nor ‐GGPP) and 22‐ nor ‐geranylfarnesyl pyrophosphate (22‐ nor ‐GFPP) by GGPP synthase (GGPPS) and GFPP synthase (GFPPS), respectively. Downstream conversion with 20 diterpene synthases (DTSs) and 10 sesterterpene synthases (StTSs) yielded in total 24 new compounds. Surprisingly, in two cases the substrate analogs were converted by GGPPS and a DTS into nor ‐sesterterpenes (C 24 ), while one combination of GFPPS and a StTS yielded a nor ‐triterpene (C 29 ), demonstrating that the lack of just one carbon allows for extension with one more terpene unit than expected, in contrast to the strict product selectivity observed for GGPPS and GFPPS with normal FPP. For certain enzyme‐substrate pairings, the altered reactivity caused by the absence of Me14 unveiled reaction pathways toward di‐ and sesterterpenes with unique frameworks, for which the mechanisms were investigated through DFT calculations. Absolute configurations of the obtained compounds were determined through chemical correlation with stereoselectively deuterated precursors or through a comparison of optical rotations to those of structurally related natural products containing Me18/Me22.

items.title: Multidisciplinary Design and Characterization of Novel cis- and trans-Ferrocene–Platinum Anticancer Candidates
items.abstract: The limitations of the classical platinum-based drugs (i.e. cisplatin, carboplatin, oxaliplatin), such as adverse side-effects and drug resistance, highlight the need to develop alternative metal-based anticancer compounds. In this context, molecules that bear two pharmacologically active motifs represent a versatile strategy, as they may enhance therapeutic efficacy through synergistic effects, being the synthesis of this type of drugs a promising research field. In the present study, we report the preparation and characterization of new heterometallic Pt(II) complexes bearing the p-ferrocenylaniline ligand ( L ) using K 2 [PtCl 4 ] and cis-[PtCl 2 (DMSO) 2 ] as precursors. The reactions lead to mixtures of the cis and trans isomers of the products [PtCl 2 L 2 ] and [PtCl 2 (DMSO) L ], isolating only one isomer in both cases: the cis isomer for the disubstituted complex and the trans for the monosubstituted product. Different synthetic routes are explored to assess the influence of solvent polarity, reaction time and temperature on the formation of the cis/trans isomers of [PtCl 2 (DMSO) L ]. The results are supported by the thermodynamic stability obtained by DFT calculations, considering none or four explicit solvent molecules of water, acetone or dichloromethane, observing an increase in the Boltzmann distribution of the cis isomer with the solvent polarity. A more in depth study of the non-covalent interactions between the isomers and the solvent molecules is performed. Alternatively, the study of the reaction mechanism to afford the isomers of [PtCl 2 (DMSO) L ] suggests an isomerization process from the cis to the trans isomer through a dissociative pathway, which is enhanced due to the presence of the aromatic moiety in the ferrocene ligand. These findings offer new insight into controlled isomer formation in ferrocene-containing Pt(II) complexes and may contribute to the rational design of heterometallic anticancer agents.

items.title: Small-Molecule Activation Reshapes the Catalytic Conformational Landscape during Ca2+ ATPase Turnover
items.abstract: Understanding how small molecules enhance enzymatic turnover is a central challenge in chemical biology because activation arises from redistribution of transient populations that are difficult to resolve during catalysis. By integrating time-resolved X-ray solution scattering, molecular dynamics simulations, and kinetic modeling, we determine how the small-molecule activator yakuchinone A modulates the catalytic cycle of the sarco/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ ATPase (SERCA), a prototypical P-type ATPase. We show that the activator accelerates the catalytic cycle by reshaping the conformational landscape during turnover, with a disproportionate enhancement of late-cycle transitions. This kinetic modulation of the rate-limiting step increases the population of Ca2+-bound E2P states, while significantly reducing accumulation of Ca2+-free E2*Pi transient states associated with dephosphorylation. Ensemble-based structural models quantitatively reproduce the experimental scattering profiles and support redistribution of conformational populations during turnover. Together, these findings provide a time-resolved mechanistic picture of how small molecules enhance enzymatic turnover through redistribution of conformational populations and selective acceleration of rate-limiting transitions.

items.title: Progress and Challenges of KRAS Degraders
Feeding A Thia-Prins Baby: A Pseudo-Telescopic Approach to Functionalized Tetrahydrothiopyranes
items.abstract: More than seven decades after its discovery, the thia-Prins reaction remains underdeveloped as a preparative route to saturated sulfur heterocycles. Its expansion offers access to tetrahydrothiopyrans in which carbonyl-derived substitution, C4 functionality, and sulfur oxidation state can be varied within a common synthetic approach. Here, we demonstrate that downstream functionalization can overcome the product-isolation problem that has restricted the reaction’s preparative use. Complex cyclization mixtures are advanced to aminium salts that can be selectively recovered without purifying the mesylate and azide intermediates. This strategy accommodates diverse aldehydes and extends to acyclic and cyclic ketones, opening access to 2,2-disubstituted and spirocyclic frameworks. Single-batch isolation of up to 187.5 g of an amine hydrochloride demonstrates the preparative utility of the approach. The crude intermediates also support diversification beyond amine synthesis, while sulfur oxidation and an additional functional group introduced through the carbonyl partner extend access to mono- and bifunctional sulfide and sulfone building blocks. These findings establish a basis for developing thia-Prins chemistry into a broader synthetic tool for exploring saturated sulfur-containing frameworks in molecular design.

items.title: Stereochemical Identity of a Single Fluorosugar Enables Noninvasive Dual-Biomarker Fingerprinting of Cancer
items.abstract: Clinical molecular imaging of cancer largely relies on single biomarker-attributable readouts. Through an efficient trapping mechanism, 2-[18F]FDG robustly links PET readouts to the Warburg effect, illuminating only a single metabolic axis within the multichannel biochemical network of cancer. The versatile chemical space of synthetic fluorosugars, however, may offer an attractive framework for broadening the repertoire of metabolic markers accessible to noninvasive imaging. Here, we report Fluorine Metabolic Imaging (FMI), a molecular MRI strategy for simultaneous in vivo mapping of two metabolic biomarkers using a single probe. FMI exploits the altered biochemistry of 3-fluoro-3-deoxy-d-galactose (3FDGal), which undergoes orthogonal intracellular redox transformations mediated by ALDH1A1 and AKR1B1, each yielding a stably trapped fluorine-labeled metabolite with a characteristic 19F-NMR peak. Concurrently mapped by 19F-MRI, these two enzyme-attributable readouts enable noninvasive spatially resolved dual-biomarker visualization. We establish the trapping mechanism of 3FDGal and its enzymatic basis, demonstrating that 3FDGal-initiated fingerprints reflect dual-biomarker variations across different cancer cells. In vivo, FMI distinguishes tumors with contrasting metabolic phenotypes, herein demonstrated in human xenografts not detectable by the canonical 2-[18F]FDG-PET approach. Establishing this proof-of-concept platform for noninvasive multilayered tumor subtyping, FMI with fluorosugars extends metabolic imaging beyond the Warburg scheme into unexplored dimensions of cancer diagnostics.

items.title: Spiroselenopyrans: Reversible Light- and Soft-Acid-Triggered Switching of Spirocyclic C–Se Bonds
items.abstract: Spiropyrans (SPs) are among the most exploited molecular scaffolds for photoswitching. Despite the potential of heavy chalcogen substitution at the spiro site to reshape bond characteristics and unlock distinct functionalities, SP analogs with chalcogens heavier than sulfur remain underexplored. Herein, we report the rational design and synthesis of spiroselenopyrans (SSPs), an emerging family of selenium-centered photoswitches, using steric hindrance engineering to suppress undesired benzoselenophene cyclization, a strategy that readily yields diversely substituted SSP derivatives. Compared with oxygen/sulfur-centered counterparts, the elongated, low-energy C–Se bond and narrowed HOMO–LUMO gap of SSPs enable efficient and accelerated photoisomerization to the trans-planar ring-opened selenomerocyanine (SMC). Notably, SSPs exhibit distinctive selectivity for soft acids, undergoing spontaneous ring-opening upon binding to Ag+ to form a cis-nonplanar Ag+-SMC complex while remaining inert toward hard protons. This work establishes SSPs as robust dual-responsive switches, broadens the chemical space of SP chemistry, and paves the way for advanced multistimuli-responsive molecular systems.

items.title: Targeting Highly Reactive Oxygen Species for Prodrug Activation Using the CReKT Approach II: The Effect of Aryl Substitution on Release Kinetics
items.abstract: We recently studied the feasibility of a prodrug system that takes advantage of the oxidation of a thioether to sulfoxide by hypochlorite to enhance the nucleophilicity of a tethered carbon with a flanking electron-withdrawing group, leading to intramolecular nucleophilic addition to an ester group for payload release. Herein, we examine the relationship between the substituent effect and payload release kinetics in depth through the synthesis and evaluation of a series of 17 analogs. First, hypochlorite oxidation of a thioether to sulfoxide in the prodrug leads to fast prodrug payload release, as designed. Second, by using different aryl substituents, the release t1/2 can be tuned within a range from minutes to hours. Third, the effect of the aryl substituent on the reaction rate follows a linear relationship with a ρ value of ∼0.5. Fourth, the computationally predicted pKa value is a strong (but not sole) predictor of the reaction rate. Fifth, whether the carbanion is conjugated (sp2) or not (sp3) seems to play an important role in determining reaction kinetics. Overall, this study strengthens the theoretical foundation of and lends additional mechanistic insights into this CReKT (cascade reaction with kinetic tunability) highly reactive oxygen species (hROS)-sensitive prodrug system. The findings also allow us to build a platform for hROS-sensitive release with tunability.

items.title: Multidrug Machine Learning Models for Predicting Human Immunodeficiency Virus‐1 Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitor Resistance
items.abstract: Drug resistance remains a major barrier to HIV/AIDS treatment, underscoring the need for rapid evaluation of resistance mechanisms and candidate inhibitors. We present a multidrug machine‐learning framework using drug‐isolate fold‐change (DIF) data to predict resistance to human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV‐1) reverse transcriptase inhibitors (RTIs). Unlike conventional isolate fold‐change (IF) models, DIF integrates viral mutation profiles with inhibitor‐specific molecular information, enabling simultaneous assessment of multiple RTIs, including unseen compounds. Artificial neural networks (ANN), XGBoost (XGB), LightGBM (LGBM), random forest (RF), and support vector regression (SVR) were evaluated. Across all algorithms, class‐specific DIF models consistently yielded higher correlation coefficients and lower mean squared errors than corresponding IF models. XGB‐DIF performed best overall, achieving a mean Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.914 and a mean squared error of 0.064. The models also captured pairwise resistance trends among FDA‐approved RTIs. External validation against an independent ChEMBL dataset yielded an accuracy of 0.824, an AUC of 0.901, and a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.773 for the best‐performing XGB model. For clinically relevant variants mean absolute errors in logarithmic fold change were as low as 0.057, with near‐perfect resistance ranking for K103N, Y181C, and Y188L. These findings support the robustness and potential utility of the DIF framework.

items.title: Thiochromen‐4‐One Derivatives as Potent Narrow‐Spectrum Antibiotics Against Moraxella
items.abstract: Thiochromen‐4‐ones represent an important class of sulfur‐containing heterocycles that have attracted increasing attention in biological chemistry. Substitution at the 3‐position of the thiochromen‐4‐one scaffold enables structural diversification and provides access to derivatives with potentially enhanced biological activity. Recent studies have indicated that thiochromen‐4‐one derivatives exhibit promising antimicrobial properties, highlighting their potential relevance in the development of new agents to combat bacterial infections. Herein, we report the synthesis and characterization of a series of 2‐alkyl‐thiochromen‐4‐one derivatives functionalized at the 3‐position. The developed synthetic strategy allows the introduction of diverse substituents at this position, thereby enabling the systematic exploration of structural variations within this heterocyclic framework. The methodology proceeds under convenient reaction conditions and employs readily accessible starting materials, affording the desired products in moderate‐to‐good yields. In particular, the most active candidates were hydroxylated compounds exhibiting low‐micromolar minimum inhibitory concentrations against the human pathogen Moraxella catarrhalis and several related Moraxella species, demonstrating unprecedented narrow‐spectrum activity. The preparation of structurally diverse 3‐substituted thiochromen‐4‐one derivatives provides valuable candidates for the development of new antimicrobial agents and important tool compounds for further mechanistic investigations. Overall, this work highlights the synthetic utility of the thiochromen‐4‐one scaffold and its potential for chemical biology.

items.title: Purinergic Imbalance and Adenosinergic Modulation of Antibacterial Activity in Severe COVID-19 and Sepsis
items.abstract: Sepsis and immunosuppression are major contributors to mortality in the intensive care unit. This study investigated dysregulated purinergic signaling, particularly systemic adenosine alterations, in relation to biomarkers and impaired antibacterial activity in severe COVID-19 and sepsis. Peripheral blood samples from COVID-19 patients at different disease stages were analyzed. Plasma purine levels were quantified by LC-MS/MS. To assess the functional effects of patient plasma, PBMCs from healthy donors were incubated with plasma from severe COVID-19 patients, resulting in increased CD39, PD-1, and KLRG1 and reduced CD73, CD28, and CD127 expression on T cells. Antibacterial activity was assessed in vitro using healthy-donor monocytes and RAW 264.7 macrophages exposed to patient plasma and challenged with GFP-expressing Escherichia coli (OP50-GFP). At hospital admission, ATP was lower, and AMP was higher in SARS-CoV-2-negative pneumonia and non-ICU and ICU COVID-19 patients than in healthy controls, whereas adenosine was lower in both COVID-19 groups. Longitudinally, nonsurvivors showed decreased ATP and increased adenosine from T1 to T2, with higher Δadenosine and lower ΔATP than survivors. Among septic patients, adenosine was higher in nonsurvivors. In vitro, cells exposed to plasma from septic ICU patients exhibited lower antibacterial activity. Adenosine and the A1/A2A antagonists DPCPX and ZM 241385 further supported a role for adenosinergic signaling: adenosine alone or combined with DPCPX reduced antibacterial activity, whereas DPCPX alone increased it. Overall, dysregulated purinergic signaling, particularly altered adenosine dynamics, may contribute to impaired antibacterial defense and immune dysfunction in severe COVID-19, with circulating plasma factors potentially increasing susceptibility to secondary infections.

items.title: para-Selective Dearomatization of N-Arylhydroxylamines for Modular Quinone Imine Synthesis
items.abstract: Dearomatization of arenes represents a pivotal transformation in organic synthesis, enabling direct access to alicyclic scaffolds prevalent in bioactive molecules. Quinone imines, though highly valuable as synthetic intermediates for complex natural products, remain challenging to prepare and isolate. We herein report a metal- and oxidant-free strategy for the modular synthesis of quinone imines through fluorosulfuryl imidazolium triflate-mediated para-selective dearomatization of N-arylhydroxylamines under mild conditions. This operationally simple protocol provides rapid access to these privileged building blocks with excellent functional group tolerance. DFT calculation was performed to elucidate the dearomatization mechanism and identify the key factors governing regioselectivity.

items.title: Novelty-stratified external validation of free in silico ADMET tools
items.abstract: Background and Purpose. Freely available in silico ADMET platforms are used routinely to triage compounds, yet each is validated by its own developers on its own training data, so reported accuracies are neither comparable across tools nor tested on novel chemistry. We asked whether any platform is generally superior, and whether structural novelty affects all endpoints alike. Experimental Approach. SwissADME, pkCSM, ADMETlab 3.0 and ADMET-AI were benchmarked on aqueous solubility, hERG blockade, blood–brain barrier penetration and drug-induced liver injury, using external datasets with identifiable training overlap removed by InChIKey. Compounds were stratified by nearest-neighbour ECFP4 Tanimoto similarity to approved drugs. Performance was computed overall, within strata and along a continuous novelty axis, tested by stratified bootstrap, and compared with a fingerprint Random Forest. Key Results. No platform was best across endpoints; the leader rotated between SwissADME, ADMETlab 3.0 and ADMET-AI. Contrary to expectation, novel chemistry was predicted no less accurately than drug-like chemistry for solubility, hERG or blood–brain barrier penetration (pooled AUROC change −0.04 and −0.02). Only drug-induced liver injury, the one endpoint lacking a structural determinant, lost accuracy (pooled AUROC −0.15), though this endpoint difference was not significant (p = 0.083). The fingerprint baseline matched or beat at least one published platform on every classification endpoint. Conclusion. These data do not support a universal collapse of accuracy on novel chemistry: three of four endpoints show none. What loss there is falls on the endpoint without a structural basis, consistently across tools but not significantly here. Tool selection should be endpoint-specific, and in silico hepatotoxicity predictions confirmed experimentally. © 2026 by the authors.
