items.title: Sequential Flow Assembly of Unsymmetrical Triaryl Architectures via Aryllithium Interception
items.abstract: The controlled generation and selective interception of aryllithium intermediates remain longstanding challenges due to their extreme reactivity and poor chemoselectivity under conventional batch conditions. Herein, we disclose a catalyst-free continuous-flow strategy that enables rapid halogen–lithium exchange using n-butyllithium (n-BuLi) as the sole activating reagent, followed by immediate and highly chemoselective electrophilic trapping under precisely defined residence times. This approach enables direct functionalization of bifunctional electrophiles bearing both carbonyl (CO) and cyano (CN) groups, affording products in yields up to 94%. Sequential interception within a single flow sequence enables programmable assembly of unsymmetrical triarylmethanol and triarylmethane architectures from simple aryl halides. These frameworks are prevalent in functional molecules, including trityl-based pharmacophores such as S-trityl-l-cysteine and triphenylmethane dyes such as crystal violet and malachite green. Notably, the method enables streamlined access to letrozole-type derivatives in a single flow sequence, highlighting its utility for the rapid construction of pharmaceutically relevant scaffolds. By harnessing microreactor-enabled kinetic control, this platform establishes a modular approach to chemoselective aryl functionalization inaccessible under traditional processing.

items.title: Multiple Chemical Class‐Based Potent VEGFR2 Inhibitors as Anticancer Therapeutics: Structure–Activity Relationship and Chemicobiological Interactions Studies
items.abstract: Angiogenesis regulation is associated with disorders such as rheumatoid arthritis, diabetes, atherosclerosis, and cancer. Tumor development and metastasis are directly affected by tumor angiogenesis. In addition to tumor cells, host cells produce pro‐ and anti‐angiogenic molecules that regulate tumor angiogenesis. VEGFs and their receptor, VEGFR2 (KDR), strongly influence angiogenesis. When activated, KDR undergoes autophosphorylation, which ultimately promotes endothelial cell proliferation, tumor angiogenesis, tumor growth, and metastasis. Overexpression of VEGFR2 has been observed in various cancer types, including hepatocellular carcinoma, renal carcinoma, non‐small cell lung cancer, breast cancer, and cervical cancer. Researchers have developed several VEGFR2 inhibitors over the past few decades. This review examines the structure–activity relationships (SARs) of several recently developed chemical classes, including chalcones, quinazolines, pyridines, pyrimidines, thiadiazoles, indazoles, triazoles, quinoxalines, and pyrazoles, as VEGFR2 inhibitors, with an emphasis on anticancer activity. We also analyze the chemico–biological interaction profiles of several small‐molecule VEGFR2 inhibitors. This review article provides an overview of the latest advances in medicinal chemistry approaches to VEGFR2 inhibitors.

items.title: Novel Mn(II) Quinaldinate Complexes With Halogenated Imidazo[1,2‐a]pyridine and Memantine: Synthesis, Spectroscopic Studies, and Selective Pro‐Apoptotic and Pro‐Oxidative Activity in Cancer Cells
items.abstract: Three novel Mn(II) complexes incorporating quinaldinate and biologically relevant N ‐donor ligands—halogenated imidazo[1,2‐a]pyridine derivatives—were synthesized and comprehensively characterized in the solid state by single‐crystal X‐ray diffraction, FT‐IR, Raman spectroscopy, and thermal analysis. The investigated compounds include two unprecedented one‐dimensional coordination polymers, [Mn 2 (6‐Brimpy) 2 (QA) 4 ] n ( 1 ) and [Mn 2 (6‐Climpy) 2 (QA) 4 ] n ( 2 ), and the mononuclear complex [Mn(QA) 3 ](H 2 O)⋅(mem) ( 3 ). FT‐IR studies in DMSO suggested the persistence of coordination species derived from compounds 1–3, while allowing for changes in solution speciation. UV–vis and emission measurements revealed ligand‐centered absorption and pronounced luminescence, indicating that the obtained systems combine selective biological activity with promising photophysical properties. Biological evaluation against metastatic melanoma (1205‐Lu), glioblastoma (T98G), and normal dermal fibroblasts (NHDF) demonstrated moderate but selective anticancer activity, with the strongest effect observed for complex 2 toward 1205‐Lu cells, while all compounds remained essentially nontoxic toward NHDF fibroblasts. Mechanistic studies revealed a concentration‐dependent increase in caspase‐3 activity and malondialdehyde levels in melanoma cells, indicating apoptosis induction accompanied by oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation. Importantly, the free ligands alone did not exhibit significant anticancer activity, demonstrating that coordination to Mn(II) is essential for the emergence and enhancement of the observed biological effects.

items.title: Artesunate Derivatives as Anticancer Agents: Hybrid Designs and Emerging Therapeutic Strategies
items.abstract: Artesunate is a semisynthetic derivative of the natural product artemisinin, isolated from Artemisia annua and characterized by the biologically important endoperoxide bridge. Beyond its established use in malaria treatment, in recent decades, artesunate has attracted growing research interest as an anticancer agent. Despite encouraging preclinical results, clinical studies demonstrated only modest efficacy when artesunate was used as a single compound, due to its low bioavailability, toxicity, and unfavorable side effects. For this reason, artesunate derivatization has attracted significant attention, as the resulting derivatives often exhibit superior anticancer activity in both in vitro and in vivo studies compared with artesunate alone. This review offers a comprehensive overview of reported artesunate derivatives, structured into sections based on the type of molecule employed for derivatization and highlights the expanding research on their anticancer activity. Currently emerging strategies that include hybridization and nanocarrier‐based delivery systems which may accelerate the clinical translation of artesunate derivatives and harness their potential in anticancer drug discovery are also discussed. While significant progress has been made, a lot of the research field still remains underexplored.

items.title: Design, Synthesis and Anti‐Proliferative Assessment of 4‐Aminoquinoline‐ and 4‐Aminoquinoline‐Benzoxaborole Conjugates
items.abstract: A series of 4‐aminoquinoline analogues and 4‐aminoquinoline‐benzoxaborole conjugates were synthesized and evaluated for their antiproliferative activities against two distinct breast cancer cell lines: MCF‐7 (estrogen receptor‐positive, ER+) and MDA‐MB‐231 (triple‐negative). Preliminary dose‐response assays revealed compound 5e , a 4‐aminoquinoline–benzoxaborole conjugate, as the most active compound against MCF‐7 cells. Structure–activity relationship (SAR) analysis indicated that the cytotoxic potency of the series increased with the length of the alkyl spacer connecting the pharmacophoric moieties. To assess selectivity, HEK‐293 cells were employed as a non‐cancerous control line, and most compounds exhibited minimal cytotoxicity, except compound 5d , which showed moderate effects. To gain preliminary structural insights, exploratory molecular docking studies were performed against the ligand‐binding domain of estrogen receptor alpha (ERα). This integrated experimental‐computational approach highlights the identification of promising preliminary hits. Overall, the findings show that 4‐aminoquinoline–benzoxaborole conjugates exhibit antiproliferative activity against breast cancer cells, with greater potency towards MCF‐7 cells.

items.title: Discovery of Novel Pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidine Derivatives as Potent and Effective RSK4 Inhibitors for the Treatment of Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma
Structure–Activity Relationships of C-2-Functionalized 4-Styrylquinoline Hybrids Reveal Divergent Effects of Styryl Halogenation on Antiproliferative and Antitrypanosomal Activity
Co-Folding Models Localize Enzyme Active Sites but Fail to Accurately Predict Enzyme–Substrate Complex Structures
items.abstract: The accurate prediction of enzyme–substrate complex structures is challenging due to the transient and dynamic nature of these interactions. We evaluated the performance of eight machine–learning (ML) docking tools and the physics–based method AutoDock Vina as a reference in the prediction of enzyme–substrate complex structures using a curated data set of 210 diverse, non–redundant enzyme–substrate complexes, equally divided into three classes: metal–free enzymes (A), and enzymes with metal ions outside (B) or inside (C) the active site. All ML–based docking tools had low geometric accuracy and physical plausibility, with fewer than 10% hit rates at the stricter 2 Å threshold for substrate root-mean-square deviation. While no ML-based tools were able to outperform Vina in modeling physically plausible complexes, co–folding tools such as AlphaFold3 and Boltz–2 excelled at active–site localization, and many algorithms performed better for class C enzymes, and worse for class B enzymes. Surprisingly, DynamicBind, which was trained on less data with fewer parameters compared to other models, matched co-folding methods in active-site elucidation. Our results show that enzyme–substrate docking can be affected by the presence of a metal ion, and suggest that better performances for complex structure prediction may be achieved with data-centric strategies including molecular dynamics simulations rather than parameter-heavy ML architectures.

items.title: Jumping from scaling to scale-up
items.abstract: Nature Chemical Engineering, Published online: 17 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s44286-026-00472-2 Jonathan Boreyko discusses how to utilize scaling analysis to progress from fundamental discovery toward practical applications with a close look at capillary-inertial jumping droplets.

items.title: Transannular Sigmatropic Rearrangement of Transient Spirocyclic C3 Ammonium Ylides: Stereospecific Access to Bridged Bicyclic Benzo[ b ]azepine Derivatives and Higher Homologues
items.abstract: We report a stereospecific entry to bicyclic benzo[b]azepines enabled by an unusual sigmatropic [1,5] carbon shift from a transient spirocyclic C3 ammonium enolate. Enantiopure aziridine-substituted chalcones undergo efficient ring expansion to deliver a broad set of benzo[b]azepin-6-ones in consistently high yields with complete transfer of stereochemical information. The strategy is generalized to larger-ring congeners, providing streamlined access to benzo[b]azocines and benzo[b,g]azecines. Mechanistic insight from density functional theory calculations, complemented by natural bond analysis and local energy decomposition, identifies a counterintuitive origin of reactivity: the stabilization of the rate-determining transition state arises predominantly from correlation energy together with geometric relaxation of the dihydroquinoline framework, rather than from strain-release.

items.title: Bispecific Nanobody Broadly Neutralizes and Cross-Protects against Three Highly Pathogenic Human Coronaviruses
items.abstract: SARS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2, and MERS-CoV continue to infect humans or pose a threat of future outbreaks, highlighting the ongoing need for effective, broad-spectrum therapeutics that target these highly pathogenic coronaviruses. As single-domain antibodies, nanobodies have a small size, high target-binding affinity, exceptional stability, low production costs, and the ability to access otherwise hidden or cryptic epitopes. Here, we identified nanobodies targeting SARS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2, and MERS-CoV receptor-binding domains (RBDs) using phage display libraries derived from immunized nanomice and generated a bispecific nanobody to evaluate its broadly neutralizing activity and cross-protective efficacy. Nanobodies 2F11 and 4D6 targeted SARS-CoV RBD, potently neutralizing the SARS-CoV original (Tor2) strain, whereas nanobody 3B11 targeted both SARS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2 RBDs, broadly neutralizing all three SARS-CoV strains (Tor2, GD03, and SZ3) and divergent SARS-CoV-2 variants. Among MERS-CoV RBD-targeting nanobodies, 1C11 demonstrated broadly neutralizing activity against multiple MERS-CoV strains, while its Fc-fused version substantially enhanced the neutralizing potency. These nanobodies exerted neutralizing effects by blocking the interaction between the RBDs and their respective receptors. Cryo-EM structures, computational modeling, and epitope-mapping analyses revealed unique epitopes of 2F11, 3B11, and 1C11 on the SARS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2, or MERS-CoV RBD, underlying their antiviral potency. Finally, a bispecific nanobody 3B11–1C11-Fc that binds to the SARS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2, and MERS-CoV RBDs exhibited high stability and robust cross-neutralizing activity against all tested SARS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2, and MERS-CoV strains, protecting mice from infection with these three coronaviruses. Overall, the identified nanobodies, particularly the bispecific nanobody, exhibit strong neutralizing potency and protective efficacy against SARS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2, and MERS-CoV, showing the potential for further therapeutic development.

items.title: Expanding Chemical Space Enables Data–Driven Structure–Activity Relationships in Cage Catalysis
items.abstract: Data-driven approaches are increasingly popular in catalysis, supplementing and even replacing traditional strategies that relied on empirical optimization. However, their application in the field of bioinspired cage catalysis remains largely unexplored, primarily due to the limited chemical space of known catalytically active cages. As a result, mechanistic insights are often obtained using computationally intensive DFT calculations on a handful of structurally similar cages. As chemical systems grow in complexity, this approach becomes impractical. Herein, we report a framework that significantly expedites the exploration of a much wider structural landscape while offering computational insights. This is made possible by a novel in situ experimental procedure─which circumvents the traditional time-consuming process of prepare, isolate, characterize, and test─coupled with data-driven methods to identify molecular features that govern activity. Using this approach, we experimentally explore 30 unique PdnL2n cages (n = 2–4) that mediate a nitro-aldol reaction with activities spanning over 4 orders of magnitude. Using this data set, a random forest model trained on molecular descriptors was developed to predict ΔG‡ (MAE of 0.4 kcal mol–1 and R2 = 0.9). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis highlighted geometric preorganization and electrostatic interactions within the cage as key determinants of catalytic efficiency. Moreover, DFT calculations on a selection of cages further validated these insights, indicating that meaningful mechanistic understanding can be achieved at significantly reduced computational cost. We anticipate that this integrated, screening, data-driven, mechanistic strategy will provide a blueprint workflow for understanding metal–organic cage reactivity and encourage the generation of more comprehensive structural data sets, ultimately enabling the rational design of improved catalytic architectures.

items.title: Advances in Near-Infrared Fluorescent Probes for Targeted Imaging of Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma
items.abstract: Molecularly targeted near-infrared fluorescence imaging offers a promising approach to delineating cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma while preserving healthy tissue. This narrative review integrates target biology, probe chemistry, experimental performance, and translational development, with particular attention to epidermal growth factor receptor, integrins, vascular endothelial growth factor, interleukin-6 receptor, and emerging molecular and organelle targets. Antibody conjugates have visualized cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma xenografts and patient-derived tumor grafts, while activatable probes and ex vivo human-specimen imaging provide a bridge to pathology-linked assessment. Studies in oral and other cancers contribute transferable strategies for topical delivery, fluorescence lifetime imaging, dual recognition, and microenvironment-responsive activation. Comparative assessment connects each probe class with its recognition mechanism, acquisition conditions, and reported biological or imaging end points. Photothermal, photodynamic, and photoimmunotherapy systems illustrate how imaging can be integrated with localized treatment and response monitoring. The review also identifies practical priorities for translation, including target accessibility, pharmacokinetics, construct-specific safety, calibrated acquisition, and prospective pathology-registered evaluation. These advances support the development of fluorescence-assisted localization and specimen assessment as complementary tools within established skin-cancer care.

items.title: Aza-Henry Reactions of Cyclic Nitrones En Route to 2 H -Imidazole-Tethered Nitrogen Heterocycles
items.abstract: An approach to a series of original 2H-imidazole-containing hybrid heterocycles is reported. The protocol is based on the DBU-mediated deoxygenative nucleophilic nitromethylation of the related aldonitrones, 2H-imidazole N-oxides, followed by a one-step transformation of thus formed (nitromethylene)imidazolines into the corresponding α-chlorooximes. The chlorooxime functionality, considered as a precursor to highly reactive nitrile oxides, is further utilized to construct a variety of bis-azaheterocycles. Overall, 28 previously unknown compounds have been synthesized in yields of up to 97%.

items.title: Electronic Polarization of Covalent Organic Framework Membranes for Precise Antibiotic Purification
items.abstract: Precise molecular separation is essential for pharmaceutical production and purification, yet existing sieving systems struggle to distinguish structurally similar molecules due to their predominant reliance on size exclusion. Herein, we fabricate a covalent organic framework (COF) membrane featuring fluorine-induced polarized nanochannels for fast organic solvent nanofiltration. The incorporation of fluorine atoms redistributes electron density along the pore walls, creating a polarized electrostatic environment while lowering surface energy. This unique pore environment promotes the uptake and transport of polar solvents, while enhancing separation selectivity by retarding highly polar solutes through polarity-dependent solute-framework interactions. Furthermore, the low surface energy imparted by the robust C–F bonds also reduces irreversible foulant adhesion and facilitates permeance recovery after cleaning. The resultant COF membrane achieves a molecular weight cutoff down to 350 Da and stable operation for over 550 h. Notably, it differentiates structurally related fluoroquinolone antibiotics according to their molecular polarity and delivers a favorable separation factor of 8.9 for norfloxacin over its synthetic intermediate piperazine. This work demonstrates that engineering pore-wall polarity in COF membranes provides a viable route to chemically regulated molecular recognition beyond size-based separation.

items.title: Synthesis of Axially, Planar and Helically Chiral Molecules via Rhodium-Catalyzed Asymmetric C–H Functionalization Reactions
items.abstract: An important goal of organic synthesis is to explore chemical space by efficiently building up molecular diversity. Axially, planar and helically chiral skeletons are prevalent in pharmaceuticals and natural products, and their significance is underscored by their widespread applications as privileged scaffolds of chiral ligands and catalysts in asymmetric catalysis. Therefore, the catalytic asymmetric synthesis of these chiral architectures has garnered considerable attention and inspired a broad range of synthetic methodologies. Among the various synthetic strategies developed, transition-metal-catalyzed asymmetric C–H functionalization has emerged as an atom- and step-economical approach. In this Account, we present a concise review of the enantioselective synthesis of different types of chiral molecules, including biaryl atropisomers, helically chiral compounds, planar chiral ferrocenes, and planar chiral macrocycles, by our group via rhodium-catalyzed asymmetric C–H functionalization reactions. Since our initial reports in 2014, we have introduced several strategies based on both Rh(I) and Rh(III) catalytic systems. For Rh(I) catalysis, TADDOL-derived chiral monophosphonite ligands were utilized to achieve enantioselective C–H arylation of 1-arylisoquinolines and planar chiral ferrocenes. For Rh(III) catalysis, chiral cyclopentadienyl (Cp) rhodium complexes, including the Cramer-type catalysts and our newly designed 1,1′-spirobiindane-derived chiral CpRh(III) complexes (SCpRh), were utilized to enable a diverse array of axially chiral 1-arylisoquinolines through atroposelective C–H arylation, alkylation, alkynylation, olefination, cyanation, indolylization, and selenylation. The same Rh(III) catalytic system enables, via C–H activation and annulation with alkynes, the synthesis of biaryl atropisomers, planar chiral metallocenes, isoquinoline-based macrocyclic atropisomers and helical azoniahelicenes. We anticipate that rhodium-catalyzed asymmetric C–H functionalization will be widely applicable in the construction of synthetically useful axially, planar, and helically chiral compounds. The development of more diverse and efficient methods for synthesizing these chiral architectures will continue to grow, opening new avenues for asymmetric catalysis, natural product synthesis, pharmaceutical science, and materials science.

items.title: Molecular Imaging of Precancerous Colorectal Lesions
items.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) has become the third leading cause of cancer-related deaths in the United States, and the incidence and death rates of the disease in Americans under 50 years-old have risen startlingly in recent years. Critically, however, the 5-year survival rate for CRC is >90% when the disease is detected early, and the malignancy can be avoided completely if lesions are detected while still precancerous. In light of this, the detection of precancerous colorectal lesions  i.e. via colonoscopy  is absolutely crucial to public health. Molecular imaging can be a valuable clinical tool for the visualization of these premalignant tissues, and modalities such as PET, CT, fluorescence, ultrasound, and photoacoustic imaging have been harnessed to detect lesions that may otherwise be difficult to identify during traditional colonoscopies. In this review, we discuss current challenges in the detection of precancerous colorectal lesions, cover the ways in which molecular imaging is currently deployed in this area, and address emergent technologies that have arisen at the intersection of these two fields.

items.title: Site-Specific Enzymatic Radiofluorination of Biomolecules: From Current Methodologies to Emerging Opportunities
items.abstract: The recent expansion of recombinant biomolecules as diagnostic and therapeutic agents has created a strong need for mild, site-specific, and universally applicable methods to radiolabel them for positron emission tomography (PET). Fluorine-18 is one of the most widely used radionuclides for PET because it combines a clinically practical half-life, high positron intensity with low mean energy, and a non-metallic footprint in the label. However, the conditions necessary for efficient nucleophilic fluorine-18 radiolabelingbasic, anhydrous media, elevated temperature, and aprotic solventsare poorly compatible with sensitive biomolecules. Therefore, prosthetic group labeling with subsequent conjugation, both site-specific and non-site-specific, and aluminum-[18F]fluoride (Al[18F]F2+) chelation have become essential workarounds. Depending on the radiolabeling site, this can yield heterogeneous products, with impaired tracer target binding and pharmacokinetics. Enzymatic ligation offers a complementary strategy, with radiofluorination done on a robust small-molecule or peptide substrate, and subsequently, an enzyme catalyzes a mild and site-specific conjugation to a genetically encoded recognition motif on the target. This ensures that each step proceeds under its own optimal conditions. This review evaluates the current state of enzymatic and chemoenzymatic radiofluorination of biomolecules, from the early fluorinase work to recent advances with lipoic acid ligase (LplA), peptide asparaginyl ligase, and sortase A (SrtA). It further reviews enzymes and techniques that could extend this toolbox. The field is still emerging, but available evidence suggests that enzyme-mediated radiofluorination can occupy a niche between classical prosthetic-group radiochemistry and kit-like radiometal labeling, especially for fragile recombinant biomolecules whose radiolabeling with fluorine-18 is currently a challenge.

items.title: A Mirror-Image L-RNA Aptamer Targeting Hypoxia-Inducible Factor-1α Promoter G-Quadruplex Potentiates Tumor Radiotherapy In Vivo
items.abstract: The hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) coordinates the response of tumors to low oxygen by stimulating genes involved in metabolism and angiogenesis. HIF pathway activation is highly associated with tumor progression and radiotherapy resistance. Ligands that target this pathway are potential agents for the treatment of solid tumor malignancies. We developed an L-RNA aptamer, L-Apt5–4, targeting the HIF-1α promoter DNA G-quadruplex (dG4) via mirror-image SELEX. This L-RNA aptamer adopts a stem-loop secondary structure, binds HIF-1α dG4 with high affinity and specificity, and enters the nucleus to effectively downregulate HIF-1α and its downstream targets in cancer cells. By suppressing HIF-1α, L-Apt5–4 not only inhibits tumor cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, but also acts as a potent radiosensitizer, synergizing with radiotherapy to enhance cancer cell death. The combination therapy significantly suppresses tumor growth and metastasis while exhibiting excellent biosafety in vivo. Thus, L-Apt5–4 represents a novel HIF-1α-targeted therapeutic and radiosensitizer for combined cancer treatment.

items.title: Small-Molecule Ligands of Epac Proteins: Tools for Studying Epac Signaling and Prospects for Drug Discovery
Three-Step Continuous-Flow Synthesis of GABA from an L-Carnitine Byproduct: Integrating Inline FTIR and Bayesian Optimization for Rapid Process Development
items.abstract: We report a three-step telescoped continuous-flow synthesis of γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) starting from ethyl 4-hydroxycrotonate (EHC), a stoichiometric byproduct generated during L-carnitine production. The route proceeds through azidation with DPPA/DBU, dual-site catalytic hydrogenation over a Pd/C fixed bed, and alkaline ester hydrolysis. All three steps are conducted in a fully integrated flow system with no intermediate isolation required. A key engineering challenge, salt-induced microchannel clogging during quenching of the azidation step, was resolved with a 22 wt % subsaturated NH4Cl solution, which simultaneously suppresses clogging and maintains stable liquid–liquid phase separation. The hydrogenation step, which must reduce both the C═C bond and the azide group in a single pass, was optimized over a five-variable parameter space using multiobjective Bayesian optimization with Gaussian process surrogate models, guided by inline FTIR spectroscopy. Starting from five Latin hypercube initialization points, the hypervolume appeared to plateau after only 21 total experiments. The three-step telescoped process delivers GABA in 75.1% overall yield. This study demonstrates how a structurally defined industrial byproduct can be valorized through a combination of inherently safe continuous-flow processing and data-driven optimization, with particular relevance to systems operating in uncharted parameter spaces under hazardous intermediate constraints.

items.title: Ubiquitination-Informed Reinforcement Learning Linker Generator Enables Discovery of Novel FGFR4 PROTAC Degraders
items.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) represent a promising therapeutic strategy, yet rational linker design is limited by inadequate theoretical guidance. Herein, we report PotentialLinker, a novel reinforcement learning framework for PROTAC linker optimization that uses a normalized weighted harmonic mean (NWHM) score to predict degradation activity. Benchmarking on ternary structures confirms its performance without precomputed protein−protein complexes. In case studies of STAT3/RIPK1, it recapitulated structure−activity relationships (SAR) and recommended appropriate E3 ligases. Then, conducted by PotentialLinker, a potent FGFR4 degrader D11 was obtained (DC50 = 56.23 nM, Dmax = 89.58%). Due to its covalent interacting with the unique Cys552 in FGFR4, D11 possesses excellent FGFR4 selectivity. Furthermore, D11 also demonstrated favorable oral bioavailability (F = 21.3%) and potent antitumor efficacy (TGI = 87.07%) with acceptable tolerability in vivo. Taken together, this framework effectively bridges degradation theory and practical PROTAC design, which can be utilized for the rational design of PROTAC-based therapeutic agents.

items.title: A Recombinant Human Serum Albumin Nanoparticle Encapsulating Dimyristoyl Gemcitabine Remodels the Fibrotic Microenvironment to Potentiate Chemo-Immunotherapy in Pancreatic Cancer
items.abstract: Pancreatic cancer is malignant and highly lethal, largely due to a dense, fibrotic tumor stroma that fosters a profoundly immunosuppressive microenvironment and obstructs drug delivery. To overcome these barriers, we developed a novel recombinant human serum albumin-based nanoparticle encapsulating dimyristoyl GEM (dm-rHSA-NPs). In vivo, dm-rHSA-NPs achieved significant tumor accumulation with the assistance of extended half-life (3.91 vs. 0.82 h, vs. GEM) and tumor targeting ability of the rHSA-based nanoparticles. Upon reaching the tumor tissue, dm-rHSA-NPs exhibited highly efficient tumor penetration and fibrotic stroma degradation, leading to adequate cellular accumulation, further assisting in improved cellular apoptosis, decreased cellular migration and invasion, as well as ICD-inducing ability. Benefiting from these effects, the profound immunosuppression characteristic of pancreatic cancer was relieved, promoting DCs maturation (22-fold), increasing infiltration of CTLs (45-fold), and decreasing the infiltration of Tregs (3.9-fold) in the tumor. All these synergistic effects contributed to the excellent in vivo anti-pancreatic cancer efficacy (89% vs. 37% of the tumor-inhibition rate), an outstanding tumor metastasis inhibition ability (2 vs. 22 of the tumor metastasis sites), and negligible systemic toxicity, superior to GEM. By combining enhanced drug delivery with potent TME remodeling and immune activation, dm-rHSA-NPs represent a promising formulation with high potential in clinical application to treat pancreatic cancer.

items.title: Oxetane-to-Cyclopropane Skeletal Editing through Oxygen Deletion
items.abstract: Oxygen-atom deletion from cyclic ethers remains challenging because selective C─O cleavage and subsequent C─C formation are difficult. We report a catalyst-free, photoinduced conversion of oxetanes to cyclopropanes. Iodoform and DMF generate a Vilsmeier–Haack reagent under blue light, producing diiodides that undergo zinc-mediated reductive cyclization. The method shows broad functional-group tolerance, supports late-stage modification, and provides evidence for rapid radical cyclization.

items.title: Computational Drug Discovery of Natural Product Compounds for Tyrosinase Inhibition
items.abstract: Plants produce chemically diverse compounds for defence and survival, many of which exhibit biological activity and offer promising starting points for drug discovery. This study thus investigated natural compounds as potential inhibitors of tyrosinase, a key enzyme in melanin production and an established target in the treatment of hyperpigmentation. A quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) machine-learning model was developed using ChEMBL tyrosinase bioactivity data and property-matched decoys. Ten models, including decision trees, random forests and gradient boosting, were evaluated; logistic regression was selected for virtual screening. To make the model generalise to unseen chemistry, the model was tested on compounds that were required to have Tanimoto similarity of 0.40 or less to every training compound and to share no Bemis–Murcko scaffold with them. The model achieved an AUC of 0.82 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.78–0.86), compared with 0.56 using physicochemical properties alone. The frozen model was then used to screen 404,570 natural products from COCONUT (COlleCtion of Open Natural prodUcTs) and IMPPAT (Indian Medicinal Plants, Phytochemistry And Therapeutics). Of the top 1% of predictions, 1,694 compounds were both structurally novel and represented new scaffolds. Following computational filters for predicted skin permeability and potentially reactive chemical groups indicating skin irritation, the 100 highest-scoring candidates were selected for molecular docking. Docking reproduced the crystallographic tropolone binding pose with a root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) of 1.20 Å, while the most predictive docking score achieved an AUC of 0.64 (95% CI, 0.61–0.66). Among the ten highest-ranked candidates, two were associated with Anisomeles indica (Indian catmint) and two with Phaseolus lunatus (lima beans). These candidates warrant experimental validation and further investigation for potential dermatological applications.

items.title: Defining the Diphyllin Pharmacophore for Broad-Spectrum Antiviral V-ATPase Inhibition by Structure-Guided Scaffold Modifications
items.abstract: The threat of emerging viral diseases presents a critical societal need for broad-spectrum antiviral therapeutics. A key contribution to antiviral options would be a broad-spectrum agent that can treat a wide variety of viral diseases. Vacuolar H-ATPase (V-ATPase), a host proton pump critical for endosomal acidification, serves an essential role in facilitating the entry of multiple viruses. Diphyllin, a naturally occurring V-ATPase inhibitor, displays potent antiviral activity but is limited by suboptimal drug-like properties, including selectivity and metabolic instability. Molecular modeling enabled the identification of a conserved binding site on the V-ATPase a-subunit consisting of three distinct sub-pockets. Docking analyses of ninety-five known diphyllin derivatives demonstrated that active analogs effectively occupy all three subpockets, informing a structure-based design approach. A library of novel diphyllin analogs with modifications to a single-ring system showed 50-fold increases in potency for antiviral activity against Ebola, Venezuelan equine encephalitis, and Chikungunya viruses and exhibiting improvements in metabolic stability and permeability.

items.title: A vacated second ligand site acts as a decoy in redocking: systematic in P-glycoprotein, intermittent across eight other proteins
items.abstract: Redocking tests whether a docking protocol can recover a deposited pose: the ligand is removed and the program is asked to put it back. Standard preparation deletes every copy. When a structure contains two copies in one cavity, the receptor passed to the program was never observed empty. We measured the effect of that deletion in deposited human P-glycoprotein structures, with the search box centred on the deposited pose so that a failure cannot be blamed on site finding. Across 15 structures the median top-pose RMSD is 8.30 Å and 1 of 15 falls within 2.0 Å. Accuracy does not track the density support of the deposited ligand. That was the registered hypothesis, and it is not supported (Spearman ρ = −0.004, p = 0.9899). In the nine structures that carry a second copy, retaining the copy as rigid receptor moves the median from 8.26 to 3.46 Å and improves 8 of 9 (p = 0.0078). A carbon-only ghost of the same shape, which the scoring function sees as apolar volume but not as a hydrogen-bonding partner, agrees with the retained copy (p = 0.1289), while a box reduced to the same volume does not (p = 0.2969). The displaced poses lie in the vacated subsite (mean overlap 0.216 to 0.539, p = 0.0078). The comparison reproduces in rDock, which shares no code with smina: 6 of 7 structures improve, and the median falls from 8.35 to 3.67 Å (p = 0.0469). On eight unrelated proteins the same protocol does not support one direction (5 of 8, p = 0.3750), although trypsin moves from 8.59 to 0.50 Å. A scan of 37,596 PDB entries found 4,774 multi-copy sites across 929 proteins. A redocking number for a multi-copy structure should be reported both with the other copies removed and with them retained. Scientific Contribution. Published evidence for this preparation effect was one ligand in one structure. The comparison here covers nine two-copy P-glycoprotein structures, and a carbon ghost together with a volume-matched box separates apolar occlusion from polar ligand chemistry and from the volume searched. Repeated on eight other proteins, the same comparison does not support a consistent direction.

items.title: Linker Architecture-Guided Design of FAPI Dimers for Improved Pharmacokinetics and FAP-Targeted Theranostics
items.abstract: Fibroblast activation protein (FAP), a type II transmembrane serine protease highly expressed in cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), represents an attractive target for tumor imaging and targeted therapy. In this study, we designed and synthesized a series of FAP-targeted dimers (FAPI-FUSCC-DIMER) based on the UAMC1110 scaffold incorporating structurally diverse linkers and evaluated these compounds using a stepwise screening strategy to identify a promising FAP-targeted theranostic radioligand candidate. All FAPI-FUSCC-DIMER derivatives were efficiently labeled with 68Ga and exhibited favorable radiochemical stability and hydrophilic properties. Selected compounds were further evaluated in vivo based on SPR affinity assays and cell uptake studies. Micro-PET/CT imaging and biodistribution studies further evaluated the tumor uptake and retention profiles of the FAPI-FUSCC-DIMER series. FAPI-FUSCC-DIMER-2 demonstrated high FAP affinity, enhanced tumor uptake and prolonged tumor retention, with favorable pharmacokinetic properties, and was subsequently selected for 177Lu-based radioligand therapy studies. [177Lu]Lu-FAPI-FUSCC-DIMER-2 exhibited prolonged tumor retention for up to 120 h and a strong inhibitory effect on tumor growth in the HT-1080-FAP tumor model, together with a favorable safety profile. These findings support continued preclinical investigation of FAPI-FUSCC-DIMER-2.

items.title: Engineering Camptothecin Prodrugs for Cancer Therapy: An Exposure-First Perspective
items.abstract: Camptothecin (CPT)-derived anticancer agents stabilize topoisomerase I (TOP1)−DNA cleavage complexes (TOP1ccs), but their therapeutic utility is constrained by lactone instability, variable pharmacokinetics, and systemic toxicity. This Perspective evaluates prodrug strategies according to their initiating activation mechanisms, distinguishing self-immolative chemistry as a payload-release module. Small-molecule prodrugs are emphasized, alongside peptide−drug conjugates, antibody−drug conjugates, polymeric prodrugs, and nanoprodrugs. We propose an exposure-first, “design backward, validate forward” framework in which intended tumor exposure to active lactone and TOP1cc formation guide the payload selection, attachment site, activation compartment, linker kinetics, and delivery platform. Translational evaluation should establish colocalization of intact prodrug and accessible activating stimulus, faithful release of the intended payload, and a favorable balance between tumor exposure and exposure in dose-limiting normal tissues. Additional platform complexity should yield measurable pharmacological benefits. This framework provides practical criteria for prioritizing CPT prodrugs with the potential to improve the therapeutic index.

items.title: A Novel Mathematical Model for Predicting the Agonist Activity of Mixtures Containing Agonist and Antagonist Ligands in Drug Discovery Screening
items.abstract: Mixture-based positional scanning libraries have been used to identify novel ligands for a variety of targets, including G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs). These mixtures may contain both agonist and antagonist ligands. Herein, a mathematical model is derived and experimentally verified to explore the effects of agonist screening in the presence of antagonists and address the decades-old question, “How can you find agonists in the presence of antagonists in mixtures?” This model is used to predict the behavior of agonist-antagonist mixtures at the melanocortin-3 and -4 (MC3R and MC4R) receptors. Based upon this model and these data, it is concluded that only in cases with a large percentage of high-potency antagonists is the agonist signal suppressed below detection levels, explaining why the presence of both ligand classes has not masked potent agonist compounds in mixture-based screening campaigns. The approaches herein may be applied globally to other robust, reproducible assays testing mixtures.

items.title: Discovery and Preclinical Characterization of Benzofuran Derivatives as Potent, Selective, and Orally Bioavailable GSPT1 Molecular Glue Degraders for the Treatment of MYC-Driven Cancers
items.abstract: Targeted protein degradation of the translation termination factor GSPT1 is a promising cancer strategy. However, current cereblon-recruiting molecular glue degraders (MGDs) lack structural diversity, being mostly IMiD derivatives. To overcome resistance and improve drug-like properties, we report the rational, structure-guided design of a novel series of benzofuran-based GSPT1 MGDs. Extensive structure−activity relationship studies and optimization led to the discovery of highly potent, orally bioavailable degraders, highlighted by compounds C-3 and C-4. Both exhibited single-digit nanomolar GSPT1 degradation (DC50 = 2.81 and 1.91 nM) and robust selectivity over IMiD off-targets IKZF1 and SALL4. In vivo, oral administration (1−2 mg/kg) of C-3 and C-4 demonstrated favorable cross-species pharmacokinetics and achieved sustained tumor regression in NCI-H1155 and MDA-MB-468 xenograft models. With a maximum tolerated dose exceeding 100 mg/kg and no hematological toxicity, these benzofuran-based MGDs are highly promising preclinical candidates for solid tumors.

items.title: GPC3-Targeted sdAb-PET Imaging of Hepatocellular Carcinoma with Single-Domain Antibody Tracers
items.abstract: Glypican-3 (GPC3) is a particular biomarker for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Theranostic strategies targeting GPC3 using single-domain antibodies (sdAbs), also known as nanobodies, show promising potential due to their high affinity and excellent tissue penetration. In this study, two novel GPC3-targeted sdAb-based PET probes were developed and tested in GPC3-positive HCC models. The GPC3-specific sdAb G6 and its albumin-binding domain (ABD)-fused variant ABDG6 were conjugated with NOTA and radiolabeled with [68Ga] to generate [68Ga]Ga-NOTA-G6 and [68Ga]Ga-NOTA-ABDG6, whose binding kinetics, in short-term vitro stability, PET/CT being explore. G6 and ABDG6 showed high affinity for GPC3, with the binding affinity (KD values) of 0.62 nM for G6 and 0.43 nM for ABDG6. After radiolabeling, [68Ga]Ga-NOTA-G6 retained high affinity (KD = 5.4 nM) and demonstrated rapid blood clearance and GPC3-specific tumor accumulation, enabling relatively high-contrast imaging of GPC3 tumors at 60minutes post-injection (p.i.). The uptake of [68Ga]Ga-NOTA-G6 in tumors reached 2.40 ± 0.21 %ID/g, resulting in a high tumor-to-muscle ratio of 3.85 ± 1.32. This uptake could be competitively blocked to a low level (0.74 ± 0.17 %ID/g, P < 0.05). In contrast, [68Ga]Ga-NOTA-ABDG6 showed prolonged circulation and relatively reduced renal uptake. However, its affinity was relatively low (KD = 15.3 nM), and tumor retention did not improve over the 6 h observation period. Taken together, Two GPC3-targeted sdAb PET probes, [68Ga]Ga-NOTA-G6 and [68Ga]Ga-NOTA-ABDG6, were successfully developed. [68Ga]Ga-NOTA-G6 enabled high-contrast, high-specificity imaging of GPC3-positive HCC lesions. Although [68Ga]Ga-NOTA-ABDG6 achieved prolonged circulation, it did not produce enhanced tumor accumulation during the six-hour observation period. Further studies with longer-half-life radionuclides are needed for extended observation.

items.title: Harnessing Enzymatic Cascade Reactions in a Glycopolymeric Nanoreactor
items.abstract: Enzyme cascade reactions are fundamental to nearly all cellular processes in living systems, which are predominantly governed by compartmentalization. Herein, we present a stimuli-responsive glycopolymeric nanoassembly that undergoes enzyme-triggered morphological evolution while fostering compartmentalized multienzyme cascade reactions. The β-galactosidase-triggered morphological transformations of the self-assembled nanostructures were systematically investigated at different time intervals using transmission electron microscopy and dynamic light scattering. The surface-exposed galactose residues endowed the glycopolymer nanoassemblies with lectin-binding capability while enabling efficient encapsulation and β-galactosidase-responsive release profiles of small-molecule anticancer drugs and therapeutic proteins (insulin and lysozyme). To further mimic the complexity of cellular systems, a co-assembled nanoaggregate was constructed by combining the glycopolymer with a PEGylated aryl boronic acid-based polymer, exploiting their inherent co-assembly formation behaviour. This co-assembled system incorporated a second enzyme cascade, enabling more sophisticated biomimetic functions. Thus, the present work demonstrates a stimuli-responsive polymeric nanosystem that functions as a compartmentalised nanoreactor harbouring multi-enzyme cascade reactions.

items.title: Metal-Centered Spin-State Switching Promotes Stereodivergent Synthesis of E - and Z -Allylamines
items.abstract: Spin state offers a fundamental yet underexplored handle for controlling stereoselectivity in transition-metal catalysis. Here we show that metal-centered spin-state switching, within an invariant weak-field bipyridine framework, promotes E/Z divergence in allylic substitution, enabling access to geometrically defined allylamines from common precursors. High-spin Ni catalysts selectively afford E-allylamines, whereas low-spin Pd catalysts deliver the corresponding Z-isomers. Broad metal studies with Fe, Rh and Ir systems further support the association between metal-centered spin state and alkene geometry. Mechanistic experiments and density functional theory (DFT) analyses reveal the origin of this stereodivergent outcome: spin-state-dependent electronic structures reshape catalyst–substrate interactions, thereby selectively stabilizing the competing E- or Z-forming transition states. The paired E/Z products enable concise syntheses of pharmaceutically relevant molecules and reveal configuration-dependent biological activities. This work establishes catalyst spin state as a design parameter for the stereodivergent control of alkene geometry.

items.title: N-Heterocyclic Carbene (NHC)-Catalyzed Synthesis of Atropisomers Beyond C–C Axial Chirality
items.abstract: Axial chirality is a prominent stereochemical element found in various natural products, pharmaceuticals, ligands, catalysts, and functional materials. While substantial progress has been made in the atroposelective synthesis of C–C axially chiral biaryls, the construction of atropisomers featuring C–N, C–O, and N–N chiral axes remains challenging owing to their lower rotational barriers and diminished configurational stability. In recent years, N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) catalysis has emerged as a versatile platform for addressing these challenges, enabling the efficient and enantioselective synthesis of diverse atropisomeric architectures through unique activation modes and reaction pathways. This Account highlights advances in NHC-catalyzed synthesis of atropisomers beyond the traditional C–C axial chirality. The utilization of the unique reactivity modes of NHCs in Stetter reaction, (3 + 3) annulation, acid activation strategy, N-acylation, O-acylation, and imine umpolung have unlocked the access to these distinct atropisomeric motifs beyond the C–C chiral axis. In 2021, we have reported the NHC-catalyzed desymmetrization of prochiral N-aryl maleimides via a Stetter–aldol cascade/oxidation sequence, providing axially chiral N-aryl succinimides with excellent stereocontrol. DFT studies indicated that the aldol step proceeds without direct involvement of carbenes. Complementarily, kinetic resolution (KR) of racemic N-aryl aminomaleimides through NHC-catalyzed (3 + 3) annulation furnished highly enantioenriched products bearing both axial and central chirality. Subsequent NHC-catalyzed atroposelective amidation provided access to N-aryl phthalimides and maleimides via direct N–C(O) bond formation. More recently, we demonstrated NHC-catalyzed dynamic kinetic resolution (DKR) of cyclic imides having rotationally restricted C–N bond for the synthesis of C–N axially chiral pyridinones through (3 + 3) annulation. Subsequently, we turned our attention to the synthesis of N–N atropisomers where NHC-catalyzed atroposelective amidation has allowed the synthesis of N–N axially chiral 3-aminoquinazolinones in high yields and enantioselectivities. Furthermore, NHC-catalyzed atroposelective (3 + 3) annulations of indole- and pyrrole-derived enamines have been achieved providing structurally complex heterocycles with N–N axial and central chirality with excellent stereoselectivity and configurational stability. Later, this annulation strategy has been extended to the diastereo- and enantioselective synthesis of N–N axially chiral quinolinones and quinoxalinones. Finally, we demonstrated the synthesis of a highly challenging class of C–O atropisomers, the diaryl ethers because of the flexibility of the dual C–O axis. The NHC-catalyzed atroposelective desymmetrization strategy enabled the enantioselective synthesis of axially chiral diaryl ethers possessing dual C–O axes, delivering products with excellent enantioselectivities. Furthermore, we have also demonstrated a DKR approach that affords C–O axially chiral benzonitriles through NHC-catalyzed atroposelective umpolung of aldimines. It is reasonable to believe that the recent advances highlight the power of NHC catalysis in expanding axial chirality beyond classical C–C biaryl frameworks. By integrating mechanistic insights, catalytic innovation, and synthetic applications, this Account is likely to provide a comprehensive overview of NHC-enabled atroposelective synthesis and serves as a valuable guide for developing novel atropisomers with potential applications in asymmetric catalysis, drug discovery, and materials science.

items.title: Photoinduced Direct N-Arylation of Nitroalkanes at Ambient Temperature via 1,2-Boronate Shift
items.abstract: Although photoexcited nitroarenes have been explored for facile reductive couplings, owing to their higher energetic n→π* electronic transition compared to the nitroarenes, the metal-free reductive C-N coupling reaction with nitroalkane under the photochemical condition is not known. We report, for the first time, the photoexcitation of nitroalkanes and their participation in metal- and photocatalyst-free reductive C−N coupling with arylboronic acids at ambient temperature via 1,2-boronate shift. This protocol overcomes the long-standing challenge of photoexciting nitroalkanes, including nitromethane, despite their volatility and explosivity. Thus, nitromethane, widely used as a solvent, is explored as a methylamine surrogate. A series of nitroalkanes conjugated with natural products and pharmaceuticals underwent metal-free reductive coupling with boronic acids, in quantitative yields. Photophysical studies and control experiments suggest that nitroalkanes were excited to the triplet diradical state near 390 nm and then participated in electron transfer with PPh3/phosphite as the deoxygenating agents. This redox process is triggered by the formation of a thermodynamically favourable nitroso intermediate and POPh3. Subsequently, a pre-nitrene intermediate may form, which attacks the electron-deficient boron centre, followed by a 1,2-boronate shift accessing the N-arylated product. Remarkably, no external photocatalyst is required, demonstrating nitroalkane as a photosensitizer for the first time. This method is operationally simple, industrially viable and valuable for synthesizing various biologically important scaffolds and late-stage modification of the drug molecules at room temperature.

items.title: An environment-conditioned QM/MM resource for protein–ligand electron densities and quantum-informed pose rescoring
items.abstract: Structure-based drug design relies on geometric and empirical features, whereas electron density encodes polarization and weak interactions but is costly to obtain at biomolecular scale. We present a multilevel QM/MM resource from MISATO trajectories and PDBbind complexes, comprising 104,636 electronic-structure records across 96,467 geometries. Physics-embedded equivariant surrogates achieve 0.326–0.384% density NMAE on PDB-disjoint tests with explicit TIP3P water; predicted receptor electrostatic potentials agree with reference values (Pearson r = 0.99529). For pose rescoring, we evaluated quantum electrostatic and non-covalent interaction descriptors on 405 four-filter generalization complexes, each with 20 poses from Vina, smina and AutoDock4, including at least one with heavy-atom RMSD <2.0 Å. Matched ablations improve Top-1 recovery by 7.41 percentage points over Vina-derived inputs and by 3.70–4.69 points over geometry-only arms. Full models achieve 69.14–70.12% Top-1 success.

items.title: Machine Learning-Driven Discovery of an Endoplasmic Reticulum-Targeting Gallium(III) Complex that Triggers Immunogenic Paraptosis in Osteosarcoma
items.abstract: Osteosarcoma is a highly aggressive bone tumor characterized by profound chemoresistance and immune evasion, resulting in poor clinical prognoses. The rational design of metallodrugs to overcome these obstacles is a formidable challenge, as traditional discovery methods are inefficient for predicting the organelle-specific targeting required for specific mechanisms of action. Here, we introduce a machine learning-driven platform to rationally design and identify endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-targeting Ga(III) complexes capable of activating nonapoptotic immunogenic cell death. This strategy identified Ga20, a complex that triggers a dual mechanism of paraptosis and immunogenic cell death (ICD), directly addressing osteosarcoma’s apoptosis resistance. Formulated as a polymeric nanoparticle (Ga NP) for targeted in vivo delivery, this nanomedicine demonstrated profound tumor growth inhibition across aggressive and clinically relevant orthotopic, metastatic, bilateral, and patient-derived xenograft models. Critically, Ga NP treatment generated a durable in situ vaccine effect, conferring long-term immune memory and preventing tumor recurrence and metastasis. This work establishes a strategy for the computational design of organelle-targeted metallodrugs and presents a powerful chemoimmunotherapy that directly addresses the core clinical challenges of osteosarcoma.

items.title: Iron‐Catalyzed Regioselective Amidation of Pyridines via Zincke Imine Intermediates
items.abstract: Achieving precise site‐selective functionalization of pyridines is highly desirable in synthetic and medicinal chemistry. Herein, we present an operationally simple iron‐catalyzed protocol for accessing C3‐amidated pyridines. The reaction harnesses an in situ‐generated Fe–acylnitrenoid that interacts with Zincke imines, which serve as temporarily dearomatized forms of pyridines. The reaction exhibits broad substrate scope across C2‐, C3‐, C4‐, or disubstituted pyridine substrates. This approach was also successfully implemented in a telescoped one‐pot procedure by directly employing pyridines. Mechanistic and computational studies revealed that a high‐spin Fe(III)–imidyl radical would be the key amidating species.

items.title: Optimization of 8-Hydroxyquinolines as Potent GLI1-Targeting Hedgehog Pathway Inhibitors with anti-SHH Medulloblastoma Activity
A Highly Active and Promiscuous Esterase for Amide Bond Synthesis under Aqueous Conditions
items.abstract: A growing number of hydrolase enzymes show acyltransferase activity under aqueous conditions. However, the competing hydrolysis reaction and the limited catalytic rates for these enzymes prevent them from being routinely used for synthetic applications. To find improved enzymes, we generated an enzyme panel based on promiscuous acyltransferase template enzymes. We identified SoEst12, a highly active and selective enzyme belonging to the family VIII carboxylesterases. Kinetics show that this enzyme is up to 8600× faster (kcatapp) than the well-studied PestE using a model reaction for amidation and that its impressive activity is not limited to the model ester. Enzyme loading studies coupled with the kinetics showed a kinetically controlled selectivity for amidation over hydrolysis, which can be best exploited when using a low enzyme loading. SoEst12 displays a wide amine substrate scope with no hydrolysis of the amide product formed. Competing hydrolysis with some of the ester substrates has been reduced by the introduction of a point mutation in the family-conserved WGG motif. Modeling of these point mutants showed that the reduced hydrolysis activity is correlated with an improved affinity for the amine. The SoEst12 crystal structure was solved, and the N-terminus of a cleaved tag of a symmetry neighbor was found inserted into the active site of the enzyme close to a bound acetate, suggesting a “cleaved amide” and giving mechanistic insight into the high activity and selectivity shown by SoEst12. We demonstrate the synthetic potential of SoEst12 by synthesizing the antiarrhythmic drug procainamide and an AKT inhibitor intermediate in buffer using a low biocatalyst loading.

items.title: Copper-Catalyzed α-C–H Cyanation of Amides via Sequential Electron Transfer/Hydrogen Atom Transfer (ET/HAT)
items.abstract: Cyanated amides, α-cyano amides and α-amino nitriles, are highly desirable motifs and valuable synthons owing to their important roles in chemical synthesis and medicinal chemistry. Conventional approaches to these compounds typically rely on the nucleophilic attack of cyanide on imines (iminium ions) or on radical transformations from prefunctionalized alkyl halides, respectively. Herein, we report a ligand-free, copper-catalyzed cyanation reaction that enables the preparation of both classes of compounds via direct C−H functionalization without light. This method harnesses the strongly reducing carbon dioxide radical anion, aryl-radical-mediated intramolecular 1,5-HAT, and Cu-catalyzed aliphatic cyanation, featuring an efficient sequence of ET/HAT events. The reaction operates simply under mild conditions, employs inexpensive commercial reagents, exhibits broad functional group compatibility and can be applied to functionalize natural products and bioactive molecules with good yields.

items.title: Novel Piperidinyl-triazinyl-phenols for the Treatment of Inflammatory Diseases including Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s Diseases
items.abstract: A series of 3-piperidyl-amino-l,2,4-triazin-6-yl-phenol analogs is described as inhibitors of NLRP3. NLR proteins are involved in the immune system. The activated NLRP3 protein assembles with other proteins into inflammasomes leading to downstream proteolytic events including the formation of proinflammatory cytokines such as IL-1B and IL 18. Inhibition of NLRP3 represents a potential treatment for multiple inflammatory diseases including Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), metabolic dysfunction-associated Steatohepatitis (MASH), and multiple sclerosis.

items.title: Chemical Control of Quorum Sensing Rewires Mixed Bacterial Communities
items.abstract: Microbial communities are central to host and environmental health, yet their dysregulation can drive diseases. Chemical strategies for selectively reprogramming community composition remain limited. Here, we show that agonists of the accessory gene regulator (agr) quorum sensing system provide a powerful, nonbactericidal approach to reshape staphylococcal biofilm communities. In mixed biofilms of multiple Staphylococcus epidermidis strains, selective agr activation produces pronounced sequence-dependent shifts in community composition in vitro. This targeted remodeling enhances the susceptibility of the community to antibiotic treatment. Extending this strategy to interspecies systems, we demonstrate that agr agonists reduce the abundance of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus by >95% in mixed biofilms with S. epidermidis without relying on bactericidal activity. Notably, the efficacy of agr-mediated community control is modulated by iron availability, revealing an environmental layer of regulation. Together, these findings support quorum sensing agonism as a chemically precise strategy to manipulate microbial communities by exploiting intrinsic signaling differences with implications spanning human health and agriculture.

items.title: Novel Triple-action Pt(IV) prodrugs with carbocyanine and chalcone in axial position: photoactivation, tumor targeting, fluorescent tumor visualization, and high therapeutic efficacy
items.abstract: Pt(IV) prodrugs are highly promising platform for anticancer agents due to the ability to fine-tune the structure and properties of the prodrug by varying the axial ligand conjugated with the Pt(IV) core. In this study, we have synthesized photoactivated Pt(IV) prodrugs with NIR-absorbing cyanine and chalcone in axial positions, which combine the advantages of dual-target chemotherapy, controlled photoactivation, photodynamic therapy, and fluorescent NIR bioimaging. The cyanine-chalcone-based prodrug Pt-4 demonstrated the ability to generate ROS, release carboplatin intracellularly and promote p53 expression under 660 nm light. Pt-4 prodrug demonstrated superior pharmacokinetic properties to carboplatin and excellent fluorescent imaging of CT-26 tumors. In vivo, Pt-4 prodrug + 660 nm light stimulated adaptive immune response in LLC tumors and significantly inhibited tumor growth of homograft CT-26 tumor. Our findings demonstrate excellent potential of Pt(IV)-carbocyanine light-activatable platform for tumor imaging, drug delivery and tumor eradication.

items.title: A Stereocontrolled Synthesis of (4R)-1-Methyl-4-Propyl-L-Proline, the Amino Acid Fragment of Lincomycin
items.abstract: We present a concise route for the stereoselective conversion of commercial (cis)-4-hydroxy-L-proline into (4R)-1-methyl-4-propyl-L-proline, the amino acid fragment found in the clinically used antibacterial antibiotic lincomycin. Our account of success is accompanied by a discussion of two failed routes. The rise of antimicrobial resistance necessitates the continued search for new antibacterial agents.

items.title: Chemical Biology in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: From Ligand Discovery to Virtual Cells
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly changing how scientists, including chemical biologists, conduct research. This review is intended to serve as an introduction for chemical biologists to applications of artificial intelligence in chemical biology. We review how chemical and biological data are featurized, the types of models commonly used in chemical biology applications, challenges in assessing accuracy of artificial intelligence models, and recent developments in agentic artificial intelligence for autonomous research. The applications we will cover include protein structure prediction, ligand discovery, peptide and protein design, prediction of mutational effects, interactomics and gene regulation, and virtual cells.

items.title: Xuandemycins A−F: Chlorinated Naphthacemycins from Marine-Derived Actinomycete Streptomyces albiaxialis NAK5495 and Their Antibacterial Activity
items.abstract: Naphthacemycin is a type of rare antibacterial aromatic polyketides containing an unique 1-phenylnaphthacene skeleton, usually substituted with one or more chlorine atoms. Here we reported the discovery of six new chlorinated naphthacemycins, xuandemycins A−F (1−6), from the culture of Streptomyces albiaxialis NAK5495, a marine-derived actinomycete strain from the Xisha Islands. The structures of these natural products were fully elucidated by NMR spectroscopy, HRESIMS and X-ray crystallographic analysis. A plausible biosynthetic pathway for 1−6 was proposed based on the analysis of their biosythetic gene cluster. All of these new xuandemycins were evaluated for antibacterial activity, with 2 and 4 exhibiting selective inhibitory activity against the aquaculture pathogen Lactococcus garvieae. These findings expand the chemical diversity of the family of naphthacemycin natural products and could offer valuable lead scaffolds for the development of novel antibacterial agents to address the growing challenge of drug resistance.

items.title: Chemical Synthesis of Thrombostasin: An Anticoagulant Protein Produced by the Horn Fly Haematobia irritans
items.abstract: Thrombostasin is a cysteine-free anticoagulant protein produced by the horn fly Haematobia irritans that features an unusual stretch of seven consecutive aspartate residues within the polypeptide sequence. Here, we report the first chemical synthesis of native thrombostasin and a hepta-glutamate analogue using one-pot, kinetically controlled peptide ligations. Both variants exhibited nanomolar inhibitory activity against α-thrombin, with the hepta-glutamate analogue 9-fold more active than the native protein. The hepta-glutamate analogue of thrombostasin also possessed potent anticoagulant activity in an activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) assay, with notable prolongation of clotting time observed down at a concentration of 300 nM.

items.title: EVALUATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS, PHYSICOCHEMICAL CHARACTERISTICS, PHYTOCHEMICAL CONSTITUENTS AND GC-MS ANALYSIS OF POLYALTHIA LONGIFOLIA ETHANOL LEAF EXTRACTS
items.abstract: In the array of traditional medicine, Polyalthia longifolia is one of the highly esteemed plants because of its high potency for curing numerous diseases. The plant contains various bioactive compounds that promote a healthy life. Purpose: This study involves the assessment of the impact of environmental conditions on the physicochemical properties, phytochemical analysis, and the GC-MS characterization of bioactive chemicals in polyalthia longifolia leaf extracts. Design of study: The leaf sample was taken at various times, including 6:00 a.m., 1:00 p.m., and 6:00 p.m. The leaf of Polyalthia longifolia was screened qualitatively for phytoconstituents using n-hexane and ethanol extracts. Method: The extraction process involved using polar solvents, maceration for 72 hours, extracting 250 g of powdered samples, decanting, filtering, drying, concentrating, and storing the crude extract for further analysis. Results: The preliminary report of these leaf extracts confirmed the presence of these phytochemicals: alkaloids, tannins, flavonoids, steroids, glycosides, saponins, carbohydrates, and anthraquinones. GC-MS characterization showed that the most abundant compounds were found to be greater than 1%. Guaia-1(10) 11-diene at all times of harvest: morning (3.81%), afternoon (8.22%), and evening (9.52%)., followed by Spiro[5.5]undec-2-ene, 3, 7, 7-trimethyl-11-methylene- morning (3.99%), afternoon (6.76%), and evening (8.39%), followed by hexadecanoic acid, ethyl ester in the morning (4.19%), afternoon (4.81%), and evening (4.70%), respectively. Conclusion: This study suggests that P. longifolia leaf extracts are rich in phytochemicals like tannin, flavonoids, saponin, glycosides, and alkaloids and have potential as a drug source. However, further studies are recommended to determine the toxicological safety of these extracts and to investigate how time, temperature and other environmental conditions affect the bioactive compounds in this leaf.

items.title: De Novo Design of Blood-Brain Barrier-Penetrant, P-Glycoprotein-Evading EGFR Inhibitors and Hypoxia-Activated Trapping Analogs for Glioblastoma
items.abstract: Background: Most Glioblastoma Multiforme (GBM) tumors about 50% grow because of a very overreactive protein called EGFR (Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor). Existing drugs like Erlotinib and Gefitinib work great for lung cancer, but they are not effective for brain cancer and subsequently fail for three main reasons. First, they are too water-attracting (polar, with TPSA > 74 Å2), and second, they are very heavy with a molecular weight above 390 Da. Due to all of these factors, they are unable to cross the Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB). Third, even if they get inside, the brain has security systems like P-glycoprotein (P-gp), which pushes them back outside into the blood, thereby wasting their potential inside the brain. Methods: In order to solve this without the use of an expensive lab, we came up with an automated cloud pipeline on GitHub Actions in collaboration with an LLM (Google Gemini). There are four tools that we used: 1. SELFIES: A system that mutates molecules with proper valency and bonding rules to make them 100% chemically valid. 2. Adaptive Mutation Scaling (σ / sigma): A controller where small tweaks are made when improving a winning molecule, and if the molecule is stuck or not what we are looking for, it makes a bigger jump to get a new mutation. 3. XGBoost: A regressor model trained on real lab data (ChEMBL203) with a similarity guardrail. 4. 3D Protein Docking (PDB: 1M17): A 3D check to test how each molecule actually fits inside the human EGFR crystal structure for Glioblastoma. In total, we completed 1,417,569 generations and the engine tested 4,317,102 unique molecules. Results: There were five reward-hacking measures taken by the regression model and mutator, which were fixed via our iterative human-in-the-loop system: 5. Self-Training Echo Chambers: First, we stopped the AI from feeding its own unverified guesses back into its training data, because those unverified guesses were providing high score results that are practically impossible (pIC50 > 150), which is what we called echo chambers. 6. Unstable Sulfur Triple Bonds: Second, we blocked unstable sulfur triple bonds (ClS#CO...) that would attack healthy cells even though they were yielding a high score in both Blood-Brain Barrier penetration and pIC50 score. 7. Flat Double-Bond Tails Crashing in 3D: Third, we caught flat double-bond tails (=CCCO and NCCC=C1...) that looked good in 2D math but crashed into the roof (Leu694) of the 3D protein pocket, which means they cannot actually attach properly to the Glioblastoma EGFR protein. 8. Tightly Bent Small Rings: Fourth, we blocked tightly bent 3- and 4-membered small rings ([r3] and OC1=NC=C1), because carbon and nitrogen bonds naturally sit at 109.5° to 120°, and forcing them into 60°–90° angles creates severe angle strain (Baeyer strain) that makes them snap open in water. 9. Reactive Chlorine Warheads: Fifth, we filtered out toxic chlorine warheads (-CH2Cl), which are similar to sulfur triple bonds where they could actually harm healthy cells even though they provided good theoretical results. After all of these conversions and fixing these loopholes, we finally got a winner, which is Lead 1 (CCc1c(Nc2cccc(F)c2)ncnc1N1CCCO1). This engine discovered a family of compact, lightweight pyrimidine molecules ranging from 268 to 309 Da that had strong EGFR blocking power (IC50 = 5.20–6.92 nM, pIC50 = 8.16–8.28) and strong 3D binding (ΔG = -7.54 to -8.90 kcal/mol). For further verification, we tested it on the SwissADME server, which confirmed that our Lead 1 can actually cross the Blood-Brain Barrier (TPSA = 50.28 Å2), escapes the P-gp pump (P-gp substrate: No), does not block liver enzymes (CYP3A4 inhibitor: No), and has zero toxicity alerts (0 PAINS / 0 Brenk alerts). This was our result for Lead 1 after the verifications and filters that we passed all the molecules through. items.title: Translational Potential of New Academic Synthetic Transformations: Lessons from the Aza Paternò–Büchi Reaction
items.abstract: Despite steady advances in synthetic methodology, the reactions routinely used in medicinal chemistry have changed little over several decades, which suggests that discovering a reaction and establishing it as a practical tool are separate challenges. Academic methods are typically judged by yield, selectivity, and scope, whereas industrial adoption also depends on supply-chain security, reagent availability, and scalability. As a supplier of building blocks for drug discovery, we at Enamine examined this gap through a collaboration with the Schindler laboratory, aimed at translating the group’s 2019 visiblelight-mediated intramolecular aza Paternò–Büchi reaction into a commercial azetidine building block pipeline. Using an inexpensive organic photosensitizer, we successfully scaled the key [2+2] photocycloaddition in batch and flow, delivering 12 unique azetidine building blocks on up to 50 g scale, and accessed five additional scaffolds through post-synthetic modification. The remaining barriers arose outside the key step and traced to the oxime auxiliary that the cycloaddition requires, which limited both substrate preparation and access to free N–H azetidines. The findings from this case study show that translational readiness depends on the full synthetic sequence, and a stage-by-stage assessment identifies where further development is needed before industry uptake can be successful.

items.title: Halonium-Induced Cyclization of 5-Polyfluoroalkyl-1-arylpentane-1,3,5-triones as a Switchable Method for the Directed Synthesis of Halogenated 4-Pyrones or 3-Hydroxyfurans
items.abstract: Halogenated 4-pyrones are privileged building blocks in organic synthesis, medicinal chemistry, and materials science, yet their direct synthesis under mild conditions remains largely unexplored. Herein, we report a halonium-induced dehydrative cyclization of 5-polyfluoroalkyl-1-arylpentane-1,3,5-triones under acidic conditions, which delivers polyfluoroalkyl-containing halogenated 4-pyrones in up to 75% yield. This one-pot, atom-economic protocol exhibits excellent chemo- and regioselectivity with chlorinating, brominating, and iodinating agents. Strikingly, shifting the tautomeric equilibrium of the triketone toward the open-chain form under basic conditions completely reverses the chemoselectivity: the reaction switches to oxidative halocyclization, affording 3-hydroxyfurans in up to 62% yield with outstanding chemo- and regiocontrol. The synthetic utility of the halocyclization products is demonstrated by gram-scale reactions and their subsequent functionalization.

items.title: Enantio- and Diastereoselective C–H [4 + 2] Annulation of Ferrocenamides with Allenes: Dynamic Kinetic Resolution Approach to Dual Chirality
items.abstract: Planar and central chiral ferrocenes are privileged ligands for enantioselective transformation in industry and academia, yet their synthesis generally involves tedious multistep routes. Herein, we report a solvent-controlled strategy that suppresses the competing β-hydride elimination pathway and redirects the catalytic manifold toward regioselective reductive elimination to enable the synthesis of ferrocene-fused six-membered N-heterocycles bearing both planar and central chirality through a scalable asymmetric [4 + 2] annulation with up to 80% yield and 98% ee. We propose that the reaction proceeds through dynamic kinetic resolution (DKR) of rhodacycle intermediates combined with chirality transfer, in which the stereochemical information embedded in the chiral allene is translated into two distinct stereogenic elements—a planar-chiral ferrocene and a point stereocenter. Mechanistic studies by KIE studies, solvent-coordinated NMR studies, control experiments and DFT calculations, reveal that solvent coordination modulates the key organometallic intermediates, favoring reductive elimination over β-hydride elimination and thereby dictating the annulation mode in the reaction.

items.title: Directed Rh(III)-Catalyzed Regioselective 2-Alkenylation of Azulenes
items.abstract: Herein, we report a rhodium-catalyzed 2-alkenylation of azulenes with styrene derivatives and activated alkenes, enabled by a readily installable N-methoxyamide directing group. This protocol provides direct access to nonannulated 2-alkenylated azulenes through C2-selective C–H functionalization, complementing established methods that exploit the inherent reactivity of the C1 and C3 positions. The reaction accommodates a broad range of styrene derivatives and activated alkenes bearing ester, ketone, amide, and phosphonate groups, affording the corresponding products in good to excellent yields. Alkenes derived from bioactive molecules, including terpene-, alkaloid-, and steroid-based substrates, were also compatible, furnishing blue-colored azulene-containing conjugates with potential utility as visual labels.

items.title: QSG-7701 is not a Normal hepatocyte line: Reassessing the claimed selectivity of mitochondria-targeted podophyllotoxin derivatives
items.abstract: This communication addresses a critical interpretation issue in a recent study on mitochondria-targeted podophyllotoxin derivatives for liver cancer therapy. The authors used QSG-7701 as a normal hepatocyte comparator to calculate selectivity indices, although QSG-7701 has been reported to be HeLa-derived. HepG2, the principal liver tumor cell model examined, is hepatoblastoma-derived rather than hepatocellular carcinoma-derived. For compound 6d, the reported ratio of 2.29 therefore represents a modest difference in potency between two tumor-derived cell lines, not selectivity for liver tumor cells over normal hepatocytes. This misclassification undermines conclusions concerning reduced normal hepatocyte toxicity and a therapeutic window, without necessarily invalidating the reported antiproliferative, mitochondrial colocalization, or apoptosis findings. Assessment of normal hepatocyte sparing requires authenticated and appropriately validated non-malignant human liver models.

items.title: Structure–activity relationship optimization of ML221-derived non-peptide Apelin receptor antagonists with anti-angiogenic activity
Photocatalytic Disruption of Concurrent Redox Axes Elicits Convergent Redox Collapse
items.abstract: The interconnected antioxidant systems of cancer cells, centered on the glutathione and thioredoxin axes, constitute a promising therapeutic vulnerability. However, simultaneous disruption of both axes by dual‐inhibitor regimens is hampered by pharmacokinetic asynchrony.
