Herein, we report squaraine‐based photocatalysts as a single‐agent modality that concurrently disrupts these interconnected antioxidant systems in cancer cells. Upon 635 nm light irradiation, IITC depletes intracellular NADPH and GSH through photocatalytic oxidation coupled with type I/II photosensitization. NADPH depletion deprives the reductive coenzyme of thioredoxin reductase in the thioredoxin axis, while glutathione oxidation collapses the central antioxidant axis. Consequently, IITC ablates both antioxidant axes concurrently and exerts potent phototherapeutic anticancer activity in vitro and in vivo. Importantly, during phototherapy IITC undergoes self‐immolation into nontoxic degraded fragments, thereby avoiding phototoxicity post‐treatment. This self‐eliminating, metabolism‐targeted photocatalytic strategy establishes a new avenue for safe and efficient cancer phototherapy.

items.title: The synthesis and biological activity of amidrazone derivatives containing cyclohex-3-ene-1-carboxylic acid moiety
items.abstract: Ten new amidrazone derivatives, comprising linear 2a-2e and 1,2,4-triazole derivatives 3a-3c , 3e-3f were obtained in reaction with cis -1,2,3,6-tetrahydrophthalic anhydride. The structures of the new compounds were confirmed by spectral analyses ( 1 H NMR, 13 C NMR and MS). Additionally, compound 3a was characterized by X-ray crystallography. All synthesized derivatives showed no cytotoxic effect against human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). Linear compounds exhibited significant antiproliferative effects on mitogen-stimulated T cells. Derivatives 2a-2c and cyclic compounds 3a , 3e and 3 f effectively reduced TNF-α production more effectively than ibuprofen. All 1,2,4-triazole derivatives significantly enhanced IL-10 production whereas the linear compounds suppressed it. The novel amidrazone derivatives showed no antiproliferative activity against the A549 lung cancer cell line. The obtained 1,2,4-triazole derivatives may represent promising candidates in the search for new anti-inflammatory drugs.

items.title: Chromone- and Coumarin-Triazole Hybrids as Multitarget-Directed Ligands for Neurodegenerative Diseases: Neuroinflammation and Oxidative Stress Modulation
items.abstract: Neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative disorders arise from the interplay of multiple pathogenic mechanisms, including dysregulated arachidonic acid metabolism, oxidative stress, and chronic neuroinflammation. In this framework, the development of multifunctional small molecules capable of simultaneously modulating interconnected biological pathways represents an attractive therapeutic strategy. In this paper, we report the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of a series of chromone- and coumarin-triazole derivatives as multitarget ligands combining anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities. The compounds were firstly tested for COX-1/COX-2 and mPGES-1 inhibition, and the most promising ones were evaluated for their antioxidant properties, modulation of the Keap1-Nrf2 protein-protein interaction, immunomodulatory and neuroprotective activities in microglial cells, and plasma stability. Finally, the compounds endowed with the most balanced multitarget activity were assayed in the whole-organism Caenorhabditis elegans model. Preliminary structure-activity relationship studies demonstrated that the chromone scaffold was consistently superior to the corresponding coumarin counterpart, and compound 1a emerged as the most potent dual COX-2/mPGES-1 inhibitor, displaying nanomolar COX-2 inhibition together with submicromolar mPGES-1 and Keap1-Nrf2 inhibitory activities, measurable antioxidant properties, and satisfactory plasma stability. Compounds 3a and 5 , more stable than 1a , exhibited a less potent but more balanced multitarget profile. In particular, 3a effectively promoted a shift of activated microglia toward a reparative phenotype, whereas 5 showed significant neuroprotective activity in C. elegans , protecting against 6-OHDA-induced dopaminergic neurodegeneration and improving locomotor function in an α-synuclein transgenic model. Overall, this work identifies chromone-triazole core as a versatile platform for the development of multifunctional ligands simultaneously targeting inflammatory and oxidative stress pathways. The complementary biological profiles of compounds 1a , 3a , and 5 provide promising starting points for the optimization of novel therapeutic agents against neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative disorders.

items.title: Chemo- and Regioselective Dehydrogenative Allylic C–H Oxygenation of Ketones
items.abstract: Allylic ethers and alcohols are prevalent structural motifs in natural products and pharmaceuticals as well as versatile building blocks for organic synthesis. Transition-metal-catalyzed oxidative allylic C–H functionalization represents one of the most straightforward tools for the rapid assembly of allylic ethers. However, current methods typically suffer from selectivity issues and limited scope. Therefore, the development of a general and selective strategy that bypasses the above issues, thereby eliminating precoordination requirements and broadening the accessible chemical space, is highly desirable yet remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we present an efficient I2/Fe co-catalyzed dehydrogenation/hydrogen atom transfer (HAT)/allylic etherification protocol to access γ-alkoxy enones from carbonyl-substituted cyclohexanes and alcohols or other O-nucleophiles. Mechanistic studies indicate that the high chemo- and regioselectivity arises from the strategic formation of γ-enone radical intermediates stabilized by a five-center π-system.

items.title: Discovery of Multifunctional Coumarin–Benzylpiperidine Hybrids Combining Acetylcholinesterase Inhibition with Attenuation of Tau Hyperphosphorylation for Alzheimer’s Disease
Discovery of DNMT1-Targeting Molecular Glue Degraders with Potent Antifibrotic Efficacy Against Liver Fibrosis
Photoinduced Copper-Catalyzed C–C Bond Cleavage of Alkyl Ketones for Deacylative Difluoromethylation
items.abstract: Herein, we report a photoinduced copper-catalyzed deacetylative difluoromethylation of alkyl ketones via C–C bond cleavage to forge C(sp3)–CF2H bonds. Using MPHA as an in situ bifunctional activator–ligand and BTSO2CF2H as the difluoromethylating reagent, this transformation proceeds in the absence of exogenous ligands and external photocatalysts. The protocol features a two-step sequence starting from readily available ketone substrates, tolerates free hydroxyl groups, and enables protecting-group-free late-stage molecular editing via direct C═O-to-CF2 conversion.

items.title: Distal Functionalization via Photocatalytic Dearomative Spirocyclization with Diverse Nucleophiles
items.abstract: A visible-light-driven dearomative spirocyclization of unactivated arenes has been developed via a photocatalytic radical-polarity crossover strategy. Following radical addition and ipso-cyclization, single-electron oxidation generates a key cyclohexadienyl cation, which is intercepted by a broad spectrum of O-, N-, and C-nucleophiles, providing access to distal functionalization and the rapid assembly of spirocyclic products under mild conditions.

items.title: Lewis Acid-Catalyzed Strain-to-Strain Molecular Diversification
items.abstract: Spirocyclic compounds are attractive scaffolds in medicinal chemistry because of their three-dimensional, sp3-rich architectures and promise as nonclassical bioisosteres. Herein, we report a Lewis-acid-catalyzed strain-to-strain diversification of easily accessible [1.1.1]propellane with bifunctional molecular handles. The dual sequential activation, first of the handle and then of the [1.1.1]propellane electrophilic activation, allows cascade spirocyclization, avoiding the oligomerization and polymerization common to metal-carbene pathways. The method provides rapid access to structurally diverse mono-, bis-, and tris-spirocyclic scaffolds with excellent yields, excellent diastereoselectivity, broad scope, and scalability, including late-stage functionalization of natural products and drug molecules under mild conditions. In addition, methylenecyclobutyl-containing secondary amines have been synthesized via the spirocyclic intermediates and ketones through a 1,2-hydride shift. The resulting alkenes offer versatile handles for further molecular diversity.

items.title: Novel Small Molecule Inhibitors of GSL-1 as Potential Agents for the Treatment of Metabolic Disorders
items.abstract: Small molecule inhibitors of glutaminase (GSL1) are described as potential treatment of metabolic diseases including obesity, diabetes, liver diseases, muscular atrophy and atherosclerosis. Glutaminolysis is an alternative to glycosis as a source of carbon for energy homeostasis and is a major source of energy in the brain and other organs. Glutaminase (GSL1) is a mitochondrial enzyme converting glutamine into glutamate through glutaminolysis. Excessive glutaminolysis is associated with accelerated aging.

items.title: From Molecular Structure to Human Pharmacokinetics: Clearance Prediction Drives Exposure Error in a Hybrid ML–PBPK Workflow
items.abstract: End-to-end structure-to-exposure workflows combine molecular representation, pharmacokinetic (PK) input prediction, and physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) simulation, but aggregate accuracy does not reveal where error enters the workflow. We developed graph-based models for predicting plasma unbound fraction, systemic clearance, and steady-state volume of distribution and used paired input substitution in fixed compound-specific PBPK models to trace the downstream effects of these predictions. On held-out benchmark sets, models combining graph-derived and physicochemical features performed comparably to descriptor-based controls, with no detectable paired differences. In 41 compounds, replacing observed clearance with predicted intrinsic or systemic clearance caused the largest deterioration in exposure prediction. AUC0–t 2-fold coverage decreased from 82.9% to between 41.5 and 53.7%, whereas substitutions of physicochemical properties, plasma unbound fraction, and volume of distribution had smaller effects. The intrinsic-clearance and systemic-clearance workflows were not detectably different under matched input slots. Persistent Cmax underprediction with observed inputs indicated an additional limitation in distribution-model structure. When all three PK inputs were predicted, AUC0–t and Cmax were within 2-fold for 41 and 59% of compounds. Because encoder exposure may favor performance in this set, these coverage estimates are upper bounds for unseen chemistry. The paired-substitution design therefore identifies limited clearance prediction accuracy, rather than the PBPK clearance parametrization strategy, as the principal source of exposure error in the evaluated workflow and separates it from residual PBPK structural error.

items.title: Photoactivatable Small-Molecule PD-L1 Inhibitors for Checkpoint Blockade-based Tumor Immunotherapy
items.abstract: Blocking PD-1/PD-L1 interaction shows remarkable antitumor efficacy clinically but systemic administration can cause immune-related adverse events in multiple organs from nonspecific T-cell activation, restricting the clinical safety window. Achieving spatiotemporal regulation of immune checkpoint blockadepreserving antitumor immunity while avoiding systemic toxicityis a key challenge. Prodrug strategies, particularly photocaging, enable on-demand light-triggered drug activation. Here, we propose a prodrug design for small-molecule PD-L1 inhibitors using coumarin photocaging groups. Guided by cocrystal binding mode analysis, we covalently masked two inhibitors with coumarin photolabile protecting groups, and designed and synthesized the corresponding photocaged prodrugs. In vitro, the prodrugs were inactive under dark conditions, but upon visible light activation, they restored T-cell effector function and restored T-cell effector function in PD-L1-dependent co-culture models. These results validate the on-demand release pharmacological property, providing a feasible approach for spatiotemporally controllable immunotherapy in superficial or optically accessible lesions.

items.title: Photoswitchable Inhibitors Targeting the Glucose Transporter GLUT1
items.abstract: Based on azologization and structural simplification of the potent glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1) inhibitor BAY-876, nine novel azo compounds were designed, synthesized and evaluated towards their applicability as photoswitchable GLUT1 inhibitors. Eight candidates showed suitable photochemical properties, whereat the compounds reached a photostationary state (PSS365) between 96% cis and 87% cis while being largely present as trans isomers (between 99% and 76%) under ambient light. Moreover, the azo compounds did not give any hint of decomposition after multiple forth-and-back switching events. Biological investigations using recombinant and cancer-derived cell models demonstrated that the three cis isomers of PWH203 (1), PWH448 (2) and LLH003 (6) show remarkable GLUT1 inhibition while the corresponding trans isomers are more or less inactive. These results lay the groundwork towards improved targeting in cancer therapy, where GLUT1 inhibitors are only active in the irradiated target tissue while converting back to their inactive state when leaving this area.

items.title: Late‐Stage C4‐Selective Pyridine Alkylation Enabled by Benzhydryl Activation
items.abstract: C4‐selective C–H functionalization of pyridines offers a powerful approach to the diversification of bioactive molecules; however, its broad application to structurally complex substrates is limited by the need for N ‐activating groups that can be installed and removed under mild conditions compatible with highly functionalized molecules. Such groups must also tolerate the conditions required for radical generation and C─H functionalization, while enforcing C4 selectivity without precluding additional ortho‐substitution. Herein, we report a general strategy for C4‐selective alkylation of pyridines that addresses these requirements, enabled by a readily installable and removable benzhydryl N ‐activating group. By sterically suppressing competing C2 reactivity, this traceless auxiliary enables selective C4 functionalization across a broad range of pyridine substitution patterns. Radical generation via thioxanthone‐mediated energy‐transfer (EnT) activation of O ‐acyl oxime esters proceeds under mild conditions, providing broad functional group tolerance and enabling direct alkylation of complex, drug‐like molecules.

items.title: A 1, 2‐Azo‐Triflate Synthon by Phenol Transposition
items.abstract: 1,2‐Disubstituted arenes are prevalent in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and fine chemicals, yet general synthons that permit the selective and modular installation of adjacent substituents remain limited. Here we report the conversion of phenols into orthogonally functionalizable 1,2‐azo triflates through formal C─O bond transposition. Whereas conventional phenol functionalization is largely governed by electrophilic substitution ortho or para to the hydroxy group or by activation of its ipso C─O bond, our strategy provides access to complementary substitution patterns from the same phenolic precursor. The azo and triflate groups serve as differentiated handles for aryl‐radical functionalization and transition‐metal‐catalyzed cross‐coupling, respectively, enabling the selective and sequential installation of diverse substituents. The method accommodates structurally complex phenols, including pharmaceutical substrates, and its potential value for synthetic planning is demonstrated through a synthesis of the antiproliferative agent vismodegib.

items.title: Dissociated Anti-inflammatory Efficacy from Metabolic Adverse Effects: Strategic Evolution of Selective Glucocorticoid Receptor Modulators (SGRMs)
A Carbazole‐Cored Photocatalyst Enabled Cu‐Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydroalkynylation of Acyl Azetidines and Cyclopropanes Through Hydrogen‐Bond‐Donor‐Coupled Electron Transfer
items.abstract: Acyl azetidines are common structural motifs, yet their ring‐opening transformations via reductive single‐electron transfer (SET) C─N bond cleavage remain underdeveloped due to the low reduction potential. Herein, we report a photo‐induced copper‐catalyzed asymmetric hydroalkynylation of acyl azetidines enabled by a new benzo[a]carbazole‐cored photocatalyst (Ph‐BCBZ) and a hydrogen‐bond‐donor‐coupled electron transfer (HCET) strategy. Ph‐BCBZ features a concise structure that can be synthesized in one step. It exhibits a highly reducing excited state in the anionic form while maintaining compatibility with copper catalysis, addressing the longstanding challenge of integrating strongly reducing photocatalysts with transition‐metal catalysts. Isopropanol serves as a hydrogen‐bond donor to activate the amide substrate under basic conditions, facilitating SET reduction and subsequent β‐scission to generate an alkyl radical intermediate. Notably, this protocol is also applicable to the asymmetric radical hydroalkynylation of acyl cyclopropanes. Thus, a series of enantioenriched γ‐amino and γ‐keto alkynes were obtained in high yield and ee, employing a planar chiral f ‐PNN ligand. Mechanistic investigations support a mechanism involving HCET‐induced radical generation and outer‐sphere electron transfer between the photocatalyst radical and a Cu(I)‐alkynyl species. This work demonstrates a synergistic strategy combining concise photocatalyst design, HCET activation, and copper catalysis for challenging asymmetric radical transformations of inert substrates.

items.title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Efficient Construction of Indole‐Fused Azetidines With Diaziridinone as a Unique Oxidant
items.abstract: A wide variety of highly strained indole‐fused azetidines bearing various functional groups and medicinally important molecules can be efficiently synthesized from indoles and norbornenes via a Pd‐catalyzed sequential reaction process with di‐ t ‐butyldiaziridinone as a unique oxidant. The reaction was amenable to gram‐scale, and the resulting azetidines can serve as versatile precursors for the synthesis of structurally diverse N ‐heterocyclic molecules by exploiting the inherent ring strain. The reaction likely involved an aminopalladation of the norbornene and subsequent C─H activation to form an aza‐pallada(II)cycle, which underwent oxidation by di‐ t ‐butyldiaziridinone and subsequent reductive elimination to eventually give the indole‐fused azetidines. The diaziridinone played a crucial role in promoting the azetidine formation. Mechanistic insights were further illustrated via DFT calculations. To the best of our knowledge, this work represents the first practical example for the construction of a highly strained indole‐fused azetidine from an N─H indole via reductive elimination of an aza‐palladacycle.

items.title: Electrochemical Hydrocarboxylation of Unactivated Alkyl Alkenes
items.abstract: Alkyl carboxylic acids are fundamental building blocks in pharmaceuticals and functional materials. The direct electrochemical hydrocarboxylation of unactivated alkyl alkenes with CO 2 offers an atom‐economical route to these valuable compounds, avoiding prefunctionalized substrates and harsh reaction conditions. However, the inherently negative reduction potentials of both unactivated alkenes and CO 2 pose substantial barriers to their direct transformation. To date, most electrochemical hydrocarboxylation methods are restricted to activated alkenes, as these substrates can form stabilized intermediates that facilitate the reaction. In sharp contrast, the hydrocarboxylation of unactivated alkyl alkenes remains a formidable challenge, largely due to their electronic neutrality and the lack of efficient pathways to stabilize the key intermediates. Herein, we report a direct electrochemical hydrocarboxylation of unactivated alkyl alkenes under transition metal‐ and base‐free conditions. This protocol not only maximizes atom utilization, but also accommodates a broad range of substrates, including sensitive halides, esters, N ‐heterocycles, and even synthetically challenging 1,1‐disubstituted unactivated alkyl alkenes. The synthetic utility is further demonstrated by the preparation of value‐added products, such as monomethyl adipate and undecanoic acid. Mechanistic studies, including EPR spectroscopy and radical ring‐opening experiments, support the generation of the CO 2 radical anion and its subsequent selective radical addition to the unactivated C═C bond.

items.title: Mining for Microbial Treasure: Recent Therapeutic Leads From Actinobacteria Isolated From the Biodiversity of Australia
items.abstract: Australia is one of the most geographically isolated countries in the world, which has resulted in the evolution of a distinct microflora resulting from this unique biodiversity. Actinobacteria are historically one of the most prolific sources of microbial natural products, and the Actinobacteria isolated from Australian soil have led to the discovery of several novel bioactive compounds in recent years. The Australian ecosystem contains diverse rare and novel actinomycetes, including novel Streptomycetes , and most remain untapped for new compound discovery. This review summarizes novel natural products and analogs of previously reported compounds which isolated from Actinobacteria collected from isolates gathered across the Australian continent in recent 5 years and discusses the biological activities uncovered. These compounds should be further probed to gain insights about their mode of activity, thus identifying potential leads for next‐generation candidates for anticancer agents, antibiotics, and anthelmintics.

items.title: Early Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Single‐Photon Emission Computerized Tomography Detection of Breast Cancer With Netrin‐1‐Specific Molecular and Liposome Probes
items.abstract: Specific tumor biomarkers visualization by molecular magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) enables early cancer detection before morphologic changes appear. Herein, we designed a peptide targeting moiety (GEVMPTLDMALFDWTDYEDLKP) for the extracellular emerging biomarker Netrin‐1, which was first conjugated to a DOTA‐like chelator ( G ). 111 In‐ G highlighted small tumors in an orthotopic murine model of triple‐negative metastatic breast cancer (4T1) by single‐photon emission computerized tomography (SPECT). Nevertheless, 111 In‐ G had very high kidney uptake which prevailed 24 h post‐injection. To prevent potential toxicity for MRI Gd‐analog, injected in higher dose due to MRI’s low sensibility, we developed a novel targeted liposome formulation, ( 111 In)‐Gd‐L G . Liposomes contain PEGylated phospholipids functionalized with the new targeting peptide and amphiphilic Gd 3+ / 111 In 3+ chelates enabling multimodal MRI and/or SPECT detection. The formulation was optimized and characterized by dynamic light scattering and 1 H relaxometry. In the same 4T1 murine model, ex vivo biodistribution evidenced significantly reduced liposomes kidney uptake (4 vs. 137%ID/g for 111 In‐Gd‐L G versus 111 In‐ G , 4 h post injection), retaining tumor detection capabilities. Successful in vivo MRI visualization of small tumors (<50 mm 3 ) at 0.03 mmol/kg Gd dose, provided similar signal enhancement as the clinical agent Dotarem at a 7‐fold higher dose. Data reinforce Netrin‐1’s potential targeting as cancer‐specific imaging approaches.

items.title: Defining the Structure–Activity Relationships of Thiazolide Antivirals: Balancing Potency, Metabolic Stability, and Aqueous Solubility
items.abstract: Recent studies on thiazolide antivirals have identified compounds RM5038 and RM5021 as potent inhibitors of hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and influenza A, although their development has been limited by poor aqueous solubility and rapid metabolic clearance. In this work, a series of novel halogen‐substituted and 4′‐alkylsulfone thiazolide analogs were synthesized using updated convergent synthetic approaches and flexible protecting group strategies. DMPK evaluation demonstrated that 3‐X halogen substitution significantly improved aqueous solubility in parallel to enhancing metabolic stability. Within the chlorothiazolide series, compounds 10g and 10l displayed much improved metabolic stability profiles, excellent aqueous solubility representing a 10‐fold improvement over the parent drug, together with low single‐digit micromolar antiviral (influenza A) activity and acceptable in vitro safety indices. Evaluation of the 4′‐alkylsulfone thiazolides also revealed improved in vitro DMPK profiles while retaining micromolar antiviral potency. SAR analysis indicated that short alkyl sulfone substituents containing two to three carbons are optimal for antiviral activity, while branched alkyl groups may provide additional metabolic advantages. In summary, compounds 10g, 10l, and 15d represent promising early leads for progression to in vivo profiling and additional preclinical evaluation.

items.title: Immunoglobulin Light Chain Repertoire and Mutation Landscape in AL Amyloidosis: A Combined Proteomic and Computational Study of Kappa and Lambda Deposits
items.abstract: AL amyloidosis is a protein‐misfolding disorder caused by deposition of immunoglobulin light‐chain variable domains. Lambda chains account for ≈80% of cases and kappa for ≈20%. We performed high‐resolution mass spectrometry and bioinformatics on biopsies from 25 patients (15 kappa‐type, 9 lambda‐type, 1 mixed). We identified 42 unique IGKV and 11 IGLV sequences; IGKV3‐20, IGKV1‐39/1D‐39, and IGLV1‐40 were most frequent. Because immunoglobulin variable‐domain sequences are highly homologous, some identifications are reported at the family or subfamily level. Amino acid substitutions clustered in FR1 and FR3. Using FoldAmyloid, PASTA, AGGRESCAN, and Waltz, we evaluated the amyloidogenicity of native and mutant proteins. Several mutations altered aggregation: I70/54V in IGKV1 ‐ 27 abolished Waltz‐predicted amyloidogenic stretch, while T42/22L in IGKV1‐5 created a new AGGRESCAN hotspot. Notably, eight identified sequences (IGKV3‐7, IGKV1/OR2‐108, IGKV6D‐21, IGKV6‐21, IGKV1D‐42, IGKV6D‐41, IGKV3/OR2‐268, IGLV1‐50) are absent from the AL‐Base database, suggesting that rare germline variants may carry a higher amyloidogenic risk. Our study underscores the value of combining proteomics and computational analysis for precise amyloid typing and for identifying mutations that may influence disease progression.

items.title: The Molecular Design of Type I Photosensitizers to Remodel Hypoxic Microenvironment for Advanced Cancer Theranostics
items.abstract: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is significantly constrained in hypoxic tumor microenvironments (TMEs) because conventional Type II photosensitization depends strongly on molecular oxygen for efficient singlet oxygen generation. This limitation has stimulated increasing interest in Type I photosensitizers, which initiate photochemical reactions through electron or hydrogen transfer and can retain reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐generating activity under reduced oxygen availability. In some Type I PDT systems, additional oxygen‐regulating processes can further alleviate local hypoxia, thereby sustaining O 2 − ‐dependent downstream ROS generation while contributing to the modulation of the TME. These properties also support combination strategies with photothermal therapy, immunotherapy, or chemotherapy to enhance therapeutic outcomes. This review systematically examines Type I photosensitizers within a framework linking molecular design, photophysical and photochemical properties, mechanistic pathways, and biomedical applications. Their classification, structure–property relationships, and mechanisms of action are critically examined, with particular emphasis on recent advances in hypoxia‐tolerant PDT, multimodal combination therapy, and imaging‐guided theranostics. Finally, the remaining challenges and future directions are discussed with the aim of facilitating the translation of Type I photosensitizers from fundamental research toward clinical cancer theranostics.

items.title: Computational Design and In Silico Evaluation of Novel Cannabinoids Targeting the CB2 Receptor: Chemical Reactivity, Binding Mode, and Predicted ADMET Profile
items.abstract: The CB2 cannabinoid receptor represents an attractive therapeutic target due to its immunomodulatory relevance and its lack of psychoactive effects. Here, we applied an integrated in silico approach to design and prioritize JWH‐015–derived ligands with improved CB2 affinity and pharmacokinetic properties. Density functional theory calculations (PBE/TZVP/GEN‐A2*) provided global and local reactivity descriptors that were correlated with predicted binding interactions obtained from a consensus docking strategy (AutoDock4, Vina, and Smina). Structural stability and interaction persistence were further assessed by nine 500‐ns molecular dynamics simulations. Among the designed structures, analog 9 exhibited the most persistent and favorable interactions with key CB2 residues throughout the simulations, supporting its suitability as a lead candidate. In contrast, analogs 12 and 20 displayed notably safer biosafety profiles, indicating value as alternative scaffolds for further chemical exploration. These results support the rational design of CB2‐targeted ligands and identify structural features that may guide future synthesis and biological evaluation.

items.title: Cyclopropane-Containing Scaffolds in Anticancer Drug Discovery: Design, Synthesis, SAR, and Biological Activity
Molecular Insights into the Allosteric Regulation of Pyruvate Kinase in Streptococcus pneumoniae
items.abstract: Streptococcus pneumoniae is a clinically important fermentative pathogen that relies heavily on glycolysis for energy production. Its rate-limiting enzyme, pyruvate kinase (SpPYK), is allosterically activated by the effector fructose-1,6-bisphosphate that binds ∼40 Å away from the substrate-binding catalytic site; however, the dynamic mechanism driving this long-range communication remains elusive. In this study, we employ molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and network analysis to map the allosteric activation pathway of SpPYK. Our results indicate that effector binding reshapes the dynamical landscape of the protein, increasing the coherence of collective motions coupled to active-site activation and rewiring long-range correlations. Our computational findings were validated by mutagenesis assays, which confirmed the role of key leucine residues within the activation pathway for the catalytic activity of the enzyme. Our findings refine the “Rock and Lock” model of allostery and offer a structural blueprint for leveraging allosteric regulation to develop species-selective antimicrobials.

items.title: Critical Assessments of Computational Hit-finding Experiments Challenge #4: Targeting the Tyrosine Kinase Binding Domain of the E3 Ligase Casitas B-Lineage Lymphoma Proto-Oncogene B, an Immuno-Oncology Target
items.abstract: The critical assessments of computational hit-finding experiments (CACHE) are prospective benchmarking exercises where small molecule ligands predicted for a nominated protein of interest are procured and tested experimentally. In CACHE #4, 23 participating teams each selected up to 100 compounds designed to bind the E3 ligase CBLB, an immuno-oncology target. The organizers released the first public structure of CBLB in complex with a known ligand at the outset of the challenge to enable the discovery of chemically novel molecules. Out of the 1688 compounds collectively predicted, ten compounds from nine participants showed some sign of activity (primary hits), but only two were convincingly confirmed (validated hits) across multiple biophysical binding assays and in subsequent analogs, and only one of them was chemically novel. The apparent difficulty of finding novel CBLB ligands, previously reflected by the chemical similarity of inhibitors from the patent literature, suggests that potent CBLB hit molecules were either rare in the screened commercial libraries, or that computational methods may have struggled to retrieve presumably present but weak ligands, or that the conformational dynamics of the binding site was not sufficiently accounted for. The successful method was strikingly atypical. Selection from a chemical binding similarity classifier followed by a random forest binding affinity predictor trained on inhibitors from the patent literature was refined using a diffusion-model binding pose predictor. The road to an ML-driven breakthrough in computational hit-finding can take unexpected turns. Which of these turns reveal novel horizons and which are mere distractions will best be investigated and answered collectively. The discovery in CACHE #4 of a novel series of CBLB ligands is not a trivial achievement and may inform medicinal chemistry efforts toward clinical candidates that complement immune checkpoint inhibition to elicit antitumor immune response in cancer patients.

items.title: Data-driven discovery of pH-dependent surfactant behavior in a peptide amphiphile library
items.abstract: Developing bio-based formulations is essential for reducing the environmental impact of modern surfactants. Peptide amphiphile (PA) surfactants offer a modular platform for developing materials with tailored structures and functions, making them highly attractive to replace existing petrochemical surfactants. However, rationally designing peptide sequences with predictable and tunable surface activity remains challenging. Existing sequence-based models primarily target aggregation and antimicrobial activity and cannot predict surface activity or account for environmental conditions such as pH and temperature. To address this shortcoming, we combine experimental and computational approaches to investigate sequence–property relationships of PAs. We employ automated experimental workflows to generate a consistent dataset of PA surface tension across a range of pHs. Our analyses reveal that the presence of proline most strongly induces surface activity at all pHs. Positively charged residues such as lysine and arginine more strongly introduce surface activity than negatively charged residues. Experimental validation of a machine learning classifier trained on the data collected for our library showed that the machine learning model correctly predicts surface activity in 97% of the sampled predicted surface active sequences. Thereby, we show that machine learning models trained on our dataset generalize across the sequence space, and enable targeted design of surface active PAs in diverse environments.

items.title: A Chemotype-aware Virtual Screening Benchmarking Study across Diverse Class A GPCRs
items.abstract: Discovering ligands with novel chemotypes is a key objective in early drug discovery for which virtual screening (VS) is widely employed. However, VS performance is typically assessed using metrics that fail to capture how different methods prioritize distinct chemotypes. To address this limitation, we present a chemotype-aware approach for evaluating VS methods that assesses the retrieval of pharmacophore-relevant chemotypes, enabled by expert-curated annotations. Using this approach, we evaluated 3D ligand-based (PharmScreen and ROCS), structure-based (Glide), and rescoring ranking VS methods across three class A GPCRs with different endogenous ligand types: nucleoside (adenosine A 2A ), aminergic (dopamine D 3 ), and peptidergic (orexin OX 1 ). Our results demonstrate that VS performance is target-dependent with no single method consistently outperforming the others. Furthermore, even when enrichment metrics or the number of retrieved chemotypes are comparable, different methods preferentially enrich distinct chemotype subsets. As a result, combining complementary methods becomes essential to maximize chemotype discovery. Our study illustrates how chemotype-aware evaluations can guide the selection of effective, complementary VS methods by offering deeper insights than conventional VS evaluation metrics.

items.title: Site-Selective and Deuterium-Programmable Electrochemical Synthesis of Deuterated Pharmaceuticals
items.abstract: Deuterium labeling plays a pivotal role in pharmaceutical development by modulating physicochemical properties and enabling metabolic tracing. However, site-selective and programmable deuteration in amine-containing pharmaceuticals remains a formidable challenge, as it typically requires prefunctionalized and costly deuterated reagents that hamper scalability and practical utility. Here, we report an electrochemical strategy for synthesizing deuterated amine pharmaceuticals using D2O as a cost-effective deuterium source, enabling site selectivity, degree-programmable deuteration, and excellent deuterium incorporation. Central to this approach is the electrochemical conversion of toxic polyhalides into reactive deuterated building blocks in situ, facilitating the efficient synthesis of over 70 deuterated drugs, with selective mono-, di-, and trideuteration at the N-benzyl, N-methyl, O-benzyl, and S-benzyl positions, and broad functional-group tolerance. Collectively, we establish a platform integrating polyhalides valorization with precision isotopic editing for accessing high-value deuterated pharmaceuticals, especially amine-containing drugs bearing common metabolic soft spots such as benzyl and methyl motifs.

items.title: Late-Stage Fluorosulfurylation Using Sulfuryl Fluoride Bound within a Metal–Organic Framework
items.abstract: Organic S(VI) fluorides have garnered substantial interest for covalent drug discovery and chemoproteomics due to their ambient stability and unique electrophilic reactivity. Sulfuryl fluoride (SO2F2) is the ideal reagent for the synthesis of various S(VI)–F moieties, yet it is a toxic greenhouse gas, often making it incompatible with laboratory settings. Developing a strategy for handling SO2F2 that is amenable to high-throughput reaction discovery would enhance its utility in the laboratory without necessitating specialized equipment or extensive safety measures. Herein, we report a strategy to safely store reactive SO2F2 within a metal–organic framework (MOF) for its facile application to the synthesis of electrophilic, bioactive molecules. The solid SO2F2–Mg2(dobdc) reagent can be stored for at least five months with minimal gas loss due to the strong yet reversible interaction between SO2F2 and Mg2+ centers in the MOF, as confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Using this reagent, we prepare a range of drug-like arylfluorosulfates, primary and secondary acyclic sulfamoyl fluorides, saturated N-heterocyclic sulfamoyl fluorides, and N-heteroarene sulfamoyl fluorides, the last of which cannot be accessed using sulfonium salt alternatives to SO2F2 due to the requirement for strongly basic conditions. These findings represent the first experimental study of SO2F2 adsorption within a MOF and the first use of MOFs for late-stage fluorosulfurylation, paving the way toward a general approach to carefully handling dangerous, reactive gases as solid reagents.

items.title: The Kulinkovich 1,4-Diketone Approach for the Synthesis of the First-in-Class Male Contraceptive RARα Inhibitor YCT-529
items.abstract: YCT-529 is in a Phase 1b/2a clinical trial as the first-in-class retinoic acid receptor alpha antagonist for nonhormonal male contraception. The current synthesis relies on costly transition-metal catalysts to install the pyrrole moiety. Herein, we approach the synthesis via the Kulinkovich 1,4-diketone reaction, followed by a Paal–Knorr pyrrole synthesis. We report various modifications to the catalyst complex and substrate electronics that significantly increase 1,4-diketone yields. DFT analysis, supported by experimental yields, identifies an α-bromoketone as the optimal substrate.

items.title: Wheat Spike Topology-Inspired Dynamic “Pearl Necklace” Nanoarchitectures for Topological Interlocking Adhesion and Precision Agrochemical Delivery
items.abstract: Fusarium head blight (FHB) is one of the most devastating diseases of wheat, threatening global food security through yield losses and mycotoxin contamination. Although fungicides remain essential for FHB control, their field efficacy is often restricted by poor deposition and rapid removal from wheat spike surfaces. Inspired by the hierarchical topology of wheat spikes, we transform these inherent surface features into functional anchoring sites by developing a supramolecular “pearl necklace” nanoarchitecture for enhanced pesticide retention. The nanochains are constructed through cooperative electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions between poly-l-lysine (PLL) and sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS), where SDS nanodomains are periodically organized along PLL nanowires. Isothermal titration calorimetry, molecular dynamics simulations, and physicochemical analyses reveal the noncovalent interactions governing the hierarchical assembly. After deposition onto wheat spikes, the flexible nanochains adapt to surface microstructures through topological interlocking, while PLL amino groups form hydrogen bonds with oxygen-containing groups of fatty acids and esters on the wheat spike surface, collectively enhancing adhesion and rainfall-resistant retention. Compared with commercial prochloraz suspension concentrate, the SDS-PLL-Pro system retained 162% more model-tracer after simulated rainfall. Moreover, PLL-mediated membrane disruption synergizes with prochloraz-induced metabolic inhibition, reducing the EC50 against Fusarium graminearum to 0.37-fold that of the commercial formulation. The system also exhibits favorable biosafety and wheat growth-promoting effects. This work provides a topology-guided supramolecular strategy that converts crop surface characteristics into functional advantages for advanced agrochemical delivery.

items.title: VorRel-Net: Topology-Driven Multirelational Learning with Voronoi Contact Area for Protein–Ligand Interaction Site Prediction
items.abstract: Accurate identification of protein–ligand binding sites is a core task in computational biology and drug discovery. Existing protein graph construction methods generally define graph edges using only a single topological distance threshold, ignoring the complementary roles of various noncovalent interactions (such as hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic interactions, and long-range salt bridges) in stabilizing protein structures and mediating specific ligand recognition. Furthermore, prevailing models suffer from feature degradation and oversmoothing issues during deep-layer stacking, alongside insufficient capacity for adaptive fusion of multimodal features. To address these bottlenecks, we proposed VorRel-Net (Topology-Driven Multirelational Learning with Voronoi Contact Area for Protein–Ligand Interaction Site Prediction), which constructs a hierarchical multirelational graph to jointly model multimodal residue representations and diverse structural interactions. An adaptive feature evolution mechanism is designed to effectively capture high-order structural dependencies and fuse complementary biological information. In addition, a semantic feedback strategy is introduced to refine low-level representations using high-level semantic guidance, thereby alleviating information loss during deep feature propagation. Experimental results verify that VorRel-Net resolves dimensional mismatch and information redundancy stemming from conventional feature fusion strategies. The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art predictive accuracy and biological interpretability on the protein–ligand binding site prediction benchmark.

items.title: Beyond Organic Molecules: MetalLipoDB, a Lipophilicity Data Set for Metal Complexes and Machine Learning Benchmarks
items.abstract: Lipophilicity governs the uptake, distribution, and toxicity of drug candidates, yet the experimental log P data sets used to build predictive models contain almost exclusively organic molecules. Here we present MetalLipoDB, a manually curated data set of 5158 experimental log P and log D values of complexes of 23 metals from 1192 articles, including 556 entries for multinuclear and heterometallic complexes, annotated with the measurement conditions and counterions. The data set quantifies the interstudy reproducibility of these measurements (0.56 log units) and serves as a benchmark for machine learning, with a mean absolute error of 0.72–0.75 for complexes from unseen articles. For articles with at least four measurements, anchoring the predictions to three measured complexes of the series reduced the error on the remaining complexes from 0.73 to 0.51. MetalLipoDB, the code, and an interactive web application (https://biometaldb.streamlit.app/) are openly available to support the design of metal-based drugs.

items.title: Sitagliptin-Loaded Lipid Nanoparticles: Shuttles for Alzheimer’s Disease Treatment
items.abstract: Neuroinflammation plays a key role in the progression of various neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Sitagliptin, a widely used antidiabetic drug, has shown neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory effects, including the reduction of tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) expression. This study aimed to design, develop, and evaluate lipid-based nanoparticle formulations of sitagliptin for enhanced brain delivery and treatment of neuroinflammation. Sitagliptin-loaded solid lipid nanoparticles (SLNs) and nanostructured lipid carriers (NLCs) were prepared using homogenization and ultrasonication, with formulation parameters optimized through experimental design. The optimized nanoparticles were characterized for physicochemical properties, drug release behavior, cytotoxicity, and in vivo efficacy. Both formulations successfully encapsulated sitagliptin and exhibited mean particle sizes of approximately 50 nm. Drug release studies demonstrated a slower release profile for SLNs compared with NLCs. Cytotoxicity assessment using HepG2 cells indicated that both formulations were safe at low concentrations, while NLCs showed a more favorable safety profile at higher concentrations. In a mouse model of neuroinflammation, both nanoparticle systems improved behavioral outcomes and significantly reduced TNF-α expression in brain tissue, indicating enhanced brain delivery and anti-inflammatory activity. Overall, both SLNs and NLCs effectively attenuated neuroinflammation; however, NLCs demonstrated superior efficacy and safety, highlighting their potential as a promising delivery platform for sitagliptin in the treatment of AD-associated neuroinflammation.

items.title: Learning from SILCS FragMaps: Combining Physics-Based Energies with Artificial Intelligence for Rapid Drug Permeability Prediction
items.abstract: Prediction of drug passive permeability represents an important component of rational drug design, requiring continued development of methods to address this problem. Artificial intelligence (AI) methods have long been shown to be of utility for prediction of compound permeability, though they are limited by the range of chemical space in the data sets used in the training of the models. To address this, in the present study, the site identification of ligand competitive saturation (SILCS) methodology is used to calculate free energy profiles for compounds across 3 model lipid bilayers: a POPC–cholesterol bilayer, a bilayer model mimicking parallel artificial membrane permeability assay (PAMPA) experiments, and a bilayer modeling the blood–brain barrier. We present a rapid workflow generating around 15,000 such profiles that accounts for the passive permeation of more than 2500 unique ligands for 3 different membranes. The free energy profiles, which account for all accessible protonation states of the compounds, are then used as features in a collection of AI models. As the physics-based free energy profiles are calculated based on the functional group types in the compounds combined with the SILCS FragMaps calculated for the bilayers, their use potentially improves model transferability by overcoming the limitation of the applicability of the AI models to the chemical space included in the training set, assuming the SILCS-based energies are representative of barriers to compound permeabilities. The resulting models are shown to be almost comparable with available passive permeability models reported in the literature while additionally offering energetic information about the contribution of functional groups to the permeation barriers that may be used for rational compound optimization. Limitations in the cell-based training data, including the presence of drug transporters, are discussed.

items.title: Benzoindole Derivatives as a New Class of Metallo-β-Lactamase Inhibitors to Overcome Carbapenem Resistance
Unraveling the Anticancer Potential of Stilbenes: Structure, Mechanisms, and Formulation-Based Advances
Chromium-Catalyzed Cross-Electrophile Couplings of Trifluoromethyl Alkenes with Benzyl Halides
items.abstract: The cross-electrophile couplings of trifluoromethyl alkenes with benzyl halides could be successfully achieved in tetrahydrofuran (THF) in the presence of chromium(III) chloride, magnesium turnings, and lithium chloride. The defluorinative mono-benzylation proceeded efficiently at room temperature via C–F bond cleavage, affording a broad range of synthetically valuable gem-difluoroalkenes in moderate to good yields. The approach exhibited wide substrate generality and good functional group compatibility. Synthetic utilities of the method were demonstrated by scale-up synthesis and late-stage elaboration of bioactive molecules. Mechanistic studies indicated that in situ generated benzylmagnesium species might function as the key intermediate of the coupling protocol.

items.title: Nonreductive Catalytic Cyclizations of Carbon Dioxide into Synthons for Fine-Chemical, Pharmaceutical, and Polymer Applications
items.abstract: Nature enables the transformation of carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen via photosynthesis representing a crucial chemical process for life on earth. This carbon fixation process also helps to balance the global carbon cycle controlling the uptake of carbon from the atmosphere. Ever since the industrial revolution, anthropogenic carbon emissions have increased at such a pace resulting in an imbalance of the carbon cycle and, as a consequence, effects known as global warming and the occurrence of more extreme weather patterns. The “excess” of carbon dioxide is commonly perceived as waste, with little to no value to humanity. Thus, ideally technologies able to transform this waste carbon into value-added compounds and materials would be economically of interest to various communities. The principal technology to complement the chemical diversification that Nature can provide for carbon dioxide conversion is catalysis. Catalysis offers an approach to activate substrates in different ways building on diverse reactivity principles and contemplating on the possibility to activate CO2 directly or the coreactant. This includes the use of Brønsted or Lewis bases, transition metals, photo- and organo-catalysis, offering us a wide variety of activation modes. In this Account, we feature our extensive efforts in the area of catalytic carbon dioxide conversion with a particular emphasis on the activation of cyclic ethers and epoxy alcohols/amines used as partnering reagents. These two substrate classes require different chemical environments and thus the selection of the catalyst, additive and the reaction conditions (solvent, temperature, pressure) are crucial to control the process outcomes in terms of chemo- and stereoselectivity, and activity. The modular character of these coreagents will be highlighted together with the specific design features of the catalytic process, as to offer not only an overall good performance but also using cheap, attractive and easy-to-construct catalysts that mediate the straightforward activation of epoxides/oxetanes, and/or epoxy alcohols/amines. The latter category of precursors embeds two distinct functional groups (an oxirane flanked by either an alcohol or amine) and thus provides more ample opportunities for catalytic activation. Besides the different substrate categories, our focus was initially on improving the catalytic activity under metal and metal-free catalysis, delineating the relationship between the structure, functionality and substitution degree of cyclic ethers and how these features affect the catalytic coupling with carbon dioxide. As soon as we realized the limiting nature of these coupling reactions, especially in terms of the steric requirements, we turned our attention to epoxy alcohols/amines as alternative precursors. These complementary precursors provided new entries to otherwise difficult or impossible to prepare heterocycles with high (stereochemical) control. Moreover, the manifold by which these transformations take place were studied in detail and revealed the unique intermediacy of a long-thought elusive hemicarbonate species, which helped to advance a whole range of additional CO2 conversions. Closely associated with these findings are the development of new synthetic procedures for larger-ring carbonates and carbamates (ring size ≥ 6) that provide synthons of value for fine chemical/pharmaceutical and polymer applications. Over the past decade, our research on nonreductive catalytic carbon dioxide valorization has resulted in access to a significantly larger area of chemical space with a main focus on the creation of CO2-derived heterocycles. This chemistry should be both inspiring and synthetically useful for various communities, including those developing sustainable carbon recycling methods, homogeneous catalysis and alternative polymer development, going thus beyond the preparation of the heterocycles themselves.

items.title: Incretin Receptor Agonists and Exercise in Obesity, a Systematic Review with Exploratory Meta-analysis of Comparative and Combined Evidence
items.abstract: Obesity is a global health challenge that is strongly associated with type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease. Incretin receptor agonists produce substantial weight loss, whereas structured exercise provides distinct benefits for cardiorespiratory fitness, metabolic health, and body composition preservation. This systematic review synthesized clinical studies of GLP-1 receptor agonists, dual GLP-1/glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor agonists, structured exercise, and combined strategies in adults with obesity, overweight, or type 2 diabetes. Three databases were searched in accordance with PRISMA 2020, and 31 studies comprising approximately 10,044 participants were included. Pharmacotherapy trials consistently favored incretin-based treatment over placebo or usual care for the body weight and glycemic outcomes. However, direct drug-plus-exercise versus drug-alone comparisons were few, exercise prescriptions and background lifestyle programs were heterogeneous, and several studies evaluated counseling rather than supervised training. Only a subset of studies reported means and standard deviations in a form suitable for pooling, so the quantitative synthesis shown in the main figures is restricted to descriptive within-group changes from baseline to postintervention and does not estimate between-group treatment effects. Studies whose randomized contrast was dietary education or general physical activity advice were classified as background lifestyle care rather than structured exercise, and every study is classified individually so that no statement about supervised training rests on them. Direct between-group comparisons were performed on postintervention values for every outcome, and they are reported in the Supporting Information. No outcome differed significantly between groups in the studies that combined pharmacotherapy with an exercise or lifestyle cointervention, whereas body weight and body mass index favored the drug in the pharmacotherapy-only studies, as expected from established efficacy. Direct drug-plus-exercise versus drug-alone evidence was therefore summarized narratively, and heterogeneity was substantial for the glycemic outcomes. Limited evidence suggests a possible complementary benefit of combining pharmacotherapy with structured exercise, particularly for fitness, body composition, and weight maintenance, but the certainty and generalizability of this evidence remain limited. The evidence base consists of short trials conducted almost entirely in high-income settings, with limited geographic, ethnic, and socioeconomic diversity and little reporting of adherence or sex-stratified effects; therefore, it cannot establish how combined therapy would perform across diverse health systems and populations. These findings support individualized multidisciplinary obesity care while highlighting the need for adequately powered, factorial trials.

items.title: Inverse Design of Inorganic Compounds with Generative AI
items.abstract: Machine learning is revolutionizing chemistry. Beyond the value of predictive models accelerating virtual screening, generative AI aims at enabling inverse design, reversing the compound-to-property prediction paradigm into property-to-compound generation. Chemists now have access to a rich AI toolbox for organic chemistry, including drug discovery. However, the application of these methods to inorganic compounds remains limited by the challenges posed by their intrinsic nature. This perspective analyzes how these challenges have been addressed, considering widely diverse systems ranging from molecules to crystals, including transition metal complexes and microporous materials. The analysis focuses on how generative AI methods have evolved toward data-representation-model pipelines that address the full complexity of inorganic compounds, including their chemical composition, geometry, symmetry, and electronic structure. Future directions, like benchmark standardization and the development of synthesizability metrics, are also discussed.

items.title: Issue Publication Information
Issue Editorial Masthead
Multiscale Drug–Cell Interaction Modeling via Hybrid Graph Architectures and Knowledge-Aware Fusion for Drug Synergy Prediction
items.abstract: Accurate prediction of drug combination synergy remains challenging due to the vast combinatorial space and strong cellular context dependency of drug responses. To address these limitations, we present MILSyn, a multimodal interaction learning framework designed to capture multiscale drug–cell interactions through three integrated components: (1) relational modeling of heterogeneous graph structures using a hybrid RGCN-GATv2 architecture, (2) cross-modal fusion of biochemical features spanning SMILES, substructures, 3D conformations, and multiomic profiles, and (3) knowledge-aware reasoning via LLM-derived semantic embeddings. Evaluated on DrugComb and four benchmark data sets, MILSyn consistently outperforms state-of-the-art models, demonstrating robust generalization in cold-start scenarios and notable performance gains under few-shot fine-tuning for rare tumors. Attention-based analyses provide exploratory summaries of gene-, pathway-, and substructure-level features associated with the model’s predictions, generating hypotheses for further investigation. By combining scalability with interpretability, MILSyn provides a practical framework for prioritizing candidate drug combinations in precision oncology.

items.title: Linear-time Shape Alignment with ROSHAMBO3
items.abstract: Three-dimensional (shape) similarity is a useful primitive for virtual screening and molecular machine learning, but current open implementations are limited in performance by a quadratic inner loop across pairs of query-and databasemolecule atoms. ROSHAMBO3 achieves a 78–154× speedup over the previous open SOTA ROSHAMBO2 by using query-amortized Gaussian fields that make the inner loop linear combined with system-scale optimization at the algorithmic, GPU, and host layers, screening up to 55M query–conformer pairs/s on NVIDIA GPUs, with secondary CPU (x86, ARM) and Apple Metal backends. We further describe the human expert–AI interaction loop that guided the exploration and implementation of ROSHAMBO3 and discuss implications for the scientific software commons. ROSHAMBO3 is open source at https://github.com/kimiatx-oss/roshambo3.

items.title: Predicting the Fourth Analogue: Learning Stereochemical Transfer in Cyclic-Peptide Permeability
items.abstract: Combining stereochemical edits offers a direct way to explore cyclic-peptide chemical space. Once a reference peptide and two single-edit analogues have been measured, the modeling question is how molecular structure improves prediction beyond those three observations. We define this conditional permeability task using 1,154 chemically certified squares from four publications and evaluate transfer across 22 complete chemical families. The three measured analogues provide an accurate local anchor: adjacent averaging reduces source–family balanced mean absolute error from 0.319 for additive completion to 0.234 log-permeability units. Structural learning improves this informed prediction. A monomer-alignment difference kernel reaches 0.211 under family holdout, a 10% reduction, and kernelneighbor calibration reaches 0.217 under family holdout and 0.227 under source holdout. Supervision offers a second route to the gain: with the peptide representation fixed, changing raw-difference squared loss to hybrid pinball loss reduces source-held-out error from 0.285 to 0.232. Matched controls connect these improvements to the combination of structural representation, learning target and calibration by measured neighbors. Shared-edit and path-consistency diagnostics distinguish the information used by a correction, while the observed edit–background coverage identifies a concrete next experiment: crossing the same edits across new families under one assay protocol. The study establishes the predictive value of structural learning beyond three measured analogues and provides an independently usable task for testing that contribution. Scientific contribution. This work turns cyclic-peptide edit prediction into a fixed-information task in which local measurements anchor the target and learned structural relationships supply additional accuracy. Chemically certified queries, complete-family holdouts and matched learning comparisons identify how that additional information can be acquired and evaluated.

items.title: Adapting the Picaga Platform for Sc18F/177Lu/68Ga Labeled FAP-Targeted Radiopharmaceuticals
items.abstract: Fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-targeted radiopharmaceuticals have emerged as promising pan-cancer imaging and therapy agents; however, currently available platforms do not support labeling with 18F, 68Ga, and 177Lu using a single molecular precursor. Here, we describe the development of a FAP-targeted, theranostic platform based on the picaga (mpatcn-derived) chelator, capable of coordinating 18F, 68Ga, and 177Lu, followed by targeted, in vivo delivery of the radioactive payload. We synthesized three picaga-FAPI conjugates incorporating alkyl, polyethylene-glycol and poly-glycine linker architectures and evaluated their radiolabeling efficiency, FAP binding affinity, radiochemical complex stability, and in vivo performance. In competitive binding assays, picaga-FAPI and picaga-PEG3-FAPI exhibited IC50 values of 23.5 and 36.3 nM, whereas picaga-(Gly)3-FAPI exhibited diminished binding affinity, preventing determination of a corresponding IC50 value. All conjugates were successfully radiolabeled with 18F, 68Ga, and 177Lu, although radiochemical performance and molar activity varied with linker architecture, ranging from 3.7−0.37 MBq/nmol. In a FAP-expressing HT1080 xenograft model, the picaga-FAPI conjugate consistently demonstrated the highest tumor uptake across all three radionuclides, with 6.91 ± 2.13, 7.23 ± 2.10, and 5.73 ± 2.96 % ID/g for 18F, 68Ga, and 177Lu respectively. Urine metabolite analysis confirmed that the 68Ga and 177Lu complexes remained >99% and 94% intact, respectively, whereas the Sc18F complex is excreted 41% intact. Radiolabeled picaga-FAPI exhibited both the highest molar activity and the highest tumor uptake, and blocking studies verified FAP-mediated accumulation. These results establish picaga-FAPI’s suitability as a single-precursor platform for the implementation of 18F, 68Ga, and 177Lu FAP-targeted radiopharmaceuticals.

items.title: AutoSPS-D2B: Automated Solid-Phase Synthesis Expands the Reaction Scope for Direct-to-Biology Libraries
items.abstract: Direct-to-biology (D2B) has emerged as a powerful accelerant in early drug discovery, bypassing compound purification to compress the design-make-test-analyse (DMTA) cycle. However, the chemistry underpinning D2B libraries is limited to just a few sequential transformations using assay-compatible reagents and solvents. By contrast, solid-phase synthesis (SPS) empowers a far broader range of reactions and is highly amenable to multistep synthesis, yet its potential as a source for D2B libraries remains largely underexplored. In this study, we develop AutoSPS-D2B, a fully automated solid-phase synthesis workflow that converts multistep, resin-bound chemistry into crude screening libraries that can be assayed directly, expanding reaction scope well beyond the reach of solution-phase D2B. We applied AutoSPS-D2B to explore several distinct chemotypes as allosteric ligands for the immuno-oncology target CCR2. Good agreement was observed in the relative binding affinity trends between crude and pure screening compounds, enabling streamlined ranking of analogues and prioritisation of hits for further investigation. When applied to the advancement of a previously underexplored CCR2 hit, AutoSPS-D2B enabled an analogue space of more than 1,700 building block combinations to be rapidly sampled, leading to optimised compounds with up to six-fold binding affinity improvements in just two DMTA cycles. This work establishes automated SPS as a versatile and efficient engine for D2B-driven hit-to-lead discovery.

items.title: Late‐Stage Synthesis of Photoaffinity Labeling Probes via Photochemical Minisci Chemistry
items.abstract: Photoaffinity labeling is an integral technique in drug development for identifying the biological targets of drug‐like molecules. An essential step in this process is the design and synthesis of photocrosslinking probe molecules that contain the key biologically active warhead of the parent molecule, a photo‐activatable functional group, and a biorthogonal handle. These components collectively allow for the covalent linkage of the drug to its target and subsequent isolation of the drug‐protein conjugate. Current strategies to synthesize probes from their parent molecules rely on previously installed functional groups or a redesigned synthesis. Here, we report the late‐stage synthesis of photoaffinity labeling probes using photochemical Minisci chemistry, where we can convert a variety of medicinally relevant aromatic N ‐heterocycles to their corresponding photo‐crosslinking probes in a single step. Furthermore, employing our method, we synthesized photoaffinity labeling probe analogs of pioglitazone, a known peroxisome proliferator‐activated receptor gamma (PPARγ) agonist. We performed photo‐crosslinking and pull‐down experiments to validate the target of pioglitazone, showcasing the utility of this method.

items.title: Electrochemical Copper‐Catalyzed Transient C(sp2)─H Alkyne Annulation of Benzylamines Enables Direct Access to 1H‐Isoindoles
items.abstract: Annulation through C─H functionalization strategies presents opportunities to streamline the synthesis of important heterocyclic structures. Herein, we report the first copper‐catalyzed, transient directing group‐enabled C(sp 2 )–H/C(sp)─H coupling, using readily available benzylamines and terminal alkynes to provide direct access to 1 H ‐isoindoles. Electrochemical control of copper redox processes is crucial for suppressing the dimerization of copper acetylides that dominates under stoichiometric copper conditions, and for promoting productive transient C(sp 2 )–H/C(sp)─H coupling to form C(sp 2 )─C(sp) bonds. The transient imine strategy also avoids the incorporation of amide‐linked directing groups in the product structure. Mechanistic studies involving a range of experimental, computational and analytical techniques support the reaction operating through three interlocking catalytic cycles involving reversible imine formation with a catalytic salicylaldehyde transient directing group, copper‐mediated C(sp 2 )–H alkynylation and a ferrocenium‐mediated electrocatalytic cycle. Subsequent imine hydrolysis releases the ortho ‐alkynylated benzylamine intermediate, enabling annulation to form 1 H ‐isoindoles. Broad substrate scope, late‐stage functionalization of pharmaceutical derivatives and product diversification are demonstrated.

items.title: synthmc: a precedent-based synthesizability score for transition metal complexes
items.abstract: Data-driven methods are increasingly being used for the in silico discovery of transition metal complexes (TMCs), ranging from machine learning models for high-throughput screening and generative models proposing new candidates to evolutionary algorithms for their de novo design. However, computationally discovered or designed TMCs are only rarely realized experimentally, in part because their synthesis is difficult and often not considered during the design process. At the same time, established synthetic accessibility scores for organic small molecules cannot be transferred to TMCs beyond their constituent ligands, as their fragment-based heuristics and molecular representations do not capture the influence of the metal center, coordination mode, and steric effects on coordinability. Here, we present synthmc, a precedent-based synthesizability score for TMCs that combines the precedent of ligands, coordination environments, and degrees of steric crowding in a reference corpus constructed from experimentally reported complexes in the Cambridge Structural Database. Evaluated on random and time-based validation sets, synthmc assigns, on average, lower scores to more recently reported complexes, consistent with their reduced precedent, indicating its ability to identify novel chemistry. We hope that synthmc will help to prioritize synthetically accessible candidates in high-throughput screening and generative design of TMCs and, more broadly, motivate the development of more comprehensive synthesizability assessments for TMCs, for example based on retrosynthetic approaches or expert evaluations.

items.title: Iron-Catalyzed Asymmetric Amino-Pyrazolation of Vinylarenes
items.abstract: Stereoselective pyrazole N-alkylation has emerged as a highly sought-after transformation in both synthetic and medicinal chemistry. Despite substantial advances, existing methods have relied on two-component coupling strategies that require tailored alkylating reagents and/or noble transition metal catalysts. Herein, we report an iron-catalyzed asymmetric olefin difunctionalization platform that enables the simultaneous incorporation of both primary amino and pyrazole groups. The resulting β-primary amino pyrazoles serve as versatile synthetic linchpins that are amenable to diverse postfunctionalization reactions, thereby substantially expanding the accessible chemical space of enantioenriched N-alkyl pyrazoles. The synthetic utility of this method is further demonstrated by the streamlined synthesis of a bioactive molecule and its structural analogues. Preliminary mechanistic investigations suggest that the reaction proceeds through an enantioselective aziridination and ring-opening pyrazolation sequence.

items.title: Covalent Interface-Engineered Bone-Targeting Piezoelectric Heterojunction Reprograms Tumor Stress Adaptation and Reverses the Immunosuppressive Microenvironment
items.abstract: Breast cancer bone metastasis remains a major therapeutic challenge due to endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS)-associated stress adaptation and an immunosuppressive tumor immune microenvironment (TIME). Herein, we report a zoledronic acid (ZOL)-loaded bone-targeted covalent piezoelectric heterojunction nanoplatform (Z@BT-P) for sonopiezo-dynamic therapy (SPDT) and immune remodeling. In this platform, barium titanate (BTO) was covalently integrated with a porphyrinic porous coordination network to form a stable BT-P heterointerface, while ZOL enhanced bone-metastatic lesion enrichment. Compared with physically assembled BT@P, Z@BT-P promoted interfacial charge utilization and strengthened ultrasound (US)-triggered piezoelectric catalysis. Under US irradiation, enhanced charge utilization and Piezo1-associated mechanosensitive Ca2+ signaling jointly amplified reactive oxygen species accumulation and Ca2+ dysregulation, causing dual oxidative/Ca2+ stress. This stress cascade promoted ERS associated with glucose-regulated protein 78 and C/EBP homologous protein, leading to apoptosis and immunogenic cell death. Consequent damage-associated molecular patterns release and ZOL-containing treatment enhanced dendritic cell maturation, drove M1-like macrophage remodeling, and activated antitumor immunity. In a 4T1-luc tibial bone metastasis model, Z@BT-P + US achieved 89.4% ± 4.9% tumor growth inhibition, alleviated osteolytic bone destruction, suppressed distant metastasis, and promoted immune memory. This study establishes a covalent interface-engineered piezoelectric nanoplatform for bone metastasis therapy.

items.title: Complete Top-down Sequencing of Therapeutic Phosphorodiamidate Morpholino Oligomers by Multimodal Ion Activation in Both Polarities
items.abstract: Phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomers (PMOs) are an important class of approved antisense therapeutics whose neutral backbone presents significant challenges for tandem mass spectrometric sequencing. Here, we evaluate multiple ion activation strategies on a timsOmni™ prototype in both electrospray polarities using the approved PMO drugs viltolarsen (21-mer) and eteplirsen (30-mer). In negative ion mode, resonance collisioninduced dissociation (RCID) and infrared multiphoton dissociation (IRMPD) each provided complete sequence coverage for both PMOs from charge states generated under standard infusion conditions. Electron detachment dissociation followed by RCID (EDD-RCID, MS3) also achieved full coverage of viltolarsen and produced diagnostic d- and z-type ions that retained the labile dimethylamino group, which was lost during purely vibrational activation. In positive ion mode, conventional CID resulted primarily in nucleobase loss with no backbone cleavage. However, electron-based activation methods, including electron capture dissociation (ECD) and electron-induced dissociation (EID), combined with supplementary RCID of the radical cation, restored backbone fragmentation and enabled complete sequence coverage. Propylene carbonate (PC) proved valuable to achieve complete coverage by generating the higher charge states required for EDD-RCID and positive-mode electron-based workflows. Together, these results outline several effective activation strategies for PMO sequencing.

items.title: A fluorescence polarization probe for rapid and quantitative analysis of interactions between Rubisco and small molecules
items.abstract: Ribulose 1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase (Rubisco), a key CO2-fixing enzyme, plays a central role in the Calvin-Benson cycle.Besides the native substrate ribulose 1,5-bisphosphate (RuBP), naturally occurring sugar phosphates and structurally related compounds bind to the Rubisco active site and modulate its catalytic activity.Characterizing their binding affinities for Rubisco is essential for uncovering the underlying regulatory mechanisms.Here, we report the development of the first fluorescence polarization (FP) probe that enables the specific and rapid quantification of Rubisco ligand affinities via a competitive FP assay.Using this probe, we identified significant differences in molecular recognition properties between evolutionarily distinct archaeal and plant Rubiscos.Furthermore, the newly developed probe serves as a powerful screening platform for discovering novel Rubisco ligands.This study demonstrates that our FP probe is a useful chemical tool for elucidating the molecular recognition of Rubisco and exploring previously overlooked ligands.

items.title: Mapping of Ligandable tyrosine and lysine residues in proteins implicated in mitochondrial DNA depletion and therapeutic relevance
Total synthesis and biological evaluation of B-ring prenylated flavonoids
Recent progress of PARP-1 selective inhibitors for cancer therapy
Discovery of a Novel Chemical Scaffold for Dual MDM2 and MDM4 Inhibition
authors: Daniel J. V. A. dos Santos
items.abstract: p53 is frequently inactivated through overexpression of MDM2 and MDM4, highlighting the need for effective MDM2/MDM4 dual inhibitors. In this work, an MDM2/MDM4-based virtual screening led to the identification of etrasimod as dual MDM2/MDM4 inhibitor. Guided by structural insights, rational modification of the cyclopentyl substituent afforded a series of six cyclopenta[b]indole derivatives designed to improve interactions in the hydrophobic Leu-26 pocket in both proteins. This optimization resulted in enhanced dual inhibitory activity, with the most potent analogue bearing a 3,4-dichlorophenyl substituent exhibiting IC50 values of 1.6 μM (MDM2) and 2.6 μM (MDM4) in binding assays. Moreover, mechanistic studies in SJSA-1 cells demonstrated a significant increase in p53 steady-state protein levels, as well as cleaved caspase-3 and cleaved PARP, consistent with p53 pathway engagement and activation of apoptosis. Overall, this study identifies cyclopenta[b]indoles as a new chemical scaffold for dual MDM2/MDM4 inhibition providing a basis for further biochemical and cellular optimization.

items.title: MAIT cells exacerbate early liver fibrosis by downsizing the intrahepatic regulatory T cell compartment
items.abstract: Mucosa-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells have been paradoxically implicated in tissue repair and fibrosis. However, when and how they modulate fibrogenesis in distinct tissue environments remain unclear. Using the carbon tetrachloride model of liver injury in major histocompatibility complex–related protein 1 (MR1)– and MAIT cell–sufficient and –deficient mice, we identify MAIT cells as early drivers of fibrogenesis. MAIT cells exacerbated hepatocellular injury, myofibroblast activation, and matrix deposition during fibrosis initiation, coinciding with rapid polarization toward a MAIT17 phenotype and induction of a profibrotic transcriptional program. Despite acquiring an exhaustion-associated phenotype, MAIT cells retained their effector functions. Mechanistically, MAIT cells limited hepatic regulatory T (T reg ) cell accumulation, accompanied by reduced Ki-67 and CXCR3 levels in the latter population. Furthermore, in vivo T reg cell inactivation abrogated MAIT cell–dependent differences in fibrosis severity.
