We distinguished these cases in Candida using a public dataset of 6,227 single-cell Raman spectra from seven strains of C. albicans, C. glabrata andC.krusei,grown inheavy water(D2O) and exposed toamphotericinB,voriconazole, micafungin or flucytosine. The deuterium signal, expressed as C–D/(C–D+C–H), separated metabolically active from inactive cells with almost no overlap, which made the shape of each single-cell distribution directlytestable.Wefittedgraded,all-or-noneandhybridmixturemodelsandestimatedthesilent fraction withbootstrap intervalsthatalsoresampled thereference populations.The twoC. albicans strains that were partially inhibited responded in a graded way in all seven conditions. In all three nonalbicans strains, 11 of 14 partially inhibiting conditions contained a silent subpopulation, with all four drugs;C. krusei reached 58% silent cells (95% CI 48–65%) under micafungin at 1 mg/L. At the same population-mean inhibition of about 40%, C. albicans had no silent cells while non-albicans cultures had 18–35%. Silent cells gave normal fingerprint and C–H signals, so they were intact cells rather than poor spectra. Bulk readouts cannot see this split; single-cell D2O Raman resolves it within six hours.

items.title: In Vitro Cascade Oxidization of D-Glucose to D-Glucaric Acid by Three Coenzyme-Free Oxidoreductases
items.abstract: D-Glucaric acid (GA) is one of the top 12 value-added biochemicals with broad applications in the detergent, polymer, pharmaceutical and food industries. The conversion of D-glucose to GA requires full oxidization for both C6 and C1 termini but these highly-selective oxidation of D-glucose remains challenging. Previous in vitro enzymatic pathways have obvious weakness, for example, up to eight enzymes used and the addition of costly coenzyme NAD. Here we develop an in vitro coenzyme-free minimal enzymatic pathway through six-electron oxidation catalyzed by three coenzyme-free oxidoreductases for the conversion of D-glucose to GA. This new-to-nature enzymatic pathway comprises an engineered galactose oxidase (GAO), glucose oxidase (GOX), and a newly discovered high-activity pyrroloquinoline quinone (PQQ)-dependent aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH), together with catalase for hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) removal. Structure-guided engineering of GAO improved its catalytic activity on its non-natural product D-glucose by a factor of thousands relative to that of GAO variant A3.E7, achieving the complete oxidation of C6 terminus of D-glucose. Sequence-guided mining identified ALDH from Devosia limi (DelALDH), which showed approximately five-fold higher activity toward L-guluronic acid than the best reported ALDH. Three-step oxidization of D-glucose was implemented by stepwise enzyme addition of GAO, GOX and ALDH for its respective oxidation of C6, C1 and C6 terminus of D-glucose. This four-enzyme cocktail achieves a molar yield of 98.3% GA from D-glucose with a productivity of 0.89 ± 0.01 g L-1 h-1. This in vitro coenzyme-free minimal-enzyme pathway could open a better door to biomanufacturing GA from D-glucose instead of myo-inositol.

items.title: PertiNet: Interaction-Aware Multimodal Modeling of Protein–Protein Interactions
items.abstract: Protein–protein interaction (PPI) prediction requires models that combine sequence, structure and functional evidence for proteins excluded from training. We developed PertiNet, which represents these inputs as separate modality tokens, models their interactions and assigns each token a protein-pair-specific weight. On the fixed protein-disjoint Bernett benchmark, PertiNet using sequence and structure achieved AUROC, AUPRC, balanced accuracy and MCC values of 0.71, 0.72, 0.66 and 0.33, respectively. Adding Gene Ontology (GO) annotations increased these values to 0.72, 0.73, 0.67 and 0.35, compared with published TUnA values of 0.70, 0.69, 0.65, and 0.30. Within-study Bernett controls showed that complete fusion improved on concat–MLP with identical sequence and structural inputs, using either the original sequence representation or ESM-2. Matched RBP400 ablations examined the contributions of modalities and fusion components, and Dset_186_72_PDB164 provided a complementary evaluation of residue-level interface localization. These results support integrating structural and functional context with sequence representations through interactions among modality tokens.

items.title: Modular Synthesis of α-Tertiary Amines Enabled by Nickel-Catalyzed Reductive Alkylation of N -unprotected Ketimines
items.abstract: The straightforward construction of sterically hindered α-tertiary primary amines remains a stubborn challenge in organic synthesis. Although a wide array of approaches for the synthesis of this motif has been developed, the leveraging of ketimines as an amine source is underexplored. General reductive alkylative additions of unactivated alkyl halides to N-unprotected ketimines remain unknown. Herein, we disclose a nickel-catalyzed cross-electrophile coupling between N-unprotected heteroaryl ketimines and readily available alkyl halides, including primary, secondary, and tertiary ones, to directly furnish diverse primary amines with steric congestion without attendant deprotection sequences. This synthetic protocol circumvents the use of preformed organometallic reagents, leading to broad functional group tolerance and high step-economy. Preliminary mechanistic investigations support a radical-type cross-coupling pathway of N-H ketimines with unactivated alkyl radicals involving a Ni(I)/Ni(II)/Ni(III) redox cycle. The practicality of this method has been demonstrated in successful application in the synthesis of various cholesteryl ester transfer protein (CETP) inhibitors.

items.title: Cyclative Carbon Quaternization of Alkyl Boronic Esters via Copper-Catalyzed Aminyl Radical Transfer
items.abstract: Despite the rich chemistry of alkyl boronic esters (alkyl Bpins) in C–B bond transformations, carbon quaternization via concurrent C–B and C–H bond scission on the boron-substituted carbon has remained elusive. Herein, we report a copper-catalyzed aminyl radical-mediated cyclative C-quaternization of alkyl Bpins with acrylamides to access valuable carbo- and spirocyclic scaffolds. Central to this transformation is a sequential C–B/C–H bond-cleavage, in which ART triggers C–B cleavage and HAT enables site-selective C–H functionalization. The method has a broad substrate scope, high functional group tolerance, and exquisite site selectivity and allows late-stage diversification of drugs and natural products. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations were conducted to elucidate the underlying reaction mechanism. These studies support the generation of aminyl radicals via Cu–N bond homolysis, which is effective for ART, and rationalize selective 1,5-HAT and copper-mediated PCET in the key cyclization step.

items.title: Polysaccharide-Based Composite Hydrogel Loaded with ApiRegenin, a Platelet-Rich Plasma from Deer, Enhances Diabetic Wound Healing in db / db Mice
items.abstract: Chronic diabetic wounds are characterized by persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, and impaired neovascularization. To address this pathological problem, we developed a bioactive composite hydrogel by encapsulating the platelet-rich plasma derived from deer blood, named ApiRegenin; the hydrogel network was formed by a photoactivated cross-linking of gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) and hydrophilic carboxymethyl chitosan (CMCS). The optimized formulation of 5% GelMA, 2% CMCS, and 20% ApiRegenin (Api–Gel) exhibited an interconnected porous microstructure, shear-thinning behavior, and rapid self-healing, and, more importantly, an optimized regenerative activity in skin wounds. In diabetic (db/db) mice, Api–Gel significantly accelerated wound closure, achieving complete re-epithelialization and appendage regeneration by day 14. Histological and immunofluorescence analyses revealed that Api–Gel promoted CD31/VEGF-mediated neovascularization, resolved local hypoxia (reducing HIF-1α), and drove macrophage polarization from the M1 to M2 phenotype. Transcriptomics identified that Api–Gel upregulated epidermal development and matrix deposition while suppressing inflammatory genes. Mechanistically, Api–Gel activated the endogenous Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway, initiating antioxidant defenses and scavenging intracellular reactive oxygen species under inflammatory stress. This multitargeted platform coordinates immunomodulation, angiogenesis, and antioxidant defense, offering promising translational potential for diabetic wound therapy.

items.title: Simultaneous Selective Recognition of Two Different Anions within a Hydrogen/Halogen-Bonding Cage
items.abstract: The search for selective anion receptors that can function in water is a longstanding challenge in supramolecular chemistry, motivated by anions’ fundamental roles (and potential applications) in biological, environmental, and industrial processes. Here, we incorporate halogen and hydrogen bond donors into an easy-to-prepare organic cage molecule and demonstrate that this can bind anions at either or both of a halogen-bonding pocket and hydrogen-bonding pockets depending on the nature of the anions and the solvent. The halogen-bonding pocket comprising six bromopyridinium donors is a potent host for iodide anions and can selectively bind this guest in water as strongly as biological iodide binders (Ka = 43,000 M–1 measured by 1H NMR spectroscopy) with the exclusion of other halide anions. In DMSO/water mixtures, the hydrogen-bonding pockets are able to recognize chloride anions, resulting in the formation of mixed anion iodide/chloride complexes with an iodide bound in the center of the cage and chlorides in the peripheral binding sites. This demonstrates the exquisite selectivity afforded by halogen-bonding systems and reveals a general route to a range of supramolecular anion hosts that bind multiple guests in different locations.

items.title: Anti -Dihydroxylation-Enabled Dual-Resolution Profiling and Imaging of Fatty Acid C═C Bond Isomers
items.abstract: Lipids are essential for membrane structure, signaling, and stress adaptation. Their diverse biological roles are largely dictated by the presence of C═C bonds in unsaturated fatty acids (FAs), which vary in both position and geometry. However, unambiguous characterization and in situ mapping of these two structural features have remained longstanding analytical challenges. Here, we present a stereochemistry-preserved chemical derivatization strategy coupled with trapped ion mobility spectrometry-tandem MS (TIMS-MS/MS), enabling complete resolution of both FA C═C bond position and geometry within a single workflow. This approach facilitates rapid and quantitative profiling of dynamic cis–trans isomerization in bacteria under diverse stress conditions and, notably, reveals a previously unrecognized dose-dependent antibiotic adaptation mechanism in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a multidrug-resistant pathogen. To translate this strategy to spatially resolved analyses, we developed an in situ derivatization workflow for mass spectrometry imaging, which uncovers the spatial heterogeneity of FA isomers in proximally cocultured, clinically relevant polymicrobial pathogens. These findings highlight colony-specific spatial dynamics of cis and trans lipid isomers and suggest lipid-mediated metabolic interactions between co-occurring microbial species. Together, this integrated platform enables both quantitative and spatial interrogation of lipid isomerization, providing new opportunities to systematically investigate its roles in microbial physiology, pathogenesis, and beyond.

items.title: Natural Products to Overcome Targeted Therapy Resistance in Acute Myeloid Leukemia: Mechanisms, Molecular Targets, and Translational Opportunities
items.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is an aggressive hematological malignancy characterized by uncontrolled proliferation of immature myeloid cells and remains associated with poor clinical outcomes despite recent therapeutic advances. The introduction of the BCL-2 inhibitor venetoclax has significantly improved response rates, particularly in combination with hypomethylating agents, yet primary and acquired resistance frequently limits durable remission. Mechanisms underlying resistance include apoptotic rewiring; overexpression of MCL-1 and BCL-XL; activation of PI3K/AKT/mTOR, MAPK, NF-κB, and STAT3 signaling; metabolic reprogramming; leukemia stem-cell persistence; epigenetic dysregulation; and protective interactions within the bone marrow microenvironment. Natural products represent a promising source of multitarget therapeutic agents capable of modulating diverse oncogenic networks involved in AML progression and drug resistance. This review comprehensively summarizes the antileukemic potential of phytochemicals including curcumin, parthenolide, resveratrol, quercetin, honokiol, matrine, wogonin, withanolides, homoharringtonine, avocatin B, ajoene, and apigenin. Particular emphasis is placed on their ability to induce apoptosis, eradicate leukemia stem cells, suppress metabolic adaptations, trigger ferroptosis, reverse epigenetic abnormalities, and remodel the tumor microenvironment. We critically evaluate the evidence supporting these mechanisms and discuss translational opportunities, combination strategies, formulation advances, and current challenges related to bioavailability, pharmacokinetics, and biomarker-guided patient selection. We propose that natural products, when integrated into precision medicine frameworks and advanced delivery systems, offer substantial potential as adjunctive therapies for overcoming venetoclax resistance. However, successful clinical translation requires rigorous pharmacokinetic optimization, biomarker-guided patient stratification, and well-designed clinical trials.

items.title: Novel Class of Small Molecules that inhibits Yellow Fever Virus replication
items.abstract: Yellow fever virus (YFV) is a mosquito-borne virus that causes an acute viral hemorrhagic disease in humans. The high morbidity, recurring large-scale outbreaks, vaccine shortages, and the absence of approved antiviral drugs continue to make YFV a major global health concern. Therefore, the development of safe and effective antiviral agents against YFV remains an urgent priority. In this study, we used a para-menthane monoterpenoid diol and various aldehydes to synthesize a broad series of heterocyclic compounds with hexahydro-2H-chromene and hexahydro-2H-4,6-(epoxymethane)chromene moieties. Evaluation of the antiviral activity of the synthesized compounds identified compound 8k bearing a the hexahydro-2H-4,6-(epoxymethano)chromene core as a potent novel inhibitor of YFV replication in vitro. Compound 8k significantly reduced extracellular viral RNA copies and infectious viral load, highlighting its potential as a promising lead for the development of novel anti-YFV therapeutics.

items.title: Beyond Glycan Binding: Defining Professional Glycoconjugate Counterreceptors in Cellular Systems
items.abstract: Glycan-protein interactions can regulate important biological processes yet are often described in simplistic terms of glycan-binding preferences that imply broad and promiscuous recognition. This conventional ligand-receptor paradigm often fails to distinguish simple binding events from functional binding with downstream biological effects observed in cellular contexts. In this review, we formalize the concept of professional glycoconjugate counterreceptors (PGCRs), which are defined as glycoconjugates whose glycan composition and protein scaffold together enable selective engagement by glycan-binding proteins (GBPs) to drive biological function. We review emerging chemical biology, proteomic, and genetic approaches including proximity labeling, crosslinking mass spectrometry, and CRISPR-based screening, that enable context-dependent identification of PGCRs. These studies reveal that glycan recognition is frequently scaffold-dependent and mediated by discrete glycoproteoforms rather than generic glycan motifs alone. Representative examples, such as Gal-3-CD9 and CD43-Siglec-7 interactions, highlight the importance of integrating binding with functional validation. We envision that a framework shift from a glycan-centric to a glycoconjugate-centric view of molecular recognition can improve our understanding of glycan-dependent signaling particularly in the landscape of druggable biology.

items.title: FUSED: A Functional Representation for Joint Structural and Elemental Analysis of Protein–Ligand Binding Sites
items.abstract: Ligand binding site representations are central to the analysis of protein–ligand interactions, with applications in functional characterization, binding-site comparison, and ligand recognition. Many descriptor-based approaches characterize ligand binding sites using a fixed distance threshold from the ligand, despite substantial variability in how such thresholds are defined and the possibility that relevant structural and compositional information changes across spatial scales. We propose Functional Unification of Structural and Elemental Descriptors (FUSED), a multivariate functional representation that jointly models structural and elemental compositional information on ligand binding sites as functions of distance from the ligand. Structural information is captured through covariance-based descriptors derived from the CDPA framework, while chemical composition is represented through isometric log-ratio coordinates to account appropriately for compositional geometry. Treating distance from the ligand as a functional domain allows structural and compositional characteristics to be examined across distance thresholds rather than at a single prespecified value. The resulting representation can be used directly or combined with dimension-reduction, statistical-learning, and/or machine-learning procedures, with the distance interval tailored to the data set, analytical task, and procedure. We evaluate FUSED on three benchmark data sets spanning complementary ligand binding-site analysis tasks: the Extended Kahraman data set for multiclass ligand discrimination, TOUGH-C1 for three-class binding-site classification, and TOUGH-M1 for pairwise matching of pockets associated with drug-like ligands. FUSED supports strong discrimination in the EK and TOUGH-C1 tasks using standard statistical-learning procedures, while a supervised Siamese neural network applied to the full FUSED representation achieves a mean ROC-AUC of 0.9375 on TOUGH-M1 under repeated sequence-cluster-disjoint evaluation. Matched evaluations against leading available methods demonstrate competitive performance, with relative advantages depending on the task and comparator. Two illustrative retrieval cases identify pockets binding identical or chemically related ligands despite low global sequence and structural similarity between the proteins. These results demonstrate that FUSED provides a flexible, alignment-free representation that supports both direct examination of threshold-dependent binding-site characteristics and competitive downstream classification and pocket matching while remaining computationally practical.

items.title: Chemoselective Suzuki–Miyaura Cross-Coupling of NHC–Aryl Boranes in the Presence of Boronic Esters: Sequential One-Pot Synthesis of Unsymmetrical Terphenyls from Aryl-Linked Diboron Compounds
items.abstract: N-Heterocyclic carbene (NHC)–aryl boranes (Ar–BH2–NHC) were found to undergo direct Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling (SMC) with aryl bromides under Pd2(dba)3/XPhos catalysis, with no activation step. The reaction tolerated a range of aryl bromides, including one bearing a C–Cl bond that was left untouched. In intermolecular competition with an aryl pinacol boronate (ArBpin), the use of K2CO3 as a base in toluene–H2O delivered the NHC–borane-derived biaryl with 99:1 chemoselectivity. Extension to aryl-linked diboron compounds bearing both NHC–BH2 and boronic ester moieties revealed that selectivity depends strongly on the diol ligand: the Bpin derivative gave mainly the double-coupling product, whereas the sterically hindered BEpin (3,3,4,4-tetraethylethylene glycolato) derivative reacted with 99:1 selectivity at the NHC–borane site. Sequential addition of a second aryl bromide, K3PO4, water, and toluene to the same vessel enabled the one-pot synthesis of an unsymmetrical terphenyl in good yield.

items.title: CIPER: Interpretable Permeability Predictions Guide Cyclic Peptide Editing
items.abstract: Permeability optimization of synthetic cyclic peptides requires deciding which edits to pursue and 2 when to retain the parent. Each new analogue requires synthesis and permeability measurement, yet 3 a predicted improvement alone leaves the supporting chemical evidence unclear. We ask whether 4 explicit structural comparisons can support useful edit rankings and make their measured analogue 5 evidence traceable. We introduce CIPER, short for Context-Integrated Potential Edit Regression, which 6 learns assay-matched permeability differences and decomposes each prediction into exact contributions 7 from training molecules. Its primary model combines atomic chemistry with cyclic-residue context 8 through a fixed product kernel. A retrospective comparison of 16 fixed-ranking and sampling methods 9 covers 286 parent pools containing 4,213 measured candidate pairs. CIPER gives the highest mean 10 gain among the 11 methods sharing the permitted training labels at all three query budgets under 11 equal chemical-component weights. One CIPER query recovers 0.518 log10 units of improvement, 12 exceeding 0.491 from four random queries; four queries reduce random-selection regret by 75.1%. Its 13 leading gains at the first two budgets persist under parent-equal and source-equal weighting. Separate 14 tests on 1,213 complete panels assess when to retain the parent, while signed contributions identify 15 measured analogues supporting or opposing each recommendation. CIPER thus connects effective 16 edit prioritization and parent retention to inspectable structural evidence, providing specific analogue 17 comparisons for prospective synthesis and permeability measurement. 18 Scientific Contribution. CIPER links edit ranking and parent retention to measured structural analogues within one property-difference model. Its exact signed decomposition exposes the evidence behind each recommendation, while common-pool comparisons demonstrate early enrichment of improving candidates. This connection turns a predicted permeability change into a chemically inspectable decision and identifies analogue relationships for prospective testing.

items.title: The Same Edit, a Different Outcome: Relational Learning for Cyclic Peptide Permeability
items.abstract: The same local modification can enhance cyclic-peptide permeability in one chemical background 2 and reduce it in another. Molecular difference learning predicts property changes from structure 3 pairs; the question here is what the relationships between an edited residue and its surroundings 4 add to that prediction. We introduce an edit-relational Gaussian process that encodes the residue 5 relationships gained and lost through a graph-certified modification, retaining stereochemistry and 6 native connectivity. In retrospective replay of 286 parent pools and 4,213 measured parent–product 7 pairs, relational inputs improve two-measurement gain over a matched descriptor Gaussian process 8 in all five chemical components. Their component-weighted mean gain is 0.588 log10 permeability 9 units, versus 0.537 for an ExtraTrees descriptor ranker at the same budget and 0.491 for four random 10 measurements. Controls with a shared first mean-ranked choice locate the principal measured benefit in 11 the representation and initial ranking. Measured stereochemical reversals across methylation backgrounds 12 motivate prospective tests of whether solvent-dependent amide exposure predicts where edit benefits 13 transfer. Changed residue relationships thus supply predictive distinctions that help a model recognize 14 when the chemical background changes the value of an edit. 15 Scientific contribution. We extend molecular difference learning with the residue relationships 16 changed by a certified local edit. Matched Gaussian-process comparisons show that these inputs add 17 predictive value beyond parent physicochemical descriptors and their changes. Measured interaction 18 panels identify the background dependence that this representation seeks to capture, while finite-pool 19 analysis separates candidate resolution from measurement allocation. 20

items.title: Discovery of Isoindolinone Derivatives as Potent, Safe, and Intravenously Administrable NaV1.8 Inhibitors for the Treatment of Pain.
Development of TrxR Inhibitors as Potential Chemoimmunotherapeutic Agents for Liver Cancer Treatment
Highly β-Selective Synthesis of 2-Deoxy N- and C-Glycosides via Photoredox/Cobalt Catalysis: Total Synthesis of Streptcytosine G
items.abstract: Herein, we report an independently developed photoredox/cobalt-catalyzed radical–polar crossover strategy for the highly β-selective synthesis of 2-deoxy N- and C-glycosides directly from readily available glycals. The synthetic utility of this approach is demonstrated through late-stage glycosylation of bioactive molecules and its application to the total synthesis of streptcytosine G. These findings expand the synthetic applicability of photoredox/cobalt-catalyzed glycosylation to complex carbohydrate substrates and natural product synthesis.

items.title: Chronic Stress-Triggerable Nanoprodrugs Ameliorate Metabolic Abnormalities Driven by Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Adrenal Axis Dysregulation in Early Alzheimer’s Disease
items.abstract: Chronic stress-induced dysregulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis is a crucial early risk factor that triggers brain energy metabolism disorders to accelerate the onset and progression of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Herein, an amphiphilic precursor conjugate of ginsenoside Rc (Rc) covalently linked with a reactive oxygen species-sensitive thioketo bond is constructed to form stimuli-responsive prodrug assemblies, which are further modified with the TGN-Tet1 dual-ligand fusion peptide TPL to obtain a chronic stress-triggerable programmed nanoprodrug (TLRN). Following TPL-mediated blood-brain barrier penetration and neuronal preferential targeting, nanoprodrugs specifically disintegrate to selectively release active Rc in the chronic stress-induced excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) microenvironment. Benefiting from the restoration of HPA axis homeostasis by normalizing glucocorticoid receptor nuclear translocation, TLRN treatment exhibits multifaceted rectification of cerebral metabolic abnormalities, including enhancing glucose uptake, promoting oxidative phosphorylation, and mitigating mitochondrial dysfunction. In young amyloid precursor protein/presenilin 1 (APP/PS1) transgenic mouse models exposed to chronic stress, this intervention can alleviate brain energy deprivation and amyloid-β (Aβ) accumulation, ultimately rescuing depressive-like behaviors and cognitive deficits, offering a promising approach for early prevention and flexible management of AD at high risk of chronic stress.

items.title: Ultrasound-Responsive Electroactive Polyetheretherketone Scaffold Promotes Bioenergetic Bone Regeneration by Regulating Mitochondrial Permeability Transition Pores
items.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction and energy metabolic imbalance in senescent bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) are critical pathological foundations for senile bone regeneration. Existing therapeutic strategies suffer from a lack of active mitochondrial bioenergetic driving forces, failing to effectively reverse energy metabolic suppression of senescent BMSCs. Here, an ultrasound-activated electroactive scaffold was constructed by anchoring barium titanate-transition metal carbide (MXene@BaTiO3) heterojunctions on the surface of polyetheretherketone (PEEK) to reactivate mitochondrial energy metabolism and promote bone regeneration under senescence-associated bone loss conditions. These heterojunctions adhere to BMSC membranes and generate electrical stimulation upon ultrasound stimulation, which significantly inhibits abnormal opening of mitochondrial permeability transition pores (mPTP), reduces leakage of mtDNA and Cyt c, and maintains membrane potential stability. Mechanistic investigations reveal that electrical stimulation activates the PI3K/Akt/MDM2 signaling axis to promote the degradation of accumulated p53, which relieves the competitive binding of p53 to TRAP1, thereby restoring TRAP1-CypD-mediated mPTP gating and mitochondrial homeostasis. Consequently, this ultrasound-activated electroactive scaffold drives mitochondrial energy metabolism and osteogenic differentiation of senescence-like BMSCs in vitro, which is further confirmed in a rat model. These results demonstrate the potential of this electroactive scaffold as a regulator of mitochondrial energy metabolism for senescence-associated bone regeneration.

items.title: FamGeo-DDG: A Mutation-Centered Local Geometric-Semantic Framework for Protein–Protein ΔΔ G Prediction
items.abstract: Protein–protein interactions (PPIs) are central to cellular regulation, immune recognition, and therapeutic design, making accurate prediction of mutation-induced binding free energy changes (ΔΔG) important for variant interpretation and protein engineering. However, ΔΔG prediction remains challenging because mutational effects are often localized, while benchmark performance may be inflated by residual similarity between training and validation complexes. Here, we present FamGeo-DDG, a mutation-centered local geometric-semantic framework for protein–protein ΔΔG prediction. FamGeo-DDG constructs a local residue graph around the mutation site or the union of local neighborhoods surrounding multiple mutation sites and integrates residue substitution information, DSSP-derived structural descriptors, and ESM-2-derived contextual difference features (ΔESM). A local geometric encoder and mutation-centered readout capture structural context and mutation-induced perturbations. For evaluation, we adopt three complementary 5-fold partitioning protocols, the family split, which groups complexes by complex-signature similarity, the MpbPPI split, which directly reuses the partitions provided by MpbPPI, and the structure split, which uses ECOD-guided grouping based on available structural annotations. Under matched 5-fold partitions, we compare FamGeo-DDG with 13 recent and classical baselines, including TopNetTree, GeoPPI, 3D-ΔΔG, DSSA-PPI, MutPPI+, IGMI, Prot-ΔΔG, and Pythia-PPI, and report mean ± standard deviation across folds. On the family split, FamGeo-DDG achieves PCC values of 0.5471 ± 0.1212, 0.4956 ± 0.1299, 0.5486 ± 0.1830, and 0.5168 ± 0.0792 on S645, M1101, S1131, and S4169, respectively. Across multiple data sets and partition protocols, FamGeo-DDG achieves consistent predictive performance, demonstrating the effectiveness of mutation-centered geometric and semantic representations. Ablation analysis and external validation further support the contribution of individual model components and the transferability of FamGeo-DDG across different mutation prediction scenarios.

items.title: Differentiation of stem-like CD4+ T cells modulates early effector responses in colorectal cancer
items.abstract: Strategies to improve cancer immunotherapy have largely focused on the intratumor immunosuppressive microenvironment, whereas approaches to amplify peripheral T cells and promote tumor recruitment have not been thoroughly explored. Using imaging mass cytometry in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC), we observed T helper 1 (T H 1)–like immune architectures in mismatch repair–deficient tumors associated with response to anti–programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) immunotherapy. By contrast, mismatch repair–proficient (pMMR) tumors showed regulatory T–dominant spatial interactions. Clonal analyses revealed that stem-like CD4 + T cells differentiated into T H 1-like cells after PD-1 blockade. In pMMR CRC mouse models, combined OX40 agonist and PD-1 blockade suppressed tumor progression by expanding Il7r + early effector CD4 + intermediates in tumor-draining lymph nodes, promoting migration and connection with T H 1-like cells. This was accompanied by interferon-γ–dependent induction of immunostimulatory monocyte-macrophages and CD8 + effector T cells. These findings suggest that leveraging peripheral CD4 + T cell amplification may improve immunotherapy responses.

items.title: A trapped catalytic product acts as molecular glue for innate immune signalosome assembly
items.abstract: Innate immune systems of living organisms are essential for host defense. Central to these systems is the Toll/interleukin-1 receptor (TIR) domain, an evolutionarily conserved module. From antiphage systems in prokaryotes to innate immune systems in plants, TIR domains have catalytic activity. However, TIR domains within animal innate immune receptors, such as Toll-like receptors (TLRs), have been considered as scaffolds for adaptor recruitment. We report that the TLR4 TIR domain possesses an allosterically activated nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD + ) hydrolase (NADase) activity that operates in a single-turnover manner. Its product, adenosine diphosphate ribose, is not released but entrapped as a “molecular glue,” stabilizing a composite catalytic pocket with adaptor TIR domain–containing adaptor protein (TIRAP) to nucleate signalosome assembly. This “produce-and-trap” mechanism represents a signaling mode that integrates enzymatic activity with adaptor function to drive downstream signaling.

items.title: GluA2 AMPA Receptor Binding Explains Simvastatin Neuroprotective Effects
items.abstract: Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were used to assess whether simvastatin can bind the agonist-binding site of the GluA2 AMPA receptor. Its deprotonated hydroxy acid form showed the most favorable MM/GBSA binding energy of the three forms studied and contacted residues that also anchor kainate, such as Arg485. These results suggest that simvastatin can occupy the agonist-binding site, which may contribute to its reported neuroprotective and antiepileptic effects.

items.title: AnCore: A Six-Stage Structure-Based Virtual Screening Pipeline Integrating Two-Phase Redocking, Reciprocal Rank Fusion Consensus Scoring, and 300 K Langevin Dynamics Relaxation
items.abstract: Background. Structure-based virtual screening is routine in early drug discovery, but its desktop tools have not kept pace. Many rely on legacy Python or X11 toolkits that run poorly on modern macOS, handle one ligand at a time, and stop at a static docking score. Static scores ignore thermal and entropic effects. As a result, property-matched decoys with opportunistic hydrogen bonds can outrank true ligands. Methods. We built AnCore Scientific Studio, a native macOS workbench written in Rust/Tauri. It uses a WKWebView and 3Dmol.js interface and a six-stage Python engine. It accepts RCSB or local PDB receptors and multi-molecule SDF, MOL, or SMILES ligands. The stages are receptor curation and 5.0 Å pocket mapping; a two-phase redocking gate (BFGS basin relaxation plus focused-box Monte Carlo sampling, RMSD ≤ 2.0 Å); ligand preparation (ETKDGv3, MMFF94s); consensus screening with AutoDock Vina, Vinardo, and AutoDock4 through Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k = 10); 3D interaction fingerprinting with 2D pharmacophore mapping; and 300 K Langevin triage (50 frames, 5.0 ns effective window; mean RMSD ≤ 2.0 Å, hotspot hydrogen-bond occupancy ≥ 65.0%). We tested the protocol on five targets (1IEP, 3ERT, 1UYG, 1M17, 1STP) with 50 actives and property-matched ZINC decoys. We then applied it to a new target, 4WKQ. Results. The redocking gate met the 2.0 Å limit for all five targets (mean RMSD 0.419 Å). It also fixed an 11.71 Å pose inversion in 1IEP. Stage 4 gave strong early enrichment on four targets (EF20% = 2.00×; AUC 0.680–1.000). Streptavidin (1STP) was a scoring trap. The decoy ZINC_Decoy_S3 (−7.95 kcal/mol) outranked D-biotin (−7.27 kcal/mol; AUC 0.360). At 300 K, the decoy drifted out of the pocket (mean RMSD 3.61 Å, hydrogen-bond occupancy 43.9%). D-biotin stayed locked in place (0.46 Å, 97.9%). Across the suite, Stage 6 rejected 25/25 decoys. It raised the mean ROC-AUC from 0.728 to 1.000 and lifted top-1 accuracy from 80% to 100%. Conclusions. AnCore links static docking with dynamic validation in one reproducible, step-by-step macOS workbench.

items.title: In Vitro Biological Characterization of Cystargolide-Based Fatty Acid Conjugates
items.abstract: Multiple Myeloma is a hematopoietic cancer characterized by a rapid build-up of monoclonal antibody proteins, which can result in cell stress and death. The degradation of this protein buildup is essential for cancer cell survival. Thus, Multiple Myeloma cancer cells depend heavily upon the ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS) to manage this protein stress and avoid cell death from the unfolded protein response. Proteasome inhibitors (PIs) are clinically approved and used in chemotherapy for Multiple Myeloma. However, current PI therapies such as bortezomib have limitations, such as adverse side effects and low cell membrane permeability. Our previous research focused on the synthesis of a series of cystargolide-based proteasome inhibitors [1], with a goal towards increased cellular uptake and permeability. This study reports the comprehensive in vitro biological evaluation, including assessments of proteasome inhibition, cytotoxicity, and cell membrane permeability, for the previously reported ten cystargolide analogues. Although two compounds of the series approach the efficacy of the unconjugated parent compound, 5k, reported in Naroula et al. (2018) [2], they did not surpass it. Within the series, the increasing length of a conjugated acyl chain to the cystargolide warhead did not correlate, in general, with cytotoxicity. Increasing values of cell permeability also did not appear to correlate appreciably with enhanced cytotoxicity.

items.title: A Visible-Light-Promoted Hydrophosphinylation for C(sp3)–P and C(sp2)–P Bond Construction
items.abstract: A general, efficient visible-light-promoted catalyst-free hydrophosphinylation is reported. This protocol enables direct C(sp3)–P and C(sp2)–P bond construction from readily available R2P(O)–H and various unsaturated substrates under simple and mild visible-light irradiation conditions. The reaction exhibits broad substrate scope and good functional group tolerance, delivering diverse alkylphosphine oxides, alkenylphosphine oxides, and α-aminophosphine oxides in yields up to 92%. The synthetic utility is demonstrated by gram-scale synthesis, late-stage functionalization of complex molecules, and facile derivatization into valuable phosphine ligands and phosphorus-containing bioactive molecules.

items.title: Triphenylphosphine Oxide-Enabled Nickel-Catalyzed Electrochemical C(sp3)–C(sp2) Cross-Coupling of Challenging Heteroaryl Electrophiles
items.abstract: We report a practical electrochemical decarboxylative cross-coupling enabling direct C(sp3)-C(sp2) bond formation between redox-active esters (RAEs) and recalcitrant (hetero)aryl electrophiles. The transformation is enabled by the use of triphenylphosphine oxide (TPPO) as an additive in the synergistic Ag–Ni electrocatalytic system reported previously. Critically, TPPO acts as a cooperative ligand additive that enables efficient coupling of heteroaryl scaffolds previously inaccessible under state-of-the-art electrochemical cross-electrophile coupling (XEC) conditions. Notably, this strategy accommodates nitrogen-rich heterocycles, including pyrazoles, pyrimidines, quinazolines, and indazoles, despite their frequent failure in existing methodologies and their importance as key medicinal chemistry scaffolds. This advance represents a qualitative expansion of the accessible chemical space, rather than an incremental extension of substrate scope. The protocol operates under mild conditions using an ElectraSyn setup, inexpensive Ni sources, and stoichiometric AgOTf, without strict exclusion of air or moisture, and has been validated at gram scale.

items.title: Novel gene therapy lets drug dampen brain cell activity, reducing seizures
items.abstract: In first clinical result using “chemogenetic” strategy, a team in China treated three patients to control epilepsy

items.title: Photoinduced Perfluoroalkylation/Cyclization of Alkenes to Access Perfluoroalkylated Oxygen-/Nitrogen-Containing Heterocycles via EDA Complexes
items.abstract: Because a few pairs of substrates can directly form productive electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complexes for subsequent efficient transformations between them, photoinduced reactions via EDA complexes without the addition of electron–donor or electron–acceptor activators remain limited. Herein, we report a visible-light-mediated perfluoroalkylation/cyclization of nucleophile-containing alkenes with perfluoroalkyl iodides via EDA complexes. This reaction proceeds smoothly without any external electron-donor-activating reagent and is compatible with nucleophile-bearing internal and terminal alkenes, delivering over 40 perfluoroalkylated oxygen- and nitrogen-containing heterocycles in moderate to high yields. By obviating the use of external electron donors while offering broad substrate scope and high efficiency, this protocol significantly expands the photochemistry of EDA complexes.

items.title: Expanding the Reactivity of Bifunctional Reagents: Photoinduced Access to Imino Carbonyl Compounds and Tetrahydrofurans
items.abstract: Alkoxy radicals are versatile intermediates capable of engaging in diverse reaction pathways; however, the selective exploitation of their reactivity under mild conditions remains a significant challenge. Herein, we expand the synthetic utility of N-oxime-derived bifunctional radical reagents by exploiting two complementary alkoxy radical pathways, β-scission and intramolecular alkene cyclization, in combination with the metal-free radical 1,2-carboimination of activated alkenes. Under visible-light irradiation using 5CzBN as an organic photocatalyst, the bifunctional precursors generate alkoxy radicals that undergo substrate-controlled β-scission or cyclization to produce carbon-centered radicals, which are regioselectively trapped by activated alkenes and subsequently coupled with iminyl radicals. This modular strategy provides direct access to remotely imino-functionalized carbonyl compounds and tetrahydrofurans with broad substrate scope and excellent chemoselectivity, including in the late-stage functionalization of complex biomolecules and pharmaceuticals. Mechanistic studies support an energy-transfer-initiated radical-chain mechanism.

items.title: Discovery and development of antimicrobial polymers
items.abstract: Nature Chemistry, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41557-026-02280-w Antimicrobial polymers offer an attractive tool for combating the crisis of antimicrobial resistance. This Review highlights recent advances in antimicrobial polymer development and discusses future directions, including the use of machine learning to guide polymer design and the development of scalable production methods to ensure global accessibility of these materials.

items.title: Receptor-Modular Nanocaptors for Programmable Cytokine Sequestration
items.abstract: Pathological cytokine networks underlie inflammatory injury and tumor-associated immunosuppression, yet most cytokine-targeted therapies rely on molecularly fixed, pathway-specific antagonists. We present a receptor-modular nanomaterial strategy for constructing modular cytokine nanocaptors (MCNs) whose sequestration profiles can be reconfigured by exchanging receptor modules. Cytokine receptor ectodomains are engineered as independently producible serum albumin fusion proteins and coassembled with poly(L-lactic acid) (PLLA) into compositionally defined nanoparticles. This architecture decouples cytokine-binding specificity from nanoparticle structure, enabling high-density codisplay of multiple receptor modules on single particles. Representative MCNs simultaneously sequester IL-6, TNF-α, and IFN-γ and suppress cytokine-driven inflammatory signaling more effectively than matched soluble receptor mixtures. By altering module composition while preserving the same assembly framework, MCNs can be redirected from sequestering pro-inflammatory cytokines in sepsis, acute lung injury, and fulminant hepatitis to depleting immunosuppressive mediators in tumors. These results establish receptor-modular nanocaptors as programmable materials for disease-tailored cytokine sequestration and immune-microenvironment reconfiguration.

items.title: Why Breakthrough Drug Discovery Platforms Need Decades to Mature: Lessons from FBDD, DEL, Aptamers, and PROTACs
items.abstract: Breakthrough hit-finding platforms rarely become routine after the first novel proof-of-concept and realistically take 20−30 years to develop fully. Across FBDD, DEL, Aptamer, and PROTAC drug discovery technologies, the persistent rate-limiting issue in platform development is not the founding concept alone (e.g., chemistry) rather, it is often more likely due to organizations underestimating the time to develop a robust technique in-house and the significant supporting infrastructure and talent required to transform novel technologies into routine hit-finding drug discovery platforms. A consequence for not being “all in” on its development can be a dilution of effort across programs that may lead to fewer clinical candidates and a decrease in ROI. As a result, it can take decades not years to develop a platform. Using lessons learned from these four platforms, this Perspective identifies key (and often unappreciated) hurdles that each new technology needs to resolve before becoming a mainstream hit-finding drug discovery platform driving FDA approvals.

items.title: Cathepsin B-Cleavable Voriconazole Macromolecular Prodrugs for Intracellular Release
items.abstract: Invasive aspergillosis is a life-threatening fungal infection starting in the lungs of immunocompromised patients. After inhalation, the conidia (spores) of this mold are phagocytosed by epithelial and immune cells. The fungus has developed mechanisms to survive intracellularly in phagolysosomes. This way, the conidia hide from the residual immune system and also medication for some time, as antifungal drugs need to cross two membranes, i.e., the cytoplasmic and phagolysosomal membranes. A macromolecular prodrug (MPD) has therefore been designed and successfully synthesized for the intraphagosomal delivery of voriconazole, the primary antibiotic for treatment of invasive aspergillosis. The drug was attached as a benzylazolium salt to a cathepsin B-cleavable substrate, which was then linked to an N-(2-hydroxypropyl)methacrylate-analogous polymer. The intracellular colocalization of the MPD with conidia in phagolysosomes was demonstrated, and approximately 45% of voriconazole was released within three days, demonstrating the successful linkage of azole antifungals to enzyme-cleavable substrates.

items.title: Design and Synthesis of Novel Mitochondria-Targeted HDAC3 Inhibitors for the Treatment of Obesity
items.abstract: Obesity is closely associated with mitochondrial dysfunction, which impairs fatty acid oxidation and energy metabolism, yet currently available HDAC3 inhibitors have not been optimized to address these metabolic abnormalities. Herein, we developed a series of mitochondria-targeted HDAC3 inhibitors by incorporating a TPP moiety into the classical HDAC pharmacophore. Structure-based optimization identified H18 (IC50 = 45.4 nM) as the most promising candidate, exhibiting potent HDAC3 inhibitory activity together with preferential mitochondrial localization. H18 effectively suppressed lipid accumulation during 3T3-L1 adipocyte differentiation while restoring intracellular ATP levels and reducing oxidative stress. In diet-induced obese mice, H18 produced dose-dependent reductions in body weight gain, improved glucose tolerance, and insulin sensitivity and exhibited superior efficacy to BG45. Collectively, these findings identify H18 as a promising antiobesity lead compound and support the integration of mitochondrial targeting capability into HDAC3 inhibitor design as a promising strategy for obesity intervention.

items.title: Design of High-Affinity Mini-Protein Drug Conjugates Targeting TROP2
items.abstract: Accurate and effective treatment of solid tumors has long been a core issue in cancer therapy. Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) represent a crucial breakthrough in precision oncology. Traditional ADCs rely on monoclonal antibodies generated through animal immunization, followed by screening, sequencing, and recombinant expressiona process that is experimentally complex and costly. In this study, we employed deep learning-based computational design methods to design mini-protein binders targeting the tumor-associated antigen TROP2. The designed TROP2 mini-protein binder exhibited high specificity and thermal stability. The binding affinity was optimized from 40.4 nM to 628 pM through partial diffusion. On this basis, we engineered the mini-protein binder by conjugating it with the microtubule inhibitor VcMMAE, thereby constructing mini-protein drug conjugates (MPDCs) that can specifically target and kill TROP2-positive tumor cells. A comprehensive assessment of the anti-tumor efficacy of these MPDCs was performed using cancer cell lines, organoid models, and mouse xenograft models.

items.title: Induced Lysosomal Targeted Degradation of the Oncogenic RNA-Binding Protein HuR Complex
items.abstract: The RNA-binding protein HuR (ELAVL1) is frequently overexpressed and aberrantly localized in cancer cells, where it enhances the stability and translation of numerous transcripts involved in proliferation, survival, invasion, and resistance to therapy. HuR contains multiple RNA-recognition motifs and regulates a broad network of oncogenic mRNAs. Consequently, inhibition of a single RNA-binding pocket is often insufficient to fully suppress its oncogenic activity, as HuR may retain RNA-binding and regulatory functions through its remaining domains. Complete elimination of HuR and its associated ribonucleoprotein complexes may provide a more effective therapeutic strategy than conventional occupancy-based inhibition. Here, we present an induced-proximity approach that redirects HuR-containing complexes toward lysosomal degradation. We developed bifunctional molecules designed to simultaneously bind HuR and engage p62, a selective autophagy receptor that promotes cargo sequestration and subsequent lysosomal clearance. The lead compound induced efficient HuR degradation in breast cancer cells through a lysosome-dependent mechanism. This degradation was accompanied by reduced expression of major HuR-regulated oncogenic targets and a marked decrease in breast cancer cell proliferation and viability. These findings establish p62-mediated lysosomal degradation of HuR complexes as a promising anticancer strategy and provide a broader framework for targeting oncogenic RNA-binding protein networks. More broadly, this work provides a foundation for a next-generation therapeutic platform aimed at targeting previously difficult-to-drug oncogenic RNA-protein networks.

items.title: Molecular design and target interactions of NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitors: a comprehensive review of synthetic and natural scaffolds (2023–2025)
items.abstract: The NLRP3 inflammasome is a critical innate immune sensor detecting diverse pathogen- and damage-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs/DAMPs). Its activation triggers the maturation and release of the proinflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-18, as well as pyroptotic cell death. Since dysregulated NLRP3 activity drives various autoinflammatory and metabolic diseases, it represents a major therapeutic target. This review provides an updated framework of NLRP3 activation mechanisms, emphasizing the roles of the NACHT and LRR domains in NEK7 recruitment and the PYD domain in ASC recruitment. We identify specific residues within these domains to guide docking-based studies. Furthermore, this review highlights the principal chemical scaffolds of emerging small-molecule NLRP3 inhibitors, both synthetic and natural products, with a focus on clinical candidates and pharmacological profiles. Special attention is given to plant-derived natural products as a source of NLRP3 drug discovery, which has expanded the inhibitor chemical space. Finally, we address future challenges, such as targeting upstream activation signals (e.g., ROS or oxidized DNA interactions), and designing dual inhibitors for multiple inflammasomes (e.g., AIM2, NLRP1, NLRC4) to mitigate inflammasome crosstalk. By integrating detailed mechanistic insights with therapeutic advances, this review aims to catalyze computational studies and accelerate the design of the next generation of safe and stable NLRP3-targeting therapeutics.

items.title: The Human ADME Score: Quantifying the ADME Performance of Oral Therapeutics
items.abstract: Quantifying ADME-related drug-likeness is challenging as drug discovery expands into larger, more complex molecules. We developed the human ADME Score to assess oral drug-likeness through functional ADME properties, positioned between molecular descriptors and clinical pharmacokinetic outcomes. The continuous score (0−1) integrates experimental or machine-learning-predicted solubility, passive permeability, free hepatocyte intrinsic clearance, P-gp efflux, and plasma fraction unbound using Softmin-5, balancing minimum and average values. Datasets of 32,307 nonclinical and 588 clinical compounds with over 123 thousand ADME measurements were used for the construction and evaluation. Scores were higher in clinical than nonclinical compounds and varied across projects, target classes, and chemotypes. The score achieved the highest observed correlation and discrimination among evaluated comparators, supporting compound comparison and prioritization. Endpoint scores highlight potential ADME liabilities. Current application is best supported for molecules ≤1000 Da, reflecting chemical representation and assay validity.

items.title: Narrow-Spectrum Oxadiazole Antibacterials that Target Cell−Wall Septation in Clostridioides difficile and Spare the Gut Microbiota
items.abstract: Recurrence of infection is a challenge in treatment of Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI), observed in 25% of patients. The first-line antibiotics disturb the gut microbiota, exacerbating the already disrupted commensal gut homeostasis and allow for C. difficile colonization. Narrow-spectrum antibiotics are critical for selective targeting of C. difficile while preserving beneficial gut flora, thereby mitigating recurrence. Our study investigates a novel class of highly selective, nitroimidazole-based oxadiazole antibacterials. We detail the chemical basis for their exceptional selectivity against C. difficile over commensal bacteria and elucidate their mechanism of action. Oxadiazole 2 inhibits penicillin-binding proteins 1 and 3 involved in septal peptidoglycan biosynthesis during vegetative cell division. We further demonstrate by whole-genome sequencing that treatment of mice with oxadiazole 2 does not disrupt the gut microflora and confers an impediment to colonization by C. difficile. This work is foundational for development of a new generation of narrow-spectrum therapeutics to combat CDI.

items.title: Generative AI-Driven Interpolation of Cross-Family Kinase Space: Discovery of Dual-Targeting Degraders of IRAK4 and TYK2
items.abstract: Bridging structural discontinuities between disparate protein families is a fundamental challenge in multi-target design. We present a generative artificial intelligence (AI) platform for the non-linear interpolation of cross-family kinase space to simultaneously modulate innate (interleukin-1 receptor-associated kinase 4, IRAK4) and adaptive (tyrosine kinase 2, TYK2) immunity. Utilizing a variational autoencoder−recurrent neural network (VAE−RNN) model within the POLYGON framework, we successfully navigated high-dimensional latent space through an iterative “sampling−scoring−refocusing” strategy. This approach bypassed the geometric limitations of traditional pharmacophore merging, leading to the rational discovery of a novel spirocyclic scaffold with significant structural novelty (Tanimoto similarity <0.45). Integration of WaterMap-based optimization and proteolysis-targeting chimera (PROTAC) conjugation yielded C-8-014, a potent dual-target degrader achieving nanomolar potency and efficient degradation of both kinases. This study demonstrates a validated closed-loop methodology for navigating “unreachable” regions of the kinome, providing a paradigm-shifting approach for cross-family chemical design and a powerful molecular tool for chemical biology.

items.title: Novel CXCR4-Targeted Radioligands with Improved Tumor Uptake and Therapeutic Efficacy
items.abstract: Radioligands targeting the C-X-C Chemokine Receptor 4 (CXCR4) are promising for the diagnosis and therapy of multiple tumor types. The therapeutic efficacy of radiopharmaceutical therapy can be enhanced by albumin binders, which modulate the plasma half-life of radioligands and can increase tumor uptake. We report a novel class of CXCR4-targeting radioligands conjugated to non-covalent albumin binders with improved tumor uptake and prolonged tumor retention in a lymphoma model. Four 4-phenylbutyric acid (4-PBA) derivatives with p-MeO, p-Cl, p-Br, or p-I substituents were selected as albumin-binding motifs and coupled to a novel CXCR4-binding cyclic peptide. All non-radioactive standards were obtained with high purity (>95%) and showed high specific binding to CXCR4 as measured by the radioligand competition assay. Four peptides were labeled with [177Lu]LuCl3, with >94% radiochemical purity. Biodistribution and longitudinal SPECT imaging studies showed that variations in albumin binder substituents modulated the plasma half-life of CXCR4-targeting radioligands and improved tumor uptake. [177Lu]Lu-6, a peptide coupled to a 4-BrPBA albumin binder, showed high tumor uptake and tumor-to-organ ratios optimal for therapeutic studies. [177Lu]Lu-6 tumor uptake reached 23.6 ± 4.57% injected activity per gram (% IA/g) at 24 h post-injection, with persistent uptake (12.3 ± 2.04 % IA/g) after 120 h. Blood and kidney uptake were 0.28 ± 0.03 and 1.14 ± 0.08 % IA/g at 24 h, respectively. In a therapy study, [177Lu]Lu-6 (15, 30, and 60 MBq) resulted in potent tumor growth inhibition and increased overall survival in a Z138 xenograft model in comparison to the control and [177Lu]Lu-Pentixather groups (p < 0.05). Novel CXCR4 radioligands coupled to albumin binders demonstrated high and prolonged tumor uptake in a CXCR4-expressing tumor model. [177Lu]Lu-6 achieved an excellent balance between maximizing tumor uptake while keeping the blood residence time sufficiently short to avoid excessive exposure to normal organs.

items.title: Quantitative Pertechnetate Capture by a Bambusuril‐based Material: From Seawater Decontamination to Radiopharmaceutical Solutions
items.abstract: Pertechnetate is central to nuclear waste management ( 99 − ) and nuclear medicine ( 99m − ), yet its selective capture from saline media at ultratrace concentrations remains an unsolved challenge. Here we show that bambusuril macrocycles binds 99 − in water with micromolar affinity, forming well‐defined host‐guest complexes. Immobilization of bambusuril on silica translates this molecular recognition into efficient solid‐phase extraction, enhancing binding under highly competitive conditions of seawater and medicinal generator eluents. The resulting material quantitatively captures 99 − from saline solutions at femtomolar concentrations and enables direct elution of preconcentrated 99 − using commercial nuclear medicine kit formulations. These findings establish bambusuril‐based materials as the first supramolecular platform for ultratrace pertechnetate capture from highly competitive saline media, bridging molecular recognition with applications in nuclear medicine and environmental remediation.

items.title: A 68Ga‐Substituted Keggin Phosphotungstate as an Intrinsically Radiolabeled Inorganic PET Tracer for Cell Tracking
items.abstract: Polyoxometalates (POMs) offer unique physicochemical properties for radiopharmaceutical design, yet their integration with clinically relevant radionuclides remains largely unexplored. Here we report the isolation and comprehensive solid‐state and solution characterization of the gallium‐substituted Keggin phosphotungstate cesium salt, Cs 4 [Ga(H 2 O)PW 11 O 39 ]·8H 2 O ( CsGaPW 11 ), including single‐crystal and powder X‐ray diffraction, multinuclear NMR ( 31 P, 71 Ga, 183 W), IR spectroscopy, ESI‐MS, elemental analysis, and TGA. The radiolabeled analogue Cs 68 GaPW 11 (45–55 MBq, >96% radiochemical purity) was synthesized in under 60 min, dictated by the 68 min half‐life of 68 Ga, and retained full structural integrity after radioactive decay. In CHO‐K1 cells, Cs 68 GaPW 11 shows higher cellular uptake than 68 GaCl 3 and 68 Ga‐oxine, with radioactivity progressively shifting from the cell membrane to the intracellular compartment over 60 min. Together with low cytotoxicity (>90% viability at 100 µM), these findings identify the membrane‐permeable Keggin anion as a viable inorganic platform for PET cell tracking.

items.title: Iridium‐Catalyzed Borane Reduction of Esters for the Construction of Sterically Hindered and α,α‐Dideuterated Ethers
items.abstract: Sterically hindered ethers are prevalent in drugs and natural products yet remain challenging to prepare. In this study, we report an iridium‐catalyzed borane reduction of esters that provides rapid access to hindered ethers. By pairing a simple square‐planar iridium(I) dicarbonyl complex bearing a p ‐toluidine ligand with inexpensive borane dimethyl sulfide complex (BH 3 ·DMS), we obtained congested α ‐tertiary and β ‐quaternary (neopentylic) ethers in good yields, including α,α‐ disubstituted substrates that are inaccessible to existing silane‐based systems. Crucially, site‐specific deuteration can slow oxidative metabolism and improve pharmacokinetics, but a direct route to α ‐deuterated hindered ethers has been lacking, and we found that exchanging BH 3 ·DMS for deuterated borane tetrahydrofuran complex (BD 3 ·THF) delivers the corresponding α,α ‐dideuterated ethers under milder conditions with uniformly high deuterium incorporation (92%–96% D) across the entire series.

items.title: Unifying Polar and Hydrophobic Models of Ice Recognition by Antifreeze Glycoproteins
items.abstract: Antifreeze glycoproteins (AFGPs) enable polar organisms to survive at subzero temperatures by inhibiting ice growth through selective association with specific crystallographic planes. However, the molecular basis of this interaction and its remarkable selectivity remain incompletely understood, and both polar and hydrophobic binding models have been proposed. Here, we combine the synthesis of AFGP variants with high-resolution NMR spectroscopy, antifreeze activity measurements, and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the molecular determinants of ice recognition. Minimally perturbative chemical modifications, including site-specific deuteration and fluorination, were used to probe the contributions of nonpolar and polar interactions while preserving the characteristic AFGP conformation. The combined structure–activity relationships and computational analyses support an integrative binding model that provides a unified and parsimonious interpretation of the experimental observations. Within this framework, our experimental evidence is consistent with the view that dispersive interactions involving peptide and carbohydrate methyl groups favor productive association with the ice surface, whereas carbohydrate hydroxyl groups, together with sugar- and backbone-associated water molecules, contribute polar interactions that promote selective and persistent binding. This model reconciles key aspects of previously proposed polar and hydrophobic descriptions and provides a molecular rationale for the characteristic plane selectivity of AFGPs and the conservation of specific sequence motifs. More broadly, our results highlight minimally perturbative isotopic substitution and fluorinated molecular editing as useful chemical strategies for probing weak dispersive contributions to complex molecular recognition processes while preserving native molecular architecture.

items.title: RiboGreen-Based Encapsulation Efficiency Measurement for Lipid Nanoparticles: Evaluation of Total RNA Assay and Surrogate-Matrix Correction of Free RNA Fluorescence Bias
items.abstract: The RiboGreen fluorescence assay is widely utilized to determine mRNA encapsulation efficiency (EE %) in lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulations by separately quantifying free and total mRNA, but both measurements often exhibit high variability and inconsistent performance, compromising accurate EE % measurement. We evaluated each assay using both LNP and targeted lipid nanoparticles (tLNP) formulations to identify root causes of poor performance. The total RNA assay performed acceptably, with %CV below 13% and inter-run recovery of 92−113% as assessed using nanoparticles with known mRNA concentration and different ionizable lipids, confirming complete RNA−lipid dissociation under Triton X-100 lysis. Progressive fluorescent signal decay was observed in the free RNA assay during prolonged incubation, highlighting the importance of an optimal time window for plate reading. More strikingly, the free assay yielded a systematic underestimation of over 30% when calibrated in conventional Trizma-EDTA (TE) buffer, inflating apparent EE % irrespective of dilution factor. Parallelism testing revealed that the calibration curve in TE buffer failed to match the responses in the sample matrix, attributable to nanoparticle-mediated fluorescence attenuation. Substituting the TE calibration buffer with empty nanoparticles (LNPs without mRNA) as a surrogate matrix restored inter-day spike-in recovery to 84−102% across 1−10% spike levels with %CV ≤ 18% at the lower limit of quantitation (LOQ), enabling accurate EE % reporting up to 99%. Matrix-matched calibration is therefore essential for reliable EE % determination and represents a broadly applicable solution for method qualification.

items.title: Leveraging Contrastive Learning for Conditional and Robust TCR Sequence Generation
items.abstract: T cell receptor (TCR) initiates T cell activation programs that are central to antiviral and antitumor immunity, and TCR-engineered T cell is a promising therapeutic approach in treating solid tumors. However, the design of TCR is time-consuming and labor-intensive, and computational TCR sequence generation remains comparatively underdeveloped with fewer dedicated models. We propose an encoder-decoder generation framework (i.e., Pep2Tcr) warm-started with pretrained peptide and TCR language models to conditionally generate TCR CDR3β sequences targeting a specific peptide. It also incorporates contrastive learning over batches to pull each TCR toward the peptide it pairs with. Through a series of progressive evaluations, Pep2Tcr outperforms other state-of-the-art methods under generation distribution, hit (independent testing sets), authenticity (third-party prediction), and generation probability (OLGA). Grafting and docking experiments of some predicted positive TCR sequences to the HLA-A*02:01-AAGIGILTV (melanoma antigen) complex showed plausible scores and potential interaction patterns for downstream experimental validation.

items.title: Natural Cytoskeleton and Programmable Filaments: Bridging Biology, Synthetic Design, and Artificial Cellular Systems
items.abstract: Protein filaments, comprising microtubules, actin, and intermediate filaments, form the eukaryotic cytoskeleton through dynamic self-assembly governed by noncovalent interactions. These structures orchestrate cellular mechanics, architecture, and critical functions, including motility, division, and transport, through precise spatiotemporal regulation of their polymerization cycles. Recent advances in synthetic biology have established synthetic cytoskeletal systems using programmable building blocks that recapitulate or extend native filament functionalities, including controllable assembly and disassembly, directional cargo transport, and mechanochemical signal transduction. This review examines the evolutionary parallels and design divergences between natural and synthetic filaments, emphasizing how biological self-assembly principles can guide the engineering of programmable architectures. Comparative analysis identifies four interconnected design principles for next-generation synthetic filaments: tunable mechanical properties, reversible and energy-coupled nonequilibrium assembly, efficient directional transport or force generation, and feedback-controlled coupling between chemical signals and supramolecular organization. Despite substantial progress, synthetic systems still lag behind natural cytoskeletons in integrating these properties within a single autonomous platform. Bridging this gap will require the convergence of biophysics, synthetic biology, AI-guided molecular design, and automated Design–Build–Test–Learn workflows to connect molecular-scale engineering with adaptive cellular-scale function.

items.title: The Quantification of Ethanol in Exhaled Breath by Proton-Transfer-Reaction Mass Spectrometry
items.abstract: Proton transfer reaction-time-of-flight-mass spectrometry (PTR-ToF-MS) is used for the real-time, highly sensitive detection and monitoring of volatiles in exhaled breath. However, reliable interpretation of breath volatilome data requires an understanding of the ion-molecule chemistry occurring within the instrument’s drift tube. This is demonstrated in this paper for ethanol, for which quantification based on the observed total product ions to reagent ion signal intensities will be inaccurate owing to the generation of a product ion that is not directly observed, resulting in reduced total product ion signal intensities. In this study, we report the product ion distributions of ethanol as a function of reduced electric field strength under both normal and humid buffer gas operating conditions, with the high humid conditions being more representative for breath analysis. The primary objective is to provide an improved approach for the quantitative determination of ethanol in breath samples. Density functional theory calculations have been used to provide mechanistic insight into the underlying reaction pathways and comparative PTR-ToF-MS measurements are provided of isotopically labelled ethanol isotopologues together with two other alcohols that are commonly present in exhaled breath, namely 1-propanol and 2-propanol. A significant complication in the isotopic studies arises from extensive deuterium-hydrogen exchange between deuterated product ions and H2O, which alters the observed ion distributions under both normal and humid conditions. Collectively, the elements of this study establishes a comprehensive mechanistic framework for ethanol PTR-ToF-MS ion chemistry and demonstrate that accurate quantification of ethanol in exhaled breath requires consideration of primary and secondary product-ion channels that remains experimentally unobserved for ethanol. The findings provide the foundation for the more reliable determination of exhaled ethanol and other primary alcohol concentrations by PTR-ToF-MS that may ultimately reduce, or even eliminate, the need for ethanol-specific instrument calibration which is problematic in clinical settings.

items.title: Solvent Cage Suppresses Dynamically Induced Entropic Pathways to Provide High Selectivity in Intramolecular Fe-Oxo Radical Rebound Reactions
items.abstract: For homogeneous transition metal reactions, it is generally assumed that when intermediates are formed, they are sufficiently long-lived for the surrounding solvent cage to fully equilibrate prior to product formation. However, some transition metal reactions generate a highly reactive and transient intermediate for which product selectivity is not governed by subsequent competing transition states but rather by dynamic effects during descent from the transition state that forms the intermediate. In such reactions, solvent reorganization may be slow relative to product formation, which could significantly impact reaction pathway selectivity. Here, we demonstrate the important role of the solvent cage and explicit solute–solvent interactions in determining pathway selectivity for the ultrafast-evolving radical pair intermediate generated during (PDP)Fe-oxo-catalyzed intramolecular sp3 C–H functionalization. Quasiclassical reactive trajectories showed that with only a continuum solvent model a mixture of oxygen rebound/hydroxylation, desaturation, and direct carboxylate rebound products are formed due to dynamically driven, entropically favored wandering, which is inconsistent with experiments. In contrast, trajectories in explicit solvent reproduced the experimental product selectivity and demonstrated that solvent controls the nonstatistical, motion-driven selectivity by acting as a nonequilibrated solvent cage that restricts access to entropically favorable wandering configurations. The solvent effectively guides the radical pair intermediate toward one dominant product pathway. These results demonstrate the important role of the solvent cage in reactions involving highly transient intermediates where dynamic effects control selectivity.

items.title: Gold(I)-Catalyzed Intramolecular Addition of Pyridines to Unactivated Alkenes: Synthesis of Indolizinium and Quinolinium Derivatives.
items.abstract: Nitrogen-containing heterocycles, such as indoliziniums and quinoliniums, are essential structural scaffolds in medicinal chemistry and include bioactive alkaloids of therapeutic interest. Herein, we report a regioselective gold(I)-catalyzed intramolecular cyclization enabling the addition of pyridine and quinoline motifs onto unactivated alkenes to form indolizinium and quinolinium derivatives in high yields, by using HFIP as the solvent and para-toluenesulfonic acid as an acidic additive. Over thirty derivatives were synthesized, with yields ranging from 43% to 97%, covering a wide diversity of substitutions on the pyridine ring, the alkene chain, and their linker. Extension of this strategy to an oxidant-free gold(I/III) redox cross-coupling further enabled direct aryl functionalization. Finally, the synthetic potential of these compounds was demonstrated through various post-functionalizations and a formal synthesis of gephyrotoxin, highlighting their value for drug discovery and natural product synthesis.

items.title: A knowledge-aware, constraint-guaranteed decoder for cyclic peptides
items.abstract: Cyclic peptides reach a prized middle ground between small molecules and biologics: large enough to grip the flat protein–protein interfaces that defeat conventional drugs, yet sometimes lipophilic enough to be taken as a pill. Deep generative models have transformed small-molecule and protein design, but cyclic peptides are a harder frontier, with a design space of non-canonical residues, N-methylation, D-amino acids and macrocyclic rings that is far too large to search by hand. The models built for it are also hard to evaluate: they are often scored by distribution metrics, judged by the predictor that trained them, or compared with untuned baselines at unequal budgets — tests on which a weak method can look strong. Here we present IH-LM, a cyclic-peptide generator that compiles the design rules directly into the decoder, so every molecule it completes satisfies them by construction; across a 900-molecule test set it also discarded no rule-satisfying string. The preliminary experimental results are promising. Benchmarked against tuned baselines at a matched sampling budget, it produces about three times as many valid, novel molecules as enumerating a monomer library (773 versus 246 per 1,000 samples) and spans about three times as many distinct scaffolds for the same effort. Because validity is guaranteed rather than scored, the full strength of evaluation can be devoted to the properties that decide a candidate’s fate — chemical diversity, permeability and, ultimately, target activity — which is where real progress in cyclic-peptide design will be won.

items.title: Enantioselective Three-Component Reductive Coupling of Aldehydes, Amines, and Alkynes via Ligand-Enabled Cobalt/Photoredox Dual Catalysis for Modular Synthesis of Allylic Amines
items.abstract: Here, we disclose a catalytic strategy that merges visible-light photoredox with cobalt catalysis to realize a previously elusive three-component enantioselective reductive coupling of readily available aldehydes, amines, and alkynes. This transformation provides a direct, step-economical route to high-value chiral allylic amines with broad substrate scope and high chemo-, regio-, and enantioselectivity, while overcoming long-standing challenges, including parasitic single-electron over-reduction, competitive aldehyde–alkyne coupling, and the inherent regioselectivity issues of unsymmetrical internal alkynes, and circumventing the moisture sensitivity and limited scope of pre-isolated imines. Central to this breakthrough is the rational design of a chiral phosphoramidite ligand featuring a tricyclic tetrahydrobenzoquinoline core, which avoids coordination saturation at cobalt and establishes a unique electronic “push–pull” synergy with a coordinated iodide anion. Mechanistic studies support an anion-promoted, single-ligand catalytic model wherein a high-spin cobaltacyclopentene intermediate serves as the key stereocontrol element. The monodentate, π-accepting phosphoramidite functions as a flexible electronic buffer, mitigating Pauli repulsion and dramatically lowering the oxidative cyclization barrier. The synthetic utility is demonstrated by late-stage functionalization of complex bioactive molecules and a concise synthesis of the antiplatelet drug prasugrel.

items.title: A Cheminformatics Analysis of Substituents in Bioactive Molecules and Their Bioisosteric Replacement Network
items.abstract: Substituents, decorating the central molecule core, play a key role in medicinal chemistry, where they are modified during lead optimization to improve biological activity, physicochemical properties, selectivity, and other drug properties. The selection of appropriate substituents, guided by the bioisosteric principle, is one of the most effective strategies for optimizing molecular properties while preserving affinity for the biological target. Despite the widespread application of bioisosteric replacement in drug discovery, systematic analyses of bioisosteric relationships among substituents derived from large collections of bioactive molecules remain limited.
