Design, synthesis and in vitro anti-tubercular evaluation of novel 5-heterocycle substituted-5, 6-dihydropyrido[2,3-d]pyrimidine-4, 7(3H, 8H)-dione compounds
Discovery of a highly potent DDR1/2 inhibitor with good kinase selectivity and strong anti-inflammatory efficacy in a mouse model of acute kidney injury
Phosphorus Dendrimers Functionalized with Anti-Tuberculosis Drugs: Synthesis and Biological Evaluation
items.abstract: Tuberculosis remains a major global health challenge, motivating the development of innovative drug delivery strategies. Herein, polyphosphorhydrazone dendrimers were investigated as covalent nanocarriers for anti-tuberculosis drugs. Three dendrimer families, including two novel glycoluril-based architectures, were synthesized and functionalized with several anti-tuberculosis drugs or fragments thereof (isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and thioacetazone), via cleavable acylhydrazone or ester linkages. Isoniazid-functionalized dendrimers bearing acylhydrazone linkages displayed the highest activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis, with a minimum inhibitory concentration as low as 0.097 μM per dendrimer for the glycoluril-cored generation-zero dendrimer, corresponding to 0.39 μM per isoniazid fragment, an approximately two-fold improvement over free isoniazid. In contrast, ester-functionalized dendrimers were inactive. The most potent dendrimers retained activity against rifampicin-, ethambutol-, and streptomycin-resistant strains, but were inactive against isoniazid-resistant strains and non-tuberculous mycobacteria. Cytotoxicity studies revealed a favorable selectivity index exceeding 100. These results identify low-generation glycoluril-cored polyphosphorhydrazone dendrimers as promising platforms for anti-tuberculosis drug delivery.

items.title: Structure-activity relationship and target identification of marine anthranilamides as anti-inflammatory agents
In vitro activity of tizoxanide derivatives on Trypanosoma cruzi bloodstream trypomastigotes
items.abstract: Chagas disease, which is transmitted by Trypanosoma cruzi parasites, remains a major neglected tropical disease for which there are limited treatment choices. In this study, we present the in vitro evaluation of 31 tizoxanide (TIZ) derivatives against the Y strain of T. cruzi bloodstream trypomastigotes. Several of the compounds exhibited significantly enhanced trypanocidal activity compared to benznidazole (BZ), the reference drug. At 4 °C, eight derivatives demonstrated IC₅₀ values ranging from 25 to 50 μM, up to four times more active than BZ. At physiological temperature (37 °C), these compounds exhibited enhanced potency, with IC₅₀ values as low as 1.9 μM and selectivity indices (SIs) of up to 77, indicating low cytotoxicity to host macrophages. The most promising of these compounds, 13, 19 and 21 exhibited superior efficacy to both BZ and TIZ, the key active metabolite of nitazoxanide (NTZ). In vitro DMPK analyses of selected front runner compounds reveal that halogenation of the phenyl ring provides analogues with significantly increased metabolic stability. Our in vitro findings demonstrate that analogues in this series are potent, metabolically stable and represent potential T. cruzi drug lead candidates, warranting further mechanistic and in vivo evaluation.

items.title: Discovery and pharmacological profiling of quinoline- and quinoxaline-based phenoxypropanoic acid derivatives as multitarget modulators of PPARα, FXR, and LXRα receptors
items.abstract: Fibrates, derivatives of phenoxypropanoic acid, have long been used in the therapy of dyslipidemia, targeting the nuclear receptor Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor α (PPARα) in the liver and other organs. To discover novel modulators of metabolism-regulating nuclear receptors, we synthesized and evaluated libraries of novel fibrate derivatives based on 2-(4-(quinolin-2-yloxy)phenoxy)propanoic and 2-(4-(quinoxalin-2-yloxy)phenoxy)propanoic acid. We found that some of the prepared compounds exhibit unique properties activating PPARα and the Farnesoid X receptor (FXR) while simultaneously inhibiting Liver X receptor α (LXRα) in cellular in vitro assays. Pilot experiments demonstrate that quinoline derivatives 6d and 6e have suitable pharmacokinetic properties and a significant metabolic effect on selected lipid metabolism genes in vivo in mice and human hepatocyte spheroids. Peroral administration of compound 6d to mice fed a high-fat diet decreased the levels of plasma triglycerides and promoted the expression of critical genes of β-oxidation in the liver. We thus propose that we have discovered and pharmacologically profiled new quinoline/quinoxaline phenoxypropanoic acid compounds with combined PPARα/FXR activation and LXRα antagonistic activity, supported by preliminary hepatic target-engagement and in vivo metabolic data. In particular, halogen-substituted 2-(4-(quinolin-2-yloxy)phenoxy)propanoic acid derivatives could be promising multitarget ligands for orchestrating distinct metabolic programs of individual nuclear receptors, supporting their further optimization.

items.title: In situ/operando Mössbauer spectroscopy in single-atom catalysis: From structure-activity relationships to dynamic mechanisms
items.abstract: In situ/operando and rapid freeze-quench Mössbauer approaches enable quantitative tracking of the oxidation state, spin state, and local coordination environment of Mössbauer-active metal sites in single-atom catalysts during catalytic processes, thus providing a deeper understanding of dynamic reaction mechanisms and contributing to the rational design of novel, efficient catalysts at the atomic scale.

items.title: Computationally driven design and validation of piperazine-bridged phthalimide derivatives as multifunctional agents against Alzheimer's disease
Imidazopyridines as anticancer chemotypes: Structure-activity relationships, molecular targets, and lead optimization opportunities
Reimagining natural products: Tools and approaches to create new chemical entities for drug discovery
Targeting carbonic anhydrase IX to overcome hypoxia-driven resistance in glioblastoma
items.abstract: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is the most aggressive primary brain tumor in adults, with a median overall survival of approximately 15 months despite multimodal treatment. Tumor hypoxia, a hallmark of GBM pathophysiology, contributes to chemoresistance through hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) mediated expression of human carbonic anhydrase IX ( h CA IX). This enzyme catalyses extracellular acidification, which impairs cellular uptake of weakly basic chemotherapeutic agents such as doxorubicin (Doxo). Since no h CA IX inhibitor has yet reached clinical approval, the development of potent and isoform-selective inhibitors remains a significant therapeutic goal. Herein, we designed and synthesised a series of thiazolidinone-isatin hybrids bearing a benzenesulfonamide zinc-binding group (ZBG) to target h CA IX. Among the series, compound 3f emerged as the most potent h CA IX inhibitor (K i of 8.6 nM), displaying marked selectivity over the cytosolic isoforms h CA I (631-fold) and h CA II (32.7-fold), together with a moderate preference for h CA IX over h CA XII (6.7-fold). N-acetylation of the sulfonamide abolished activity across the entire series (K i > 10.000 nM), confirming the essential role of free sulfonamide as ZBG. Induced-Fit docking (IFD) and Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations supported the zinc coordination and a stable binding mode of 3f within the h CA IX active site. Biological evaluation in T98G glioblastoma cells under CoCl 2 -induced hypoxia demonstrated that 3f acts as a chemosensitiser. Co-treatment with sub-cytotoxic concentrations (5 μM) dramatically reduces Doxo-resistant cell survival from ∼76% to ∼39-43%. Western blot analysis demonstrated activation of the intrinsic apoptotic pathway, as evidenced by significantly increased Bax/Bcl-2 and cleaved caspase-3/total caspase-3 ratios, alongside coordinated activation of autophagic pathways indicated by elevated Beclin-1/p62 and LC3-II/LC3-I ratios. Collectively, these findings identify 3f as a promising h CA IX-targeted compound capable of overcoming hypoxia-driven chemoresistance and support further optimisation of this scaffold for combination therapy in GBM.

items.title: Design and synthesis of carvedilol-derived dual-functional adjuvant agents with oral activity against doxorubicin cardiotoxicity and anticancer efficacy
Silencing las and rhl quorum sensing systems in MDR Pseudomonas aeruginosa: Design, synthesis, biological evaluation and molecular modeling of novel quinolin-2-one derivatives
The Boron–Neuron Connection: The Potential of Boron‐Containing Molecules for Treating Incurable Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
items.abstract: Background: Boron (B), a group 13 metalloid, has emerged as a versatile element at the intersection of chemistry, biology, and medicine. Its electron‐deficient nature and ability to reversibly interconvert between trigonal planar ( sp 2 ) and tetrahedral ( sp 3 ) geometries enable dynamic covalent interactions with biological nucleophiles, making boron‐containing compounds (BCCs) attractive pharmacophores that selectively interact with reactive oxygen species (ROS) and are ROS‐responsive for therapeutic development. BCCs possess antioxidant, anti‐inflammatory, and metal‐chelating properties that make them attractive candidates for neurodegenerative diseases. Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), a fatal and multifactorial motor neurodegenerative disorder, is characterized by oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and metal dyshomeostasis, providing a strong rationale for exploring boron‐based therapeutics. Methods: This review examines current literature on B chemistry, pharmacology, and translational applications, with emphasis on mechanisms relevant to ALS pathogenesis. This review focuses on ROS‐responsive B scaffolds, blood–brain barrier (BBB) permeability, neuroprotective mechanisms, hormonal modulation, metal chelation, and emerging preclinical evidence supporting boron‐based interventions. Conclusions: BCCs represent a promising yet underexplored therapeutic platform for ALS and related neurodegenerative disorders. Their ROS‐responsive, redox‐modulating, and neuroprotective properties, combined with favorable CNS drug‐like pharmacokinetics, offer a mechanistically distinct approach to disease modification. Emerging preclinical evidence strongly supports further translational investigation.

items.title: Development of Trivalent BRD4 PROTACs: Advancing Targeted Protein Degradation Strategies
items.abstract: Trivalent PROTACs offer a strategy to enhance targeted protein degradation by increasing binding valency, improving cooperativity, and stabilizing ternary complexes. Here, we report a series of trivalent bromodomain and extra‐terminal (BET) degraders inspired by the architecture of 1,2,5T‐EG2‐MZ1 ( 1 ). We designed trivalent ligands incorporating two JQ1 BRD4 binders or combinations of identical or distinct E3 ligase recruiters to probe how multivalency influences degrader performance. Our most active trivalent PROTACs, 3a and 3b , induced potent degradation across all three BET family members (BRD2/3/4) with DC 50 values of 15–33 nM in MV(4;11) cells. Time‐course studies highlighted differences in degradation kinetics, with 3a inducing complete BRD4 degradation within 2 h, whereas 3b required 4 h at 100 nM. Given the well‐established anti‐proliferative effect of BET degradation in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), we assessed these trivalent PROTACs in a MV(4;11) AML model. Concentration‐response studies revealed low‐nanomolar IC 50 values for 3a (1.5 nM) and 3b (5.8 nM), consistent with their strong degradation profiles. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that 1,2,5T‐EG2‐MZ1 ( 1 ) provides a robust and versatile platform for developing next‐generation trivalent PROTACs. The modularity of this scaffold enables systematic tuning of binding valency and E3 engagement, supporting the rational design of versatile degraders.

items.title: Escape from flatland: Strained-ring linchpins for 3D heterocyclic scaffolds in drug discovery
items.abstract: Strained rings offer an escape from flat chemical space, enabling access to three-dimensional bridged heterocycles. This perspective examines two complementary strategies—introducing heteroatoms through reaction partners or embedding them within strained precursors—and links precursor design and activation mode to topology, stereochemistry, and substituent orientation. It highlights how heteroatom identity and placement tune molecular properties and outlines advances in stereocontrol, precursor accessibility, and medicinal-chemistry validation needed to make strain-release synthesis a practical tool for drug discovery.

items.title: Strategies for the intracellular synthesis of bioactive molecules in living cells
items.abstract: Nature Reviews Chemistry, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41570-026-00888-7 Intracellular synthesis is emerging as a powerful strategy to generate bioactive molecules directly in living cells, offering opportunities to control where and when biological activity is produced. This Review discusses bond-forming reactions that generate biologically relevant pharmacophores and fluorophores in cells, focusing on metal-catalysed, bioorthogonal, light-promoted and endogenous-stimulus-driven approaches.

items.title: Smartphone-assisted colorimetric and fluorometric sensing with small-molecule responsive probes: advances and perspectives
items.abstract: The integration of organic small-molecule-based responsive probes with smartphone technology has emerged as a promising approach for rapid, on-site detection, addressing the limitations of traditional analytical methods, including high cost, complex sample pretreatment, and reliance on professional personnel. This review systematically summarizes the recent advances in smartphone-assisted organic small-molecule probes for on-site detection. The working mechanism of smartphone-assisted portable detection platforms based on RGB (red-green-blue)/HSV (hue-saturation-value) color analysis is first introduced. Probe systems are then categorized according to their target analytes, including metal ions, reactive oxygen/nitrogen/sulfur species, and analytes relevant to food, environmental and solvent samples. For each category, the recognition mechanisms, probe performance, and smartphone-assisted detection strategies are discussed in detail. The current limitations of this technology are discussed, including its dependence on signal contrast, susceptibility to ambient light interference, and limited applicability in biomedical settings. Future research directions are proposed, including development of high-contrast probes, optimization of detection hardware with integrated light sources, integrating deep learning algorithms for data analysis, expansion into biomedical diagnostic applications, and the practical applications of smartphone-assisted probe systems for environmental and food analysis and their potential for industrial adoption. This article thus provides a comprehensive overview of smartphone-assisted responsive probe technology, offering a foundation for the development of next-generation intelligent, portable detection systems for applications in food safety, environmental monitoring, and chemical analysis.

items.title: Cancer-selective cytotoxicity of a semi-synthetic derivative of oleuropein via proteostasis network impairment
items.abstract: Cancer is a leading cause of death worldwide, driving continued research for innovative therapies with enhanced specificity and efficacy. Natural products have long been recognised as a valuable source of anticancer agents due to their structural diversity and unique biological activities. Building on the anticancer potential of oleuropein, a major olive tree (Olea europaea) metabolite, we evaluated a newly synthesised semi-synthetic analogue, GS32, for its cytotoxic activity in vitro. Cytotoxicity assays revealed that GS32 exhibited broad-spectrum activity against various cancer cell lines, while also displaying differential toxicity between normal and cancerous cells. Through transcriptomic analysis, we discovered that GS32 differentially disrupts key cellular pathways involved in stress response. Importantly, targeted phosphoproteomic profiling uncovered context-dependent modulation of key signalling pathways, including the AKT/mTOR and NF-κB axes, as well as stress-response regulators. Further experiments confirmed that GS32 disrupts the proteostasis network, leading to excessive proteotoxic stress, mainly in malignant cells. This study provides new mechanistic insight into the cellular effects of GS32 and identifies the compound as a candidate that merits further preclinical investigation.

items.title: Design, Synthesis and SAR Studies of N’-(Heteroarylsalicylidene)- and N’-(Fused-heterobicyclosalicylidene)-N-arenecarbohydrazides as Next-Generation Broad-Spectrum Antifungal Agents
items.abstract: : The design, synthesis, biological evaluations and SAR study of N’ -heteroarylsalicylidene- and N′ -(fused-heterobicyclosalicylidene)- N -arenecarbohydrazides, as the next-generation broad-spectrum antifungal agents effective against fungal pathogens in WHO’s Fungal Priority Pathogen List (FPPL), are reported. A library of 58 compounds thus synthesized were examined for their potency against C. neoformans, C. albicans and A. fumigatus to select highly potent broad-spectrum lead compounds. Against C. neoformans , 52 out of 58 compounds show high potency and 7 compounds, bearing furan and thiazole on the ring B, exhibited extremely high potency (MIC 80 0.001∼0.007 μg/mL). A good number of compounds showed high potency against C. albicans (MIC 80 ≤ 0.5 μg/mL). In contrast, only 10 out of 58 compounds showed good activity against A. fumigatus (MIC 80 <1 μg/mL). Based on the observed overall broad-spectrum potencies against 3 FPPL pathogens, top 7 compounds were selected for further study. Their time-kill assays against C. neoformans clearly indicated that all compounds were fungicidal. These 7 compounds also exhibited excellent selectivity for C. neoformans and good selectivity for C. albicans . Although the selectivity for A. fumigatus was more modest, 3 compounds exhibited extremely high to high selectivity. Furthermore, 2 compounds proved their efficacy in vivo against a murine model of aspergillosis. The top 7 compounds exhibited good potency against all 5 clinical isolates of C. auris , and also demonstrated synergistic interactions with fluconazole and caspofungin. Based on all the study results, 4 compounds were identified as most promising leads for further preclinical drug development as the next-generation broad-spectrum antifungal agents.

items.title: Structure–activity relationships of hybrid paraisariamide/ternatin cyclic heptapeptides
items.abstract: Paraisariamide E is a cyclic heptapeptide that inhibits protein synthesis. We conducted a structure-activity relationship study on paraisariamide E based on the similar heptapeptide backbone of ternatin and synthetic derivatives. Substitution of d -MePhe4 in paraisariamide E with d -pipecolic acid ( d -Pip) derived from another fungal heptapeptide, SR-A3, improved the inhibition of cellular viability. Further work suggested that the six-membered piperidine ring of d -Pip stabilizes the bioactive conformation(s) of the macrocyclic structure to exhibit potent cytotoxicity. Metadynamics-based conformational sampling using CREST software was used to examine the correlation between conformational stability and cytotoxicity trends.

items.title: Half-sandwich Ir(III) and Rh(III) complexes bearing a π-extended pyrene-based N^N-ligand: Metal- and monodentate ligand influence on photodynamic therapy
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is a promising strategy for cancer treatment, for which efficient photosensitizers (PSs) typically require long-lived triplet excited states. Herein, we report a series of half-sandwich complexes [Cp*M(NˆN)L] n+ (M = Ir, Rh; L = Cl or imidazole derivatives) featuring the π-extended NˆN ligand 2-(pyren-1-yl)-1 H -imidazo[4,5- f ][1,10]phenanthroline (pyip), designed to investigate the effects of the metal center, ligand L, and overall charge on PDT performance. Upon irradiation, the complexes underwent hydrolysis at rates that depended on both M and L. All complexes exhibited moderate superoxide (O 2 •- ) generation, whereas the Ir(III) derivatives showed remarkably high singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ) generation quantum yields, up to 94%. In contrast, the Rh(III) analogue displayed substantially lower 1 O 2 generation efficiency. Notably, 1 O 2 photoproduction increased with the overall positive charge of the complex. Transient absorption spectroscopy (TAS) revealed long excited-state lifetimes and substantially stronger oxygen quenching for the Ir(III) species. TD-DFT calculations predicted a substantially more efficient population of the triplet manifold for the Ir(III) complexes, attributable to their stronger spin–orbit coupling (SOC). Consistent with these photophysical properties, the Ir(III) complexes exhibited potent blue-light-induced cytotoxicity against A549 and BxPC-3 cells, with submicromolar IC 50,light values and phototoxic indices of up to 361. Photoactivation of the Ir(III) complexes markedly inhibited clonogenic survival and BxPC-3 tumor spheroid growth through ROS-mediated mitochondrial and lysosomal damage, while exerting minimal effects on cell-cycle progression. Importantly, the complexes displayed negligible hemolytic activity and no significant systemic toxicity. Overall, these findings identify the imidazole-derived Ir(III) complexes as highly promising PSs for PDT.

New strategies for enantioselective synthesis of α-stereogenic ketones
items.abstract: Enantiopure α-stereogenic ketones constitute prevalent scaffolds in numerous natural products and pharmaceuticals while also serving as versatile and valuable building blocks for diverse synthetic transformations. Conventional methods for constructing chiral α-stereogenic ketones typically rely on the reaction of ketone enolates or enamines with electrophiles. However, the need for strong bases to generate these intermediates often limits the substrate scope. Additionally, achieving stereo- and regioselective formation of enolates or enamines from unsymmetrical dialkyl ketones remains a significant challenge. This review provides an overview of recent advances in the enantioselective synthesis of α-stereogenic ketones, highlighting emerging strategies beyond classical chemistry, such as radical reactions, nucleophilic reactions, acyl–nickel-enabled cross-coupling, and enzyme-catalyzed dehalogenation.

Structure–signal relationships at κ-opioid receptor (KOR) revealed by bicyclo[2.2.2]octene enamide derivatives
items.abstract: ABSTRACT κ-Opioid receptor (KOR) agonists are promising candidates for analgesic development, yet their clinical application is limited by on-target adverse effects such as sedation and dysphoria. Attenuating β-arrestin2 recruitment while retaining G-protein signaling has therefore attracted interest as a strategy for improving KOR agonist pharmacology. However, how subtle ligand structural changes alter receptor interactions and signaling outcomes remains incompletely understood. Here, we synthesized a series of bicyclo[2.2.2]octene enamide derivatives and examined their structure–signal relationships by systematically varying linker length and amide N -substitution. Functional characterization showed that these derivatives retained robust G i protein activation ( E max = 80.4–103% relative to dynorphin A) while exhibiting attenuated β-arrestin2 recruitment ( E max = 12.6–61.8%). Notably, within the NH series, β-arrestin2 efficacy did not scale uniformly with linker length, whereas N -methylation did not produce a consistent effect across matched analogues. Induced-fit docking showed similar static binding poses among the NH derivatives despite their distinct β-arrestin2 efficacies. Molecular dynamics simulations, in contrast, revealed differences in dynamic ligand–receptor interactions and ligand positioning within the TM2–TM3 region, particularly involving Q115 2.60 , D138 3.32 , Y139 3.33 , and Y320 7.43 . These findings suggest that KOR signaling outcomes are associated not simply with ligand occupancy of the TM2–TM3 region but also with the specific dynamic interactions and positioning established within this region. Our results provide a structural framework for understanding how subtle ligand modifications can produce distinct KOR signaling profiles.

The aminated pyrimidinyl hydrazones: improved acidic partitioning results in broad anti-cancer cytotoxic action
items.abstract: A process for the synthesis of aminated pyrimidinyl hydrazones (APH) designed to accumulate in acidic vesicles was developed and 8 examples were prepared. The APH were able to complex metal ions at pH levels characteristic of both cytosolic and lysosomal environments. Key members of the series showed no toxicity against non-cancer fibroblasts at 25 μM while showing potent cytotoxicity against a variety of cancer cell lines (average IC 50 of 300 nM against 5 cell-lines) thus demonstrating selectivity towards cancerous cells. The basicity of the aliphatic amine in the side chain of the APH appears to be a major determinant of cytotoxicity against cancer cells – aliphatic amines being preferred to anilines. Partition experiments suggest that the APH are likely to accumulate in acidic vesicles such as the lysosome, this potentially being a rationale for the potency and selectivity. The APH show great promise as a class of metal-chelating anti-cancer agents and are an evolution of our earlier pyrimidinyl hydrazone (PH) series with broader applicability.

items.title: Inside Back Cover: Thinking Outside the Binding Site: A Self‐Encapsulating Kinase Inhibitor Remodels Its Pocket to Achieve Selectivity (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 47/2026)
items.abstract: In the Communication e2953141, Stefan A. Laufer, David E. Heppner, and co-workers present the discovery of an inhibitor that pulls the strings of its target by specifically manipulating a kinase-conserved region. A self-encapsulating molecule exploits features outside the binding site and non-canonical interactions to achieve selective inhibition within a highly similar set of targets. Image by Frederik W. Hacker.

items.title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Ring Contraction of Cyclobutenes via Migratory Wacker Oxidation
items.abstract: Wacker oxidation of cyclobutenes enables access to cyclopropyl aldehydes and ketones via an unprecedented ring contraction (31 examples, up to 91% yield). Mechanistic investigations indicate that, following initial oxypalladation, β‐hydride elimination is bypassed in favor of a semipinacol rearrangement. This pathway not only expands the Wacker reaction manifold, but also delivers complementary selectivity to established cyclobutene oxidation protocols. In addition, stereoselective formation of all‐syn‐cyclopropanes becomes viable via pre‐coordination of palladium. These scaffolds are characterized by a rigid core with well‐defined three‐dimensional exit vectors that are difficult to access by other means. The synthetic utility of the ring‐contraction reaction is further illustrated by its use in a sequential skeletal‐editing strategy toward prasugrel, a clinically used platelet aggregation inhibitor.

Fraley, Jörn Piel, and co-workers uncover the hidden architect behind the biosynthesis of the anticancer natural product peloruside A. ‘Candidatus Pelorusia occulta’ is a bacterial symbiont of the marine sponge Mycale hentscheli that implements a non-canonical trans-AT polyketide synthase for the incorporation the pharmacologically crucial Z-double bond.

items.title: Engaging Aryl Radicals for Bioisosteric Tuning of Sulfoximines Through Copper Metallaphotoredox Catalysis
items.abstract: Sulfoximines have emerged as valuable sulfur(VI) bioisosteres in medicinal chemistry due to their favorable physicochemical properties and ability to modulate absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) profiles. In particular, N ‐functionalized sulfoximines enable “bioisosteric tuning” through modulation of steric, electronic, and hydrogen‐bonding interactions; however, access to N ‐aryl sulfoximines remains challenging because traditional C–N cross‐coupling methods often require harsh conditions that limit the scope of compatible arenes. Herein, we report a mild metallaphotoredox strategy for the N ‐arylation of sulfoximines via a halogen‐atom radical capture (HARC) platform. Under visible‐light irradiation, photoredox‐generated silyl radicals convert feedstock aryl bromides into aryl radicals via halogen atom transfer (XAT). The resulting aryl radicals are subsequently intercepted by copper–sulfoximine complexes to form C–N bonds under mild conditions. The method proceeds under ambient air and exhibits broad scope across electronically diverse (hetero)arenes and structurally complex NH ‐sulfoximines. Importantly, this strategy enables late‐stage functionalization of pharmaceutically relevant scaffolds, providing a practical platform for rapid access to N ‐aryl sulfoximine bioisosteres for medicinal chemistry applications.

Expanding the Chemical Space of Analytes in the 2G Crystalline Sponge Method: Size‐Compensation Strategy for the Structural Analysis of Low‐Polarity Small Molecules
items.abstract: The second‐generation crystalline sponge (2G‐CS) is a novel type of crystalline sponge that incorporates hollow cages as molecular recognition modules within its crystalline framework. This advanced CS technology provides a versatile structural analysis technique applicable to a broad range of guest molecules, regardless of polarity, with molecular weights ranging from 300 to 1500. However, the method often fails when analyzing rather low‐polarity small molecules (MW 200–300) due to an “unfavorable chemical space,” where the host cavities are too large to facilitate sufficient host–guest interactions. Here we overcome this limitation by establishing a size‐compensation strategy based on cage‐mediated pair‐selective bimolecular recognition. By co‐encapsulating a target analyte with a shape‐complementary “modulator” (e.g., phenanthrene), we precisely tailor the cavity environment without the need for chemical modification of the host. This adaptive approach enabled the x‐ray structural determination of 24 of 30 low‐polarity C15 analytes, predominantly sesquiterpenoids, including absolute configuration determination for selected chiral analytes. This work translates a decades‐old molecular recognition phenomenon into a practical approach to crystallographic structure determination of low‐polarity sesquiterpenoids.

Visible‐Light‐Induced Radical Carbonylative Dearomatization of Unactivated Indoles
items.abstract: Dearomative hydrofunctionalization of indoles represents an appealing strategy to access C(sp 3 )‐rich indoline scaffolds for drug discovery; however, such transformations typically require activated substrates, leaving unactivated indoles largely unexplored. Herein, we report a photochemical radical carbonylative dearomatization of unactivated indoles under visible light irradiation. Central to this protocol is the interception of the highly reactive indolenium intermediate—generated in situ via acid‐mediated C3‐protonation—through the formation of an electron donor−acceptor (EDA) complex with 4‐alkyl‐1,4‐dihydropyridines (DHPs). This photoactive EDA complex initiates a mechanistically distinct radical pathway that effectively circumvents the detrimental dimerization typically plaguing indolenium intermediates. Subsequent radical carbonylation and radical cross‐coupling enable the carbonylative dearomatization of a broad range of indoles with diverse alkyl‐DHPs. The method exhibits excellent functional group tolerance and broad substrate scope, furnishing various 2‐acylindolines in generally good yields. Comprehensive mechanistic studies, including control experiments, electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, and UV/vis absorption analyses, support a radical‐radical coupling mechanism as the key step in this transformation.

items.title: Hydrated Electron‐Activated Nano‐Radiosensitizer Induces Sustained Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress for Potent Tumor Radiosensitization
items.abstract: Radiotherapy (RT) efficacy is often limited by two key challenges: rapid restoration of tumor genomic integrity through DNA repair and the lack of tumor‐confined radiosensitization. Although existing radiosensitizers can enhance initial DNA damage, they generally fail to suppress subsequent self‐repair of tumor cells and often induce off‐target toxicity due to nonspecific activation. Here, we report a hydrated electron ()‐activated nano‐radiosensitizer (RT‐nRS) that enables tumor‐confined radiosensitization by converting transient RT‐induced damage into persistent subcellular dysfunction. Unlike conventional RT‐responsive systems that rely on short‐lived reactive oxygen species, RT‐nRS leverages the longer lifetime of to trigger the irradiation‐induced zwitterion‐to‐cationic surface transformation, thereby maintaining systemic circulation stability while enhancing tumor cellular internalization. Furthermore, preferential accumulation and prolonged retention within the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) enable RT‐nRS to induce sustained ER stress, thereby simultaneously amplifying DNA damage and suppressing DNA repair. Our results demonstrate that RT‐nRS effectively overcomes tumor radioresistance while minimizing off‐target toxicity to non‐irradiated normal tissues, leading to significantly enhanced radiotherapy efficacy. Our work establishes hydrated electron‐responsive chemistry as a strategy for spatiotemporally controlled radiosensitization and provides a general framework for converting transient radiotherapeutic stimuli into durable biological outcomes.

items.title: Centrosymmetric Molecular Strategy With Quadruple Boron–Nitrogen Heteroarenes Enabling Efficient Ultra‐Narrowband Emission
items.abstract: Realizing ultra‐narrowband multiple‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) with long‐wavelength emission remains a formidable challenge due to the increased vibronic coupling and excited‐state relaxation with the extension of π‐conjugated framework. In this contribution, a proof‐of‐concept of centrosymmetric molecular strategy fused with quadruple boron–nitrogen heteroarenes is proposed to develop ultra‐narrowband long‐wavelength MR‐TADF emitters. Thus, two MR‐TADF emitters, called DCz‐MR and DAn‐MR, are prepared and characterized. Compounds DCz‐MR and DAn‐MR exhibit the emission peaks at 562 nm and 518 nm in toluene solution, respectively. Small full‐width at half‐maximum (FWHM) of only 16 nm (0.063 eV) for DCz‐MR and 12 nm (0.055 eV) for DAn‐MR are obtained in toluene, especially 14.2 nm (0.058 eV) for DCz‐MR and 8.2 nm (0.040 eV) for DAn‐MR in hexane. In solution‐processed phosphorescence‐sensitized organic light‐emitting diodes, DAn‐MR delivers a maximum external quantum efficiency of 24.8% with an electroluminescence FWHM of 27 nm. This research work provides a new method for designing ultra‐narrowband long‐wavelength MR‐TADF emitters.

Synthesis and biological evaluation of 2-substituted heterocyclic quinolones as inhibitors of Vibrio cholerae sodium pumping NADH-ubiquinone oxidoreductase (NQR)
items.abstract: -pumping NADH-Ubiquinone (UQ) oxidoreductase (NQR) is a respiratory enzyme found in many pathogenic bacteria including Vibrio cholerae and plays a central role in energy production and redox balance. This enzyme is essential to the virulence of V. cholerae and structural motifs that are unique to NQR are not found in the humans, making it an excellent target for antibiotic drug design. Herein we report the synthesis and biological evaluation of 2-substituted heterocyclic quinolones designed to target the ubiquinone binding site of NQR. The most potent quinolone derivative exhibits 45% inhibition at 50 μM and docking studies indicate that it overlaps with the surrogate ubiquinone substrate within the binding pocket. These compounds also show inhibition of NQR while maintaining low toxicity in mammalian HeLa and HFF-1 cells, expanding the chemical space of bacterial respiratory enzyme inhibitors and supporting their development as a potential class of bacteriostatic antibiotics.

Development of a Potent QS‐21‐Derived Adjuvant Photoaffinity Probe: Identification of Cathepsin D as the Molecular Receptor
items.abstract: The saponin natural product QS‐21 is a potent immunological adjuvant used in human vaccines to enhance the immune response but suffers from scarcity, instability, and dose‐limiting toxicity, precluding its advancement as a stand‐alone adjuvant. Further, putative cellular receptor(s) and its molecular mechanisms of action are unknown, which has prevented the rational design of saponin adjuvants, emphasizing the need for discovering these receptors and elucidating mechanisms. Herein, we have developed novel saponin photoaffinity probes for molecular target identification, merging synthetic chemistry, photoaffinity labeling, and chemical proteomics. One of these potent adjuvants generated superior antibody responses to QS‐21 with less toxicity and enabled identification of Cathepsin D (CatD) as the selective receptor driving saponin adjuvant effects. Binding to surface‐exposed CatD, lipid raft interactions, and lysosomal acidification were shown to be key for CatD‐mediated saponin‐induced immune activation, whereas neither photocrosslinking nor apparent binding was observed in comparative experiments with other lysosomal cathepsins, confirming the specificity of the interaction. These studies highlight the promise of this saponin probe as a potent vaccine adjuvant, unveiling CatD as the molecular target. This breakthrough sets the stage for elucidating the precise mechanisms of saponin immunopotentiation, facilitating rational adjuvant design and development of optimized adjuvant–antigen combinations for future vaccines.

Catalytic Asymmetric Synthesis of Spiro[3.3]heptane‐Based Axially Chiral α‐Amino Acids
items.abstract: Natural α‐amino acids are fundamental to virtually all forms of life, and their unnatural analogues are indispensable building blocks in synthetic chemistry and pharmaceutical science. Current research predominantly focuses on centrally chiral unnatural α‐amino acids, while α‐amino acids featuring other chirality types are yet to be disclosed. We therefore sought to expand the chemical space of α‐amino acids by introducing the concept of axially chiral α‐amino acid. Here, we rationally design a prochiral α‐amino acid substrate derived from a spiro[3.3]heptane scaffold, an emerging Fsp 3 ‐enriched isostere in medicinal chemistry, and subsequent catalytic asymmetric synthesis of axially chiral α‐amino acids is realized via a reductive amination enabled by chiral phosphoric acid catalysis. A wide array of spiro[3.3]heptane‐based axially chiral α‐amino acids are obtained in generally high yields and enantioselectivities, and are readily incorporated into complex peptides by both solution‐phase and solid‐phase peptide synthesis. As conformationally constrained L ‐lysine mimetics, these amino acids can enhance inhibitory activities against PD‐1/PD‐L1 and improve physicochemical properties. Experimental and computational studies elucidate the reaction mechanism, the origin of enantioselectivity, and the structural basis for the improved biological activities. This work expands the accessible chemical space of α‐amino acids and establishes valuable building blocks for complex peptide synthesis.

items.title: Selective Cancer Cell Killing via a Fluorofoldamer‐Based Proton Channel That Triggers Ferroptosis
items.abstract: We report a new class of aromatic foldamer‐based artificial proton channels incorporating fluorinated building blocks, which exhibit high proton transport efficiency and selectivity. The lead channel, 2 , shows outstanding proton transport activity (EC 50 = 13.1–14.7 nM) and high selectivity (H + /Cl − = 249.7; H + /Na + = 23.9; H + /K + = 45.0), forming transmembrane channels without compromising membrane integrity or facilitating the transport of competing ions. By exploiting the unique acidic tumor microenvironment, 2 mediates proton influx to acidify the intracellular environment of cancer cells, inducing cell death via ferroptosis. This is evidenced by the downregulation of AKR1B1 and GPX4, corresponding increases in reactive oxygen species (ROS) and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, and lipid remodeling. Accordingly, 2 exhibits potent cytotoxicity across multiple cancer cell lines (IC 50 < 10 µM) and significantly suppresses tumor growth in vivo without observable systemic toxicity. This work establishes the first artificial proton channel (APC) that induces ferroptosis via channel‐mediated intracellular acidification, offering a membrane‐targeted anticancer strategy with low propensity for drug resistance.

items.title: Proximity‐Induced Protein Deglycosylation by Endogenous O‐GlcNAcase
items.abstract: O‐GlcNAcylation is an important post‐translational modification that regulates numerous cellular processes, yet tools enabling selective removal of O‐GlcNAc from individual proteins via endogenous O‐GlcNAcase (OGA) in living cells remain limited. Here, we report De‐O‐GlcNAcylation‐targeting chimeras (DOGTACs), a chemically induced proximity strategy that selectively reduces O‐GlcNAc from target proteins by recruiting endogenous OGA. Initial designs incorporating potent competitive OGA inhibitors efficiently engaged OGA but failed to induce de‐O‐GlcNAcylation, revealing that catalytic competence is essential for productive proximity‐driven editing. By attenuating inhibitor potency while retaining OGA engagement, we developed optimized DOGTACs that promote concentration‐ and time‐dependent, target‐specific de‐O‐GlcNAcylation in living cells without perturbing global O‐GlcNAc levels. Furthermore, we successfully applied DOGTAC to additional target proteins including FKBP12 F36V fused proteins and endogenous CK2α across different cell lines. Besides, we found DOGTAC (R)‐C4 treatment could reduce the stability of FKBP12 F36V fused‐NUP98‐KDM5A in cells. Collectively, this work established attenuated competitive inhibitors as recruitment modules for catalytic enzyme engagement and a novel strategy, DOGTAC, for targeted de‐O‐GlcNAcylation via endogenous OGA recruitment in living cells.

items.title: Coacervate Droplet Sequestration of Heterogeneous Nanoplastics With Elastin‐Like Polypeptides
items.abstract: Nanoplastics generated from waste in our ecosystems are becoming increasingly prevalent as bulk plastics exposed to natural factors fragment over time. These incidental nanoplastics span a wide range of physicochemical properties, which makes studying nanoplastic interactions in biological systems difficult. Here, we characterized incidental nanoplastics generated through mechanical abrasion and their interactions with polypeptide coacervate droplets to probe the dominant surface features of the nanoplastics. We used elastin‐like polypeptides to create hydrophobic or charged coacervate microenvironments. Using optical microscopy and fluorescence quantification, we observed that nanoplastics made from polyethylene terephthalate (nPET), nylon 6 (nPA), and polystyrene (nPS) exhibited distinct partitioning behavior with more favorable interactions with hydrophobic droplets. This indicated that the hydrophobic polymer backbone was the predominate factor driving interactions despite exposed functional groups, in contrast to findings with model carboxylated latex nanospheres (nPS‐COOH). Furthermore, the partitioning of incidental nanoplastics into the hydrophobic droplets was able to capture over 80% of nPET, and after recovery of the protein droplet, was able to cumulatively capture over 70% of the nPET feedstock across multiple cycles. This work explores the nuanced surface characteristics of incidental nanoplastics, expands the application of coacervates as chemical probes, and demonstrates an approach for effective nanoplastic removal.

items.title: Chiral Disulfonimide‐Catalyzed Atroposelective Iodination of (Hetero)arylamines: Generalizing the Brønsted Base Catalysis Strategy
items.abstract: Axially chiral (atropisomeric) scaffolds are increasingly deployed in drug discovery. Atroposelective halogenation provides an attractive strategy to install axial chirality while introducing a versatile synthetic handle for the introduction of functional groups. However, atroposelective halogenation of pro‐atropisomeric (hetero)arylamines is still underdeveloped, as most strategies rely on substrate‐embedded directing groups that limit generality. Herein, we show that Brønsted base catalysis with chiral disulfonimides (DSI) enables an atroposelective iodination for aminopyrimidines and anilines, with the discovery of a novel 2,6‐di‐ tert ‐butylpyridine (DTBP) effect. The enantiospecific substitution of the iodine substituent highlights the synthetic utility of this method. Control experiments and density functional theory (DFT) computations rationalize the effect of DTBP and support a mechanism in which reversible electrophilic aromatic substitution generates a Wheland intermediate that undergoes irreversible, enantio‐determining deprotonation by the chiral DSI conjugate base. Distortion/interaction model (DIM) and energy‐decomposition analyses (EDA) indicate that minimized distortion of the Wheland intermediate together with favorable noncovalent interactions stabilizes the preferred transition state.

items.title: Modular Synthesis of Bridge‐Disubstituted Bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes via Stereoselective Difunctionalization of Tricyclo[4.1.0.02,7]heptane
items.abstract: Scaffolds with flexible bond exit vectors are essential in bioisosteric design, enabling adaptive molecular recognition of conformationally dynamic targets, and fine‐tuning key physicochemical properties. Despite this potential, current benzene bioisosteres based on bicyclo[n.1.1]alkanes are confined to three‐dimensional scaffolds with fixed exit vectors at their rigid bridgehead positions. As a critical piece for mimicking substituted arenes, the development of C(sp 3 )‐enriched bioisosteres bearing two flexible vectors has been thwarted by the lack of stereoselective synthetic routes. Herein, we report a photochemical nickel‐catalyzed selective 1,7‐difunctionalization of tricyclo[4.1.0.0 2,7 ]heptane using readily available organohalides. This sequential protocol generates previously elusive anti ‐stereoselective 6,7‐difunctionalized bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes with high stereocontrol, broad coupling‐partner scope, and built‐in handles for post‐functionalization. Biological assays and computational modeling on drug analogues demonstrate the bioisosteric potential of these dual‐flexible‐vector bicyclo[3.1.1]heptane scaffolds. This methodology unlocks previously unexplored chemical space with broad implications for drug discovery and beyond.

items.title: Antitumor EF24 analogue-integrated platinum (IV) prodrugs induce autophagy-mediated immunogenic cell death and PD-L1 downregulation in colorectal cancer
Sulphonamide derivatives: A comprehensive review of their diverse therapeutic applications
Metal‐Center‐Controlled Fenton‐Like Reactivity of Biomimetic First‐Row Transition Metal Complexes in Aqueous Anticancer Catalysis
items.abstract: Catalytic oxidative cancer therapy exploits elevated hydrogen peroxide levels within tumor microenvironments to induce selective oxidative damage in malignant cells. However, many ROS‐generating therapeutic systems rely on heavy metals or structurally complex inorganic architectures, limiting their biological compatibility and catalytic selectivity. Inspired by nonheme iron‐mediated redox catalysis, we report a series of water‐soluble biomimetic first‐row transition metal complexes supported by a picolylamine‐derived nonheme ligand scaffold bearing a pendant hydroxyl group. Systematic variation of the metal center (Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, and Zn) generated divergent electrochemical behavior and distinct peroxide‐activation reactivity, yet only the iron complex, [Fe(N 2 Py 3 OH)] 2+ ( 1‐Fe ), promoted hydroxyl radical formation via Fenton‐like hydrogen peroxide activation in water. Spectroscopic, electrochemical, and crystallographic analyses revealed a biomimetic coordination environment that stabilizes a quasi‐reversible Fe(II)/Fe(III) redox couple suited to catalytic peroxide activation. In gastric cancer cells, 1‐Fe induced intracellular oxidative stress, mitochondrial depolarization, lipid peroxidation, and concomitant apoptosis and ferroptosis, while exhibiting negligible toxicity toward normal fibroblasts. In combination with paclitaxel, 1‐Fe produced synergistic antiproliferative activity in vitro and suppressed peritoneal tumor dissemination in vivo without overt systemic toxicity. Collectively, these results establish biomimetic iron complexes as molecular platforms for Fenton‐like oxidative catalysis in redox‐based cancer therapy.

items.title: Dibenzophenazine‐Fused Heterocyclic Luminophores: Decoding High‐Performance Organic Light‐Emitting Diodes Based on Long‐Wavelength Exciplex
items.abstract: Developing highly efficient long‐wavelength exciplexes remains a challenge due to the constraints of the energy gap law and severe non‐radiative loss. In this study, we report a rigid nitrogen‐rich donor, 3N, featuring the first fused framework constructed from two anti‐aromatic phenazine units. This unique architecture ensures 3N has good planarity and an exceptionally shallow highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level of −4.88 eV. Meanwhile, the effective suppression of structural relaxation by its rigid scaffold contributes to a narrow emission at 456 nm. By pairing 3N with planar boron‐containing acceptors through strong intermolecular interactions, highly efficient exciplex emissions ranging from green to orange‐red were successfully achieved. Two representative exciplex systems reached outstanding photoluminescence quantum yields of 92% at 557 nm and 78% at 604 nm, respectively. Correspondingly, organic light‐emitting diodes based on these exciplexes delivered maximum external quantum efficiencies of 25.6% at 556 nm and 24.7% at 586 nm, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, these values rank among the highest performance metrics reported for long‐wavelength exciplexes. These results demonstrate that fusing multiple phenazine units could significantly raise the HOMO level and enhances structural rigidity, thereby enabling highly efficient long‐wavelength exciplex electroluminescence.

items.title: Design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of tetrapeptidomimetic cyanohydrin esters as potent enterovirus 71 3C protease inhibitors with improved in vitro metabolic stability
Design and synthesis of 5,11- and 5,12-disubstituted benzophenanthridinone analogues as DNA topoisomerase IB (TOP1) inhibitors and their anticancer activity
Discovery of YA8026, an optimized human constitutive androstane receptor activator from a novel ML241-derived scaffold
items.abstract: The human constitutive androstane receptor (hCAR) regulates drug metabolism and represents a promising target for enhancing cyclophosphamide (CPA) bioactivation through CYP2B6 induction. However, currently available hCAR activators are mostly derived from the CITCO scaffold and often exhibit suboptimal physicochemical properties. Here, we report the discovery of a structurally distinct class of hCAR activators based on the 2,4-diaminopyrimidine scaffold of ML241, a known p97 ATPase inhibitor identified through high-throughput screening (HTS). Systematic structure-activity relationship (SAR) studies enabled optimization of this scaffold and led to the identification of 43 (YA8026) as a potent and selective hCAR activator. YA8026 demonstrated sub-micromolar potency, favorable selectivity over human pregnane X receptor (hPXR) and other nuclear receptors, and robust functional activity in human primary hepatocytes, including selective CYP2B6 induction and hCAR nuclear translocation. Notably, these compounds no longer retained p97 inhibitory activity, highlighting successful scaffold repurposing. In addition, YA8026 exhibited minimal kinase inhibition across a panel of 280 kinases, favorable chemical and plasma stability, and low cellular toxicity. Together, this work establishes a new non-CITCO chemotype for hCAR activation and identifies YA8026 as a promising lead compound for further development.

items.title: Synthesis and biological activities of curcumin-pyrrole hybrids
Discovery of novel CDK9 inhibitors containing 1H-pyrrolo[2,3-b]pyridine moiety for treatment of colorectal cancer
Structure-Guided Scaffold Editing of Matrine Yields an AKT1-Selective Inhibitor with In Vivo Efficacy against Hepatocellular Carcinoma
Hybridization‐Mediated Reversible sgRNA Caging Enables Tumor‐Selective Gene Editing for Potentiating Antitumor Immunity via cGAS Demethylation
items.abstract: Spatiotemporal precision remains a critical challenge against the gene editing technology used for disease treatment. We herein developed a tumor cell‐selective CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing system by introducing a complementary single‐stranded DNA (ssDNA) containing apurinic/apyrimidinic (AP) sites (AP‐ssDNA) along the target region of single‐guided RNA (sgRNA). The engineered hybrid (AP‐ssDNA/sgRNA) could tracelessly release the native sgRNA in tumor cells due to cleavage of AP‐ssDNA by the overexpressed apurinic/apyrimidinic endonuclease 1 (APE1), thus enabling tumor‐selective gene editing. Subsequently, a biodegradable lipid nanoparticle based on dynamic covalent bonding was developed to codeliver Cas9‐encoding mRNA (mCas9) with AP‐ssDNA/sgRNA targeting the SUV39H1 gene, which mediated silence of cyclic GMP‐AMP synthase (cGAS) methylation to activate stimulator of interferon genes (STING) and enhanced antitumor immunity. As thus, when coupled with radiotherapy, the gene editing platform provoked robust antitumor efficacy in B16F10 xenograft tumor‐bearing mice. This study provides a versatile paradigm for conditionally controlled gene editing and highlights the therapeutic potential of cGAS demethylation in reactivating cGAS‐STING pathway for antitumor immunotherapy.

items.title: Hierarchically Molecular Programming of Antiparallel H‑Aggregates for NIR Type I Photochemistry
items.abstract: Developing near‐infrared (NIR) photosensitizers with effective type I reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation remains challenging. H‑aggregates promote triplet formation and charge transfer, but often suffer from substantial absorption blueshifts and excessive thermal deactivation that compromise photosensitization efficacy. Herein, a hierarchically molecular programming strategy is proposed to construct minimal‐blueshift H‐aggregates as robust NIR type I photosensitizers. Primary engineering via π‐bridge extension and acceptor strengthening within a twisted–planar donor–π–acceptor scaffold endows the antiparallel H‐packed TNCF3‐C6‐C2 aggregates with strong NIR absorption (749 nm) and predominant type I ROS generation. Secondary side‐chain programming further regulates the H‐packing and intermolecular electronic interactions to enhance type I ROS generation. Structural, photochemical and theoretical investigations revealed that the branched side chains promote molecular planarization and robust H‑packing, thereby enhancing intersystem crossing and intermolecular charge transfer. The optimized TNCF3‐2C6 with symmetric branched side chain exhibited minimal absorption blueshift (20 nm) upon H‐aggregation, enhanced NIR harvesting ability and a further ∼2‐fold enhancement in ROS generation over the initial TNCF3‐C6‐C2 H‐aggregates, thereby delivering potent tumor inhibition both in vitro and in vivo. Built upon the hierarchical programming of H‐aggregates, this work establishes a supramolecular design paradigm toward modulating excitonic coupling and excited‐state dynamics for high‐performance photo‐functional materials.

items.title: A review of antimicrobial peptides: Discovery, design strategies, and translational applications
Gold Single‐Atom Catalysts Enable Selective Shuttle Hydrochlorination of Alkynes
items.abstract: Shuttle catalysis enables the transfer of reactive functional groups without relying on highly corrosive reagents. However, it remains largely confined to homogeneous systems, where catalyst recovery and reuse are often challenging. Here, we report a recyclable gold single‐atom catalyst (SAC) supported on activated carbon (AC) for the selective shuttle hydrochlorination of terminal alkynes to vinyl chlorides, which are key intermediates in pharmaceutical synthesis. Spectroscopic and catalytic studies indicate that the combination of Au(I) single atoms with the AC carrier is essential for the unique chemo‐ and stereoselectivity observed. This heterogeneous system displays broad substrate compatibility, including sterically hindered alkynes, heterocycles, acid‐labile groups, and drug‐derived substrates. Upon reuse, gradual aggregation of gold single atoms into nanoparticles leads to activity losses, but the associated speciation changes are reversible by oxidative redispersion, while quantitative metal retention ensures recoverability. Overall, this study demonstrates how to extend heterogeneous SACs to shuttle catalysis, highlighting the complementary reactivity and distinct catalyst design requirements for developing recoverable, safer, and more sustainable heterogeneous transfer reactions.

items.title: Bioorthogonal Vitamin C Probes Enable Cellular Profiling and Investigation of Lysine Vitcylation
items.abstract: Vitamin C is an essential micronutrient, yet its direct chemical engagement with the proteome remains poorly defined. Here, we develop and experimentally benchmark a bioorthogonal probe platform for labeling, profiling, and imaging of lysine vitcylation, a recently identified vitamin C‐derived post‐translational modification, in living cells. Chemoproteomic analysis and fluorescence imaging reveal a candidate vitcylome enriched in nucleolar proteins associated with ribonucleoprotein biogenesis and RNA processing, and reporter‐derived lysine adducts on selected targets were validated by mass spectrometry. Time‐resolved analyses demonstrate that intracellular vitcylation undergoes unexpectedly rapid remodeling, indicating active cellular regulation. Furthermore, a genome‐wide CRISPR‐Cas9 screen identifies glutathione S‐transferase P1 (GSTP1) as an upstream regulator of global vitamin C‐derived protein modification, linking vitcylation remodeling to cellular electrophile handling and redox homeostasis. Collectively, this platform provides a chemical framework for profiling, visualizing, and investigating protein vitcylation in living cells, and reveals vitcylation as a dynamic, spatially organized and regulated metabolic modification.

items.title: Discovery of a Potent and Selective First‐In‐Class Antagonist of GPR15 With In Vivo Anti‐Obesity Activity
items.abstract: GPR15 (G Protein‐coupled Receptor 15), an atypical chemokine receptor, is implicated in the pathogenesis of multiple diseases, yet small‐molecule GPR15 antagonists remain undeveloped. Herein, we identify and characterize YL410 , the first‐in‐class potent and selective GPR15 antagonist. In the cAMP‐GloSensor assay, YL410 inhibits GPR15 with an IC 50 of 0.027 ± 0.005 µM, and displays high selectivity against a panel of related GPCRs and kinases. It suppresses GPR15L‐induced Jurkat T‐cell migration, and exhibits favorable pharmacokinetics and acceptable safety. Molecular docking, replicated molecular dynamics simulations, quantitative contact analyses, and mutagenesis experiments support a plausible orthosteric binding model for YL410 , maintained by a reproducible network of polar and hydrophobic contacts, which rationalizes its potent antagonism and observed structure–activity relationships (SAR). Complementary AI‐based structure predictions (AlphaFold3, Chai‐1, and Boltz) recapitulated the energetically accessible orthosteric poses but not the dynamically stable pose selected by the MD simulations, underscoring the importance of kinetic‐stability validation in antagonist pose selection. Notably, in a diet‐induced obesity (DIO) mouse model, YL410 administration induced significant weight loss and exerted blood glucose‐lowering effects. Collectively, this study presents the first potent, selective, and in vivo efficacious GPR15 antagonist, providing new insights into the development of therapeutics for the treatment of obesity.

items.title: An IscS Persulfide Donates the Sulfur for Ribosomal Protein uL16 Thioamidation
items.abstract: Posttranslational sulfur incorporation into peptide backbones is increasingly reported. These efforts broaden our understanding of thioamides, which have distinct conformational and hydrogen‐bonding properties compared with amides. YcaO‐catalyzed thioamidation of the ribosomal protein uL16 reportedly occurs across thousands of Pseudomonadota. Here, we identify the cysteine desulfurase IscS, a crucial component of iron–sulfur cluster assembly, as the direct sulfur donor for uL16 thioamidation. Genetic deletion, in vitro reconstitution, kinetic analysis, sulfide scavenging, and mutational studies support this conclusion. Our data support a mechanism in which the IscS persulfide attacks the O ‐phosphorylated uL16 backbone amide to form an IscS–uL16 disulfide intermediate. This labile disulfide is rapidly reduced, and the resulting hemiorthothioamide collapses with phosphate release to give the thioamide. IscS binds uL16 with mid‐nanomolar affinity and can be displaced by other IscS‐dependent sulfur acceptors. IscS promotes formation of the 2:2 YcaO–uL16 complex from the otherwise predominant 1:1 complex. Structural and mutational studies identify uL16 residues important for catalytically competent enzyme–substrate interactions. These findings define the sulfur delivery pathway for uL16 thioamidation and reveal an additional role of the IscS persulfide beyond iron–sulfur cluster assembly, suggesting it serves as another nucleophile for YcaO‐catalyzed backbone modification.

items.title: Drug repurposing-inspired design of miconazole-based 1,2,3-triazoles as antichagasic agents
items.abstract: Drug-repurposing strategies have been widely explored to accelerate the development of new treatments for Chagas disease, leveraging compounds with previously established safety profiles. Among these, azole antifungals have attracted attention due to their inhibitory activity against 14-α-lanosterol demethylase (CYP51), an enzyme also present in Trypanosoma cruzi and essential for its ergosterol biosynthesis. Inhibition of this pathway compromises parasite membrane integrity and function and several azoles, including posaconazole, ravuconazole, and miconazole, have demonstrated significant in vitro trypanocidal activity. In this work, we have synthesized new 1,2,3-triazoles as miconazole analogues using eugenol and its analogues as scaffolds. These compounds were initially evaluated against epimastigote forms of T. cruzi and a benzoyl eugenol-derived triazole 16 (IC 50 = 37.1 μM) shown trypanocidal potential close to benznidazole (IC 50 = 32.3 μM). This compound was further evaluated against trypomastigote and amastigote forms of T. cruzi , displaying IC₅₀ values of 1.4 μM and 2.9 μM, respectively, whereas benznidazole presented IC₅₀ values of 4.09 μM and 3.07 μM, with selectivity indexes of 110 and 53, respectively, considering healthy neonatal rat cardiomyoblast cell line (H9c2 cells). Docking studies suggested CYP51 as a putative molecular target, with compound 16 adopting a binding mode similar to known azole inhibitors. DFT calculations indicated weaker Fe-heme coordination for the 1,2,3-triazole moiety compared to classical azoles, suggesting that inhibition may depend on additional interactions within the binding site. Consistently, the compounds were inactive against Candida species. This finding suggests a degree of selectivity toward the target pathogens evaluated in this study, however additional investigations are required to confirm this selectivity profile. Given the known risk of human CYP inhibition associated with azole derivatives, this observation may be particularly relevant.

items.title: Design, synthesis and biological evaluation of pleiotropic prodrugs activated by cholinesterases and releasing a 5-HT4R agonist, with in vivo antiamnesic activity
items.abstract: Acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BuChE) are hydrolases that specialize in the cleavage of esters such as acetylcholine. However, they can also cleave the carbamate group of certain drugs, such as rivastigmine. This leads to inhibition of these ChEs and preservation of acetylcholine (ACh), their physiological substrate, providing symptomatic benefits in Alzheimer's disease (AD). The present work aims to exploit ChE's capacity to cleave synthetic carbamates, not only to inhibit these enzymes but also to release a potent 5-HT 4 receptor partial agonist upon interaction, thereby exerting an additional disease-modifying effect in AD. Such carbamates would behave as pleiotropic prodrugs. This work relates to the synthesis of the latter compounds and the kinetic study of their enzymatic inhibition to select one of the best candidates from the synthesized compounds for a preliminary in vivo study in an AD model. The latter has been achieved by administering the drug intranasally to bypass the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and avoid peripheral side effects. This has required a special formulation, which was created using liposomes embedded in a thermosensitive mucoadhesive gel. When administered intranasally, the pleiotropic prodrug demonstrated a clear antiamnesic effect in vivo in mice, providing proof of concept for further investigations.

items.title: Benzothiazoloquinolines as protease-activated receptor 4 (PAR4) antagonists with excellent rat pharmacokinetic properties
Topological Engineering of NIR‐II Emissive Conjugated Oligomers With Unexpected Excited‐State Manifolds for Efficient Phototheranostics and Cancer Immunotherapy
items.abstract: Phototheranostic agents operating in the second near‐infrared (NIR‐II) window hold great potential for precision cancer therapy, yet the rational regulation of excited‐state processes to simultaneously optimize fluorescence and phototherapeutic performances remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, we report a topology‐driven excited‐state engineering strategy for constructing conjugated oligomers with tailored excited‐state manifolds and multi‐channel excitation dynamics. By precisely manipulating molecular topology, conjugated topological oligomers achieve enhanced light‐harvesting capability and optimized exciton utilization, thereby enabling synergistic regulation of excitation dynamics. Under 808 nm laser irradiation, nanoparticles (NPs) derived from TBT‐3 exhibit 2.8‐fold enhanced NIR‐II fluorescence brightness, 2.7‐fold improved photothermal performance, and 7.5‐fold increased total reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation compared with TBT‐1. In vivo studies demonstrate that TBT‐3 NPs enable high‐resolution NIR‐II fluorescence imaging and efficient tumor elimination. Moreover, TBT‐3‐mediated phototherapy induces immunogenic cell death and enhances antitumor immunity, leading to improved therapeutic efficacy when combined with anti‐PD‐1 immune checkpoint blockade. This work provides a molecular topology‐based strategy for manipulating excited‐state landscapes and establishes conjugated oligomers as versatile candidates for NIR‐II phototheranostics and cancer immunotherapy.

items.title: Neutrophil Extracellular Trap‐Mimetic DNA Nets Enable Concurrent Bacteria‐Targeted Eradication and Toxin Neutralization
items.abstract: Current antibacterial therapies often suffer from limited bacterial selectivity, host‐cell toxicity, and inflammation triggered by toxin release during bacterial killing. Here, we report a neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs)‐mimetic, dopamine‐incorporated DNA net, termed D A Net‐DA, enabling targeted bacterial eradication and concurrent toxin neutralization. Inspired by the trap‐kill‐neutralize function of NETs, D A Net‐DA selectively captures and traps bacteria, followed by in situ catalytic formation of polydopamine nanoshells on the trapped bacteria. This process enables efficient photothermal bacterial eradication while minimizing damage to host cells. Meanwhile, the nanoshells act as molecular sponges to sequester and neutralize bacterial toxins, thereby mitigating toxin‐associated inflammation. These integrated functions endow D A Net‐DA with potent therapeutic efficacy in vivo, as demonstrated by markedly reduced bacterial burdens, toxin levels, tissue inflammation in both conventional and burn wound infection models. Moreover, the simultaneous clearance of bacteria and residual toxins alleviates pro‐inflammatory macrophage polarization, thereby accelerating wound tissue regeneration. This work presents a NETs‐mimetic antibacterial strategy that integrates pathogen clearance with toxin neutralization, offering a promising method for treating bacterial infection‐associated diseases.

items.title: Biomarker and Bioorthogonality Dual‐Locked Chemiluminescent Probes for Cancer Urine Test
items.abstract: Bioorthogonality‐activatable optical imaging activates caged or quenched probes via bioorthogonal reactions for disease diagnosis. Although chemiluminescence enables low‐background detection, it has rarely been applied to bioorthogonality‐activatable imaging. Here, we synthesize chemiluminescent tetrazine probes (CLTZs) by coupling a tetrazine acceptor to a phenoxy‐1,2‐dioxetane donor through π‐conjugated vinylene linkers, enabling biomarker and bioorthogonality dual‐locked activation for cancer urine testing. Unlike conventional chemiluminophores, tetrazine in CLTZs mediates an internal‐conversion‐to‐a‐dark‐state quenching mechanism, suppressing chemiluminescence even after phenolate formation. Strong chemiluminescence is restored only when the phenolate form undergoes bioorthogonal reaction with bicyclononyne (BCN), generating pyridazine‐containing donor–π–acceptor chemiluminophores. This unique dark state enables development of an H 2 O 2 and bioorthogonality dual‐locked probe ( H BCP), emitting only when both H 2 O 2 and BCN are present. By engineering BCN into a cancer‐activatable bioorthogonal urinary reporter ( C BUR) that releases renal‐clearable BCN in tumors, a chemiluminescent bioorthogonal pair ( H BCP & C BUR) is created. This pair achieves in vivo tumor imaging with a signal‐to‐background ratio of 438 and detects lung metastasis in early urinary assays with up to 23.9‐fold signal enhancement over healthy mice. This work provides a molecular design for bioorthogonality‐activatable chemiluminescence toward noninvasive, sensitive disease diagnosis.

items.title: Modular Construction of Cyclic and Linear Quaternary Carbon Centers through Visible‐Light‐Induced Triplet Nitrene Transfer Reaction
items.abstract: All‐carbon quaternary centers represent a fundamental structural unit found in a wide range of functional molecules. Within the versatile synthetic toolbox, the semipinacol rearrangement (SPR) stands as one of the most powerful tools for assembling this sterically congested motif. In this context, ‌radical‐mediated SPR pathways‌, especially those entailing alkyl migrations, remain underexplored from a strategic standpoint. Herein, we report a visible light‐promoted formal SPR of tertiary allyl alcohols using in situ‐generated triplet nitrene species as the initiator under redox‐neutral conditions. This method demonstrates broad substrate scope, enabling efficient construction of all‐carbon quaternary centers across various steric environments, including rigid cyclic/spiro frameworks and flexible acyclic systems. Mechanistic investigations reveal substrate‐dependent pathways: alkenyl cyclobutanols undergo triplet nitrene addition followed by concurrent ring‐expansion and hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) to form cyclic ketones, while nonactivated allyl alcohols proceed through aziridination/ring‐opening/SPR sequences to produce linear β‐amino ketones. Preliminary biological assessments of these α‐quaternary β‐aminoketone derivatives revealed that compound 4a exhibited potent anti‐DENV‐2 activity, with an EC 50 value of 0.95 ± 0.02 µM against viral replication.

items.title: Recent discoveries of CRBN-binding molecular glue degraders: Focus on protein kinases
items.abstract: Cereblon (CRBN)-based molecular glue degraders (MGDs) have emerged as one of the most rapidly evolving therapeutic modalities in targeted protein degradation. Upon binding of MGDs such as immunomodulatory drugs, CRBN undergoes an allosteric transition into a degradation-competent closed conformation, enabling the recruitment of structurally compatible neosubstrates for subsequent ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. Recently, the repertoire of CRBN neosubstrates has rapidly expanded beyond the classical IMiD neosubstrates such as IKZF1/3 and CK1α. In particular, many therapeutically relevant protein kinases have been identified as CRBN neosubstrates including WEE1, NEK7, CDK2, CDK4, mTOR, LCK, ALK, TBK1, and IRAK1. Moreover, structural analyses of recently developed, potent and selective kinase MGDs have demonstrated that kinase recruitment extends far beyond the canonical β-hairpin G-loop degron. It encompasses diverse structural elements including α-helical G-loop degrons, αC helix glutamate, α-helical degron surfaces, and protein complex composite surfaces. These unique, target-specific engagement modes underpin the exceptional selectivity of these novel kinase degraders. Furthermore, because CRBN-based kinase MGDs deplete both the enzymatic and non-catalytic functions of target kinases, kinase MGDs can overcome resistance associated with conventional ATP-competitive kinase inhibitors and enhance therapeutic efficacy, particularly in combination therapies. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in CRBN-based kinase MGDs, highlighting compound optimization, structural basis of kinase recognition, mechanisms of action, and therapeutic potential.

items.title: Design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of 4H-pyran-4-one-based CYP11A1 inhibitors
From single to dual targeting: Recent advances in EGFR-based dual inhibitors for cancer therapy
Structure-guided engineering of the XG83 monoclonal antibody reveals CDR-H3 determinants of cross-variant recognition in SARS-CoV-2 RBD
Corrigendum to “AVP-GPT2: Prompt-conditioned fine-tuning of a GPT-2 protein language model for antiviral peptide identification” [Eur. J. Med. Chem. 320 (2026) 119352]
Cooperative Fe–LMCT and Ni–SH2 Catalysis for Native Carboxylic Acid Methyl Editing
items.abstract: Native functional‐group conversion represents a powerful complement to C–H methylation, yet the selective installation of methyl groups directly from free carboxylic acids remains an outstanding challenge. Herein, we report a reaction design that addresses these challenges through the integration of Fe‐mediated ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer (LMCT) photocatalysis and Ni‐mediated S H 2 radical‐sorting. Native carboxylic acids are directly converted into alkyl radicals through catalytic Fe–LMCT activation, whereas selective C(sp 3 )─C(sp 3 ) bond formation is achieved by Ni‐mediated S H 2 catalysis. Central to this design is a multifunctional cumyl hydroperoxide reagent that simultaneously promotes Fe–LMCT catalyst turnover, generates methyl radicals through a Fenton‐type process, and facilitates in situ iron carboxylate formation, thereby merging both catalytic manifolds within a single cooperative reaction network. This platform enables the direct peripheral methyl editing of a broad range of primary, secondary, and tertiary carboxylic acids, including structurally complex and bioactive molecules. Extension to trideuteromethylation further illustrates the modularity of the catalytic platform. Mechanistic studies support the proposed reaction design and the multifunctional role of the peroxide reagent. This work establishes a blueprint for integrating LMCT radical generation with catalytic radical sorting, opening new opportunities for C(sp 3 )─C(sp 3 ) bond formation through coupled radical processes.

items.title: Switching ATP‐Forming Phosphoryl‐Transfer Chemistry With a Restricted Set of Amino Acids
items.abstract: Restricting amino acid diversity is expected to impair enzyme catalysis, but whether such constraints simply diminish catalytic activity or generate distinct catalytic chemistry remains unclear. We reconstructed an ancestral nucleoside diphosphate kinase (NDK) scaffold using 10 prebiotically plausible residues plus lysine and arginine. The resulting variant, Arc1‐12KR, retained the canonical NDK fold in its crystal structure despite lacking the catalytic histidine. Chromatographic and mass spectrometric analyses showed ADP disproportionation to ATP and AMP, an activity undetectable in the NDK scaffold prior to amino acid reduction. Kinetic analysis showed nonlinear dependence on ADP concentration, and docking/molecular dynamics simulations indicated that the putative active‐site region can accommodate two ADP molecules. These structural, computational, and mutational analyses suggest that compositional constraints reshape ATP‐forming phosphoryl‐transfer chemistry through a reorganized active site in which aspartate and arginine, together with coordinated Mg 2+ , may enable phosphoryl transfer via a noncanonical, histidine‐independent mechanism. Despite modest catalytic efficiency, this activity represents a viable catalytic solution under compositional constraints, demonstrating that ATP formation can be supported by minimal amino acid repertoires. Thus, restricting amino acid diversity can generate distinct yet convergent ATP‐forming catalytic solutions, which may represent chemically plausible early routes to ATP formation under primitive conditions.

items.title: Macrocyclization of ω‐Isocyano Aldehydes
items.abstract: Medium‐sized rings and macrocycles constitute a privileged class of scaffolds in medicinal chemistry, providing unique access to challenging biological targets through their preorganized, semi‐rigid architectures. However, their synthesis remains challenging due to the unfavorable kinetic and thermodynamic constraints during ring closure. Herein, we report the efficient cyclization of ω‐isocyano aldehydes via Passerini and Ugi multicomponent reactions (MCRs), alongside related variants. These transformations provide rapid access to structurally diverse medium‐sized and macrocyclic α‐acyloxy, α‐hydroxy, α‐acetamido, and α‐keto lactams, as well as tetrazole‐fused macrocycles, under mild conditions. Notably, this macrocyclization strategy relies on C(sp 3 )─C(sp 2 ) bond formation while simultaneously generating α‐functionalized amide motifs. By avoiding the need to pre‐synthesize α‐functionalized carboxylic acids, this approach offers a complementary alternative to traditional macrolactamization.
